    # Odin destruction lab
    
    A standalone implementation of `destruction-model-implementation-plan.md`, using Odin's bundled Box2D and raylib libraries. The workspace did not contain an existing engine or transport, so this project includes a small native debug application and a localhost snapshot transport.
    
    ## Run
    
    Requires an Odin installation with compiled `vendor:box2d` and `vendor:raylib` libraries. Tested on Windows with Odin `dev-2026-05-nightly:ea5175d`.
    
    ```powershell
    odin run .
    odin test .
    odin build . -o:speed -out:BOM.exe
    ```
    
    The application starts with three connected wall subdivisions. Physics uses a fixed 60 Hz tick with four Box2D substeps and zero gravity. Press **I** to launch a projectile into the wall.
    
    | Control | Action |
    | --- | --- |
    | Left click | Blast at the cursor |
    | Right click, then D or Delete | Select and directly remove a subdivision |
    | Ctrl + left click | Directly remove the hovered subdivision |
    | Shift + left click, or X near a yellow anchor | Break a connection |
    | 1 / 2 / 3 | Reset with chunk / splinter / shatter material |
    | T | Reset with terminal seed zero or generative seed 42 |
    | Q / E | Decrease / increase blast radius |
    | Space / N | Pause / advance one physics tick |
    | R / I | Reset / launch a projectile |
    | Mouse wheel / middle drag | Zoom / pan |
    | J / V | Toggle joints / cosmetic flexible surface |
    | S / L | Save / receive `snapshot.json` |
    
    For automated execution:
    
    ```powershell
    odin run . -- --headless
    odin run . -- --smoke
    ```
    
    `--headless` evaluates a blast, runs 60 physics ticks, validates the graph, writes `snapshot.json`, and reconstructs a receiver. `--smoke` renders two frames in a hidden window, exports `debug-preview.png`, and exits.
    
    ## Live transmission
    
    Build once, then run these in separate terminals:
    
    ```powershell
    .\BOM.exe --serve
    .\BOM.exe --receive
    ```
    
    The sender listens on **127.0.0.1:9901** for one receiver. It sends explicit complete snapshots after structural changes and at 10 Hz for motion. The receiver renders polygons, connections, ownership and interpolated motion without simulating physics. Destroy or split the wall in the sender to see the receiver update.
    
    Frames contain a four byte little endian payload length followed by UTF-8 JSON, capped at 4 MiB. Partial reads, partial writes, coalesced frames and disconnects are handled. One in-flight send is retained; the sender does not accumulate a queue of old states. `read_state`, `encode_snapshot` and `decode_snapshot` can also be used with another transport.
    
    Snapshots carry current geometry, materials, stable IDs, piece memberships, future generation seeds, structural revision, and body motion. They reconstruct derived anchors from the transmitted outlines. Infinite strengths have explicit flags so snapshots remain valid JSON. A piece's current seed is never used to reconstruct its existing damaged geometry.
    
    ## Implementation
    
    | File | Responsibility |
    | --- | --- |
    | `model.odin` | Stable identity, shared reference vertex pool, retained memberships, component traversal and width filtering |
    | `geometry.odin` | Shared boundaries, displaced cuts, convex hull and collision decomposition |
    | `destruction.odin` | Seeded generation, blast evaluation and the shared structural update |
    | `physics.odin` | Box2D bodies, fixtures, weld joints, interaction aggregation and load policy |
    | `state.odin` | State reader, snapshot validation, serialization and pose interpolation |
    | `transmission.odin` | Framed localhost TCP snapshots and the receiver application |
    | `debug_view.odin` | Native controls, rendering and material presets |
    | `behavior_test.odin` | Focused behavior and integration checks |
    
    IDs are monotonic and mapped to storage rows. Removed rows and outline ranges remain retained until `scene_destroy`; no world repacking is performed. Subdivision outlines use ranges into one append-only vertex pool in a common undeformed reference frame. Their `outline` slices are derived views refreshed when the pool grows. Borrowed polygon views must not be held across scene mutations. `add_subdivision` copies its input; the caller retains ownership of that input allocation. `make_polygon` creates an owned polygon.
    
    `apply_failures` stages one generation, preserves old neighbor relationships, inherits only surviving boundary attachments, regroups affected pieces with temporary adjacency, filters connected groups, and leaves physics synchronization to the between-step adapter. A failed connection cannot be healed by proximity. Failure IDs and new groups use stable ordering, including when storage rows are shuffled. `discard_subdivisions` provides direct removal independently of a generative piece seed.
    
    Generation clips convex regions and ear-clips supported simple concave polygons. Each internal displaced cut is generated once and installed in both adjacent outlines. Outside boundaries remain intact. Count is a target before final triangulation; concave outlines and the shatter preset can produce more children. Aspect ratio biases cut direction. Self-intersecting outlines and polygons with holes are outside this implementation's input domain.
    
    The load policy uses the strongest individual interaction, preserving opposing interactions against different bodies. Contact points and convex fixtures against the same other body are combined. Joint reactions also load their endpoint subdivisions. Thresholds use `load > 0 && load >= strength`; strength records are never reduced by prior events. `physics_tick` accepts a replacement `Load_Calculator` function.
    
    The provided plan refers to a handoff's fixed blast falloff but does not supply its numeric curve. This implementation uses `10 * (1 - distance / radius)` inside the radius and zero outside. Impulses are `direction * load * mass * 0.1`. Both tuning constants and the falloff live in `destruction.odin`. The torque reference length is one world unit, and global joint damping is 0.7. Flexibility zero selects a stiff weld; positive flexibility selects spring softness.
    
    Contact `totalNormalImpulse` is converted using the full tick interval. The installed binding's tangent and rolling impulses use the final substep interval. Joint reactions already supply force and torque. See the [Box2D simulation documentation](https://box2d.org/documentation/md_simulation.html) and [contact solver source](https://github.com/erincatto/box2d/blob/v3.1.1/src/contact_solver.c) for the underlying quantities.
    
    Collision decomposition merges adjacent convex regions. Box2D can collapse microscopic ears during hull welding; those ears are omitted from fixtures, and a subdivision with no resolvable fixture receives a small bounding box proxy. The destruction outline, logical identity, polygon mass and inertia remain retained. Collision fixtures never become additional destruction entities.
    
    Group width is the minimum projection width of its reference geometry's convex hull. Small subdivisions remain live when their connected group is wide enough. Narrow resulting groups become one second visual remnants before fading. New groups are filtered before any new bodies are created. Rendering interpolates poses and optionally blends shared presentation vertices across flexible joints; it does not modify collision or failure geometry.
    
    ## Verification
    
    `odin test .` covers bridge and subdivision removal; surviving and broken inherited attachments; simultaneous endpoint replacement; processing and storage order independence; seed zero; subthreshold and infinite strengths; one generation per pass; rotational motion inheritance; a single blast impulse transfer; rotation independent width; group filtering; retained bodies; concave collision fixtures; physical impacts; overloaded joints; replaceable load policies; flexibility; repeated blasts for all presets; snapshots; interpolation; and real TCP transfer of a wall and its split. Odin's test allocator tracks allocations and reports leaks.
    
    The implementation intentionally uses ordinary arrays, complete affected-piece membership rebuilds, local candidate scans, and explicit snapshots. Large-world spatial selection, compression, rollback and parallel simulation can be added when a measured workload calls for them.

## User

I found one concrete bug and one gameplay choice I’d change:
1. Generation can replace a failed subdivision with an identical copy indefinitely.
   In destruction.odin:84, reaching the minimum area stops splitting but can leave the unchanged parent as the sole child. Continued overload then creates new IDs and bodies without changing its shape. A small subdivision attached to a larger piece can survive the piece-width filter.
   Simple fix: if generation cannot produce a genuine partition, use the existing direct-removal outcome. Add a regression test for repeated failure of that small attached subdivision.
2. Direct blast load is capped at 10.
   destruction.odin:196 uses 10 * (1 - distance/radius). Consequently, a strength of 20 can never fail the direct blast check, regardless of radius.
   Our plan left the numeric curve unspecified, so this is an implementation choice. Given my  intention that radius controls power, I’d use something like k * max(0, radius - distance), with one fixed global multiplier.

## Assistant

I’ll make failed generation fall back to removal when it cannot produce a genuine partition, change blast load so radius controls power, and add regression tests for both.

    #+feature dynamic-literals
    package main
    
    import "core:math"
    
    polygon_area :: proc(p: Polygon) -> f32 {
        a: f32
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) { a += vcross(p.points[i],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]) }
        return math.abs(a)*0.5
    }
    clip_polygon :: proc(p: Polygon, axis: int, cut: f32, keep_low: bool) -> Polygon {
        points: [dynamic]Vec2
        defer delete(points)
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) {
            a,b := p.points[i],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]
            av,bv := a.x-cut,b.x-cut
            if axis == 1 { av = a.y-cut; bv = b.y-cut }
            if !keep_low { av = -av; bv = -bv }
            inside_a, inside_b := av <= 0.00001,bv <= 0.00001
            if inside_a { append(&points,a) }
            if inside_a != inside_b {
                t := av/(av-bv)
                append(&points,vadd(a,vmul(vsub(b,a),t)))
            }
        }
        return make_polygon(points[:])
    }
    is_convex :: proc(p: Polygon) -> bool {
        if len(p.points) < 3 { return false }
        sign: f32
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) {
            cross := vcross(vsub(p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)],p.points[i]),vsub(p.points[(i+2)%len(p.points)],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]))
            if math.abs(cross) < 0.00001 { continue }
            if sign == 0 { sign = cross } else if cross*sign < 0 { return false }
        }
        return true
    }
    point_in_triangle :: proc(p,a,b,c: Vec2, orientation: f32) -> bool {
        return vcross(vsub(b,a),vsub(p,a))*orientation >= -0.00001 &&
               vcross(vsub(c,b),vsub(p,b))*orientation >= -0.00001 &&
               vcross(vsub(a,c),vsub(p,c))*orientation >= -0.00001
    }
    triangulate_polygon :: proc(p: Polygon) -> [dynamic]Polygon {
        result: [dynamic]Polygon
        indices: [dynamic]int
        defer delete(indices)
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) { append(&indices,i) }
        signed: f32
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) { signed += vcross(p.points[i],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]) }
        orientation := f32(1)
        if signed < 0 { orientation = -1 }
        for len(indices) > 3 {
            found := false
            for k in 0..<len(indices) {
                i,j,l := indices[(k+len(indices)-1)%len(indices)],indices[k],indices[(k+1)%len(indices)]
                a,b,c := p.points[i],p.points[j],p.points[l]
                if vcross(vsub(b,a),vsub(c,b))*orientation <= 0.00001 { continue }
                contains := false
                for n in indices { if n != i && n != j && n != l && point_in_triangle(p.points[n],a,b,c,orientation) { contains = true; break } }
                if contains { continue }
                append(&result,make_polygon([]Vec2{a,b,c}))
                ordered_remove(&indices,k)
                found = true
                break
            }
            if !found { break }
        }
        if len(indices) == 3 { append(&result,make_polygon([]Vec2{p.points[indices[0]],p.points[indices[1]],p.points[indices[2]]})) }
        return result
    }
    // Straight shared cuts are constructed by clipping both sides at one value.
    // Outside edges are never moved; no gap or overlap is introduced at the cut.
    generate_children :: proc(parent: Polygon, recipe: Material, seed: u8) -> [dynamic]Polygon {
        result: [dynamic]Polygon
        if seed == 0 { return result }
        if !is_convex(parent) || recipe.triangulate { result = triangulate_polygon(parent) } else {
            append(&result,make_polygon(parent.points))
        }
        target := max(recipe.generation_count,len(result))
        for len(result) < target {
            chosen := -1
            largest: f32
            for p,i in result { a := polygon_area(p); if a > largest { largest = a; chosen = i } }
            if chosen < 0 || largest < 0.0001 { break }
            p := result[chosen]
            min_x,min_y := f32(1e30),f32(1e30)
            max_x,max_y := f32(-1e30),f32(-1e30)
            for point in p.points { min_x=min(min_x,point.x); max_x=max(max_x,point.x); min_y=min(min_y,point.y); max_y=max(max_y,point.y) }
            axis := 0
            if (max_x-min_x) < (max_y-min_y)*max(recipe.aspect_ratio,0.1) { axis = 1 }
            fraction := 0.4+0.2*f32(derive_seed(seed,u64(len(result))))/255
            cut := min_x+(max_x-min_x)*fraction
            if axis == 1 { cut = min_y+(max_y-min_y)*fraction }
            low, high := clip_polygon(p,axis,cut,true),clip_polygon(p,axis,cut,false)
            if polygon_area(low) < 0.0001 || polygon_area(high) < 0.0001 { delete(low.points); delete(high.points); break }
            delete(p.points)
            result[chosen] = low
            append(&result,high)
        }
        displace_shared_boundaries(result[:],seed)
        if recipe.triangulate {
            triangles: [dynamic]Polygon
            for polygon in result {
                parts:=triangulate_polygon(polygon)
                for part in parts { append(&triangles,part) }
                delete(parts); delete(polygon.points)
            }
            delete(result)
            result=triangles
        }
        return result
    }

            if old_length <= 0 { continue }
            for a in left {
                for b in right {
                    if inherits_old_boundary(s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[a]].outline,s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[b]].outline,old_a.outline,old_b.outline) { add_connection(s,a,b) }
                }
            }
        }
        for id in failed_subs {
            children := replacements[id]
            for i in 0..<len(children) { for j in i+1..<len(children) { add_connection(s,children[i],children[j]) } }
        }
        owners: [dynamic]u64
        defer delete(owners)
        for owner in affected { append(&owners,owner) }
        sort_ids(owners[:])
        for owner in owners { rebuild_piece(s,owner) }
    }
    
    BLAST_MAX_LOAD :: f32(10)
    BLAST_IMPULSE_SCALE :: f32(0.1)
    blast_load :: proc(distance,radius: f32) -> f32 {
        if radius <= 0 || distance >= radius { return 0 }
        return BLAST_MAX_LOAD*(1-distance/radius)
    }
    fails :: proc(load,strength: f32) -> bool { return load > 0 && load >= strength }
    evaluate_blast :: proc(s: ^Scene, blast: Blast) -> Failures {
        f := Failures{}
        for i in 0..<len(s.subdivisions) {
            sub := &s.subdivisions[i]
            if !sub.live { continue }
            offset := vsub(subdivision_sample(sub^),blast.position)
            distance := vlen(offset)
            load := blast_load(distance,blast.radius)
            if load <= 0 { continue }
            if distance > 0.00001 { apply_blast_motion(s,sub,vmul(offset,1/distance),load) }
            if fails(load,s.materials[sub.material].subdivision_strength) { append(&f.subdivisions,sub.id) }
        }
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            a := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]]
            load := blast_load(vlen(vsub(connection_sample(s,c),blast.position)),blast.radius)
            if fails(load,s.materials[a.material].connection_strength) { append(&f.connections,c.id) }
        }
        return f
    }
    blast_pass :: proc(s: ^Scene, blast: Blast) {
        physics_read_motion(s)
        f := evaluate_blast(s,blast)
        apply_failures(s,f)
        delete(f.subdivisions); delete(f.connections)
        physics_sync_structure(s)
    }
    fade_step :: proc(s: ^Scene, dt: f32) {
        for i := len(s.remnants)-1; i >= 0; i -= 1 {
            s.remnants[i].age += dt
            if s.remnants[i].age >= 1 { ordered_remove(&s.remnants,i) }
        }
    }
    
    package main
    
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:math"
    
    Physics :: struct {
        world: b2.WorldId,
        bodies: map[u64]b2.BodyId,
        joints: map[u64]b2.JointId,
        fixture_counts: map[u64]int,
        active: bool,
    }
    Interaction :: struct { force: Vec2, torque: f32 }
    REFERENCE_LENGTH :: f32(1)
    PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS :: 4
    GLOBAL_DAMPING :: f32(0.7)
    
    to_b2 :: proc(v: Vec2) -> b2.Vec2 { return {v.x,v.y} }
    from_b2 :: proc(v: b2.Vec2) -> Vec2 { return {v.x,v.y} }
    interaction_load :: proc(i: Interaction) -> f32 {
        return max(vlen(i.force),math.abs(i.torque)/REFERENCE_LENGTH)
    }
    equivalent_force :: proc(impulse: Vec2, interval: f32) -> Vec2 {
        assert(interval > 0)
        return vmul(impulse,1/interval)
    }
    physics_init :: proc(s: ^Scene, gravity: Vec2 = {}) {
        assert(!s.physics.active)
        def := b2.DefaultWorldDef()
        def.gravity = to_b2(gravity)
        s.physics = Physics{world=b2.CreateWorld(def),bodies=make(map[u64]b2.BodyId),joints=make(map[u64]b2.JointId),fixture_counts=make(map[u64]int),active=true}
        physics_sync_structure(s)
    }
    physics_destroy :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        if !s.physics.active { return }
        b2.DestroyWorld(s.physics.world)
        delete(s.physics.bodies); delete(s.physics.joints); delete(s.physics.fixture_counts)
        s.physics = {}
    }
    physics_read_motion :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        if !s.physics.active { return }
        for id,body in s.physics.bodies {
            row := s.sub_rows[id]
            rotation := b2.Body_GetRotation(body)
            s.subdivisions[row].pose = Pose{
                position=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(body)),angle=math.atan2(rotation.s,rotation.c),
                velocity=from_b2(b2.Body_GetLinearVelocity(body)),angular_velocity=b2.Body_GetAngularVelocity(body),
            }
        }
    }
    physics_create_fixture :: proc(s: ^Scene, body: b2.BodyId, sub: Subdivision, outline: Polygon) -> bool {
        points: [dynamic]b2.Vec2
        defer delete(points)
        for point in outline.points { append(&points,to_b2(vsub(point,sub.rest_center))) }
        hull := b2.ComputeHull(points[:])
        // Hull welding can collapse a thin ear below Box2D's collision tolerance.
        if hull.count < 3 { return false }
        polygon := b2.MakePolygon(hull,0)
        def := b2.DefaultShapeDef()
        def.density = 1
        _ = b2.CreatePolygonShape(body,def,polygon)
        s.physics.fixture_counts[sub.id] += 1
        return true
    }
    physics_finish_mass :: proc(s: ^Scene,body: b2.BodyId,sub: Subdivision) {
        if s.physics.fixture_counts[sub.id]==0 {
            // A microscopic attached subdivision is still one live logical entity.
            // Use a bounding fixture when the engine cannot resolve any of its ears.
            lo,hi:=Vec2{1e30,1e30},Vec2{-1e30,-1e30}
            for rest in sub.outline.points { p:=vsub(rest,sub.rest_center); lo={min(lo.x,p.x),min(lo.y,p.y)}; hi={max(hi.x,p.x),max(hi.y,p.y)} }
            polygon:=b2.MakeOffsetBox(max(f32(0.0025),(hi.x-lo.x)*0.5),max(f32(0.0025),(hi.y-lo.y)*0.5),to_b2(vmul(vadd(lo,hi),0.5)),b2.MakeRot(0))
            def:=b2.DefaultShapeDef(); def.density=1
            _ = b2.CreatePolygonShape(body,def,polygon)
            s.physics.fixture_counts[sub.id]=1
        }
        // Keep mass and the body origin tied to the exact logical polygon, including
        // when Box2D simplifies a fixture. This also makes rotational inheritance exact.
        inertia: f32
        for i in 0..<len(sub.outline.points) {
            a,b:=vsub(sub.outline.points[i],sub.rest_center),vsub(sub.outline.points[(i+1)%len(sub.outline.points)],sub.rest_center)
            inertia+=vcross(a,b)*(vdot(a,a)+vdot(a,b)+vdot(b,b))/12
        }
        b2.Body_SetMassData(body,b2.MassData{mass=polygon_area(sub.outline),center={},rotationalInertia=math.abs(inertia)})
        b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(body,to_b2(sub.pose.velocity))
        b2.Body_SetAngularVelocity(body,sub.pose.angular_velocity)
    }
    // This runs only between World_Step calls. Existing handles survive ownership changes.
    physics_sync_structure :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        if !s.physics.active { return }
        dead_joints: [dynamic]u64
        dead_bodies: [dynamic]u64
        defer delete(dead_joints); defer delete(dead_bodies)
        for id,joint in s.physics.joints {
            row,ok := s.conn_rows[id]
            if !ok || !s.connections[row].live { b2.DestroyJoint(joint); append(&dead_joints,id) }
        }
        for id in dead_joints { delete_key(&s.physics.joints,id) }
        for id,body in s.physics.bodies {
            row,ok := s.sub_rows[id]
            if !ok || !s.subdivisions[row].live { b2.DestroyBody(body); append(&dead_bodies,id) }
        }
        for id in dead_bodies { delete_key(&s.physics.bodies,id); delete_key(&s.physics.fixture_counts,id) }
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            if _,exists := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]; exists { continue }
            def := b2.DefaultBodyDef()
            def.type = .dynamicBody
            def.position = to_b2(sub.pose.position)
            def.rotation = b2.MakeRot(sub.pose.angle)
            def.linearVelocity = to_b2(sub.pose.velocity)
            def.angularVelocity = sub.pose.angular_velocity
            body := b2.CreateBody(s.physics.world,def)
            s.physics.bodies[sub.id] = body
            if is_convex(sub.outline) && len(sub.outline.points) <= 8 {
                physics_create_fixture(s,body,sub,sub.outline)
            } else {
                triangles := convex_decomposition(sub.outline)
                for triangle in triangles { physics_create_fixture(s,body,sub,triangle); delete(triangle.points) }
                delete(triangles)
            }
            physics_finish_mass(s,body,sub)
        }
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            if _,exists := s.physics.joints[c.id]; exists { continue }
            a := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]]
            b := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
            def := b2.DefaultWeldJointDef()
            def.bodyIdA = s.physics.bodies[c.a]
            def.bodyIdB = s.physics.bodies[c.b]
            def.localAnchorA = to_b2(c.local_a)
            def.localAnchorB = to_b2(c.local_b)
            // All outlines share one undeformed frame. Its relative rest angle is zero.
            def.referenceAngle = 0
            flexibility := max(s.materials[a.material].flexibility,s.materials[b.material].flexibility)
            if flexibility > 0 {
                def.linearHertz = 1/max(flexibility,0.01)
                def.angularHertz = def.linearHertz
            }
            def.linearDampingRatio = GLOBAL_DAMPING
            def.angularDampingRatio = GLOBAL_DAMPING
            s.physics.joints[c.id] = b2.CreateWeldJoint(s.physics.world,def)
        }
    }
    apply_blast_motion :: proc(s: ^Scene, sub: ^Subdivision, direction: Vec2, load: f32) {
        delta_v := vmul(direction,load*BLAST_IMPULSE_SCALE)
        if s.physics.active {
            body := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]
            impulse := vmul(delta_v,b2.Body_GetMass(body))
            b2.Body_ApplyLinearImpulseToCenter(body,to_b2(impulse),true)
            sub.pose.velocity = from_b2(b2.Body_GetLinearVelocity(body))
        } else {
            sub.pose.velocity = vadd(sub.pose.velocity,delta_v)
        }
    }
    // Contact points and fixtures against the same other body form one interaction.
    // Joint reactions are already forces; totalNormalImpulse covers the full tick.
    // Box2D's tangent/rolling impulses cover the final substep in this binding version.
    calculate_physics_loads :: proc(s: ^Scene, dt: f32) -> Failures {
        assert(dt > 0)
        failures := Failures{}
        loads := make(map[u64]f32)
        defer delete(loads)
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            body := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]
            capacity := int(b2.Body_GetContactCapacity(body))
            buffer := make([]b2.ContactData,capacity)
            contacts := b2.Body_GetContactData(body,buffer)
            interactions := make(map[b2.BodyId]Interaction)
            for contact in contacts {
                body_a,body_b := b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdA),b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdB)
                other := body_b
                sign := f32(-1)
                if body_b == body { other=body_a; sign=1 }
                normal := from_b2(contact.manifold.normal)
                tangent := Vec2{normal.y,-normal.x}
                interaction := interactions[other]
                for k in 0..<int(contact.manifold.pointCount) {
                    point := contact.manifold.points[k]
                    force := vadd(equivalent_force(vmul(normal,point.totalNormalImpulse*sign),dt),equivalent_force(vmul(tangent,point.tangentImpulse*sign),dt/f32(PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS)))
                    interaction.force = vadd(interaction.force,force)
                    interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(from_b2(point.point),sub.pose.position),force)
                }
                interaction.torque += contact.manifold.rollingImpulse*sign/(dt/f32(PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS))
                interactions[other] = interaction
            }
            for _,interaction in interactions { loads[sub.id] = max(loads[sub.id],interaction_load(interaction)) }
            delete(interactions); delete(buffer)
        }
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            joint := s.physics.joints[c.id]
            interaction := Interaction{force=from_b2(b2.Joint_GetConstraintForce(joint)),torque=b2.Joint_GetConstraintTorque(joint)}
            load := interaction_load(interaction)
            a,b := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]],s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
            a_interaction,b_interaction := interaction,interaction
            a_interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(posed_point(a,c.rest_point),a.pose.position),interaction.force)
            b_interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(posed_point(b,c.rest_point),b.pose.position),interaction.force)
            loads[c.a] = max(loads[c.a],interaction_load(a_interaction))
            loads[c.b] = max(loads[c.b],interaction_load(b_interaction))
            material := s.materials[s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]].material]
            if fails(load,material.connection_strength) { append(&failures.connections,c.id) }
        }
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if sub.live && fails(loads[sub.id],s.materials[sub.material].subdivision_strength) { append(&failures.subdivisions,sub.id) }
        }
        return failures
    }
    Load_Calculator :: #type proc(s: ^Scene,dt: f32) -> Failures
    physics_tick :: proc(s: ^Scene, dt: f32,calculate_loads: Load_Calculator = calculate_physics_loads) {
        assert(s.physics.active && dt > 0)
        physics_sync_structure(s)
        b2.World_Step(s.physics.world,dt,PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS)
        physics_read_motion(s)
        failures := calculate_loads(s,dt)
        apply_failures(s,failures)
        delete(failures.subdivisions); delete(failures.connections)
        delete(failures.discard_subdivisions)
        physics_sync_structure(s)
        fade_step(s,dt)
    }

    counts :: proc(s: ^Scene) -> (int,int,int) {
        a,b,c := 0,0,0
        for x in s.subdivisions { if x.live { a+=1 } }
        for x in s.connections { if x.live { b+=1 } }
        for x in s.pieces { if x.live { c+=1 } }

    }

        f := Failures{}
        for id in ids { append(&f.subdivisions,id) }
        return f
    }

    }

    # Odin destruction lab
    
    A standalone implementation of `destruction-model-implementation-plan.md`, using Odin's bundled Box2D and raylib libraries. The workspace did not contain an existing engine or transport, so this project includes a small native debug application and a localhost snapshot transport.
    
    ## Run
    
    Requires an Odin installation with compiled `vendor:box2d` and `vendor:raylib` libraries. Tested on Windows with Odin `dev-2026-05-nightly:ea5175d`.
    
    ```powershell
    odin run .
    odin test .
    odin build . -o:speed -out:BOM.exe
    ```
    
    The application starts with three connected wall subdivisions. Physics uses a fixed 60 Hz tick with four Box2D substeps and zero gravity. Press **I** to launch a projectile into the wall.
    
    | Control | Action |
    | --- | --- |
    | Left click | Blast at the cursor |
    | Right click, then D or Delete | Select and directly remove a subdivision |
    | Ctrl + left click | Directly remove the hovered subdivision |
    | Shift + left click, or X near a yellow anchor | Break a connection |
    | 1 / 2 / 3 | Reset with chunk / splinter / shatter material |
    | T | Reset with terminal seed zero or generative seed 42 |
    | Q / E | Decrease / increase blast radius |
    | Space / N | Pause / advance one physics tick |
    | R / I | Reset / launch a projectile |
    | Mouse wheel / middle drag | Zoom / pan |
    | J / V | Toggle joints / cosmetic flexible surface |
    | S / L | Save / receive `snapshot.json` |
    
    For automated execution:
    
    ```powershell
    odin run . -- --headless
    odin run . -- --smoke
    ```
    
    `--headless` evaluates a blast, runs 60 physics ticks, validates the graph, writes `snapshot.json`, and reconstructs a receiver. `--smoke` renders two frames in a hidden window, exports `debug-preview.png`, and exits.
    
    ## Live transmission
    
    Build once, then run these in separate terminals:
    
    ```powershell
    .\BOM.exe --serve
    .\BOM.exe --receive
    ```
    
    The sender listens on **127.0.0.1:9901** for one receiver. It sends explicit complete snapshots after structural changes and at 10 Hz for motion. The receiver renders polygons, connections, ownership and interpolated motion without simulating physics. Destroy or split the wall in the sender to see the receiver update.
    
    Frames contain a four byte little endian payload length followed by UTF-8 JSON, capped at 4 MiB. Partial reads, partial writes, coalesced frames and disconnects are handled. One in-flight send is retained; the sender does not accumulate a queue of old states. `read_state`, `encode_snapshot` and `decode_snapshot` can also be used with another transport.
    
    Snapshots carry current geometry, materials, stable IDs, piece memberships, future generation seeds, structural revision, and body motion. They reconstruct derived anchors from the transmitted outlines. Infinite strengths have explicit flags so snapshots remain valid JSON. A piece's current seed is never used to reconstruct its existing damaged geometry.
    
    ## Implementation
    
    | File | Responsibility |
    | --- | --- |
    | `model.odin` | Stable identity, shared reference vertex pool, retained memberships, component traversal and width filtering |
    | `geometry.odin` | Shared boundaries, displaced cuts, convex hull and collision decomposition |
    | `destruction.odin` | Seeded generation, blast evaluation and the shared structural update |
    | `physics.odin` | Box2D bodies, fixtures, weld joints, interaction aggregation and load policy |
    | `state.odin` | State reader, snapshot validation, serialization and pose interpolation |
    | `transmission.odin` | Framed localhost TCP snapshots and the receiver application |
    | `debug_view.odin` | Native controls, rendering and material presets |
    | `behavior_test.odin` | Focused behavior and integration checks |
    
    IDs are monotonic and mapped to storage rows. Removed rows and outline ranges remain retained until `scene_destroy`; no world repacking is performed. Subdivision outlines use ranges into one append-only vertex pool in a common undeformed reference frame. Their `outline` slices are derived views refreshed when the pool grows. Borrowed polygon views must not be held across scene mutations. `add_subdivision` copies its input; the caller retains ownership of that input allocation. `make_polygon` creates an owned polygon.
    
    `apply_failures` stages one generation, preserves old neighbor relationships, inherits only surviving boundary attachments, regroups affected pieces with temporary adjacency, filters connected groups, and leaves physics synchronization to the between-step adapter. A failed connection cannot be healed by proximity. Failure IDs and new groups use stable ordering, including when storage rows are shuffled. `discard_subdivisions` provides direct removal independently of a generative piece seed.
    
    Generation clips convex regions and ear-clips supported simple concave polygons. Each internal displaced cut is generated once and installed in both adjacent outlines. Outside boundaries remain intact. Count is a target before final triangulation; concave outlines and the shatter preset can produce more children. Aspect ratio biases cut direction. Self-intersecting outlines and polygons with holes are outside this implementation's input domain.
    
    The load policy uses the strongest individual interaction, preserving opposing interactions against different bodies. Contact points and convex fixtures against the same other body are combined. Joint reactions also load their endpoint subdivisions. Thresholds use `load > 0 && load >= strength`; strength records are never reduced by prior events. `physics_tick` accepts a replacement `Load_Calculator` function.
    
    The provided plan refers to a handoff's fixed blast falloff but does not supply its numeric curve. This implementation uses `10 * (1 - distance / radius)` inside the radius and zero outside. Impulses are `direction * load * mass * 0.1`. Both tuning constants and the falloff live in `destruction.odin`. The torque reference length is one world unit, and global joint damping is 0.7. Flexibility zero selects a stiff weld; positive flexibility selects spring softness.
    
    Contact `totalNormalImpulse` is converted using the full tick interval. The installed binding's tangent and rolling impulses use the final substep interval. Joint reactions already supply force and torque. See the [Box2D simulation documentation](https://box2d.org/documentation/md_simulation.html) and [contact solver source](https://github.com/erincatto/box2d/blob/v3.1.1/src/contact_solver.c) for the underlying quantities.
    
    Collision decomposition merges adjacent convex regions. Box2D can collapse microscopic ears during hull welding; those ears are omitted from fixtures, and a subdivision with no resolvable fixture receives a small bounding box proxy. The destruction outline, logical identity, polygon mass and inertia remain retained. Collision fixtures never become additional destruction entities.
    
    Group width is the minimum projection width of its reference geometry's convex hull. Small subdivisions remain live when their connected group is wide enough. Narrow resulting groups become one second visual remnants before fading. New groups are filtered before any new bodies are created. Rendering interpolates poses and optionally blends shared presentation vertices across flexible joints; it does not modify collision or failure geometry.
    
    ## Verification
    
    `odin test .` covers bridge and subdivision removal; surviving and broken inherited attachments; simultaneous endpoint replacement; processing and storage order independence; seed zero; subthreshold and infinite strengths; one generation per pass; rotational motion inheritance; a single blast impulse transfer; rotation independent width; group filtering; retained bodies; concave collision fixtures; physical impacts; overloaded joints; replaceable load policies; flexibility; repeated blasts for all presets; snapshots; interpolation; and real TCP transfer of a wall and its split. Odin's test allocator tracks allocations and reports leaks.
    
    The implementation intentionally uses ordinary arrays, complete affected-piece membership rebuilds, local candidate scans, and explicit snapshots. Large-world spatial selection, compression, rollback and parallel simulation can be added when a measured workload calls for them.

    #+feature dynamic-literals
    package main
    
    import "core:math"
    import "core:testing"
    import "core:sync"
    import "core:net"
    import "core:time"
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    
    // Box2D's process-wide world registry is not safe for concurrent world creation.
    physics_test_mutex: sync.Mutex
    
    counts :: proc(s: ^Scene) -> (int,int,int) {
        a,b,c := 0,0,0
        for x in s.subdivisions { if x.live { a+=1 } }
        for x in s.connections { if x.live { b+=1 } }
        for x in s.pieces { if x.live { c+=1 } }
        return a,b,c
    }
    expect_valid :: proc(t: ^testing.T,s: ^Scene) { ok,message:=validate_scene(s); testing.expect(t,ok,message) }
    close :: proc(a,b: f32) -> bool { return math.abs(a-b) < 0.001 }
    close_vec :: proc(a,b: Vec2) -> bool { return vlen(vsub(a,b)) < 0.001 }
    failure_for :: proc(ids: ..u64) -> Failures {
        f := Failures{}
        for id in ids { append(&f.subdivisions,id) }
        return f
    }
    free_failures :: proc(f: ^Failures) { delete(f.subdivisions); delete(f.connections); delete(f.discard_subdivisions); f^={} }

    broken_boundaries_do_not_heal :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        s:=make_wall(42); defer scene_destroy(&s)
        left:=s.subdivisions[0].id
        f:=failure_for(s.subdivisions[1].id); defer free_failures(&f)
        append(&f.connections,s.connections[0].id)
        apply_failures(&s,f)
        a,_,c:=counts(&s)
        testing.expect(t,a==4 && c==2)
        for connection in s.connections { testing.expect(t,!connection.live || (connection.a!=left && connection.b!=left)) }
        expect_valid(t,&s)
    }
    @(test)
    simultaneous_endpoint_replacement :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        s:=make_wall(42); defer scene_destroy(&s)
        f:=failure_for(s.subdivisions[0].id,s.subdivisions[1].id); defer free_failures(&f)
        apply_failures(&s,f)
        a,_,c:=counts(&s)
        testing.expect(t,a==5 && c==1)
        expect_valid(t,&s)
    }
    @(test)
    storage_and_failure_order_independence :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        s:=make_wall(42); defer scene_destroy(&s)
        r:=make_wall(42); defer scene_destroy(&r)
        f:=failure_for(s.subdivisions[0].id,s.subdivisions[1].id); defer free_failures(&f)
        g:=failure_for(r.subdivisions[1].id,r.subdivisions[0].id); defer free_failures(&g)
        r.subdivisions[0],r.subdivisions[2]=r.subdivisions[2],r.subdivisions[0]
        r.connections[0],r.connections[1]=r.connections[1],r.connections[0]
        for sub,i in r.subdivisions { r.sub_rows[sub.id]=i }
        for conn,i in r.connections { r.conn_rows[conn.id]=i }
        apply_failures(&s,f); apply_failures(&r,g)
        a,a_ok:=encode_snapshot(&s); defer delete(a)
        b,b_ok:=encode_snapshot(&r); defer delete(b)
        testing.expect(t,a_ok && b_ok && string(a)==string(b))
        expect_valid(t,&s); expect_valid(t,&r)
    }
    @(test)
    one_generation_per_blast :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        s:=make_wall(42); defer scene_destroy(&s)
        s.materials[0].connection_strength=math.inf_f32(1)
        blast_pass(&s,Blast{position={1.5,0.5},radius=0.8})
        a,_,_:=counts(&s)
        testing.expect(t,a==4 && len(s.subdivisions)==5)
        for i in 3..<len(s.subdivisions) { testing.expect(t,s.subdivisions[i].live) }
        expect_valid(t,&s)
    }
    @(test)
    motion_includes_rotation :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        s:=make_wall(42); defer scene_destroy(&s)
        parent:=s.subdivisions[1]
        parent.pose=Pose{position={10,4},angle=0.7,velocity={1,2},angular_velocity=3}
        s.subdivisions[1]=parent
        f:=failure_for(parent.id); defer free_failures(&f)
        apply_failures(&s,f)
        for i in 3..<len(s.subdivisions) {
            child:=s.subdivisions[i]
            r:=vsub(child.pose.position,parent.pose.position)
            expected:=vadd(parent.pose.velocity,Vec2{-3*r.y,3*r.x})
            testing.expect(t,close_vec(child.pose.velocity,expected) && close(child.pose.angular_velocity,3))
            testing.expect(t,close_vec(child.pose.position,posed_point(parent,child.rest_center)))
        }
    }
    @(test)
    blast_is_not_reapplied_to_children :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        s:=make_wall(42); defer scene_destroy(&s)
        s.materials[0].subdivision_strength=0
        s.materials[0].connection_strength=math.inf_f32(1)
        blast_pass(&s,Blast{position={1.4,0.5},radius=0.4})
        for i in 3..<len(s.subdivisions) { testing.expect(t,close_vec(s.subdivisions[i].pose.velocity,Vec2{0.75,0})) }
    }
    @(test)
    width_is_rotation_independent :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        s:=make_wall(); defer scene_destroy(&s)
        ids:=s.pieces[0].subdivisions[:]
        before:=piece_width(&s,ids)
        for i in 0..<len(s.subdivisions) { for j in 0..<len(s.subdivisions[i].outline.points) { s.subdivisions[i].outline.points[j]=vrotate(s.subdivisions[i].outline.points[j],0.738) } }
        testing.expect(t,close(before,piece_width(&s,ids)))
    }
    @(test)
    small_subdivisions_can_form_large_piece :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        s:=make_wall(42,0.75); defer scene_destroy(&s)
        f:=failure_for(s.subdivisions[1].id); defer free_failures(&f)
        apply_failures(&s,f)
        a,_,c:=counts(&s)
        testing.expect(t,a==4 && c==1 && len(s.remnants)==0)
    }

    # Next step: a playable destruction sandbox
    
    Make the local Odin lab comfortable to play with: one small side-view test yard, one movable character, the existing click-to-blast action, a quick reset and a compact settings panel. This is the next user-facing milestone for the rewrite.
    
    The reference was a brief look at the original [Bomb README](https://github.com/jblick1327/Bomb/blob/main/README.md) and repository layout. Its move/jump/bomb/reset loop supplies context. The implementation baseline here is the Odin prototype already shared in this conversation; this plan does not involve migrating the Unity project.
    
    The loop should be: launch, walk and jump around, preview and trigger a blast, interact with the fragments, then press R to try again with the same setup.
    
    **What the first version should feel like**
    
    - The application opens directly into the yard, ready to play.
    - A simple capsule or rectangle clearly marks the character. It collides with the floor and destruction geometry, can stand on fragments and can push loose pieces.
    - A fixed camera comfortably frames the whole small yard. Resizing the window preserves that framing; flying fragments do not move or zoom the camera.
    - The blast preview makes the effect's location and radius clear before clicking.
    - A short control hint and small settings/reset buttons leave most of the window available for the world.
    - The player is invulnerable during experimentation and returns to spawn after falling outside the yard.
    
    **Controls**
    
    | Input | Normal play |
    | --- | --- |
    | A/D or left/right arrows | Move |
    | Space | Jump |
    | Left click in the world | Trigger one blast at a valid cursor position |
    | Mouse wheel over the world | Adjust blast radius |
    | R | Reset the yard with the current applied settings |
    | Tab or Escape | Open the settings panel and pause; close it to resume |
    | F3 | Toggle inspection tools and diagnostics |
    
    Use a hint such as â€œA/D Move Â· Space Jump Â· Click Blast Â· R Resetâ€ along one edge, with â€œTab Settingsâ€ on the settings button. Put the complete controls in the panel. Keep the existing subdivision IDs, connection lines, counts and manual removal tools behind F3. Use Delete for selected-subdivision removal so D always remains movement.
    
    Configure the window library so Escape opens or closes the panel instead of exiting the application.
    
    **The yard and player**
    
    Build one fixed scene: a static floor, a spawn point on the left and a small destructible stepped wall or tower to the right. Use the existing generator and model to create the structure. Keep enough clear floor space to approach the wall and move around the debris.
    
    Use ordinary world gravity for this scene. Tune its starting material strengths and blast scale so the structure rests stably on the floor and responds clearly to deliberate actions. Leave the physics adapter's zero-gravity test fixtures available for existing tests.
    
    Give the player one Box2D body with a capsule or simple rectangular collider and fixed rotation. Keep its small controller state separate from destruction subdivisions: structural failure passes should not replace or remove the player. Reuse contact information to determine support. Control horizontal movement and jumping while Box2D handles vertical motion and collision. A short jump buffer and coyote window, initially around 0.1 seconds each, are enough jump assistance for this version.
    
    Put the movement constants together: speed, acceleration, jump speed and the two jump-assistance times. Resetting or respawning clears grounded state and jump timers. The player uses the same world as the fragments, so jumping onto and pushing debris exercises the actual simulation.
    
    **Aiming and interaction feedback**
    
    Draw a small cursor marker and a thin circle showing the current blast radius. Fire once per mouse press. Keep the model's outside-origin assumption: when the cursor is inside live destruction geometry, show an invalid marker and suppress the blast. A short message such as â€œAim outside the solid shapeâ€ explains the blocked action. Use the logical posed outlines for this test.
    
    Give UI and inspection actions priority over world actions. A click on any button, slider or panel must never also trigger a blast. Mouse-wheel input over the panel belongs to the panel. While the panel is open, player and world actions are suspended. Clear pending jump/blast input on opening it, and resume without accumulating paused time into a physics catch-up burst.
    
    Keep feedback brief: a small temporary message for reset, invalid aim or settings applied. Let the geometry and motion show successful destruction.
    
    **One compact settings panel**
    
    Open a panel that pauses the simulation and contains Resume, Apply & Reset and the following existing settings:
    
    | Control | Behavior |
    | --- | --- |
    | Blast radius | The same value adjusted by the mouse wheel. |
    | Breakup pattern: Chunk / Splinter / Shatter | Set generation count, aspect ratio and triangulation through the existing presets. Keep strength and flexibility independent. |
    | Fragment strength | Edit the existing subdivision-strength value. |
    | Connection strength | Edit the existing connection-strength value. |
    | Flexibility | Edit the existing softness value. |
    | Generate children | On uses the current nonzero seed; off uses seed zero. Existing geometry remains live until it fails. |
    
    The strength and flexibility fields can sit in one collapsed Tuning section. Reuse UI widgets already available in the project; a few fixed controls are sufficient. Use plain labels rather than component or storage terminology.
    
    Store these selections in one small settings record. Radius updates the preview immediately. Stage the other edits until Apply & Reset, which rebuilds the yard and resumes play. This gives material and joint changes a clear moment to take effect. R resets the last applied setup, including its seed; it does not silently generate a different experiment. Keep detailed recipe editing and seed randomization for a later need.
    
    **Implementation order**
    
    1. **Check the starting behavior.** Fix the known generation case that returns an unchanged single replacement when splitting cannot proceed. Use the existing direct-removal outcome for that failed subdivision. Settle the radius-to-load curve: the current normalized curve caps direct load at 10; a fixed multiplier times `max(0, radius - distance)` supports the intended radius/power relationship. Keep these as focused changes and add the small-generation regression case.
    
    2. **Build the yard, player and shared reset.** Add the floor, gravity, player controller and fixed framing. Implement one reset function that recreates the scene and player, clears remnants and pending inputs, and restores the spawn. Preserve the applied settings. Verify movement, support on fragments and repeatable reset before changing the interface.
    
    3. **Add the normal play input route.** Map movement, jump, blast, radius and reset. Add the blast preview and invalid-position feedback. Resolve Space/D conflicts and ensure the player can no longer accidentally invoke the old debug shortcuts.
    
    4. **Replace the large debug text with the compact HUD and panel.** Route input through the panel first, stage settings edits, and implement pause/resume and Apply & Reset. Put the original inspection affordances behind F3. Keep the main application loop straightforward.
    
    5. **Play through the complete loop and tune it.** Adjust movement, jump timing, starting material values, radius and framing by playing. Prioritize clear feedback, reliable controls and rapid repeat attempts.
    
    A modest code split is enough: one player module, a small yard/reset helper and changes to the existing application/view loop. The destruction passes remain the shared simulation path. This milestone is local; player replication and changes to the snapshot protocol are outside its implementation scope.
    
    **Completion checks**
    
    - On launch, the player and target are visible and the essential controls are discoverable without reading the README.
    - Movement, jumping, landing on debris and pushing fragments work. Holding jump does not produce repeated airborne jumps.
    - The starting structure remains stable under ordinary gravity and routine contact.
    - Previewed blast radius matches the applied radius. UI clicks and invalid origins cause no world blast.
    - R works after an explosion, while fragments are moving, and after player respawn. It restores one player and a clean yard with the same applied settings and seed.
    - The settings panel pauses physics, fading and player actions. Closing it produces no jump, blast or simulation catch-up from menu input.
    - Apply & Reset applies breakup pattern, strengths, flexibility and generation eligibility together. Selecting a breakup pattern does not unexpectedly change strength or flexibility.
    - Normal play has a small HUD; inspection details appear when F3 is requested. D and Space keep their normal play meanings.
    - Existing behavior tests still pass. Add focused automated checks where practical for reset, input consumption and the no-progress generation fix; verify feel and visual clarity by playing the application.
    
    The first checkpoint is the player moving and jumping around the fixed yard with a reliable R reset. Once that works, finish the preview, compact panel and input routing in the same milestone.

    package main
    
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:math"
    
    View :: struct { offset: Vec2, scale: f32 }
    screen_point :: proc(view: View,point: Vec2) -> rl.Vector2 { return {view.offset.x+point.x*view.scale,view.offset.y-point.y*view.scale} }
    world_point :: proc(view: View,point: rl.Vector2) -> Vec2 { return {(point.x-view.offset.x)/view.scale,(view.offset.y-point.y)/view.scale} }
    piece_color :: proc(id: u64,alpha: u8 = 255) -> rl.Color {
        colors := [6]rl.Color{{64,173,165,255},{97,142,206,255},{194,134,204,255},{212,161,88,255},{139,178,113,255},{211,116,125,255}}
        c:=colors[id%6]; c.a=alpha; return c
    }
    render_subdivision :: proc(s: ^Scene,sub: Subdivision,poses: map[u64]Pose) -> Subdivision {
        result:=sub
        if pose,ok:=poses[sub.id]; ok { result.pose=pose }
        return result
    }
    point_on_boundary :: proc(point: Vec2,a,b: Polygon) -> bool {
        for i in 0..<len(a.points) {
            for j in 0..<len(b.points) {
                if segment,ok:=segment_overlap(Segment{a.points[i],a.points[(i+1)%len(a.points)]},Segment{b.points[j],b.points[(j+1)%len(b.points)]}); ok {
                    d:=vsub(segment.b,segment.a); length:=vlen(d)
                    projection:=vdot(vsub(point,segment.a),d)/(length*length)
                    if projection >= -0.0001 && projection <= 1.0001 && math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(point,segment.a))) < 0.0001*length { return true }
                }
            }
        }
        return false
    }
    // Only presentation vertices are blended. Stored outlines and fixtures stay exact.
    cosmetic_point :: proc(s: ^Scene,sub: Subdivision,rest: Vec2,poses: map[u64]Pose) -> Vec2 {
        self:=render_subdivision(s,sub,poses)
        point:=posed_point(self,rest)
        flex:=clamp(s.materials[sub.material].flexibility,f32(0),f32(1))
        if flex==0 { return point }
        weighted:=point
        count:=f32(1)
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            other_id:=u64(0)
            if c.a==sub.id { other_id=c.b } else if c.b==sub.id { other_id=c.a }
            if other_id==0 { continue }
            other:=render_subdivision(s,s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[other_id]],poses)
            if point_on_boundary(rest,sub.outline,other.outline) { weighted=vadd(weighted,posed_point(other,rest)); count+=1 }
        }
        return vadd(point,vmul(vsub(vmul(weighted,1/count),point),flex))
    }
    draw_polygon :: proc(view: View,outline: Polygon,color: rl.Color,stroke: rl.Color) {
        triangles:=triangulate_polygon(outline)
        for triangle in triangles {
            a,b,c:=screen_point(view,triangle.points[0]),screen_point(view,triangle.points[1]),screen_point(view,triangle.points[2])
            // Raylib's triangle winding uses the screen's downward Y axis.
            cross:=vcross(vsub(triangle.points[1],triangle.points[0]),vsub(triangle.points[2],triangle.points[0]))
            if cross > 0 { rl.DrawTriangle(a,b,c,color) } else { rl.DrawTriangle(c,b,a,color) }
            delete(triangle.points)
        }
        delete(triangles)
        for i in 0..<len(outline.points) { rl.DrawLineEx(screen_point(view,outline.points[i]),screen_point(view,outline.points[(i+1)%len(outline.points)]),2,stroke) }
    }
    pick_subdivision :: proc(s: ^Scene,point: Vec2) -> u64 {
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            points: [dynamic]rl.Vector2
            for rest in sub.outline.points { p:=posed_point(sub,rest); append(&points,rl.Vector2{p.x,p.y}) }
            hit:=rl.CheckCollisionPointPoly({point.x,point.y},raw_data(points),i32(len(points)))
            delete(points)
            if hit { return sub.id }
        }
        return 0
    }
    pick_connection :: proc(s: ^Scene,point: Vec2,max_distance: f32) -> u64 {
        best:=u64(0); distance:=max_distance
        for c in s.connections { if c.live { d:=vlen(vsub(point,connection_sample(s,c))); if d<distance { distance=d; best=c.id } } }
        return best
    }
    material_preset :: proc(index: int) -> Material {
        switch index {
        case 1: return Material{name="splinter",subdivision_strength=7,connection_strength=6,flexibility=0.6,generation_count=5,aspect_ratio=0.2}
        case 2: return Material{name="shatter",subdivision_strength=5,connection_strength=4,flexibility=0.05,generation_count=6,aspect_ratio=1,triangulate=true}
        }
        return Material{name="chunk",subdivision_strength=6,connection_strength=4,flexibility=0.25,generation_count=3,aspect_ratio=1}
    }
    reset_demo :: proc(s: ^Scene,preset: int,terminal: bool) {
        scene_destroy(s)
        seed:=u8(42); if terminal { seed=0 }
        s^=make_wall(seed,0.08)
        s.materials[0]=material_preset(preset)
        physics_init(s)
    }
    add_projectile :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        material:=add_material(s,Material{name="projectile",subdivision_strength=math.inf_f32(1),connection_strength=math.inf_f32(1),generation_count=2,aspect_ratio=1})
        owner:=add_piece(s,material,0)
        points:=[4]Vec2{{-1.2,0.3},{-0.8,0.3},{-0.8,0.7},{-1.2,0.7}}
        outline:=make_polygon(points[:]); defer delete(outline.points)
        id:=add_subdivision(s,owner,outline,Pose{position=centroid(outline),velocity={8,0}})
        append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].subdivisions,id)
        physics_sync_structure(s)

    draw_scene :: proc(s: ^Scene,view: View,poses: map[u64]Pose,selected: u64,surface,joints: bool) {
        for i in -20..=20 {
            tint:=rl.Color{31,44,62,255}
            if i==0 { tint={45,65,85,255} }
            rl.DrawLineEx(screen_point(view,Vec2{f32(i),-20}),screen_point(view,Vec2{f32(i),20}),1,tint)
            rl.DrawLineEx(screen_point(view,Vec2{-20,f32(i)}),screen_point(view,Vec2{20,f32(i)}),1,tint)
        }
        for remnant in s.remnants {
            sub:=s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[remnant.subdivision]]; sub.pose=remnant.pose
            outline:=posed_polygon(sub)
            draw_polygon(view,outline,rl.Color{140,152,170,u8(160*(1-remnant.age))},rl.Color{140,152,170,u8(160*(1-remnant.age))})
            delete(outline.points)
        }
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            outline:=Polygon{points=make([]Vec2,len(sub.outline.points))}
            posed:=render_subdivision(s,sub,poses)
            for rest,i in sub.outline.points {
                point:=posed_point(posed,rest)
                if surface { point=cosmetic_point(s,sub,rest,poses) }
                outline.points[i]=point
            }
            stroke:=rl.Color{202,220,231,255}
            if sub.id==selected { stroke={255,255,255,255} }
            draw_polygon(view,outline,piece_color(sub.owner,210),stroke)
            delete(outline.points)
            center:=screen_point(view,posed.pose.position)
            rl.DrawText(rl.TextFormat("%d",sub.id),i32(center.x)-5,i32(center.y)-23,16,rl.Color{16,29,40,255})
        }
        if joints {
            for c in s.connections {
                if !c.live { continue }
                a,b:=render_subdivision(s,s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]],poses),render_subdivision(s,s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]],poses)
                anchor:=vmul(vadd(posed_point(a,c.rest_point),posed_point(b,c.rest_point)),0.5)
                color:=rl.Color{248,205,109,255}
                rl.DrawLineEx(screen_point(view,a.pose.position),screen_point(view,b.pose.position),2,color)
                rl.DrawCircleV(screen_point(view,anchor),5,color)
                p:=screen_point(view,anchor)
                rl.DrawText(rl.TextFormat("c%d",c.id),i32(p.x)+7,i32(p.y)+7,14,color)
            }
        }
    }

    counts_runtime :: proc(s: ^Scene) -> (int,int,int) {
        a,b,c:=0,0,0
        for sub in s.subdivisions { if sub.live { a+=1 } }
        for conn in s.connections { if conn.live { b+=1 } }
        for piece in s.pieces { if piece.live { c+=1 } }
        return a,b,c
    }

    import "core:fmt"

    main :: proc() {
        for arg in os.args[1:] {
            if arg=="--smoke" { run_debug_view(true); return }
            if arg=="--headless" { run_headless(); return }
            if arg=="--serve" { run_debug_view(false,true); return }
            if arg=="--receive" { run_receiver(); return }
            if arg=="--help" { fmt.println("odin run . -- [--headless | --smoke | --serve | --receive | --help]"); return }
        }
        run_debug_view(false)
    }
    
    run_headless :: proc() {
        s:=make_wall(42,0.08)
        defer scene_destroy(&s)
        physics_init(&s)
        fmt.println("Initial:",counts_runtime(&s))
        blast_pass(&s,Blast{position={1.5,0.5},radius=0.8})
        fmt.println("After blast:",counts_runtime(&s))
        for _ in 0..<60 { physics_tick(&s,1.0/60.0) }
        valid,message:=validate_scene(&s)
        assert(valid,message)
        assert(save_snapshot(&s,"snapshot.json"))
        fmt.println("After 60 ticks:",counts_runtime(&s),"| snapshot.json saved")
        receiver,ok:=load_snapshot("snapshot.json")
        assert(ok,"Snapshot receiver failed")
        defer scene_destroy(&receiver)
        fmt.println("Receiver:",counts_runtime(&receiver))
    }

    Vec2 :: struct { x, y: f32 }

    Scene :: struct {
        physics: Physics,
        materials: [dynamic]Material,
        owned_names: [dynamic]string,
        subdivisions: [dynamic]Subdivision,
        vertices: [dynamic]Vec2,
        connections: [dynamic]Connection,
        pieces: [dynamic]Piece,
        remnants: [dynamic]Remnant,

        next_id: u64,

    vadd :: proc(a, b: Vec2) -> Vec2 { return {a.x+b.x, a.y+b.y} }
    vsub :: proc(a, b: Vec2) -> Vec2 { return {a.x-b.x, a.y-b.y} }
    vmul :: proc(a: Vec2, s: f32) -> Vec2 { return {a.x*s, a.y*s} }
    vdot :: proc(a, b: Vec2) -> f32 { return a.x*b.x+a.y*b.y }
    vcross :: proc(a, b: Vec2) -> f32 { return a.x*b.y-a.y*b.x }
    vlen :: proc(a: Vec2) -> f32 { return math.sqrt(vdot(a,a)) }
    vrotate :: proc(a: Vec2, angle: f32) -> Vec2 {
        c, s := f32(math.cos(angle)), f32(math.sin(angle))
        return {a.x*c-a.y*s,a.x*s+a.y*c}
    }
    centroid :: proc(p: Polygon) -> Vec2 {
        area, x, y: f32
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) {
            a, b := p.points[i], p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]
            cross := vcross(a,b)
            area += cross
            x += (a.x+b.x)*cross
            y += (a.y+b.y)*cross
        }
        if math.abs(area) < 0.00001 {
            for point in p.points { x += point.x; y += point.y }
            return {x/f32(len(p.points)),y/f32(len(p.points))}
        }
        return {x/(3*area),y/(3*area)}
    }
    posed_point :: proc(sub: Subdivision, rest: Vec2) -> Vec2 {
        return vadd(sub.pose.position,vrotate(vsub(rest,sub.rest_center),sub.pose.angle))
    }
    posed_polygon :: proc(sub: Subdivision) -> Polygon {
        result := Polygon{points=make([]Vec2,len(sub.outline.points))}
        for point,i in sub.outline.points { result.points[i]=posed_point(sub,point) }
        return result
    }
    make_polygon :: proc(points: []Vec2) -> Polygon {
        result:=Polygon{points=make([]Vec2,len(points))}
        copy(result.points,points)
        return result
    }
    // Returns the common collinear edge length and its length-weighted midpoint.
    shared_boundary :: proc(a, b: Polygon) -> (f32, Vec2) {
        total: f32
        weighted := Vec2{}
        for i in 0..<len(a.points) {
            p, q := a.points[i], a.points[(i+1)%len(a.points)]
            d := vsub(q,p)
            length := vlen(d)
            if length < 0.00001 { continue }
            unit := vmul(d,1/length)
            for j in 0..<len(b.points) {
                r, s := b.points[j], b.points[(j+1)%len(b.points)]
                if math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(r,p))) > 0.0001*length || math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(s,p))) > 0.0001*length { continue }
                t0, t1 := vdot(vsub(r,p),unit), vdot(vsub(s,p),unit)
                lo := max(f32(0),min(t0,t1))
                hi := min(length,max(t0,t1))
                if hi-lo > 0.0001 {
                    span := hi-lo
                    total += span
                    weighted = vadd(weighted,vmul(vadd(p,vmul(unit,(lo+hi)*0.5)),span))
                }
            }
        }
        if total == 0 { return 0, {} }
        return total,vmul(weighted,1/total)
    }
    new_id :: proc(s: ^Scene) -> u64 { s.next_id += 1; return s.next_id }
    new_scene :: proc(minimum_width: f32) -> Scene {
        return Scene{sub_rows=make(map[u64]int),conn_rows=make(map[u64]int),piece_rows=make(map[u64]int),minimum_width=minimum_width}
    }
    add_material :: proc(s: ^Scene, m: Material) -> int { append(&s.materials,m); return len(s.materials)-1 }
    add_piece :: proc(s: ^Scene, material: int, seed: u8) -> u64 {
        id := new_id(s)
        s.piece_rows[id] = len(s.pieces)
        append(&s.pieces,Piece{id=id,material=material,seed=seed,live=true})
        return id
    }
    add_subdivision :: proc(s: ^Scene, owner: u64, outline: Polygon, pose: Pose) -> u64 {
        id := new_id(s)
        retain_subdivision(s,Subdivision{id=id,owner=owner,material=s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].material,outline=outline,pose=pose,live=true})

    }
    // Outlines use ranges in one append-only undeformed vertex pool. The outline
    // slice is a derived read view, refreshed whenever appending can move the pool.
    // Callers may release their source polygon immediately after this call.
    retain_subdivision :: proc(s: ^Scene,source: Subdivision) {
        sub:=source
        points:=make_polygon(source.outline.points)
        defer delete(points.points)
        sub.rest_center=centroid(points)
        sub.outline_start=len(s.vertices); sub.outline_count=len(points.points)
        for point in points.points { append(&s.vertices,point) }
        for i in 0..<len(s.subdivisions) {
            existing:=&s.subdivisions[i]
            existing.outline.points=s.vertices[existing.outline_start:existing.outline_start+existing.outline_count]
        }
        sub.outline.points=s.vertices[sub.outline_start:sub.outline_start+sub.outline_count]
        s.sub_rows[sub.id]=len(s.subdivisions)
        append(&s.subdivisions,sub)
    }
    add_connection :: proc(s: ^Scene, a, b: u64) -> u64 {
        if a == b { return 0 }
        for c in s.connections { if c.live && ((c.a == a && c.b == b) || (c.a == b && c.b == a)) { return c.id } }
        sa, sb := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[a]],s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[b]]
        length, point := shared_boundary(sa.outline,sb.outline)
        if length <= 0 { return 0 }
        id := new_id(s)
        s.conn_rows[id] = len(s.connections)
        append(&s.connections,Connection{id=id,a=a,b=b,rest_point=point,local_a=vsub(point,sa.rest_center),local_b=vsub(point,sb.rest_center),live=true})
        return id
    }
    connection_sample :: proc(s: ^Scene, c: Connection) -> Vec2 {
        a,b := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]],s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
        return vmul(vadd(vadd(a.pose.position,vrotate(c.local_a,a.pose.angle)),vadd(b.pose.position,vrotate(c.local_b,b.pose.angle))),0.5)
    }
    subdivision_sample :: proc(sub: Subdivision) -> Vec2 { return sub.pose.position }
    contains_id :: proc(ids: []u64,id: u64) -> bool { for x in ids { if x == id { return true } }; return false }
    sort_ids :: proc(ids: []u64) {
        for i in 1..<len(ids) {
            j := i
            for j > 0 && ids[j] < ids[j-1] { ids[j],ids[j-1] = ids[j-1],ids[j]; j -= 1 }
        }
    }
    sorted_ids :: proc(ids: []u64) -> [dynamic]u64 {
        result: [dynamic]u64
        for id in ids { if !contains_id(result[:],id) { append(&result,id) } }
        sort_ids(result[:])
        return result
    }
    derive_seed :: proc(seed: u8, identity: u64) -> u8 {
        if seed == 0 { return 0 }
        x := identity ~ (u64(seed)*0x9e3779b97f4a7c15)
        x ~= x >> 30; x *= 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
        x ~= x >> 27; x *= 0x94d049bb133111eb

    piece_width :: proc(s: ^Scene, ids: []u64) -> f32 {
        if len(ids) == 0 { return 0 }
        points: [dynamic]Vec2

        for id in ids { for point in s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[id]].outline.points { append(&points,point) } }
