    package main
    
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:math"
    
    Physics :: struct {
        world: b2.WorldId,
        bodies: map[u64]b2.BodyId,
        joints: map[u64]b2.JointId,
        fixture_counts: map[u64]int,
        active: bool,
    }
    Interaction :: struct { force: Vec2, torque: f32 }
    REFERENCE_LENGTH :: f32(1)
    PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS :: 4
    GLOBAL_DAMPING :: f32(0.7)
    
    to_b2 :: proc(v: Vec2) -> b2.Vec2 { return {v.x,v.y} }
    from_b2 :: proc(v: b2.Vec2) -> Vec2 { return {v.x,v.y} }
    interaction_load :: proc(i: Interaction) -> f32 {
        return max(vlen(i.force),math.abs(i.torque)/REFERENCE_LENGTH)
    }
    equivalent_force :: proc(impulse: Vec2, interval: f32) -> Vec2 {
        assert(interval > 0)
        return vmul(impulse,1/interval)
    }
    physics_init :: proc(s: ^Scene, gravity: Vec2 = {}) {
        assert(!s.physics.active)
        def := b2.DefaultWorldDef()
        def.gravity = to_b2(gravity)
        s.physics = Physics{world=b2.CreateWorld(def),bodies=make(map[u64]b2.BodyId),joints=make(map[u64]b2.JointId),fixture_counts=make(map[u64]int),active=true}
        physics_sync_structure(s)
    }
    physics_destroy :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        if !s.physics.active { return }
        b2.DestroyWorld(s.physics.world)
        delete(s.physics.bodies); delete(s.physics.joints); delete(s.physics.fixture_counts)
        s.physics = {}
    }
    physics_read_motion :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        if !s.physics.active { return }
        for id,body in s.physics.bodies {
            row := s.sub_rows[id]
            rotation := b2.Body_GetRotation(body)
            s.subdivisions[row].pose = Pose{
                position=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(body)),angle=math.atan2(rotation.s,rotation.c),
                velocity=from_b2(b2.Body_GetLinearVelocity(body)),angular_velocity=b2.Body_GetAngularVelocity(body),
            }
        }
    }
    physics_create_fixture :: proc(s: ^Scene, body: b2.BodyId, sub: Subdivision, outline: Polygon) -> bool {
        points: [dynamic]b2.Vec2
        defer delete(points)
        for point in outline.points { append(&points,to_b2(vsub(point,sub.rest_center))) }
        hull := b2.ComputeHull(points[:])
        // Hull welding can collapse a thin ear below Box2D's collision tolerance.
        if hull.count < 3 { return false }
        polygon := b2.MakePolygon(hull,0)
        def := b2.DefaultShapeDef()
        def.density = 1
        _ = b2.CreatePolygonShape(body,def,polygon)
        s.physics.fixture_counts[sub.id] += 1
        return true
    }
    physics_finish_mass :: proc(s: ^Scene,body: b2.BodyId,sub: Subdivision) {
        if s.physics.fixture_counts[sub.id]==0 {
            // A microscopic attached subdivision is still one live logical entity.
            // Use a bounding fixture when the engine cannot resolve any of its ears.
            lo,hi:=Vec2{1e30,1e30},Vec2{-1e30,-1e30}
            for rest in sub.outline.points { p:=vsub(rest,sub.rest_center); lo={min(lo.x,p.x),min(lo.y,p.y)}; hi={max(hi.x,p.x),max(hi.y,p.y)} }
            polygon:=b2.MakeOffsetBox(max(f32(0.0025),(hi.x-lo.x)*0.5),max(f32(0.0025),(hi.y-lo.y)*0.5),to_b2(vmul(vadd(lo,hi),0.5)),b2.MakeRot(0))
            def:=b2.DefaultShapeDef(); def.density=1
            _ = b2.CreatePolygonShape(body,def,polygon)
            s.physics.fixture_counts[sub.id]=1
        }
        // Keep mass and the body origin tied to the exact logical polygon, including
        // when Box2D simplifies a fixture. This also makes rotational inheritance exact.
        inertia: f32
        for i in 0..<len(sub.outline.points) {
            a,b:=vsub(sub.outline.points[i],sub.rest_center),vsub(sub.outline.points[(i+1)%len(sub.outline.points)],sub.rest_center)
            inertia+=vcross(a,b)*(vdot(a,a)+vdot(a,b)+vdot(b,b))/12
        }
        b2.Body_SetMassData(body,b2.MassData{mass=polygon_area(sub.outline),center={},rotationalInertia=math.abs(inertia)})
        b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(body,to_b2(sub.pose.velocity))
        b2.Body_SetAngularVelocity(body,sub.pose.angular_velocity)
    }
    // This runs only between World_Step calls. Existing handles survive ownership changes.
    physics_sync_structure :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        if !s.physics.active { return }
        dead_joints: [dynamic]u64
        dead_bodies: [dynamic]u64
        defer delete(dead_joints); defer delete(dead_bodies)
        for id,joint in s.physics.joints {
            row,ok := s.conn_rows[id]
            if !ok || !s.connections[row].live { b2.DestroyJoint(joint); append(&dead_joints,id) }
        }
        for id in dead_joints { delete_key(&s.physics.joints,id) }
        for id,body in s.physics.bodies {
            row,ok := s.sub_rows[id]
            if !ok || !s.subdivisions[row].live { b2.DestroyBody(body); append(&dead_bodies,id) }
        }
        for id in dead_bodies { delete_key(&s.physics.bodies,id); delete_key(&s.physics.fixture_counts,id) }
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            if _,exists := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]; exists { continue }
            def := b2.DefaultBodyDef()
            def.type = .dynamicBody
            def.position = to_b2(sub.pose.position)
            def.rotation = b2.MakeRot(sub.pose.angle)
            def.linearVelocity = to_b2(sub.pose.velocity)
            def.angularVelocity = sub.pose.angular_velocity
            body := b2.CreateBody(s.physics.world,def)
            s.physics.bodies[sub.id] = body
            if is_convex(sub.outline) && len(sub.outline.points) <= 8 {
                physics_create_fixture(s,body,sub,sub.outline)
            } else {
                triangles := convex_decomposition(sub.outline)
                for triangle in triangles { physics_create_fixture(s,body,sub,triangle); delete(triangle.points) }
                delete(triangles)
            }
            physics_finish_mass(s,body,sub)
        }
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            if _,exists := s.physics.joints[c.id]; exists { continue }
            a := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]]
            b := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
            def := b2.DefaultWeldJointDef()
            def.bodyIdA = s.physics.bodies[c.a]
            def.bodyIdB = s.physics.bodies[c.b]
            def.localAnchorA = to_b2(c.local_a)
            def.localAnchorB = to_b2(c.local_b)
            // All outlines share one undeformed frame. Its relative rest angle is zero.
            def.referenceAngle = 0
            flexibility := max(s.materials[a.material].flexibility,s.materials[b.material].flexibility)
            if flexibility > 0 {
                def.linearHertz = 1/max(flexibility,0.01)
                def.angularHertz = def.linearHertz
            }
            def.linearDampingRatio = GLOBAL_DAMPING
            def.angularDampingRatio = GLOBAL_DAMPING
            s.physics.joints[c.id] = b2.CreateWeldJoint(s.physics.world,def)
        }
    }
    apply_blast_motion :: proc(s: ^Scene, sub: ^Subdivision, direction: Vec2, load: f32) {
        delta_v := vmul(direction,load*BLAST_IMPULSE_SCALE)
        if s.physics.active {
            body := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]
            impulse := vmul(delta_v,b2.Body_GetMass(body))
            b2.Body_ApplyLinearImpulseToCenter(body,to_b2(impulse),true)
            sub.pose.velocity = from_b2(b2.Body_GetLinearVelocity(body))
        } else {
            sub.pose.velocity = vadd(sub.pose.velocity,delta_v)
        }
    }
    // Contact points and fixtures against the same other body form one interaction.
    // Joint reactions are already forces; totalNormalImpulse covers the full tick.
    // Box2D's tangent/rolling impulses cover the final substep in this binding version.
    calculate_physics_loads :: proc(s: ^Scene, dt: f32) -> Failures {
        assert(dt > 0)
        failures := Failures{}
        loads := make(map[u64]f32)
        defer delete(loads)
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            body := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]
            capacity := int(b2.Body_GetContactCapacity(body))
            buffer := make([]b2.ContactData,capacity)
            contacts := b2.Body_GetContactData(body,buffer)
            interactions := make(map[b2.BodyId]Interaction)
            for contact in contacts {
                body_a,body_b := b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdA),b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdB)
                other := body_b
                sign := f32(-1)
                if body_b == body { other=body_a; sign=1 }
                normal := from_b2(contact.manifold.normal)
                tangent := Vec2{normal.y,-normal.x}
                interaction := interactions[other]
                for k in 0..<int(contact.manifold.pointCount) {
                    point := contact.manifold.points[k]
                    force := vadd(equivalent_force(vmul(normal,point.totalNormalImpulse*sign),dt),equivalent_force(vmul(tangent,point.tangentImpulse*sign),dt/f32(PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS)))
                    interaction.force = vadd(interaction.force,force)
                    interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(from_b2(point.point),sub.pose.position),force)
                }
                interaction.torque += contact.manifold.rollingImpulse*sign/(dt/f32(PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS))
                interactions[other] = interaction
            }
            for _,interaction in interactions { loads[sub.id] = max(loads[sub.id],interaction_load(interaction)) }
            delete(interactions); delete(buffer)
        }
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            joint := s.physics.joints[c.id]
            interaction := Interaction{force=from_b2(b2.Joint_GetConstraintForce(joint)),torque=b2.Joint_GetConstraintTorque(joint)}
            load := interaction_load(interaction)
            a,b := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]],s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
            a_interaction,b_interaction := interaction,interaction
            a_interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(posed_point(a,c.rest_point),a.pose.position),interaction.force)
            b_interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(posed_point(b,c.rest_point),b.pose.position),interaction.force)
            loads[c.a] = max(loads[c.a],interaction_load(a_interaction))
            loads[c.b] = max(loads[c.b],interaction_load(b_interaction))
            material := s.materials[s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]].material]
            if fails(load,material.connection_strength) { append(&failures.connections,c.id) }
        }
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if sub.live && fails(loads[sub.id],s.materials[sub.material].subdivision_strength) { append(&failures.subdivisions,sub.id) }
        }
        return failures
    }
    Load_Calculator :: #type proc(s: ^Scene,dt: f32) -> Failures
    physics_tick :: proc(s: ^Scene, dt: f32,calculate_loads: Load_Calculator = calculate_physics_loads) {
        assert(s.physics.active && dt > 0)
        physics_sync_structure(s)
        b2.World_Step(s.physics.world,dt,PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS)
        physics_read_motion(s)
        failures := calculate_loads(s,dt)
        apply_failures(s,failures)
        delete(failures.subdivisions); delete(failures.connections)
        delete(failures.discard_subdivisions)
        physics_sync_structure(s)
        fade_step(s,dt)
    }

    # Odin destruction sandbox
    
    A standalone implementation of `destruction-model-implementation-plan.md` and `playable-sandbox-ux-plan.md`, using Odin's bundled Box2D, raylib and raygui libraries. The default application is a small playable destruction yard. The original diagnostic lab and localhost snapshot transport remain available.
    
    ## Run
    
    Requires an Odin installation with compiled `vendor:box2d` and `vendor:raylib` libraries. Tested on Windows with Odin `dev-2026-05-nightly:ea5175d`.
    
    ```powershell
    odin run .
    odin test .
    odin build . -o:speed -out:BOM.exe
    ```
    
    The application opens into a fixed side-view yard with a floor, an invulnerable capsule player and a destructible stepped tower. Walk, jump onto or push debris, aim outside a solid shape and click to blast. Ordinary gravity runs at a fixed 60 Hz with four Box2D substeps. The camera keeps the yard framed when the window resizes. Falling outside the yard returns the player to spawn.
    
    | Control | Action |
    | --- | --- |
    | A / D or left / right arrows | Move |
    | Space | Jump, with a 0.1 second jump buffer and coyote window |
    | Left click in the world | One blast at a valid cursor position |
    | Mouse wheel over the world | Adjust blast radius and power |
    | R / Reset button | Restore the same applied setup and seed |
    | Tab / Escape / Settings button | Open settings and pause; close to resume |
    | F3 | Toggle IDs, connections, counts and inspection tools |
    
    The aiming circle shows the active blast radius. A red cross and message mark origins inside or on live logical outlines; those blasts are suppressed. UI clicks do not blast the world. The settings panel pauses physics, fading and player actions without accumulating simulation time.
    
    Radius changes are immediate, including inside settings. Breakup pattern, fragment strength, connection strength, flexibility and Generate children are staged until **Apply & Reset**. Resume keeps the previously applied setup. Strength and flexibility stay independent of Chunk / Splinter / Shatter. The initial setup uses seed 42, strengths 30 / 24, flexibility 0.15 and radius 4.2. Turning Generate children off uses seed zero; geometry stays live until it fails.
    
    With F3 enabled: right click selects, Delete or Ctrl+click directly removes a region, Shift+click or X near an anchor breaks a connection, J toggles links, V toggles the cosmetic surface, and S saves `snapshot.json`. D and Space retain movement and jump in inspection mode.
    
    Run `odin run . -- --lab` for the original zero-gravity diagnostic fixture and its legacy shortcuts (projectile I, presets 1/2/3, terminal T, pause/step Space/N, radius Q/E, pan/zoom, and snapshot save/load S/L). The existing sender and receiver use that diagnostic fixture; player and floor replication are outside this local milestone.
    
    For automated execution:
    
    ```powershell
    odin run . -- --headless
    odin run . -- --smoke
    odin run . -- --smoke-settings
    odin run . -- --smoke-input
    ```
    
    `--headless` evaluates the original diagnostic blast, runs 60 physics ticks, validates the graph, writes `snapshot.json`, and reconstructs a receiver. `--smoke` renders the yard in a hidden window to `sandbox-preview.png`. `--smoke-settings` renders the expanded paused panel to `sandbox-settings-preview.png`. Both exit after two frames.
    
    `--smoke-input` uses raylib's native automation events in a hidden window to exercise the actual keyboard bindings and raygui widgets: movement, holding jump through landing, paused settings, closing a slider drag with Escape, immediate radius updates, staged pattern/generation changes, Apply & Reset, the first subsequent blast click, inspection and R reset. It asserts the results and exports `sandbox-playthrough.png`. The normal behavior suite stays independent of a window or display.
    
    ## Live transmission
    
    Build once, then run these in separate terminals:
    
    ```powershell
    .\BOM.exe --serve
    .\BOM.exe --receive
    ```
    
    The sender listens on **127.0.0.1:9901** for one receiver. It sends explicit complete snapshots after structural changes and at 10 Hz for motion. The receiver renders polygons, connections, ownership and interpolated motion without simulating physics. Destroy or split the wall in the sender to see the receiver update.
    
    Frames contain a four byte little endian payload length followed by UTF-8 JSON, capped at 4 MiB. Partial reads, partial writes, coalesced frames and disconnects are handled. One in-flight send is retained; the sender does not accumulate a queue of old states. `read_state`, `encode_snapshot` and `decode_snapshot` can also be used with another transport.
    
    Snapshots carry current geometry, materials, stable IDs, piece memberships, future generation seeds, structural revision, and body motion. Version 2 retains each subdivision's birth seed context; version 1 snapshots still load using their original piece contexts. Widths and anchors are derived from the transmitted outlines. Infinite strengths have explicit flags so snapshots remain valid JSON. Seeds never reconstruct existing damaged geometry.
    
    ## Implementation
    
    | File | Responsibility |
    | --- | --- |
    | `model.odin` | Stable identity, shared reference vertex pool, birth contexts, cached outline widths, memberships and group filtering |
    | `geometry.odin` | Shared boundaries, displaced cuts, convex hull and collision decomposition |
    | `destruction.odin` | Seeded generation, blast evaluation and the shared structural update |
    | `physics.odin` | Box2D bodies, fixtures, weld joints, interaction aggregation and load policy |
    | `state.odin` | State reader, snapshot validation, serialization and pose interpolation |
    | `transmission.odin` | Framed localhost TCP snapshots and the receiver application |
    | `debug_view.odin` | Native controls, rendering and material presets |
    | `player.odin` | Capsule controller, contact support, buffered jumps and respawn |
    | `yard.odin` | Yard creation/reset, applied and staged settings, aim validation and input routing |
    | `sandbox_view.odin` | Fixed camera, compact HUD, raygui panel and inspection input |
    | `sandbox_smoke.odin` | Hidden-window native input and widget playthrough |
    | `behavior_test.odin` | Focused behavior and integration checks |
    | `recursive_blast_test.odin` | Same-blast termination, child contexts, conservative deletion and recursive agreement |
    | `sandbox_test.odin` | Gravity stability, movement, debris contact, resets, settings and input consumption |
    
    IDs are monotonic and mapped to storage rows. Removed rows and outline ranges remain retained until `scene_destroy`; no world repacking is performed. Subdivision outlines use ranges into one append-only vertex pool in a common undeformed reference frame. Their `outline` slices are derived views refreshed when the pool grows. Borrowed polygon views must not be held across scene mutations. `add_subdivision` copies its input; the caller retains ownership of that input allocation. `make_polygon` creates an owned polygon.
    
    Current subdivisions and connections exist when a piece is created. Future geometry is generated only when a subdivision fails. `apply_failures` stages one generation for physics reactions and manual failures. `blast_pass` reuses that staging operation in a simple loop: evaluate the current geometry, replace failures, and evaluate new children and connections against the same blast until nothing else fails. Only then regroup affected pieces, filter connected groups and synchronize physics. A failed connection cannot be healed by proximity; only surviving old attachments are inherited. Failure IDs and groups use stable ordering, including when storage rows are shuffled. `discard_subdivisions` provides direct removal independently of a generative seed.
    
    Each child receives its future seed context at birth, derived from its parent's context and child ordinal. Allocation IDs and later ownership changes do not affect that context. When every sibling's cached outline width is at or below the subdivision cutoff, the whole batch receives seed zero. Mixed batches retain nonzero contexts, with an individual width guard before further generation. Seed-zero geometry remains live until it fails. Connected-group width filtering remains a separate final step.
    
    Before generating a failed outline, the blast can remove it directly when its farthest posed vertex proves every descendant will fail. This assumes partition-preserving generation, shared material strength, an unoccluded radial load and unchanged transforms during the event. The bound rounds distance outward with `nextafter`, uses a strict `1e-4` load margin and declines nonfinite inputs. Skipping a branch leaves other branches' seeds unchanged. `blast_pass(..., false)` disables the shortcut for correctness comparisons; normal play enables it.
    
    Generation clips convex regions and ear-clips supported simple concave polygons. Each internal displaced cut is generated once and installed in both adjacent outlines. Displacement is limited by clearance to other edges as well as area and length. Outside boundaries remain intact. Count is a target before final triangulation; concave outlines and the shatter preset can produce more children. If generation cannot produce a genuine partition of at least two smaller regions, the failed subdivision is removed directly. A valid partition is retained even when area limits prevent reaching the requested count. Aspect ratio biases cut direction. Self-intersecting outlines and polygons with holes are outside this implementation's input domain.
    
    The load policy uses the strongest individual interaction, preserving opposing interactions against different bodies. Contact points and convex fixtures against the same other body are combined. Joint reactions also load their endpoint subdivisions. Thresholds use `load > 0 && load >= strength`; strength records are never reduced by prior events. `physics_tick` accepts a replacement `Load_Calculator` function.
    
    Blast radius controls both reach and power: direct load is `10 * max(0, radius - distance)`, with zero load for nonpositive radii. The fixed global `BLAST_LOAD_MULTIPLIER` is 10; increasing radius increases load at a fixed distance, without a fixed maximum. For example, a sample 0.5 units away receives load 5 at radius 1 and load 25 at radius 3, enough to fail strength 20. Impulses are `direction * load * mass * 0.1`, applied once at each final survivor's own sample. Generated motion includes the parent's linear and angular motion; removed ancestors receive no blast impulse. New contact and joint reactions wait for the next solver step. Both tuning constants and the falloff live in `destruction.odin`. The torque reference length is one world unit, and global joint damping is 0.7. Flexibility zero selects a stiff weld; positive flexibility selects spring softness.
    
    Contact `totalNormalImpulse` is converted using the full tick interval. The installed binding's tangent and rolling impulses use the final substep interval. Joint reactions already supply force and torque. See the [Box2D simulation documentation](https://box2d.org/documentation/md_simulation.html) and [contact solver source](https://github.com/erincatto/box2d/blob/v3.1.1/src/contact_solver.c) for the underlying quantities.
    
    Collision decomposition merges adjacent convex regions. Box2D can collapse microscopic ears during hull welding; those ears are omitted from fixtures, and a subdivision with no resolvable fixture receives a small bounding box proxy. The destruction outline, logical identity, polygon mass and inertia remain retained. Collision fixtures never become additional destruction entities.
    
    Group width is the minimum projection width of its reference geometry's convex hull. Small subdivisions remain live when their connected group is wide enough. Narrow resulting groups become one second visual remnants before fading. New groups are filtered before any new bodies are created. Rendering interpolates poses and optionally blends shared presentation vertices across flexible joints; it does not modify collision or failure geometry.
    
    ## Verification
    
    `odin test .` covers bridge and subdivision removal; surviving and broken inherited attachments; simultaneous endpoint replacement; processing and storage order independence; seed zero; subthreshold and infinite strengths; same-blast child and connection failure; shared terminal batches and mixed-width guards; termination even with a zero width cutoff; removal of unsplittable attached regions under repeated failure; valid partial partitions; radius-dependent blast power above strength 20; rotational motion inheritance; a single impulse per final survivor; rotation independent width; group filtering; retained bodies; concave collision fixtures; physical impacts; overloaded joints; replaceable load policies; flexibility; repeated blasts for all presets; snapshots; interpolation; and real TCP transfer of a wall and its split. Shortcut comparisons check exact surviving outlines, seeds, links, memberships, fading and motion against ordinary recursive evaluation for partial and complete deletion in all three patterns, including a later blast. Odin's test allocator tracks allocations and reports leaks.
    
    Sandbox checks exercise the intact tower under gravity, player movement and a full jump, buffered and coyote jumps, standing on and pushing an actual detached region, repeated clean resets after blasts and respawn, independent staged tuning, menu/UI input consumption, frozen fading, valid/invalid posed aim, and fixed framing at multiple window sizes. The playable controls and settings remain independent of the destruction transaction.
    
    The implementation intentionally uses ordinary arrays, complete affected-piece membership rebuilds, local candidate scans, and explicit snapshots. Large-world spatial selection, compression, rollback and parallel simulation can be added when a measured workload calls for them.

    physics_finish_mass :: proc(s: ^Scene,body: b2.BodyId,sub: Subdivision) {
        if s.physics.fixture_counts[sub.id]==0 {
            // A microscopic attached subdivision is still one live logical entity.
            // Use a bounding fixture when the engine cannot resolve any of its ears.
            lo,hi:=Vec2{1e30,1e30},Vec2{-1e30,-1e30}
            for rest in sub.outline.points { p:=vsub(rest,sub.rest_center); lo={min(lo.x,p.x),min(lo.y,p.y)}; hi={max(hi.x,p.x),max(hi.y,p.y)} }
            polygon:=b2.MakeOffsetBox(max(f32(0.0025),(hi.x-lo.x)*0.5),max(f32(0.0025),(hi.y-lo.y)*0.5),to_b2(vmul(vadd(lo,hi),0.5)),b2.MakeRot(0))
            def:=b2.DefaultShapeDef(); def.density=1
            _ = b2.CreatePolygonShape(body,def,polygon)
            s.physics.fixture_counts[sub.id]=1
        }
        // Keep mass and the body origin tied to the exact logical polygon, including
        // when Box2D simplifies a fixture. This also makes rotational inheritance exact.
        inertia: f32
        for i in 0..<len(sub.outline.points) {
            a,b:=vsub(sub.outline.points[i],sub.rest_center),vsub(sub.outline.points[(i+1)%len(sub.outline.points)],sub.rest_center)
            inertia+=vcross(a,b)*(vdot(a,a)+vdot(a,b)+vdot(b,b))/12
        }
        b2.Body_SetMassData(body,b2.MassData{mass=polygon_area(sub.outline),center={},rotationalInertia=math.abs(inertia)})
        b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(body,to_b2(sub.pose.velocity))
        b2.Body_SetAngularVelocity(body,sub.pose.angular_velocity)
    }
    // This runs only between World_Step calls. Existing handles survive ownership changes.
    physics_sync_structure :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        if !s.physics.active { return }
        dead_joints: [dynamic]u64
        dead_bodies: [dynamic]u64
        defer delete(dead_joints); defer delete(dead_bodies)
        for id,joint in s.physics.joints {
            row,ok := s.conn_rows[id]
            if !ok || !s.connections[row].live { b2.DestroyJoint(joint); append(&dead_joints,id) }
        }
        for id in dead_joints { delete_key(&s.physics.joints,id) }
        for id,body in s.physics.bodies {
            row,ok := s.sub_rows[id]
            if !ok || !s.subdivisions[row].live { b2.DestroyBody(body); append(&dead_bodies,id) }
        }
        for id in dead_bodies { delete_key(&s.physics.bodies,id); delete_key(&s.physics.fixture_counts,id) }
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            if _,exists := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]; exists { continue }
            def := b2.DefaultBodyDef()
            def.type = .dynamicBody
            def.position = to_b2(sub.pose.position)
            def.rotation = b2.MakeRot(sub.pose.angle)
            def.linearVelocity = to_b2(sub.pose.velocity)
            def.angularVelocity = sub.pose.angular_velocity
            body := b2.CreateBody(s.physics.world,def)
            s.physics.bodies[sub.id] = body
            if is_convex(sub.outline) && len(sub.outline.points) <= 8 {
                physics_create_fixture(s,body,sub,sub.outline)
            } else {
                triangles := convex_decomposition(sub.outline)

            physics_finish_mass(s,body,sub)

        for c in s.connections {

            b := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]

            def.linearDampingRatio = GLOBAL_DAMPING

    // Random number generators.
    package rand
    
    import "base:intrinsics"
    import "base:runtime"
    import "core:math"
    
    Generator :: runtime.Random_Generator
    
    Generator_Query_Info :: runtime.Random_Generator_Query_Info
    
    Default_Random_State :: runtime.Default_Random_State
    
    /*
    Returns an instance of the runtime pseudorandom generator.  If no
    initial state is provided, the PRNG will be lazily initialized with
    entropy from the system entropy source on first-use.
    
    The cryptographic security of the returned random number generator
    is directly dependent on the quality of the initialization entropy.
    Calling `reset`/`create` SHOULD be done with no seed/state, or
    32-bytes of high-quality entropy.
    
    WARNING:
    - The lazy initialization will panic if there is no system entropy
      source available.
    - While the generator is cryptographically secure, developers SHOULD
      prefer `crypto.random_generator()` for cryptographic use cases such
      as key generation.
    
    Inputs:
    - state: Optional initial PRNG state.
    
    Returns:
    - A `Generator` instance.
    */
    default_random_generator :: runtime.default_random_generator
    
    @(require_results)
    create_u64 :: proc(seed: u64) -> (state: Default_Random_State) {
        seed := seed
        runtime.default_random_generator_proc(&state, .Reset, ([^]byte)(&seed)[:size_of(seed)])
        return
    }
    
    @(require_results)
    create_bytes :: proc(seed: []byte) -> (state: Default_Random_State) {
        runtime.default_random_generator_proc(&state, .Reset, seed)
        return
    }
    
    create :: proc {
        create_u64,
        create_bytes,
    }
    
    /*
    Reset the seed used by the context.random_generator.
    
    Inputs:
    - seed: The seed value
    
    Example:
        import "core:math/rand"
        import "core:fmt"
    
        reset_example :: proc() {
            rand.reset(1)
            fmt.println(rand.uint64())
        }
    
    Possible Output:
    
        10
    */
    reset :: proc {
        reset_u64,
        reset_bytes,

    package main
    
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:math/rand"
    
    Blast_Mode :: enum { Manual, Falling_Bombs }
    BOMB_RADIUS :: f32(0.18)
    BOMB_FUSE :: f32(1)
    BOMB_DROP_MIN :: f32(1)
    BOMB_DROP_MAX :: f32(2.5)
    BOMB_SKY_HEIGHT :: f32(7.3)
    BOMB_BURST_TIME :: f32(0.3)
    
    Bomb :: struct {
    	body: b2.BodyId,
    	previous: Vec2,
    	landed: bool,
    	fuse: f32,
    }
    Bomb_Burst :: struct { position: Vec2, radius, age: f32 }
    Bomb_Rain :: struct {
    	bombs: [dynamic]Bomb,
    	bursts: [dynamic]Bomb_Burst,
    	random: rand.Default_Random_State,
    	until_drop: f32,
    }
    bomb_drop_delay :: proc(rain: ^Bomb_Rain) -> f32 {
    	return rand.float32_range(BOMB_DROP_MIN,BOMB_DROP_MAX,rand.default_random_generator(&rain.random))
    }
    bomb_rain_reset :: proc(rain: ^Bomb_Rain,seed: u8) {
    	// The old physics world has already been destroyed. Keep the small list buffers.
    	clear(&rain.bombs); clear(&rain.bursts)
    	// A separate stream leaves procedural destruction seeds independent of drops.
    	rain.random=rand.create(u64(seed)+0x626f6d62)
    	rain.until_drop=bomb_drop_delay(rain)
    }
    bomb_rain_clear :: proc(rain: ^Bomb_Rain) {
    	for bomb in rain.bombs { b2.DestroyBody(bomb.body) }
    	clear(&rain.bombs); clear(&rain.bursts)
    }
    sandbox_set_blast_mode :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,mode: Blast_Mode) {
    	if mode==game.applied.blast_mode { return }
    	game.applied.blast_mode=mode
    	game.draft.blast_mode=mode
    	bomb_rain_clear(&game.bomb_rain)
    	game.bomb_rain.until_drop=bomb_drop_delay(&game.bomb_rain)
    	if mode==.Falling_Bombs { sandbox_notice(game,"Falling bombs: one-second fuse after landing") }
    	else { sandbox_notice(game,"Manual blast placement") }
    }
    bomb_spawn :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,position: Vec2) {
    	def:=b2.DefaultBodyDef()
    	def.type=.dynamicBody
    	def.position=to_b2(position)
    	def.isBullet=true
    	body:=b2.CreateBody(game.scene.physics.world,def)
    	shape:=b2.DefaultShapeDef()
    	shape.density=0.4
    	shape.material.friction=0.7
    	shape.material.restitution=0.05
    	_ = b2.CreateCircleShape(body,shape,b2.Circle{radius=BOMB_RADIUS})
    	append(&game.bomb_rain.bombs,Bomb{body=body,previous=position,fuse=BOMB_FUSE})
    }
    bomb_has_landed :: proc(bomb: Bomb) -> bool {
    	position:=b2.Body_GetPosition(bomb.body)
    	buffer:=make([]b2.ContactData,int(b2.Body_GetContactCapacity(bomb.body)))
    	defer delete(buffer)
    	for contact in b2.Body_GetContactData(bomb.body,buffer) {
    		normal:=from_b2(contact.manifold.normal)
    		if b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdA)==bomb.body { normal=vmul(normal,-1) }
    		if normal.y<0.55 { continue }
    		for i in 0..<int(contact.manifold.pointCount) {
    			point:=contact.manifold.points[i]
    			if point.separation<=0.025 && point.point.y<position.y { return true }
    		}
    	}
    	return false
    }
    bomb_rain_before_step :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,dt: f32) {
    	if game.applied.blast_mode!=.Falling_Bombs { return }
    	rain:=&game.bomb_rain
    	for &bomb in rain.bombs { bomb.previous=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(bomb.body)) }
    	rain.until_drop-=dt
    	if rain.until_drop<=0 {
    		x:=rand.float32_range(-7,8,rand.default_random_generator(&rain.random))
    		bomb_spawn(game,{x,BOMB_SKY_HEIGHT})
    		rain.until_drop+=bomb_drop_delay(rain)
    	}
    }
    bomb_rain_after_step :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,dt: f32) {
    	rain:=&game.bomb_rain
    	burst_count:=0
    	for burst in rain.bursts {
    		next:=burst; next.age+=dt
    		if next.age<BOMB_BURST_TIME { rain.bursts[burst_count]=next; burst_count+=1 }
    	}
    	resize(&rain.bursts,burst_count)
    	// Read landing contacts for all bombs before any blast changes the collision world.
    	for &bomb in rain.bombs {
    		if bomb.landed { bomb.fuse=max(f32(0),bomb.fuse-dt) }
    		else if bomb_has_landed(bomb) { bomb.landed=true }
    	}
    	first_burst:=len(rain.bursts)
    	bomb_count:=0
    	for bomb in rain.bombs {
    		position:=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(bomb.body))
    		explode:=bomb.landed && bomb.fuse<=0.000001
    		if explode { append(&rain.bursts,Bomb_Burst{position=position,radius=game.applied.blast_radius}) }
    		if explode || position.y < -3 || position.x < -9 || position.x > 10 {
    			b2.DestroyBody(bomb.body)
    		} else { rain.bombs[bomb_count]=bomb; bomb_count+=1 }
    	}
    	resize(&rain.bombs,bomb_count)
    	for burst in rain.bursts[first_burst:] { sandbox_explode(game,burst.position) }
    }

    package main

    @(test)
    falling_bomb_waits_for_landing_then_explodes_once :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
    	sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
    	settings:=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS; settings.blast_mode=.Falling_Bombs
    	game:=sandbox_create(settings); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
    	game.bomb_rain.until_drop=1000
    	bomb_spawn(&game,{-2,4.5})
    	body:=game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].body
    	sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    	testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetPosition(body).y<4.5 && b2.Body_GetLinearVelocity(body).y<0)
    	testing.expect(t,!game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed && game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].fuse==BOMB_FUSE)
    	for _ in 0..<180 {
    		if game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed { break }
    		sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    	}
    	testing.expect(t,game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed && game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].fuse==BOMB_FUSE)
    	testing.expect(t,close(b2.Body_GetPosition(body).y,BOMB_RADIUS))
    	for _ in 0..<59 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
    	testing.expect(t,b2.Body_IsValid(body) && len(game.bomb_rain.bursts)==0,"The bomb must remain physical for a full second after first landing")
    	sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    	testing.expect(t,!b2.Body_IsValid(body) && len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)==0 && len(game.bomb_rain.bursts)==1)
    	testing.expect(t,close_vec(game.bomb_rain.bursts[0].position,{-2,BOMB_RADIUS}))
    	for _ in 0..<60 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
    	testing.expect(t,len(game.bomb_rain.bursts)==0 && b2.World_GetCounters(game.scene.physics.world).bodyCount==11,"An exploded bomb must leave no physics object or repeated explosion")
    }
    
    @(test)
    bomb_fuse_needs_support_and_accepts_destructible_surfaces :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
    	sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
    	settings:=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS; settings.blast_mode=.Falling_Bombs
    	game:=sandbox_create(settings); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
    	game.bomb_rain.until_drop=1000
    	bomb_spawn(&game,{-2,4})
    	body:=game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].body
    	b2.Body_SetGravityScale(body,0)
    	for _ in 0..<120 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
    	testing.expect(t,!game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed && game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].fuse==BOMB_FUSE,"Time spent airborne must not light the fuse")
    	b2.Body_SetTransform(body,{1.5-BOMB_RADIUS-0.005,1.25},b2.MakeRot(0))
    	b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(body,{1,0})
    	for _ in 0..<20 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
    	testing.expect(t,!game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed,"Brushing a vertical wall must not count as landing")
    	b2.Body_SetTransform(body,{2.8,3.2},b2.MakeRot(0))
    	b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(body,{})
    	b2.Body_SetGravityScale(body,1)
    	for _ in 0..<90 {
    		if game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed { break }
    		sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    	}
    	testing.expect(t,game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed && b2.Body_GetPosition(body).y>2.6,"A bomb should rest and arm on the tower, not pass through it")
    }
    
    @(test)
    bomb_blasts_use_current_radius_and_remove_all_expired_bodies :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
    	sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
    	settings:=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS; settings.blast_mode=.Falling_Bombs; settings.blast_radius=0.5
    	game:=sandbox_create(settings); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
    	game.bomb_rain.until_drop=1000
    	bomb_spawn(&game,{1,BOMB_RADIUS}); bomb_spawn(&game,{6,BOMB_RADIUS})
    	first,second:=game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].body,game.bomb_rain.bombs[1].body
    	for _ in 0..<10 {
    		sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    		if game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed && game.bomb_rain.bombs[1].landed { break }
    	}
    	testing.expect(t,game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed && game.bomb_rain.bombs[1].landed)
    	revision:=game.scene.revision
    	testing.expect(t,!sandbox_blast(&game,{1,1.3}) && game.scene.revision==revision,"Manual clicks must be disabled while bombs are active")
    	sandbox_set_radius(&game,4.2)
    	for _ in 0..<60 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
    	testing.expect(t,len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)==0 && !b2.Body_IsValid(first) && !b2.Body_IsValid(second))
    	testing.expect(t,len(game.bomb_rain.bursts)==2 && game.bomb_rain.bursts[0].radius==4.2)
    	testing.expect(t,game.scene.revision>revision && counts_live_subdivisions(&game.scene)<9,"Landed bombs must invoke real destruction using the live radius")
    	testing.expect(t,b2.Body_IsValid(game.player.body) && b2.Body_IsValid(game.floor))
    	expect_valid(t,&game.scene)
    }
    
    @(test)
    bomb_rain_random_drops_pause_switch_and_reset :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
    	sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
    	settings:=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS; settings.blast_mode=.Falling_Bombs
    	game:=sandbox_create(settings); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
    	first_delay:=game.bomb_rain.until_drop
    	testing.expect(t,first_delay>=BOMB_DROP_MIN && first_delay<=BOMB_DROP_MAX)
    	for _ in 0..<160 {
    		sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    		if len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)>0 { break }
    	}
    	first_body:=game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].body
    	first_position:=game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].previous
    	second_delay:=game.bomb_rain.until_drop
    	testing.expect(t,first_position.y==BOMB_SKY_HEIGHT && first_position.x>=-7 && first_position.x<=8)
    	testing.expect(t,second_delay>=BOMB_DROP_MIN-1.0/60.0 && second_delay<=BOMB_DROP_MAX && second_delay!=first_delay)
    	_ = sandbox_route_input(&game,{},false)
    	input:=sandbox_route_input(&game,{blast_pressed=true,blast_down=true},false)
    	testing.expect(t,!input.blast_pressed,"Input routing must also suppress manual blasts in bomb mode")
    	for _ in 0..<160 {
    		sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    		if game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed { break }
    	}
    	fuse:=game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].fuse
    	delay:=game.bomb_rain.until_drop
    	position:=b2.Body_GetPosition(first_body)
    	bomb_count:=len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)
    	sandbox_set_panel(&game,true)
    	sandbox_advance(&game,5,{})
    	testing.expect(t,game.bomb_rain.until_drop==delay && len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)==bomb_count)
    	testing.expect(t,game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].fuse==fuse && b2.Body_GetPosition(first_body)==position,"Settings must pause landed fuses as well as the spawn schedule and physics")
    	revision:=game.scene.revision
    	sandbox_set_blast_mode(&game,.Manual)
    	testing.expect(t,game.applied.blast_mode==.Manual && game.draft.blast_mode==.Manual && game.scene.revision==revision)
    	testing.expect(t,len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)==0 && !b2.Body_IsValid(first_body),"Switching back must clear existing bombs without resetting the yard")
    	sandbox_set_panel(&game,false)
    	_ = sandbox_route_input(&game,{},false)
    	input=sandbox_route_input(&game,{blast_pressed=true},false)
    	testing.expect(t,input.blast_pressed)
    	// Reset repeats the applied seed's drops and restores clean physics ownership.
    	sandbox_set_blast_mode(&game,.Falling_Bombs)
    	sandbox_reset(&game)
    	testing.expect(t,game.bomb_rain.until_drop==first_delay && len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)==0 && len(game.bomb_rain.bursts)==0)
    	for _ in 0..<160 {
    		sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    		if len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)>0 { break }
    	}
    	testing.expect(t,close_vec(game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].previous,first_position))
    	game.bomb_rain.until_drop=0
    	sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    	testing.expect(t,len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)==2 && game.bomb_rain.bombs[1].previous.x!=first_position.x,"Successive drops should use different random sky positions")
    	b2.Body_SetTransform(game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].body,{-2,-4},b2.MakeRot(0))
    	sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    	testing.expect(t,len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)==1 && len(game.bomb_rain.bursts)==0,"Bombs lost outside the yard must be cleaned up")
    	sandbox_reset(&game)
    	testing.expect(t,b2.World_GetCounters(game.scene.physics.world).bodyCount==11 && len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)==0)
    }

## User

Fix the repeated corner fans of extremely thin triangles visible in the screenshot. Keep this a small, focused change to subdivision generation.

In an earlier version, the suspected cause was:

- Shared-edge displacement adds small bends, making some polygons concave.
- Concave parents get triangulated even when the material’s `triangulate` setting is false.
- Those triangles become separate logical subdivisions.
- The triangulator’s fixed processing order produces long, skinny triangles converging on one corner.

Verify whether this chain exists in the current build. First confirm that the visible diagonals are logical subdivision boundaries rather than rendering-only edges. Temporarily disabling shared-edge displacement in Chunk/Splinter is a useful diagnostic.

If confirmed, make the smallest correction so handling a slightly concave polygon does not automatically turn it into a fan of independent fragments. Prefer reusing the existing convex-decomposition-and-merge helper if it solves the problem.

Preserve the intended material differences: Chunk produces chunky partitions, Splinter produces elongated partitions, and Shatter can deliberately produce triangles. Keep valid shared boundaries and the existing subdivision settings.

Also check whether adjacent blocks repeat because they accidentally receive identical generation inputs. Correct accidental seed reuse through the existing deterministic seed mechanism if needed.

Keep the blast rules, data model, and playable UX intact. Preserve shared-edge displacement where practical; disabling it is initially a diagnostic.

Check the starting yard and a few subsequent fractures visually, run the relevant existing checks, and verify that the changed partitions preserve area without gaps or overlaps. Briefly report the confirmed cause and the fix.[Image #1]

    #+feature dynamic-literals
    package main
    
    import "core:math"
    
    polygon_area :: proc(p: Polygon) -> f32 {
        a: f32
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) { a += vcross(p.points[i],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]) }
        return math.abs(a)*0.5
    }
    clip_polygon :: proc(p: Polygon, axis: int, cut: f32, keep_low: bool) -> Polygon {
        points: [dynamic]Vec2
        defer delete(points)
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) {
            a,b := p.points[i],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]
            av,bv := a.x-cut,b.x-cut
            if axis == 1 { av = a.y-cut; bv = b.y-cut }
            if !keep_low { av = -av; bv = -bv }
            inside_a, inside_b := av <= 0,bv <= 0
            if inside_a { append(&points,a) }
            if inside_a != inside_b {
                t := av/(av-bv)
                append(&points,vadd(a,vmul(vsub(b,a),t)))
            }
        }
        return make_polygon(points[:])
    }
    is_convex :: proc(p: Polygon) -> bool {
        if len(p.points) < 3 { return false }
        sign: f32
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) {
            cross := vcross(vsub(p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)],p.points[i]),vsub(p.points[(i+2)%len(p.points)],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]))
            if math.abs(cross) < 0.00001 { continue }
            if sign == 0 { sign = cross } else if cross*sign < 0 { return false }
        }
        return true
    }
    point_in_triangle :: proc(p,a,b,c: Vec2, orientation: f32) -> bool {
        return vcross(vsub(b,a),vsub(p,a))*orientation >= -0.00001 &&
               vcross(vsub(c,b),vsub(p,b))*orientation >= -0.00001 &&
               vcross(vsub(a,c),vsub(p,c))*orientation >= -0.00001
    }
    triangulate_polygon :: proc(p: Polygon) -> [dynamic]Polygon {
        result: [dynamic]Polygon
        indices: [dynamic]int
        defer delete(indices)
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) { append(&indices,i) }
        signed: f32
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) { signed += vcross(p.points[i],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]) }
        orientation := f32(1)
        if signed < 0 { orientation = -1 }
        for len(indices) > 3 {
            found := false
            for k in 0..<len(indices) {
                i,j,l := indices[(k+len(indices)-1)%len(indices)],indices[k],indices[(k+1)%len(indices)]
                a,b,c := p.points[i],p.points[j],p.points[l]
                if vcross(vsub(b,a),vsub(c,b))*orientation <= 0.00001 { continue }
                contains := false
                for n in indices { if n != i && n != j && n != l && point_in_triangle(p.points[n],a,b,c,orientation) { contains = true; break } }
                if contains { continue }
                append(&result,make_polygon([]Vec2{a,b,c}))
                ordered_remove(&indices,k)
                found = true
                break
            }
            if !found { break }
        }
        if len(indices) == 3 { append(&result,make_polygon([]Vec2{p.points[indices[0]],p.points[indices[1]],p.points[indices[2]]})) }
        return result
    }
    // Straight shared cuts are constructed by clipping both sides at one value.
    // Outside edges are never moved; no gap or overlap is introduced at the cut.
    generate_children :: proc(parent: Polygon, recipe: Material, seed: u8) -> [dynamic]Polygon {
        result: [dynamic]Polygon
        if seed == 0 { return result }
        if !is_convex(parent) || recipe.triangulate { result = triangulate_polygon(parent) } else {
            append(&result,make_polygon(parent.points))
        }
        target := max(recipe.generation_count,len(result))
        for len(result) < target {
            chosen := -1
            largest: f32
            for p,i in result { a := polygon_area(p); if a > largest { largest = a; chosen = i } }
            if chosen < 0 || largest < 0.0001 { break }
            p := result[chosen]
            min_x,min_y := f32(1e30),f32(1e30)
            max_x,max_y := f32(-1e30),f32(-1e30)
            for point in p.points { min_x=min(min_x,point.x); max_x=max(max_x,point.x); min_y=min(min_y,point.y); max_y=max(max_y,point.y) }
            axis := 0
            if (max_x-min_x) < (max_y-min_y)*max(recipe.aspect_ratio,0.1) { axis = 1 }
            fraction := 0.4+0.2*f32(derive_seed(seed,u64(len(result))))/255
            cut := min_x+(max_x-min_x)*fraction
            if axis == 1 { cut = min_y+(max_y-min_y)*fraction }
            low, high := clip_polygon(p,axis,cut,true),clip_polygon(p,axis,cut,false)
            if polygon_area(low) < 0.0001 || polygon_area(high) < 0.0001 { delete(low.points); delete(high.points); break }
            delete(p.points)
            result[chosen] = low
            append(&result,high)
        }
        displace_shared_boundaries(result[:],seed)
        if recipe.triangulate {
            triangles: [dynamic]Polygon
            for polygon in result {
                parts:=triangulate_polygon(polygon)
                for part in parts { append(&triangles,part) }
                delete(parts); delete(polygon.points)
            }
            delete(result)
            result=triangles
        }
        // Incomplete triangulation or a no-progress recipe must remove the failed
        // outline, rather than retaining an equivalent child or a partial partition.
        area: f32
        genuine := len(result)>=2
        parent_area := polygon_area(parent)
        for child in result {
            child_area := polygon_area(child)
            genuine = genuine && child_area>0 && child_area<parent_area
            area += child_area
        }
        if !genuine || math.abs(area-parent_area)>max(f32(0.000002),parent_area*0.0002) {
            for child in result { delete(child.points) }
            delete(result)
            return nil
        }
        return result
    }
    
    apply_failures :: proc(s: ^Scene, failures: Failures) {
        if len(failures.subdivisions) == 0 && len(failures.connections) == 0 && len(failures.discard_subdivisions) == 0 { return }
        s.revision+=1
        affected := make(map[u64]bool)
        defer delete(affected)
        stage_failures(s,failures,&affected)
        rebuild_affected_pieces(s,affected)
    }
    // Reuse the existing one-wave graph update for physics and for each blast wave.
    // Ownership, size filtering and engine handles are committed only at the end.
    stage_failures :: proc(s: ^Scene, failures: Failures, affected: ^map[u64]bool) {
        replacements := make(map[u64][dynamic]u64)
        defer { for _,children in replacements { delete(children) }; delete(replacements) }
        failed_subs := sorted_ids(failures.subdivisions[:])
        for id in failures.discard_subdivisions { if !contains_id(failed_subs[:],id) { append(&failed_subs,id) } }
        sort_ids(failed_subs[:])
        failed_conns := sorted_ids(failures.connections[:])
        defer delete(failed_subs); defer delete(failed_conns)
        old_connection_count := len(s.connections)
        old_connections: [dynamic]u64
        defer delete(old_connections)
        for i in 0..<old_connection_count { append(&old_connections,s.connections[i].id) }
        sort_ids(old_connections[:])
        for id in failed_subs {
            row, ok := s.sub_rows[id]
            if !ok || !s.subdivisions[row].live { continue }
            parent := s.subdivisions[row]
            affected[parent.owner] = true
            seed := parent.seed
            if parent.width<=s.minimum_width || contains_id(failures.discard_subdivisions[:],id) { seed=0 }
            children := generate_children(parent.outline,s.materials[parent.material],seed)
            max_width: f32
            for outline,ordinal in children {
                center := centroid(outline)
                world_center := posed_point(parent,center)
                r := vsub(world_center,parent.pose.position)
                pose := Pose{position=world_center,angle=parent.pose.angle,velocity=vadd(parent.pose.velocity,Vec2{-parent.pose.angular_velocity*r.y,parent.pose.angular_velocity*r.x}),angular_velocity=parent.pose.angular_velocity}
                child := add_subdivision(s,parent.owner,outline,pose)
                child_row := s.sub_rows[child]
                // Parent context plus child ordinal is independent of other branches'
                // allocations. A deletion shortcut cannot perturb their future seeds.
                s.subdivisions[child_row].seed=derive_seed(parent.seed,u64(ordinal+1))
                max_width=max(max_width,s.subdivisions[child_row].width)
                delete(outline.points)
                child_ids := replacements[id]
                append(&child_ids,child)
                replacements[id] = child_ids
            }
            delete(children)
            if max_width<=s.minimum_width {
                child_ids := replacements[id]
                for child in child_ids { s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[child]].seed=0 }
            }
            s.subdivisions[row].live = false
        }
        for id in failed_conns {
            row, ok := s.conn_rows[id]
            if ok && s.connections[row].live {
                c := s.connections[row]
                affected[s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]].owner] = true
                affected[s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]].owner] = true
                s.connections[row].live = false
            }
        }
        for old_id in old_connections {
            i := s.conn_rows[old_id]
            c := s.connections[i]
            if !c.live { continue }
            a_dead := !s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]].live
            b_dead := !s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]].live
            if !a_dead && !b_dead { continue }
            s.connections[i].live = false
            left_default,right_default := [1]u64{c.a},[1]u64{c.b}
            left,right := left_default[:],right_default[:]
            if a_dead { left = replacements[c.a][:] }
            if b_dead { right = replacements[c.b][:] }
            old_a,old_b := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]],s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
            old_length,_ := shared_boundary(old_a.outline,old_b.outline)
            if old_length <= 0 { continue }
            for a in left {
                for b in right {
                    if inherits_old_boundary(s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[a]].outline,s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[b]].outline,old_a.outline,old_b.outline) { add_connection(s,a,b) }
                }
            }
        }
        for id in failed_subs {
            children := replacements[id]
            for i in 0..<len(children) { for j in i+1..<len(children) { add_connection(s,children[i],children[j]) } }
        }
    }
    rebuild_affected_pieces :: proc(s: ^Scene, affected: map[u64]bool) {
        owners: [dynamic]u64
        defer delete(owners)
        for owner in affected { append(&owners,owner) }
        sort_ids(owners[:])
        for owner in owners { rebuild_piece(s,owner) }
    }
    
    BLAST_LOAD_MULTIPLIER :: f32(10)
    BLAST_IMPULSE_SCALE :: f32(0.1)
    blast_load :: proc(distance,radius: f32) -> f32 {
        if radius <= 0 || distance >= radius { return 0 }
        return BLAST_LOAD_MULTIPLIER*max(f32(0),radius-distance)
    }
    fails :: proc(load,strength: f32) -> bool { return load > 0 && load >= strength }
    evaluate_blast :: proc(s: ^Scene, blast: Blast, first_subdivision: int = 0, first_connection: int = 0) -> Failures {
        f := Failures{}
        for i in first_subdivision..<len(s.subdivisions) {
            sub := &s.subdivisions[i]
            if !sub.live { continue }
            offset := vsub(subdivision_sample(sub^),blast.position)
            distance := vlen(offset)
            load := blast_load(distance,blast.radius)
            if load <= 0 { continue }
            if fails(load,s.materials[sub.material].subdivision_strength) { append(&f.subdivisions,sub.id) }
        }
        for i in first_connection..<len(s.connections) {
            c := s.connections[i]
            if !c.live { continue }
            a := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]]
            load := blast_load(vlen(vsub(connection_sample(s,c),blast.position)),blast.radius)
            if fails(load,s.materials[a.material].connection_strength) { append(&f.connections,c.id) }
        }
        return f
    }
    // Descendants partition the outline, inherit its material and keep its rigid
    // transform during this event. Their samples lie in the posed convex hull.
    // Outward rounding and a strict load margin avoid pruning borderline failures.
    blast_erases_descendants :: proc(sub: Subdivision, blast: Blast, strength: f32) -> bool {
        if !finite(strength) || !finite(blast.radius) || !valid_vec(blast.position) { return false }
        farthest: f32
        for point in sub.outline.points {
            distance := vlen(vsub(posed_point(sub,point),blast.position))
            if !finite(distance) { return false }
            farthest=max(farthest,distance)
        }
        farthest=math.nextafter(farthest,math.inf_f32(1))
        return blast_load(farthest,blast.radius)>strength+0.0001
    }
    blast_pass :: proc(s: ^Scene, blast: Blast, deletion_shortcut: bool = true) {
        physics_read_motion(s)
        affected := make(map[u64]bool)
        defer delete(affected)
        f := evaluate_blast(s,blast)
        changed := false
        for len(f.subdivisions)>0 || len(f.connections)>0 {
            changed=true
            if deletion_shortcut {
                for id in f.subdivisions {
                    sub := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[id]]
                    if sub.seed!=0 && sub.width>s.minimum_width && blast_erases_descendants(sub,blast,s.materials[sub.material].subdivision_strength) { append(&f.discard_subdivisions,id) }
                }
            }
            first_subdivision,first_connection := len(s.subdivisions),len(s.connections)
            stage_failures(s,f,&affected)
            delete(f.subdivisions); delete(f.connections); delete(f.discard_subdivisions)
            // Earlier survivors have unchanged samples. Only children and new links
            // need this blast again; failed old links are already excluded from inheritance.
            f=evaluate_blast(s,blast,first_subdivision,first_connection)
        }
        delete(f.subdivisions); delete(f.connections); delete(f.discard_subdivisions)
        if changed { s.revision+=1; rebuild_affected_pieces(s,affected) }
        physics_sync_structure(s)
        for i in 0..<len(s.subdivisions) {
            sub := &s.subdivisions[i]
            if !sub.live { continue }
            offset := vsub(subdivision_sample(sub^),blast.position)
            distance := vlen(offset)
            load := blast_load(distance,blast.radius)
            if load>0 && distance>0.00001 { apply_blast_motion(s,sub,vmul(offset,1/distance),load) }
        }
    }
    fade_step :: proc(s: ^Scene, dt: f32) {
        for i := len(s.remnants)-1; i >= 0; i -= 1 {
            s.remnants[i].age += dt
            if s.remnants[i].age >= 1 { ordered_remove(&s.remnants,i) }
        }
    }

    import "core:math"
    
    Segment :: struct { a,b: Vec2 }
    Cut_Boundary :: struct { a,b: int, segment: Segment }
    convex_hull :: proc(points: []Vec2) -> [dynamic]Vec2 {
        sorted: [dynamic]Vec2
        defer delete(sorted)
        for point in points { append(&sorted,point) }
        for i in 1..<len(sorted) {
            j:=i
            for j>0 && (sorted[j].x<sorted[j-1].x || (sorted[j].x==sorted[j-1].x && sorted[j].y<sorted[j-1].y)) { sorted[j],sorted[j-1]=sorted[j-1],sorted[j]; j-=1 }
        }
        hull: [dynamic]Vec2
        if len(sorted)<2 { for p in sorted { append(&hull,p) }; return hull }
        for p in sorted {
            for len(hull)>=2 && vcross(vsub(hull[len(hull)-1],hull[len(hull)-2]),vsub(p,hull[len(hull)-1]))<=0 { resize(&hull,len(hull)-1) }
            append(&hull,p)
        }
        upper_start:=len(hull)+1
        for i:=len(sorted)-2; i>=0; i-=1 {
            p:=sorted[i]
            for len(hull)>=upper_start && vcross(vsub(hull[len(hull)-1],hull[len(hull)-2]),vsub(p,hull[len(hull)-1]))<=0 { resize(&hull,len(hull)-1) }
            append(&hull,p)
        }
        resize(&hull,len(hull)-1)
        return hull
    }
    segment_overlap :: proc(a,b: Segment) -> (Segment,bool) {
        d := vsub(a.b,a.a)
        length := vlen(d)
        if length < 0.00001 { return {},false }
        if math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(b.a,a.a))) > 0.0001*length || math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(b.b,a.a))) > 0.0001*length { return {},false }
        unit := vmul(d,1/length)
        t0,t1 := vdot(vsub(b.a,a.a),unit),vdot(vsub(b.b,a.a),unit)
        lo,hi := max(f32(0),min(t0,t1)),min(length,max(t0,t1))
        if hi-lo <= 0.0001 { return {},false }
        return Segment{vadd(a.a,vmul(unit,lo)),vadd(a.a,vmul(unit,hi))},true
    }
    shared_segments :: proc(a,b: Polygon) -> [dynamic]Segment {
        result: [dynamic]Segment
        for i in 0..<len(a.points) {
            for j in 0..<len(b.points) {
                if segment,ok := segment_overlap(Segment{a.points[i],a.points[(i+1)%len(a.points)]},Segment{b.points[j],b.points[(j+1)%len(b.points)]}); ok { append(&result,segment) }
            }
        }
        return result
    }
    inherits_old_boundary :: proc(a,b,old_a,old_b: Polygon) -> bool {
        current := shared_segments(a,b)
        original := shared_segments(old_a,old_b)
        defer delete(current); defer delete(original)
        for x in current { for y in original { if _,ok := segment_overlap(x,y); ok { return true } } }
        return false
    }
    insert_polygon_vertex :: proc(p: ^Polygon,index: int,point: Vec2) {
        points:=make([]Vec2,len(p.points)+1)
        copy(points[:index],p.points[:index]); points[index]=point
        copy(points[index+1:],p.points[index:])
        delete(p.points); p.points=points
    }
    insert_boundary_endpoint :: proc(p: ^Polygon,point: Vec2) {
        for existing in p.points { if vlen(vsub(existing,point)) < 0.00001 { return } }
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) {
            a,b := p.points[i],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]
            edge := vsub(b,a)
            length := vlen(edge)
            if length < 0.00001 { continue }
            t := vdot(vsub(point,a),edge)/(length*length)
            if t > 0 && t < 1 && math.abs(vcross(edge,vsub(point,a))) < 0.00001*length { insert_polygon_vertex(p,i+1,point); return }
        }
    }
    insert_shared_midpoint :: proc(p: ^Polygon,segment: Segment,point: Vec2) {
        insert_boundary_endpoint(p,segment.a)
        insert_boundary_endpoint(p,segment.b)
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) {
            a,b := p.points[i],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]
            if (vlen(vsub(a,segment.a)) < 0.00001 && vlen(vsub(b,segment.b)) < 0.00001) || (vlen(vsub(b,segment.a)) < 0.00001 && vlen(vsub(a,segment.b)) < 0.00001) {
                insert_polygon_vertex(p,i+1,point)
                return
            }
        }
    }
    // Capture each common cut once, then install the exact same displaced midpoint
    // in both outlines. Parent boundary vertices are untouched, including T junctions.
    displace_shared_boundaries :: proc(children: []Polygon,seed: u8) {
        boundaries: [dynamic]Cut_Boundary
        defer delete(boundaries)
        for i in 0..<len(children) {
            for j in i+1..<len(children) {
                segments := shared_segments(children[i],children[j])
                for segment in segments { append(&boundaries,Cut_Boundary{i,j,segment}) }
                delete(segments)
            }
        }
        for boundary,index in boundaries {
            edge := vsub(boundary.segment.b,boundary.segment.a)
            length := vlen(edge)
            normal := Vec2{-edge.y/length,edge.x/length}
            amplitude := min(length*0.04,min(polygon_area(children[boundary.a]),polygon_area(children[boundary.b]))/length*0.08)
            base := vmul(vadd(boundary.segment.a,boundary.segment.b),0.5)
            // The area cap alone can cross another edge in thin or concave children.
            // Bound displacement by clearance, as in the reference partition generator.
            neighbors := [2]int{boundary.a,boundary.b}
            for index in neighbors {
                polygon := children[index]
                for a,i in polygon.points {
                    b := polygon.points[(i+1)%len(polygon.points)]
                    edge := vsub(b,a)
                    if vdot(edge,edge)<0.000000000001 { continue }
                    if _,shared := segment_overlap(Segment{a,b},boundary.segment); shared { continue }
                    t := clamp(vdot(vsub(base,a),edge)/vdot(edge,edge),f32(0),f32(1))
                    amplitude=min(amplitude,vlen(vsub(base,vadd(a,vmul(edge,t))))*0.2)
                }
            }
            if derive_seed(seed,u64(index+1))%2 == 0 { amplitude = -amplitude }
            mid := vadd(base,vmul(normal,amplitude))
            insert_shared_midpoint(&children[boundary.a],boundary.segment,mid)
            insert_shared_midpoint(&children[boundary.b],boundary.segment,mid)
        }
    }
    
    // Merge adjacent triangles whenever their union is convex. In particular this
    // avoids feeding thin ears from a displaced boundary to Box2D as tiny fixtures.
    convex_decomposition :: proc(outline: Polygon) -> [dynamic]Polygon {
        parts:=triangulate_polygon(outline)
        for {
            merged:=false
            for i in 0..<len(parts) {
                for j in i+1..<len(parts) {
                    if length,_:=shared_boundary(parts[i],parts[j]); length<=0 { continue }
                    points: [dynamic]Vec2
                    for point in parts[i].points { append(&points,point) }
                    for point in parts[j].points { append(&points,point) }
                    hull:=convex_hull(points[:]); delete(points)
                    combined:=make_polygon(hull[:]); delete(hull)
                    error:=math.abs(polygon_area(combined)-polygon_area(parts[i])-polygon_area(parts[j]))
                    if len(combined.points)<=8 && error<0.000001 {
                        delete(parts[i].points); delete(parts[j].points)
                        parts[i]=combined; ordered_remove(&parts,j); merged=true; break
                    }
                    delete(combined.points)
                }
                if merged { break }
            }
            if !merged { break }
        }
        return parts
    }
