    rebuild_piece :: proc(s: ^Scene, old_id: u64) {
        old_row, ok := s.piece_rows[old_id]
        if !ok || !s.pieces[old_row].live { return }
        material := s.pieces[old_row].material
        groups: [dynamic][dynamic]u64
        visited := make(map[u64]bool)
        adjacency:=make(map[u64][dynamic]u64)
        defer delete(visited)
        defer { for _,neighbors in adjacency { delete(neighbors) }; delete(adjacency) }
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            a,b:=s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]],s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
            if !a.live || !b.live || a.owner!=old_id || b.owner!=old_id { continue }
            left,right:=adjacency[c.a],adjacency[c.b]
            append(&left,c.b); append(&right,c.a)
            adjacency[c.a]=left; adjacency[c.b]=right
        }
        defer {
            for group in groups { delete(group) }
            delete(groups)
        }
        // Find the lowest unvisited ID each time, independent of storage order.
        for {
            start := u64(0)
            for sub in s.subdivisions {
                if sub.live && sub.owner == old_id && !visited[sub.id] && (start == 0 || sub.id < start) { start = sub.id }
            }
            if start == 0 { break }
            group: [dynamic]u64
            queue := [dynamic]u64{start}
            visited[start] = true
            for head := 0; head < len(queue); head += 1 {
                id := queue[head]
                append(&group,id)
                neighbors:=adjacency[id]
                for other in neighbors {
                    if !visited[other] {
                        visited[other] = true; append(&queue,other)
                    }
                }
            }
            delete(queue)
            sort_ids(group[:])
            append(&groups,group)
        }
        s.pieces[old_row].live = false
        for group in groups {
            if piece_width(s,group[:]) < s.minimum_width {
                for id in group {
                    row := s.sub_rows[id]
                    append(&s.remnants,Remnant{subdivision=id,pose=s.subdivisions[row].pose})
                    s.subdivisions[row].live = false
                }
                continue
            }
            // Subdivision contexts belong to their geometry, never allocation-order
            // IDs or a later ownership change. Keep a representative piece context.
            seed: u8
            for id in group { if child_seed := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[id]].seed; child_seed != 0 { seed=child_seed; break } }
    package main
    
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:math"
    
    Physics :: struct {
        world: b2.WorldId,
        bodies: map[u64]b2.BodyId,
        joints: map[u64]b2.JointId,
        fixture_counts: map[u64]int,
        active: bool,
    }
    Interaction :: struct { force: Vec2, torque: f32 }
    REFERENCE_LENGTH :: f32(1)
    PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS :: 4
    GLOBAL_DAMPING :: f32(0.7)
    
    to_b2 :: proc(v: Vec2) -> b2.Vec2 { return {v.x,v.y} }
    from_b2 :: proc(v: b2.Vec2) -> Vec2 { return {v.x,v.y} }
    interaction_load :: proc(i: Interaction) -> f32 {
        return max(vlen(i.force),math.abs(i.torque)/REFERENCE_LENGTH)
    }
    equivalent_force :: proc(impulse: Vec2, interval: f32) -> Vec2 {
        assert(interval > 0)
        return vmul(impulse,1/interval)
    }
    physics_init :: proc(s: ^Scene, gravity: Vec2 = {}) {
        assert(!s.physics.active)
        def := b2.DefaultWorldDef()
        def.gravity = to_b2(gravity)
        s.physics = Physics{world=b2.CreateWorld(def),bodies=make(map[u64]b2.BodyId),joints=make(map[u64]b2.JointId),fixture_counts=make(map[u64]int),active=true}
        physics_sync_structure(s)
    }
    physics_destroy :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        if !s.physics.active { return }
        b2.DestroyWorld(s.physics.world)
        delete(s.physics.bodies); delete(s.physics.joints); delete(s.physics.fixture_counts)
        s.physics = {}
    }
    physics_read_motion :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        if !s.physics.active { return }
        for id,body in s.physics.bodies {
            row := s.sub_rows[id]
            rotation := b2.Body_GetRotation(body)
            s.subdivisions[row].pose = Pose{
                position=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(body)),angle=math.atan2(rotation.s,rotation.c),
                velocity=from_b2(b2.Body_GetLinearVelocity(body)),angular_velocity=b2.Body_GetAngularVelocity(body),
            }
        }
    }
    physics_create_fixture :: proc(s: ^Scene, body: b2.BodyId, sub: Subdivision, outline: Polygon) -> bool {
        points: [dynamic]b2.Vec2
        defer delete(points)
        for point in outline.points { append(&points,to_b2(vsub(point,sub.rest_center))) }
        hull := b2.ComputeHull(points[:])
        // Hull welding can collapse a thin ear below Box2D's collision tolerance.
        if hull.count < 3 { return false }
        polygon := b2.MakePolygon(hull,0)
        def := b2.DefaultShapeDef()
        def.density = 1
        _ = b2.CreatePolygonShape(body,def,polygon)
        s.physics.fixture_counts[sub.id] += 1
        return true
    }
    physics_finish_mass :: proc(s: ^Scene,body: b2.BodyId,sub: Subdivision) {
        if s.physics.fixture_counts[sub.id]==0 {
            // A microscopic attached subdivision is still one live logical entity.
            // Use a bounding fixture when the engine cannot resolve any of its ears.
            lo,hi:=Vec2{1e30,1e30},Vec2{-1e30,-1e30}
            for rest in sub.outline.points { p:=vsub(rest,sub.rest_center); lo={min(lo.x,p.x),min(lo.y,p.y)}; hi={max(hi.x,p.x),max(hi.y,p.y)} }
            polygon:=b2.MakeOffsetBox(max(f32(0.0025),(hi.x-lo.x)*0.5),max(f32(0.0025),(hi.y-lo.y)*0.5),to_b2(vmul(vadd(lo,hi),0.5)),b2.MakeRot(0))
            def:=b2.DefaultShapeDef(); def.density=1
            _ = b2.CreatePolygonShape(body,def,polygon)
            s.physics.fixture_counts[sub.id]=1
        }
        // Keep mass and the body origin tied to the exact logical polygon, including
        // when Box2D simplifies a fixture. This also makes rotational inheritance exact.
        inertia: f32
        for i in 0..<len(sub.outline.points) {
            a,b:=vsub(sub.outline.points[i],sub.rest_center),vsub(sub.outline.points[(i+1)%len(sub.outline.points)],sub.rest_center)
            inertia+=vcross(a,b)*(vdot(a,a)+vdot(a,b)+vdot(b,b))/12
        }
        b2.Body_SetMassData(body,b2.MassData{mass=polygon_area(sub.outline),center={},rotationalInertia=math.abs(inertia)})
        b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(body,to_b2(sub.pose.velocity))
        b2.Body_SetAngularVelocity(body,sub.pose.angular_velocity)
    }
    // This runs only between World_Step calls. Existing handles survive ownership changes.
    physics_sync_structure :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        if !s.physics.active { return }
        dead_joints: [dynamic]u64
        dead_bodies: [dynamic]u64
        defer delete(dead_joints); defer delete(dead_bodies)
        for id,joint in s.physics.joints {
            row,ok := s.conn_rows[id]
            if !ok || !s.connections[row].live { b2.DestroyJoint(joint); append(&dead_joints,id) }
        }
        for id in dead_joints { delete_key(&s.physics.joints,id) }
        for id,body in s.physics.bodies {
            row,ok := s.sub_rows[id]
            if !ok || !s.subdivisions[row].live { b2.DestroyBody(body); append(&dead_bodies,id) }
        }
        for id in dead_bodies { delete_key(&s.physics.bodies,id); delete_key(&s.physics.fixture_counts,id) }
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            if _,exists := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]; exists { continue }
            def := b2.DefaultBodyDef()
            def.type = .dynamicBody
            def.position = to_b2(sub.pose.position)
            def.rotation = b2.MakeRot(sub.pose.angle)
            def.linearVelocity = to_b2(sub.pose.velocity)
            def.angularVelocity = sub.pose.angular_velocity
            body := b2.CreateBody(s.physics.world,def)
            s.physics.bodies[sub.id] = body
            if is_convex(sub.outline) && len(sub.outline.points) <= 8 {
                physics_create_fixture(s,body,sub,sub.outline)
            } else {
                triangles := convex_decomposition(sub.outline)
                for triangle in triangles { physics_create_fixture(s,body,sub,triangle); delete(triangle.points) }
                delete(triangles)
            }
            physics_finish_mass(s,body,sub)
        }
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            if _,exists := s.physics.joints[c.id]; exists { continue }
            a := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]]
            b := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
            def := b2.DefaultWeldJointDef()
            def.bodyIdA = s.physics.bodies[c.a]
            def.bodyIdB = s.physics.bodies[c.b]
            def.localAnchorA = to_b2(c.local_a)
            def.localAnchorB = to_b2(c.local_b)
            // All outlines share one undeformed frame. Its relative rest angle is zero.
            def.referenceAngle = 0
            flexibility := max(s.materials[a.material].flexibility,s.materials[b.material].flexibility)
            if flexibility > 0 {
                def.linearHertz = 1/max(flexibility,0.01)
                def.angularHertz = def.linearHertz
            }
            def.linearDampingRatio = GLOBAL_DAMPING
            def.angularDampingRatio = GLOBAL_DAMPING
            s.physics.joints[c.id] = b2.CreateWeldJoint(s.physics.world,def)
        }
    }
    apply_blast_motion :: proc(s: ^Scene, sub: ^Subdivision, direction: Vec2, load: f32) {
        delta_v := vmul(direction,load*BLAST_IMPULSE_SCALE)
        if s.physics.active {
            body := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]
            impulse := vmul(delta_v,b2.Body_GetMass(body))
            b2.Body_ApplyLinearImpulseToCenter(body,to_b2(impulse),true)
            sub.pose.velocity = from_b2(b2.Body_GetLinearVelocity(body))
        } else {
            sub.pose.velocity = vadd(sub.pose.velocity,delta_v)
        }
    }
    // Contact points and fixtures against the same other body form one interaction.
    // Joint reactions are already forces; totalNormalImpulse covers the full tick.
    // Box2D's tangent/rolling impulses cover the final substep in this binding version.
    calculate_physics_loads :: proc(s: ^Scene, dt: f32) -> Failures {
        assert(dt > 0)
        failures := Failures{}
        loads := make(map[u64]f32)
        defer delete(loads)
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            body := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]
            capacity := int(b2.Body_GetContactCapacity(body))
            buffer := make([]b2.ContactData,capacity)
            contacts := b2.Body_GetContactData(body,buffer)
            interactions := make(map[b2.BodyId]Interaction)
            for contact in contacts {
                body_a,body_b := b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdA),b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdB)
                other := body_b
                sign := f32(-1)
                if body_b == body { other=body_a; sign=1 }
                normal := from_b2(contact.manifold.normal)
                tangent := Vec2{normal.y,-normal.x}
                interaction := interactions[other]
                for k in 0..<int(contact.manifold.pointCount) {
                    point := contact.manifold.points[k]
                    force := vadd(equivalent_force(vmul(normal,point.totalNormalImpulse*sign),dt),equivalent_force(vmul(tangent,point.tangentImpulse*sign),dt/f32(PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS)))
                    interaction.force = vadd(interaction.force,force)
                    interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(from_b2(point.point),sub.pose.position),force)
                }

    # Odin destruction sandbox
    
    A standalone implementation of `destruction-model-implementation-plan.md` and `playable-sandbox-ux-plan.md`, using Odin's bundled Box2D, raylib and raygui libraries. The default application is a small playable destruction yard. The original diagnostic lab and localhost snapshot transport remain available.
    
    ## Run
    
    Requires an Odin installation with compiled `vendor:box2d` and `vendor:raylib` libraries. Tested on Windows with Odin `dev-2026-05-nightly:ea5175d`.
    
    ```powershell
    odin run .
    odin test . -out:BOM-tests.exe
    odin build . -o:speed -out:BOM.exe
    ```
    
    The application opens into a fixed side-view yard with a floor, an invulnerable capsule player and a destructible stepped tower. Walk, jump onto or push debris, aim outside a solid shape and click to blast. Ordinary gravity runs at a fixed 60 Hz with four Box2D substeps. The camera keeps the yard framed when the window resizes. Falling outside the yard returns the player to spawn.
    
    | Control | Action |
    | --- | --- |
    | A / D or left / right arrows | Move |
    | Space | Jump, with a 0.1 second jump buffer and coyote window |
    | Left click in the world | One blast at a valid cursor position |
    | Mouse wheel over the world | Adjust blast radius and power |
    | R / Reset button | Restore the same applied setup and seed |
    | Tab / Escape / Settings button | Open settings and pause; close to resume |
    | F3 | Toggle IDs, connections, counts and inspection tools |
    
    The aiming circle shows the active blast radius. A red cross and message mark origins inside or on live logical outlines; those blasts are suppressed. UI clicks do not blast the world. The settings panel pauses physics, fading and player actions without accumulating simulation time.
    
    In Settings, switch **Manual blasts / Falling bombs** to choose the explosion source immediately, without resetting the yard. Falling bombs spawn at random horizontal positions across the yard every 1â€“2.5 seconds. Each is an ordinary circle body that collides with the floor, debris and player. Its one-second fuse starts on first landing on a supporting surface, including the tower; airborne time and side contacts do not start the fuse. A red countdown ring marks a lit fuse. The body disappears when it explodes at its current position, using the current blast radius, with a brief expanding flash. Manual placement and its aiming circle are disabled in this mode. Returning to Manual clears pending bombs. Settings pauses drops, fuses and flashes along with physics. Reset clears bombs and repeats the applied seed's drop sequence, independently of destruction generation.
    
    Mode and radius changes are immediate, including inside settings. Breakup pattern, fragment strength, connection strength, flexibility and Generate children are staged until **Apply & Reset**. Resume keeps the previously applied setup. Strength and flexibility stay independent of Chunk / Splinter / Shatter. The initial setup uses manual blasts, seed 42, strengths 30 / 24, flexibility 0 (stiff welds) and radius 5.0. Positive flexibility remains available in Settings. Turning Generate children off uses seed zero; geometry stays live until it fails.
    
    With F3 enabled: right click selects, Delete or Ctrl+click directly removes a region, Shift+click or X near an anchor breaks a connection, J toggles links, V toggles the cosmetic surface, and S saves `snapshot.json`. D and Space retain movement and jump in inspection mode.
    
    Run `odin run . -- --lab` for the original zero-gravity diagnostic fixture and its legacy shortcuts (projectile I, presets 1/2/3, terminal T, pause/step Space/N, radius Q/E, pan/zoom, and snapshot save/load S/L). The existing sender and receiver use that diagnostic fixture; player and floor replication are outside this local milestone.
    
    For automated execution:
    
    ```powershell
    odin run . -- --headless
    odin run . -- --smoke
    odin run . -- --smoke-settings
    odin run . -- --smoke-input
    ```
    
    `--headless` evaluates the original diagnostic blast, runs 60 physics ticks, validates the graph, writes `snapshot.json`, and reconstructs a receiver. `--smoke` renders the yard in a hidden window to `sandbox-preview.png`. `--smoke-settings` renders the expanded paused panel to `sandbox-settings-preview.png`. Both exit after two frames.
    
    `--smoke-input` uses raylib's native automation events in a hidden window to exercise the actual keyboard bindings and raygui widgets: movement, holding jump through landing, paused settings, closing a slider drag with Escape, immediate radius updates, staged pattern/generation changes, Apply & Reset, the first subsequent blast click, inspection, R reset, switching into Falling bombs, automatic spawning, landing, detonation and switching back to manual placement. It asserts the results and exports `sandbox-playthrough.png` and `sandbox-bombs-preview.png`. The normal behavior suite stays independent of a window or display.
    
    ## Live transmission
    
    Build once, then run these in separate terminals:
    
    ```powershell
    .\BOM.exe --serve
    .\BOM.exe --receive
    ```
    
    The sender listens on **127.0.0.1:9901** for one receiver. It sends explicit complete snapshots after structural changes and at 10 Hz for motion. The receiver renders polygons, connections, ownership and interpolated motion without simulating physics. Destroy or split the wall in the sender to see the receiver update.
    
    Frames contain a four byte little endian payload length followed by UTF-8 JSON, capped at 4 MiB. Partial reads, partial writes, coalesced frames and disconnects are handled. One in-flight send is retained; the sender does not accumulate a queue of old states. `read_state`, `encode_snapshot` and `decode_snapshot` can also be used with another transport.
    
    Snapshots carry current geometry, materials, stable IDs, piece memberships, future generation seeds, structural revision, and body motion. Version 2 retains each subdivision's birth seed context; version 1 snapshots still load using their original piece contexts. Widths and anchors are derived from the transmitted outlines. Infinite strengths have explicit flags so snapshots remain valid JSON. Seeds never reconstruct existing damaged geometry.

    +// A blast near the end of a huge rectangle can miss its centre. Refine only
    +// floor outlines whose edge reaches failure load while their centre survives.
    +// Each step preserves the existing geometry, contexts and inherited attachments;
    +// blast_pass then resolves actual damage before creating final physics bodies.
    +sandbox_refine_ground :: proc(s: ^Scene,blast: Blast) {
    +	for {
    +		failures:=Failures{}
    +		for sub in s.subdivisions {
    +			if !sub.live || sub.rest_center.y>=0 || sub.seed==0 || sub.width<=s.minimum_width { continue }
    +			strength:=s.materials[sub.material].subdivision_strength
    +			if fails(blast_load(vlen(vsub(sub.pose.position,blast.position)),blast.radius),strength) { continue }
    +			distance:=f32(1e30)
    +			if point_in_subdivision(sub,blast.position) { distance=0 }
    +			else {
    +				for rest,i in sub.outline.points {
    +					a,b:=posed_point(sub,rest),posed_point(sub,sub.outline.points[(i+1)%len(sub.outline.points)])
    +					edge:=vsub(b,a); squared:=vdot(edge,edge)
    +					if squared<=0 { continue }
    +					t:=clamp(vdot(vsub(blast.position,a),edge)/squared,f32(0),f32(1))
    +					distance=min(distance,vlen(vsub(blast.position,vadd(a,vmul(edge,t)))))
    +				}
    +			}
    +			if fails(blast_load(distance,blast.radius),strength) { append(&failures.subdivisions,sub.id) }
    +		}
    +		if len(failures.subdivisions)==0 { break }
    +		apply_failures(s,failures)
    +		delete(failures.subdivisions)
    +	}
    +}

    package main
    
    import "core:math"
    import "core:sync"
    import "core:testing"
    
    // Independent double-precision area and triangle intersection checks catch
    // compensating gaps/overlaps that a sum of the generator's f32 areas can miss.
    Partition_Point :: struct { x,y: f64 }
    partition_area :: proc(points: []Vec2) -> f64 {
        area: f64
        for p,i in points {
            q:=points[(i+1)%len(points)]
            area+=(f64(p.x)-f64(points[0].x))*(f64(q.y)-f64(points[0].y))-(f64(p.y)-f64(points[0].y))*(f64(q.x)-f64(points[0].x))
        }
        return math.abs(area)*0.5
    }
    partition_side :: proc(a,b,p: Partition_Point) -> f64 { return (b.x-a.x)*(p.y-a.y)-(b.y-a.y)*(p.x-a.x) }
    partition_triangle_overlap :: proc(a,b: Polygon) -> f64 {
        points: [12]Partition_Point
        for p,i in a.points { points[i]={f64(p.x),f64(p.y)} }
        count:=len(a.points)
        clip: [3]Partition_Point
        for p,i in b.points { clip[i]={f64(p.x),f64(p.y)} }
        orientation:=f64(1)
        if partition_side(clip[0],clip[1],clip[2])<0 { orientation=-1 }
        for edge in 0..<3 {
            next: [12]Partition_Point
            next_count:=0
            for i in 0..<count {
                p,q:=points[i],points[(i+1)%count]
                ps:=orientation*partition_side(clip[edge],clip[(edge+1)%3],p)
                qs:=orientation*partition_side(clip[edge],clip[(edge+1)%3],q)
                if ps>=0 { next[next_count]=p; next_count+=1 }
                if (ps>=0)!=(qs>=0) {
                    fraction:=ps/(ps-qs)
                    next[next_count]={p.x+(q.x-p.x)*fraction,p.y+(q.y-p.y)*fraction}; next_count+=1
                }
            }
            points=next; count=next_count
        }
        area: f64
        for i in 0..<count { area+=partition_side(points[0],points[i],points[(i+1)%count]) }
        return math.abs(area)*0.5
    }
    expect_generation_partition :: proc(t: ^testing.T,parent: Polygon,children: []Polygon) {
        testing.expect(t,len(children)>=2)
        parent_area:=partition_area(parent.points)
        tolerance:=max(f64(0.00000005),parent_area*0.00005)
        parent_triangles:=triangulate_polygon(parent)
        defer { for triangle in parent_triangles { delete(triangle.points) }; delete(parent_triangles) }
        triangles: [dynamic][dynamic]Polygon
        defer { for batch in triangles { for triangle in batch { delete(triangle.points) }; delete(batch) }; delete(triangles) }
        area: f64
        for child in children {
            child_area:=partition_area(child.points)
            area+=child_area
            testing.expect(t,child_area>0 && child_area<parent_area)
            parts:=triangulate_polygon(child)
            inside: f64

        for i in 0..<len(triangles) {

                for a in triangles[i] { for b in triangles[j] { overlap+=partition_triangle_overlap(a,b) } }
                testing.expect(t,overlap<=tolerance,"Sibling interiors must not overlap")

        }
        // Each child edge must be covered by the parent boundary or an exact sibling
        // seam. T junctions may split one side into several collinear segments.
        for child,i in children {
            perimeter,covered:=f32(0),f32(0)
            for p,k in child.points { perimeter+=vlen(vsub(child.points[(k+1)%len(child.points)],p)) }
            segments:=shared_segments(child,parent)
            for segment in segments { covered+=vlen(vsub(segment.b,segment.a)) }; delete(segments)
            for other,j in children {
                if i==j { continue }
                seams:=shared_segments(child,other)
                for seam in seams { covered+=vlen(vsub(seam.b,seam.a)) }; delete(seams)
            }
            testing.expect(t,math.abs(covered-perimeter)<0.0001,"Every generated edge must retain a matching shared boundary")
        }
    }

    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:math"
    
    Player_Tuning :: struct {
        speed, acceleration, jump_speed, coyote_time, jump_buffer: f32,
    }
    PLAYER_TUNING :: Player_Tuning{4,32,6.3,0.1,0.1}
    PLAYER_RADIUS :: f32(0.26)
    PLAYER_SEGMENT :: f32(0.30)
    PLAYER_HALF_HEIGHT :: PLAYER_RADIUS+PLAYER_SEGMENT
    PLAYER_SPAWN :: Vec2{-4.5,0.65}
    
    // The player is an ordinary body in the shared world, outside the destruction graph.
    Player :: struct {
        body: b2.BodyId,
        grounded: bool,
        coyote, buffered_jump: f32,
        support_velocity: Vec2,
    }
    player_create :: proc(world: b2.WorldId) -> Player {
        def:=b2.DefaultBodyDef()
        def.type=.dynamicBody
        def.position=to_b2(PLAYER_SPAWN)
        def.fixedRotation=true
        def.enableSleep=false
        body:=b2.CreateBody(world,def)
        shape:=b2.DefaultShapeDef()
        shape.density=0.65
        shape.material.friction=0.15
        _ = b2.CreateCapsuleShape(body,shape,b2.Capsule{center1={0,-PLAYER_SEGMENT},center2={0,PLAYER_SEGMENT},radius=PLAYER_RADIUS})
        return Player{body=body}
    }
    player_respawn :: proc(player: ^Player) {
        body:=player.body
        b2.Body_SetTransform(body,to_b2(PLAYER_SPAWN),b2.MakeRot(0))
        b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(body,{})
        b2.Body_SetAngularVelocity(body,0)
        player^=Player{body=body}
    }
    player_clear_input :: proc(player: ^Player) {
    }
    bomb_rain_clear :: proc(rain: ^Bomb_Rain) {
        for bomb in rain.bombs { b2.DestroyBody(bomb.body) }
        clear(&rain.bombs); clear(&rain.bursts)
    }
    sandbox_set_blast_mode :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,mode: Blast_Mode) {
        if mode==game.applied.blast_mode { return }
        game.applied.blast_mode=mode
        game.draft.blast_mode=mode
        bomb_rain_clear(&game.bomb_rain)
        game.bomb_rain.until_drop=bomb_drop_delay(&game.bomb_rain)
        if mode==.Falling_Bombs { sandbox_notice(game,"Falling bombs: one-second fuse after landing") }
        else { sandbox_notice(game,"Manual blast placement") }
    }
    bomb_spawn :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,position: Vec2) {
        def:=b2.DefaultBodyDef()
        def.type=.dynamicBody
        def.position=to_b2(position)
        def.isBullet=true
        body:=b2.CreateBody(game.scene.physics.world,def)
        shape:=b2.DefaultShapeDef()
        shape.density=0.4
        shape.material.friction=0.7
        shape.material.restitution=0.05
        _ = b2.CreateCircleShape(body,shape,b2.Circle{radius=BOMB_RADIUS})
        append(&game.bomb_rain.bombs,Bomb{body=body,previous=position,fuse=BOMB_FUSE})
    }
    bomb_has_landed :: proc(bomb: Bomb) -> bool {
        position:=b2.Body_GetPosition(bomb.body)
        buffer:=make([]b2.ContactData,int(b2.Body_GetContactCapacity(bomb.body)))
        defer delete(buffer)
        for contact in b2.Body_GetContactData(bomb.body,buffer) {
            normal:=from_b2(contact.manifold.normal)
            if b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdA)==bomb.body { normal=vmul(normal,-1) }
            if normal.y<0.55 { continue }
            for i in 0..<int(contact.manifold.pointCount) {
                point:=contact.manifold.points[i]
                if point.separation<=0.025 && point.point.y<position.y { return true }
            }
        }
        return false
    }

        rain:=&game.bomb_rain

    ground_descendants_release_when_they_lose_the_support_edge :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
    	sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
    	s:=new_scene(0.1); defer scene_destroy(&s)
    	recipe:=material_preset(0)
    	recipe.subdivision_strength=math.inf_f32(1); recipe.connection_strength=math.inf_f32(1)
    	material:=add_material(&s,recipe)
    	owner:=add_piece(&s,material,42)
    	points:=[4]Vec2{{-1,-1},{1,-1},{1,1},{-1,1}}
    	outline:=Polygon{points=points[:]}
    	root:=add_subdivision(&s,owner,outline,Pose{position=centroid(outline)})
    	append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].subdivisions,root)
    	physics_init(&s,{0,-9.8},-1)
    	testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetType(s.physics.bodies[root])==.staticBody)
    	failures:=Failures{}; append(&failures.subdivisions,root)
    	apply_failures(&s,failures); free_failures(&failures)
    	physics_sync_structure(&s)
    	anchored,loose:=0,u64(0)
    	for sub in s.subdivisions {
    		if !sub.live { continue }
    		if b2.Body_GetType(s.physics.bodies[sub.id])==.staticBody { anchored+=1 }
    		else { loose=sub.id }
    	}
    	testing.expect(t,anchored>=1 && loose!=0,"Cuts must leave both anchored ground and ordinary movable debris")
    	for c in s.connections { if c.live && (c.a==loose || c.b==loose) { append(&failures.connections,c.id) } }
    	apply_failures(&s,failures); free_failures(&failures)
    	physics_sync_structure(&s)
    	body:=s.physics.bodies[loose]
    	before:=b2.Body_GetPosition(body)
    	b2.Body_ApplyLinearImpulseToCenter(body,{0,2},true)
    	physics_tick(&s,1.0/60.0)
    	testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetPosition(body).y>before.y,"Detached ground must respond to impulses through the ordinary solver")
    	expect_valid(t,&s)
    }

    sandbox_valid_aim :: proc(s: ^Scene,point: Vec2) -> bool {
        for sub in s.subdivisions { if sub.live && point_in_subdivision(sub,point) { return false } }
        return true
    }
    sandbox_blast :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,point: Vec2) -> bool {
        if game.panel_open || game.applied.blast_mode!=.Manual { return false }
        if !sandbox_valid_aim(&game.scene,point) { sandbox_notice(game,"Aim outside the solid shape"); return false }
        sandbox_explode(game,point)
        return true
    }
    sandbox_explode :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,point: Vec2) {
        blast:=Blast{position=point,radius=game.applied.blast_radius}
        physics_read_motion(&game.scene)
        revision:=game.scene.revision
        refined:=sandbox_refine_ground(&game.scene,blast)
        blast_pass(&game.scene,blast)
        if refined && game.scene.revision==revision { game.scene.revision+=1 }
        clear(&game.previous)
    }
    
    // A blast near the end of a huge rectangle can miss its centre. Refine only
    // floor outlines whose edge reaches failure load while their centre survives.
    // Each step preserves the existing geometry, contexts and inherited attachments;
    // blast_pass then resolves actual damage before creating final physics bodies.
    sandbox_refine_ground :: proc(s: ^Scene,blast: Blast) -> bool {
        affected:=make(map[u64]bool)
        defer delete(affected)
        changed:=false
        for {
            failures:=Failures{}
            for sub in s.subdivisions {
                if !sub.live || sub.rest_center.y>=0 || sub.seed==0 || sub.width<=s.minimum_width { continue }
                strength:=s.materials[sub.material].subdivision_strength
                if fails(blast_load(vlen(vsub(sub.pose.position,blast.position)),blast.radius),strength) { continue }
                distance:=f32(1e30)
                if point_in_subdivision(sub,blast.position) { distance=0 }
                else {
                    for rest,i in sub.outline.points {
                        a,b:=posed_point(sub,rest),posed_point(sub,sub.outline.points[(i+1)%len(sub.outline.points)])
                        edge:=vsub(b,a); squared:=vdot(edge,edge)
                        if squared<=0 { continue }
                        t:=clamp(vdot(vsub(blast.position,a),edge)/squared,f32(0),f32(1))
                        distance=min(distance,vlen(vsub(blast.position,vadd(a,vmul(edge,t)))))
                    }
                }
                if fails(blast_load(distance,blast.radius),strength) { append(&failures.subdivisions,sub.id) }
            }
            if len(failures.subdivisions)==0 { break }
            stage_failures(s,failures,&affected)
            changed=true
            delete(failures.subdivisions)
        }
        if changed { rebuild_affected_pieces(s,affected) }
        return changed
    }

    // This runs only between World_Step calls. Existing handles survive ownership changes.
    physics_sync_structure :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        if !s.physics.active { return }
        anchored:=make(map[u64]bool)
        defer delete(anchored)
        if s.physics.anchor_y>-1e30 {
            for sub in s.subdivisions {
                if !sub.live || anchored[sub.owner] { continue }
                for a,i in sub.outline.points {
                    b:=sub.outline.points[(i+1)%len(sub.outline.points)]
                    if math.abs(a.y-s.physics.anchor_y)<0.00001 && math.abs(b.y-s.physics.anchor_y)<0.00001 && math.abs(a.x-b.x)>0.00001 { anchored[sub.owner]=true; break }
                }
            }
        }
        dead_joints: [dynamic]u64
        dead_bodies: [dynamic]u64
        defer delete(dead_joints); defer delete(dead_bodies)
        for id,joint in s.physics.joints {
            row,ok := s.conn_rows[id]
            if !ok || !s.connections[row].live || anchored[s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[s.connections[row].a]].owner] { b2.DestroyJoint(joint); append(&dead_joints,id) }
        }
        for id in dead_joints { delete_key(&s.physics.joints,id) }
        for id,body in s.physics.bodies {
            row,ok := s.sub_rows[id]
            if !ok || !s.subdivisions[row].live { b2.DestroyBody(body); append(&dead_bodies,id) }
        }
        for id in dead_bodies { delete_key(&s.physics.bodies,id); delete_key(&s.physics.fixture_counts,id) }
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            type:=b2.BodyType.dynamicBody
            if anchored[sub.owner] { type=.staticBody }
            if body,exists := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]; exists {
                if b2.Body_GetType(body)!=type {
                    b2.Body_SetType(body,type)
                    if type==.dynamicBody { physics_finish_mass(s,body,sub) }
                }
                continue
            }
            def := b2.DefaultBodyDef()
            // Refining a supported piece must not change its behaviour under gravity.
            // Once its connection to a support edge breaks, its bodies become dynamic.
            def.type = type
            def.position = to_b2(sub.pose.position)
            def.rotation = b2.MakeRot(sub.pose.angle)
            def.linearVelocity = to_b2(sub.pose.velocity)
            def.angularVelocity = sub.pose.angular_velocity
            body := b2.CreateBody(s.physics.world,def)
            s.physics.bodies[sub.id] = body
            if is_convex(sub.outline) && len(sub.outline.points) <= 8 {
                physics_create_fixture(s,body,sub,sub.outline)
            } else {
                triangles := convex_decomposition(sub.outline)
                for triangle in triangles { physics_create_fixture(s,body,sub,triangle); delete(triangle.points) }
                delete(triangles)
            }
            physics_finish_mass(s,body,sub)
        }
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            if _,exists := s.physics.joints[c.id]; exists { continue }
            a := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]]
            b := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
            def := b2.DefaultWeldJointDef()
            def.bodyIdA = s.physics.bodies[c.a]
            def.bodyIdB = s.physics.bodies[c.b]
            // Their logical attachment still participates in blasts; two anchored
            // regions need no solver constraint between them.
            if b2.Body_GetType(def.bodyIdA)==.staticBody && b2.Body_GetType(def.bodyIdB)==.staticBody { continue }
            def.localAnchorA = to_b2(c.local_a)
            def.localAnchorB = to_b2(c.local_b)
            // All outlines share one undeformed frame. Its relative rest angle is zero.
            def.referenceAngle = 0
            flexibility := max(s.materials[a.material].flexibility,s.materials[b.material].flexibility)
            if flexibility > 0 {
                def.linearHertz = 1/max(flexibility,0.01)
                def.angularHertz = def.linearHertz
            }
            def.linearDampingRatio = GLOBAL_DAMPING
            def.angularDampingRatio = GLOBAL_DAMPING
            s.physics.joints[c.id] = b2.CreateWeldJoint(s.physics.world,def)
        }
    }

        for row in 0..<3 {
            for column in 0..<4-row {
                // Start on the floor: the former 5 mm drop overloaded stiff joints on landing.
                x,y:=f32(1.5)+f32(column)*0.85,f32(row)*0.85
                points:=[4]Vec2{{x,y},{x+0.85,y},{x+0.85,y+0.85},{x,y+0.85}}
                outline:=Polygon{points=points[:]}
                id:=add_subdivision(s,owner,outline,Pose{position=centroid(outline)})
                // Stable block coordinates give neighboring roots distinct birth contexts.
                s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[id]].seed=derive_seed(seed,u64(row*4+column+1))
                append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].subdivisions,id)
            }
        }
        for a in 0..<len(s.subdivisions) {
            for b in a+1..<len(s.subdivisions) { add_connection(s,s.subdivisions[a].id,s.subdivisions[b].id) }

        for connection in s.connections { append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].connections,connection.id) }
        // One large root, with future floor detail generated only near a blast.
        ground:=add_piece(s,material,derive_seed(seed,13))
        ground_points:=[4]Vec2{{-8,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM},{9,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM},{9,0},{-8,0}}
        ground_outline:=Polygon{points=ground_points[:]}
        id:=add_subdivision(s,ground,ground_outline,Pose{position=centroid(ground_outline)})
        append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[ground]].subdivisions,id)
        physics_init(s,{0,-9.8},YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM)
        def:=b2.DefaultBodyDef()
        def.position={0.5,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM-YARD_BASE_DEPTH*0.5}
        game.floor=b2.CreateBody(s.physics.world,def)
        shape:=b2.DefaultShapeDef(); shape.material.friction=0.65
        // Extend beyond the playable edges so excavation never opens the screen bottom.
        _ = b2.CreatePolygonShape(game.floor,shape,b2.MakeBox(10,YARD_BASE_DEPTH*0.5))
        game.player=player_create(s.physics.world)
        bomb_rain_reset(&game.bomb_rain,game.applied.seed)
        game.selected=0
        sandbox_clear_input(game)
        sandbox_notice(game,"Yard reset")
    }

    // Inclusive edges are solid too. Use the logical posed outline, not the cosmetic mesh.
    point_in_subdivision :: proc(sub: Subdivision,point: Vec2) -> bool {
        local:=vadd(sub.rest_center,vrotate(vsub(point,sub.pose.position),-sub.pose.angle))
        inside:=false
        for a,i in sub.outline.points {
            b:=sub.outline.points[(i+1)%len(sub.outline.points)]
            edge:=vsub(b,a); relative:=vsub(local,a)
            if math.abs(vcross(edge,relative))<0.00001 && vdot(relative,edge)>=0 && vdot(relative,edge)<=vdot(edge,edge) { return true }
            if (a.y>local.y)!=(b.y>local.y) && local.x<(b.x-a.x)*(local.y-a.y)/(b.y-a.y)+a.x { inside=!inside }
        }
        return inside
    }
    sandbox_valid_aim :: proc(s: ^Scene,point: Vec2) -> bool {
        for sub in s.subdivisions { if sub.live && point_in_subdivision(sub,point) { return false } }
        return true
    }
    sandbox_blast :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,point: Vec2) -> bool {
        if game.panel_open || game.applied.blast_mode!=.Manual { return false }
        if !sandbox_valid_aim(&game.scene,point) { sandbox_notice(game,"Aim outside the solid shape"); return false }
        sandbox_explode(game,point)
        return true
    }
    sandbox_explode :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,point: Vec2) {
        blast:=Blast{position=point,radius=game.applied.blast_radius}
        physics_read_motion(&game.scene)
        revision:=game.scene.revision
        refined:=sandbox_refine_ground(&game.scene,blast)
        blast_pass(&game.scene,blast)
        if refined && game.scene.revision==revision { game.scene.revision+=1 }
        clear(&game.previous)
    }
    
    // A blast near the end of a huge rectangle can miss its centre. Refine only
    // floor outlines whose edge reaches failure load while their centre survives.
    // Each step preserves the existing geometry, contexts and inherited attachments;
    // blast_pass then resolves actual damage before creating final physics bodies.
    sandbox_refine_ground :: proc(s: ^Scene,blast: Blast) -> bool {
        affected:=make(map[u64]bool)
        defer delete(affected)
        unrefinable:=make(map[u64]bool)
        defer delete(unrefinable)
        changed:=false
        for {
            failures:=Failures{}
            for sub in s.subdivisions {
                if !sub.live || sub.rest_center.y>=0 || sub.seed==0 || sub.width<=s.minimum_width || unrefinable[sub.id] { continue }
                strength:=s.materials[sub.material].subdivision_strength
                if fails(blast_load(vlen(vsub(sub.pose.position,blast.position)),blast.radius),strength) { continue }
                distance:=f32(1e30)
                if point_in_subdivision(sub,blast.position) { distance=0 }
                else {
                    for rest,i in sub.outline.points {
                        a,b:=posed_point(sub,rest),posed_point(sub,sub.outline.points[(i+1)%len(sub.outline.points)])
                        edge:=vsub(b,a); squared:=vdot(edge,edge)
                        if squared<=0 { continue }
                        t:=clamp(vdot(vsub(blast.position,a),edge)/squared,f32(0),f32(1))
                        distance=min(distance,vlen(vsub(blast.position,vadd(a,vmul(edge,t)))))
                    }
                }
                if fails(blast_load(distance,blast.radius),strength) { append(&failures.subdivisions,sub.id) }
            }
            if len(failures.subdivisions)==0 { break }
            stage_failures(s,failures,&affected,true)
            for id in failures.subdivisions {
                if s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[id]].live { unrefinable[id]=true }
                else { changed=true }
            }
            delete(failures.subdivisions)
        }
        if changed { rebuild_affected_pieces(s,affected) }
        return changed
    }
    
    // Input routing is independent of raylib, so menu consumption has a direct regression check.
    Sandbox_Input :: struct {
        move: f32,
        jump_pressed,jump_down,blast_pressed,blast_down: bool,
        menu_pressed,reset_pressed,inspection_pressed: bool,
        wheel: f32,
    }
    sandbox_route_input :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,raw: Sandbox_Input,over_ui: bool) -> Sandbox_Input {
        if raw.inspection_pressed { game.inspection=!game.inspection }
        if raw.menu_pressed {
            sandbox_set_panel(game,!game.panel_open)
            game.block_jump=raw.jump_down
            game.block_blast=raw.blast_down
            return {}
        }
        if !raw.jump_down { game.block_jump=false }
        if !raw.blast_down { game.block_blast=false }
        if game.panel_open { return {} }
        if raw.reset_pressed {
            sandbox_reset(game)
            game.block_jump=raw.jump_down
            game.block_blast=raw.blast_down
            return {}
        }
        result:=raw
        result.jump_pressed=raw.jump_pressed && !game.block_jump
        result.blast_pressed=raw.blast_pressed && !game.block_blast && !over_ui && game.applied.blast_mode==.Manual
        if over_ui { result.wheel=0 }
        if result.wheel!=0 { sandbox_set_radius(game,game.applied.blast_radius+result.wheel*0.2) }
        return result
    }
    sandbox_tick :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,move: f32,jump: bool,dt: f32 = 1.0/60.0) {
        clear(&game.previous)
        for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { if sub.live { game.previous[sub.id]=sub.pose } }
        game.previous_player=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body))
        bomb_rain_before_step(game,dt)
        player_before_step(&game.player,move,jump,dt)
        physics_tick(&game.scene,dt)
        bomb_rain_after_step(game,dt)
        if player_after_step(&game.player) {
            game.previous_player=PLAYER_SPAWN
            sandbox_notice(game,"Back at spawn")
        }
    }
    sandbox_advance :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,dt: f32,input: Sandbox_Input) {
        if game.panel_open { game.accumulator=0; game.jump_queued=false; return }
        if input.jump_pressed { game.jump_queued=true }
        game.status_time=max(f32(0),game.status_time-dt)
        game.accumulator+=clamp(dt,f32(0),f32(0.1))
        for game.accumulator>=1.0/60.0 {
            sandbox_tick(game,input.move,game.jump_queued)
            game.jump_queued=false
            game.accumulator-=1.0/60.0
        }
    }

    import "core:fmt"
    import "core:os"
    import "core:strings"
    import "core:math"
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    
    review_name: string
    review_output: string
    review_log: strings.Builder
    review_duration := 360
    review_point := Vec2{1,1.3}
    review_radius := f32(5)
    
    main :: proc() {
        assert(len(os.args)==3)
        review_name,review_output=os.args[1],os.args[2]
        switch review_name {
        case "small-r2": review_radius=2
        case "side-r4": review_radius=4
        case "side-r6": review_radius=6
        case "nearby-r5": review_point={1.1,1.3}
        case "rim-r5": review_point={-1.24,0.56}
        case "overhead-r5": review_point={2.75,3.15}
        case "repeat-r5": review_duration=480
        }
        _ = fmt.sbprintf(&review_log,"frame,phase,regions,links,pieces,area,linear_energy,area_times_speed,moving_area,max_speed,max_spin,in_yard_max_speed,mean_rest_displacement\n")
        run_sandbox(true)
        assert(os.write_entire_file(fmt.tprintf("%s/telemetry.csv",review_output),transmute([]byte)strings.to_string(review_log))==nil)
        strings.builder_destroy(&review_log)
        fmt.println("Completed destruction playback:",review_name)
    }
    
    review_create :: proc() -> Sandbox {
        settings:=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS
        settings.blast_radius=review_radius
        return sandbox_create(settings)
    }
    review_before_frame :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,view: View,frame: int) {
        if frame==0 { rl.PlayAutomationEvent(smoke_mouse(30,40)) }
        shots:=[2]int{120,240}
        for at in shots {
            if at==240 && review_name!="repeat-r5" { continue }
            if frame==at {
                aim:=screen_point(view,review_point)
                rl.PlayAutomationEvent(smoke_mouse(i32(aim.x),i32(aim.y)))
            }
            if frame==at+1 { rl.PlayAutomationEvent(smoke_button(true)) }
            if frame==at+4 { rl.PlayAutomationEvent(smoke_button(false)) }
            if frame==at+6 { rl.PlayAutomationEvent(smoke_mouse(30,40)) }
        }
    }
    review_record :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,frame: int,phase: string) {
        a,b,c:=counts_runtime(&game.scene)
        area,linear_energy,weighted_speed,moving_area,max_speed,max_spin,in_yard_max_speed,displacement: f32
        for sub in game.scene.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            mass:=polygon_area(sub.outline)
            speed:=vlen(sub.pose.velocity)
            area+=mass
            linear_energy+=0.5*mass*speed*speed
            weighted_speed+=mass*speed
            if speed>0.2 { moving_area+=mass }
            max_speed=max(max_speed,speed)
            max_spin=max(max_spin,math.abs(sub.pose.angular_velocity))
            if sub.pose.position.x>=-8 && sub.pose.position.x<=9 && sub.pose.position.y>=-1 { in_yard_max_speed=max(in_yard_max_speed,speed) }
            displacement+=mass*vlen(vsub(sub.pose.position,sub.rest_center))
        }
        if area>0 { displacement/=area }
        _ = fmt.sbprintf(&review_log,"%d,%s,%d,%d,%d,%.7f,%.7f,%.7f,%.7f,%.7f,%.7f,%.7f,%.7f\n",frame,phase,a,b,c,area,linear_energy,weighted_speed,moving_area,max_speed,max_spin,in_yard_max_speed,displacement)
    }
    review_before_step :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,frame: int,point: Vec2) {
        if frame==120 {
            review_record(game,frame,"before")
            assert(save_snapshot(&game.scene,fmt.tprintf("%s/before.json",review_output)))
        }
        if frame==121 || (frame==241 && review_name=="repeat-r5") {
            assert(sandbox_valid_aim(&game.scene,point))
            review_record(game,frame,"blast")
            assert(save_snapshot(&game.scene,fmt.tprintf("%s/blast-%d.json",review_output,frame)))
            fmt.printf("%s: blast at (%.4f, %.4f), radius %.1f\n",review_name,point.x,point.y,review_radius)
        }
    }
    review_after_frame :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,target: rl.RenderTexture2D,frame: int) {
        review_record(game,frame,"tick")
        if frame%3==1 {
            image:=rl.LoadImageFromTexture(target.texture)
            rl.ImageFlipVertical(&image)
            rl.ImageResize(&image,960,600)
            assert(rl.ExportImage(image,fmt.ctprintf("%s/frame-%04d.jpg",review_output,(frame-1)/3)))
            rl.UnloadImage(image)
        }
        if frame%30==0 || frame==122 || frame==242 {
            valid,message:=validate_scene(&game.scene)
            assert(valid,message)
            assert(save_snapshot(&game.scene,fmt.tprintf("%s/tick-%04d.json",review_output,frame)))
        }
    }
    Destruction-only verdict: the blast responds immediately and produces readable secondary collisions, but its physical punch is uneven across strengths. High power removes most of the material before it can become moving rubble. Marginal hits can fracture the structure while leaving its silhouette almost unchanged.
    
    This follow-up isolates the explosion system. The player stays at spawn without movement input. Nine native-input playbacks cover 56 seconds of simulation, using the unchanged current Chunk material, seed 42, strengths 30/24, flexibility 0 and impulse scale 0.2. Blasts occur after two seconds of settling. Only radius, placement or the presence of a second shot changes. As in the earlier recordings, the capture build uses the normal 60 Hz physics step and records at 20 fps independently of slow desktop readback. Production gameplay sources and BOM.exe remain unchanged.
    
    The clearest comparison is the same side hit at increasing radius:
    
    | Radius | Material removed immediately | Remaining material moving after 0.1 s | Initial survivor linear kinetic energy |
    | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    | 4 | 5.0% | 6.18 area units | 52.20 |
    | 5 | 49.8% | 3.27 area units | 36.23 |
    | 6 | 83.2% | 1.09 area units | 14.97 |
    
    The original tower has 6.50 area units. â€œMovingâ€ means a subdivision centre exceeds 0.2 units/s. Linear energy is measured immediately after the blast, before the solver runs, in game units; rotational energy is excluded. These figures describe this specific side hit, rather than universal percentages for every blast.
    
    The surviving fragments travel farther as power increases, but there is much less surviving material. In the radius-6 recording, most of the structure disappears in one update and a few pieces move away. The radius-4 hit leaves large chunks to detach, tilt and collide. My judgement from the rendered sequences is that the strongest shot looks cleaner and lighter, despite creating the largest hole. The removed core creates no physical debris under the current rules; the surviving rim carries the impact.
    
    [Animated strength comparison](blast-strength-comparison.gif) Â· [Strength contact sheet](strengths.jpg) Â· [Placement contact sheet](placement.jpg)
    
    Other findings:
    
    - A radius-2 hit removes no material. Within 0.5 s, solver reactions have changed the tower to 13 logical regions and two pieces, but average subdivision displacement is only 0.022 units. New cracks appear while the tower barely moves. That is a weak physical response for a successful fracture event.
    - The more distant radius-5 hit also removes no material. After 0.5 s it has 27 regions in three pieces; the structure shifts about 0.28 units on average and retains its stepped silhouette. This is another case where crack generation is much more obvious than chunk release.
    - An overhead hit removes 28.9% of the material immediately. Downward motion rapidly meets the floor: survivor linear energy falls from 54.57 to 2.59 within 0.1 s, with substantial secondary fracture. It reads as compression and crumbling, distinct from the side hit's launch and toppling.
    - Moving the side origin about 0.107 units toward the tower changes immediate removal from 49.8% to 52.3%. The crack layout and later collapse change, while the amount removed remains close. Macro damage is reasonably stable under this small aim change.
    - A fresh repeat of the standard shot produces a byte-for-byte identical snapshot immediately after the blast, including geometry and initial motion. Later contact outcomes can vary slightly. Initial shot repeatability holds up.
    - A second blast from the same point, two seconds later, removes no additional material immediately. It applies another kick to the remaining rubble and changes its connections. The shot's useful effect follows the current positions of the survivors.
    
    The immediate response, repeatable initial cut and collision-driven toppling are useful foundations. The next destruction tuning target should be the balance between **material removal, chunk release and ejection**. Stronger shots should communicate their power through a clear physical result; marginal hits should visibly loosen something when they fracture it. Increasing the impulse multiplier alone does not address the large amount of material that has already disappeared.

        rows=[json.loads(line) for line in (folder/'telemetry.jsonl').read_text().splitlines()]

                'after_3s':ticks.get(301),'final':rows[-1]}

            moving=[ticks[151][key]['visible_moving_area'] for key in ['ground','tower']]

            print(f'{folder.name:20} lost soil/tower {removed[0]:5.2f}/{removed[1]:4.2f}; '
                  f'moving @.5s {moving[0]:5.2f}/{moving[1]:4.2f}; energy @.1s {energy:7.2f}; '
                  f'pieces @.5s {ticks[151]["ground"]["pieces"]}/{ticks[151]["tower"]["pieces"]}')
        else:
            print(folder.name,'final ground/tower area',rows[-1]['ground']['area'],rows[-1]['tower']['area'])
    (output/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary,indent=2))

    from pathlib import Path
    from PIL import Image,ImageDraw,ImageFont
    import json,shutil,subprocess
    
    root=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    output=root/'playtests/2026-11-01-strengths/fixed-floor'
    variants=['30-24','35-24','35-20']
    font=ImageFont.truetype('C:/Windows/Fonts/consola.ttf',18)
    for case in ['side-r4','side-r5','side-r6','rim-r5','ground-r5','rain','splinter','shatter']:
        if not all((output/f'{case}-{variant}'/'telemetry.jsonl').exists() for variant in variants):continue
        frames=[124,151,181,241,358]
        if case=='rain':frames=[240,480,720,960,1198]
        crop=(0,80,960,550)
        if case in ['side-r4','side-r5','side-r6','splinter','shatter']:crop=(450,80,950,550)
        sheet=Image.new('RGB',(1280,840),(19,28,42))
        draw=ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
        for row,variant in enumerate(variants):
            draw.text((8,row*280+5),f'{case}: {variant}',font=font,fill=(229,239,241))
            for col,frame in enumerate(frames):
                image=Image.open(output/f'{case}-{variant}'/f'frame-{(frame-1)//3:04d}.jpg')
                image=image.crop(crop).resize((256,224))
                sheet.paste(image,(col*256,row*280+52))
                seconds=frame/60 if case=='rain' else (frame-121)/60
                draw.text((col*256+6,row*280+28),f'{seconds:.2f}s',font=font,fill=(229,239,241))
        sheet.save(output/f'{case}-comparison.jpg',quality=94)
        if case in ['side-r5','ground-r5','rim-r5']:
            gif=[]
            for index in range(39,120,2):
                frame=Image.new('RGB',(1152,220),(19,28,42));draw=ImageDraw.Draw(frame)
                for col,variant in enumerate(variants):
                    image=Image.open(output/f'{case}-{variant}'/f'frame-{index:04d}.jpg').crop((0,80,960,550)).resize((384,188))
                    frame.paste(image,(col*384,32))
                    draw.text((col*384+8,6),variant,font=font,fill=(229,239,241))
                gif.append(frame)
            gif[0].save(output/f'{case}-comparison.gif',save_all=True,append_images=gif[1:],duration=100,loop=0,optimize=True)
        for variant in variants:
            video=output/f'{case}-{variant}.mp4'
            if video.exists():continue
            subprocess.run([shutil.which('ffmpeg'),'-hide_banner','-loglevel','error','-y',
                            '-framerate','20','-start_number','0','-i',str(output/f'{case}-{variant}'/'frame-%04d.jpg'),
                            '-c:v','libx264','-preset','veryfast','-crf','21','-pix_fmt','yuv420p',
                            '-movflags','+faststart',str(video)],check=True)
        print('Saved',case,'comparison and clips',flush=True)

    package main
    
    import "core:math"
    
    Segment :: struct { a,b: Vec2 }
    Cut_Boundary :: struct { a,b: int, segment: Segment }
    convex_hull :: proc(points: []Vec2) -> [dynamic]Vec2 {
        sorted: [dynamic]Vec2
        defer delete(sorted)
        for point in points { append(&sorted,point) }
        for i in 1..<len(sorted) {
            j:=i
            for j>0 && (sorted[j].x<sorted[j-1].x || (sorted[j].x==sorted[j-1].x && sorted[j].y<sorted[j-1].y)) { sorted[j],sorted[j-1]=sorted[j-1],sorted[j]; j-=1 }
        }
        hull: [dynamic]Vec2
        if len(sorted)<2 { for p in sorted { append(&hull,p) }; return hull }
        for p in sorted {
            for len(hull)>=2 && vcross(vsub(hull[len(hull)-1],hull[len(hull)-2]),vsub(p,hull[len(hull)-1]))<=0 { resize(&hull,len(hull)-1) }
            append(&hull,p)
        }
        upper_start:=len(hull)+1
        for i:=len(sorted)-2; i>=0; i-=1 {
            p:=sorted[i]
            for len(hull)>=upper_start && vcross(vsub(hull[len(hull)-1],hull[len(hull)-2]),vsub(p,hull[len(hull)-1]))<=0 { resize(&hull,len(hull)-1) }
            append(&hull,p)
        }
        resize(&hull,len(hull)-1)
        return hull
    }
    segment_overlap :: proc(a,b: Segment) -> (Segment,bool) {
        d := vsub(a.b,a.a)
        length := vlen(d)
        if length < 0.00001 { return {},false }
        if math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(b.a,a.a))) > 0.0001*length || math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(b.b,a.a))) > 0.0001*length { return {},false }
        unit := vmul(d,1/length)
        t0,t1 := vdot(vsub(b.a,a.a),unit),vdot(vsub(b.b,a.a),unit)
        lo,hi := max(f32(0),min(t0,t1)),min(length,max(t0,t1))
        if hi-lo <= 0.0001 { return {},false }
        return Segment{vadd(a.a,vmul(unit,lo)),vadd(a.a,vmul(unit,hi))},true
    }
    shared_segments :: proc(a,b: Polygon) -> [dynamic]Segment {
        result: [dynamic]Segment
        for i in 0..<len(a.points) {

    point_in_triangle :: proc(p,a,b,c: Vec2, orientation: f32, tolerance: f32 = 0.00001) -> bool {
        return vcross(vsub(b,a),vsub(p,a))*orientation >= -tolerance &&
               vcross(vsub(c,b),vsub(p,b))*orientation >= -tolerance &&
               vcross(vsub(a,c),vsub(p,c))*orientation >= -tolerance
    }
    triangulate_polygon :: proc(p: Polygon) -> [dynamic]Polygon {
        result: [dynamic]Polygon
        indices: [dynamic]int
        defer delete(indices)
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) { append(&indices,i) }
        signed: f32
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) { signed += vcross(p.points[i],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]) }
        orientation := f32(1)
        if signed < 0 { orientation = -1 }
        for len(indices) > 3 {
            found := false
            // Keep the normal ear order; only retry exact predicates if its tolerance
            // rejects every ear of a small valid corner on a refined shared seam.
            tolerances:=[2]f32{0.00001,0}
            for tolerance in tolerances {
            for k in 0..<len(indices) {
                i,j,l := indices[(k+len(indices)-1)%len(indices)],indices[k],indices[(k+1)%len(indices)]
                a,b,c := p.points[i],p.points[j],p.points[l]
                if vcross(vsub(b,a),vsub(c,b))*orientation <= tolerance { continue }
                contains := false
                for n in indices { if n != i && n != j && n != l && point_in_triangle(p.points[n],a,b,c,orientation,tolerance) { contains = true; break } }
                if contains { continue }
                append(&result,make_polygon([]Vec2{a,b,c}))
                ordered_remove(&indices,k)
                found = true
                break
            }
            if found { break }
            }
            if !found { break }
        }
        if len(indices) == 3 { append(&result,make_polygon([]Vec2{p.points[indices[0]],p.points[indices[1]],p.points[indices[2]]})) }
        return result
    }

        report='''Selected starting strengths: **35 fragment / 20 connection**, with radius 5, flexibility 0 and impulse multiplier 0.2. The playable BOM.exe now uses these defaults.
        
        I compared 30/24, 35/24 and 35/20 in 27 native-input playbacks covering 204 seconds of simulation. Every playback uses the default 17-by-3 destructible floor, seed 42 and the same initial tower. The player remains idle. The cases cover side hits at radii 4, 5 and 6; distant and closer edge hits; an isolated ground hit; Splinter and Shatter at radius 5; and a 20-second falling-bomb run for each setting.
        
        These are controlled, rendered playbacks through the existing input and simulation code. Physics advances at the normal 60 Hz and rendered frames are recorded at 20 fps independently of desktop capture overhead. The clips play at simulation speed. This comparison evaluates physical response rather than hardware input latency.
        
        For the same default side hit:
        
        | Fragment/connection strength | Tower material removed immediately | Moving tower area at 0.5 s | Visible debris linear energy at 0.1 s |
        | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
        '''+ '\n'.join(rows)+f'''
        
        The selected 35/20 recording retained **{retention:.0f}% more tower material** immediately after the hit and had **{energy:.0f}% more early visible debris energy** than 30/24, without increasing the impulse multiplier. More of the response comes from large chunks moving, rotating and colliding. Areas and energies are in game units; moving area uses a speed threshold of 0.2. Energy includes terrain and tower linear motion, excludes rotation and ignores centres outside the visible yard.
        
        Raising fragment strength supplies most of the improvement. Lowering connections to 20 gives a looser collapse and more visible tilt/separation on the closer edge hit. The difference between 35/24 and 35/20 is smaller and depends on the collision sequence; 35/24 is a reasonable alternative for more cohesive rubble. In the isolated crater case it produced slightly more moving ground at 0.5 s. I selected 20 for the clearer structural breakaway.
        
        The ground hit at (-2, 0.2) removed about 2.8 area units immediately with 35/20, compared with 5.8 for 30/24. Craters remain shallower and leave material for later hits. All three breakup patterns retained their characteristic shapes, and the bomb runs continued to excavate and redistribute rubble. Bomb landing heights change with the evolving terrain, so final areas after 20 seconds are not an isolated comparison of material strength.
        
        Higher power still removes more of the central material, leaving less to fly. These settings improve the physical response; they do not eliminate that tradeoff. Later contact trajectories can vary, so the measurements describe these recordings rather than statistical averages.
        
        [Default side-hit animation](final/side-r5-comparison.gif) · [Ground-hit animation](final/ground-r5-comparison.gif) · [Edge-hit animation](final/graze-r5-comparison.gif)
        
        | Comparison | Contact sheet | Clips, in strength order |
        | --- | --- | --- |
        '''
        for case,label in [('side-r4','Side hit, radius 4'),('side-r5','Side hit, radius 5'),('side-r6','Side hit, radius 6'),('rim-r5','Distant edge hit'),('graze-r5','Closer edge hit'),('ground-r5','Ground hit'),('splinter','Splinter'),('shatter','Shatter'),('rain','Falling bombs')]:
         clips=' / '.join(f'[{v}](final/{case}-{v}.mp4)' for v in ['30-24','35-24','35-20'])
         report+=f'| {label} | [Frames](final/{case}-comparison.jpg) | {clips} |\n'
        report+='''
        The sweep also exposed two bugs, now covered by regressions:

        - The triangulator's fixed tolerance could reject every remaining ear around valid corners only 0.00003 units apart, leaving part of a polygon untriangulated. It now retries exact predicates only when the normal pass stalls, preserving the usual ear order. Shared-boundary checks now measure the union of matching intervals, so duplicate tolerance-near matches cannot hide gaps or create false coverage failures. Their coverage tolerance is unchanged.

All 55 existing and new tests, native input smoke (including bombs and ground excavation in all patterns), and headless snapshot reconstruction passed. All 231 sampled scene validations in the final 27 playbacks passed. The current build preserves one impulse per final survivor, deterministic birth contexts, inherited broken connections and on-demand floor detail.

Production changes are the two new default strengths and the focused floor/triangulation corrections; the blast falloff, impulse multiplier and physics layout are unchanged.

    package main
    
    import "core:math"
    import "core:sync"
    import "core:testing"
    
    // Independent double-precision area and triangle intersection checks catch
    // compensating gaps/overlaps that a sum of the generator's f32 areas can miss.
    Partition_Point :: struct { x,y: f64 }
    partition_area :: proc(points: []Vec2) -> f64 {
        area: f64
        for p,i in points {
            q:=points[(i+1)%len(points)]
            area+=(f64(p.x)-f64(points[0].x))*(f64(q.y)-f64(points[0].y))-(f64(p.y)-f64(points[0].y))*(f64(q.x)-f64(points[0].x))
        }
        return math.abs(area)*0.5
    }
    partition_side :: proc(a,b,p: Partition_Point) -> f64 { return (b.x-a.x)*(p.y-a.y)-(b.y-a.y)*(p.x-a.x) }
    partition_triangle_overlap :: proc(a,b: Polygon) -> f64 {
        points: [12]Partition_Point
        for p,i in a.points { points[i]={f64(p.x),f64(p.y)} }
        count:=len(a.points)
        clip: [3]Partition_Point
        for p,i in b.points { clip[i]={f64(p.x),f64(p.y)} }
        orientation:=f64(1)
        if partition_side(clip[0],clip[1],clip[2])<0 { orientation=-1 }
        for edge in 0..<3 {
            next: [12]Partition_Point
            next_count:=0
            for i in 0..<count {
                p,q:=points[i],points[(i+1)%count]
                ps:=orientation*partition_side(clip[edge],clip[(edge+1)%3],p)
                qs:=orientation*partition_side(clip[edge],clip[(edge+1)%3],q)
                if ps>=0 { next[next_count]=p; next_count+=1 }
                if (ps>=0)!=(qs>=0) {
                    fraction:=ps/(ps-qs)
                    next[next_count]={p.x+(q.x-p.x)*fraction,p.y+(q.y-p.y)*fraction}; next_count+=1
                }
            }
            points=next; count=next_count
        }
        area: f64
        for i in 0..<count { area+=partition_side(points[0],points[i],points[(i+1)%count]) }
        return math.abs(area)*0.5
    }
    expect_generation_partition :: proc(t: ^testing.T,parent: Polygon,children: []Polygon) {
        testing.expect(t,len(children)>=2)
        parent_area:=partition_area(parent.points)
        tolerance:=max(f64(0.00000005),parent_area*0.00005)
        parent_triangles:=triangulate_polygon(parent)
        defer { for triangle in parent_triangles { delete(triangle.points) }; delete(parent_triangles) }
        triangles: [dynamic][dynamic]Polygon
        defer { for batch in triangles { for triangle in batch { delete(triangle.points) }; delete(batch) }; delete(triangles) }
        area: f64
        for child in children {
            child_area:=partition_area(child.points)
            area+=child_area
            testing.expect(t,child_area>0 && child_area<parent_area)
            parts:=triangulate_polygon(child)
            inside: f64
            for part in parts { for triangle in parent_triangles { inside+=partition_triangle_overlap(part,triangle) } }
            testing.expectf(t,math.abs(inside-child_area)<=tolerance,"Every child must stay within its parent, including displaced seams: area %.8f, clipped %.8f, points %v",child_area,inside,child.points)
            append(&triangles,parts)
        }
        testing.expect(t,math.abs(area-parent_area)<=tolerance,"The partition must preserve its parent's area")
        for i in 0..<len(triangles) {
            for j in i+1..<len(triangles) {
                overlap: f64
                for a in triangles[i] { for b in triangles[j] { overlap+=partition_triangle_overlap(a,b) } }
                testing.expect(t,overlap<=tolerance,"Sibling interiors must not overlap")
            }
        }
        // Each child edge must be covered by the parent boundary or an exact sibling
        // seam. T junctions may split one side into several collinear segments.
        for child,i in children {
            perimeter,covered:=f32(0),f32(0)
            boundaries: [dynamic]Polygon
            append(&boundaries,parent)
            for other,j in children { if i!=j { append(&boundaries,other) } }
            for p,k in child.points {
                q:=child.points[(k+1)%len(child.points)]
                length:=vlen(vsub(q,p)); perimeter+=length
                if length==0 { continue }
                unit:=vmul(vsub(q,p),1/length)
                intervals: [dynamic][2]f32
                for other in boundaries {
                    for a,j in other.points {
                        if seam,ok:=segment_overlap(Segment{p,q},Segment{a,other.points[(j+1)%len(other.points)]}); ok {
                            lo,hi:=vdot(vsub(seam.a,p),unit),vdot(vsub(seam.b,p),unit)
                            append(&intervals,[2]f32{max(f32(0),min(lo,hi)),min(length,max(lo,hi))})
                        }
                    }
                }
                for j in 1..<len(intervals) {
                    n:=j
                    for n>0 && intervals[n][0]<intervals[n-1][0] { intervals[n],intervals[n-1]=intervals[n-1],intervals[n]; n-=1 }
                }
                // Measure the union: tolerance-near seams can overlap, and a duplicate
                // match must neither fail coverage nor cancel a real gap elsewhere.
                end:=f32(0)
                for interval in intervals {
                    if interval[1]>end { covered+=interval[1]-max(end,interval[0]); end=interval[1] }
                }
                delete(intervals)
            }
            delete(boundaries)
            testing.expectf(t,math.abs(covered-perimeter)<0.0001,"Every generated edge must retain a matching shared boundary: perimeter %.8f, coverage %.8f, points %v",perimeter,covered,child.points)
        }
    }

    @(test)
    concave_generation_merges_ears_and_preserves_material_patterns :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        points:=[4]Vec2{{1.5,0.005},{2.35,0.005},{2.35,0.855},{1.5,0.855}}
        parent:=Polygon{points=points[:]}
        seeds:=[4]u8{42,85,177,98}
        for pattern in 0..<3 {
            recipe:=material_preset(pattern)
            concave_parents:=0
            refined_triangles:=0
            for seed in seeds {
                // Sweep the affected non-triangular recipes; one known Shatter fixture
                // checks that its deliberately triangular generations remain available.
                if recipe.triangulate && seed!=42 { continue }
                children:=generate_children(parent,recipe,seed)
                defer { for child in children { delete(child.points) }; delete(children) }
                if !testing.expectf(t,len(children)>=2,"Pattern %d, seed %d did not produce a partition",pattern,seed) { continue }
                expect_generation_partition(t,parent,children[:])
                if !recipe.triangulate { testing.expect(t,len(children)==recipe.generation_count) }
                largest:=0
                for child,i in children { if polygon_area(child)>polygon_area(children[largest]) { largest=i } }
                for child,i in children {
                    if recipe.triangulate {
                        testing.expect(t,len(child.points)==3,"Shatter deliberately retains triangular subdivisions")
                        if i!=largest { continue } // Refine a triangle large enough for the existing area guard.
                    }
                    if !is_convex(child) { concave_parents+=1 }
                    if pattern==1 {
                        lo,hi:=Vec2{1e30,1e30},Vec2{-1e30,-1e30}
                        for point in child.points { lo={min(lo.x,point.x),min(lo.y,point.y)}; hi={max(hi.x,point.x),max(hi.y,point.y)} }
                        testing.expect(t,hi.y-lo.y>2*(hi.x-lo.x),"Splinter must keep its elongated cuts")
                    }
                    grandchildren:=generate_children(child,recipe,derive_seed(seed,u64(i+1)))
                    defer { for grandchild in grandchildren { delete(grandchild.points) }; delete(grandchildren) }
                    expect_generation_partition(t,child,grandchildren[:])
                    if !recipe.triangulate {
                        testing.expect(t,len(grandchildren)==recipe.generation_count,"A bent boundary must not turn triangulation ears into extra fragments")
                    }
                    for grandchild in grandchildren {
                        if pattern==0 {
                            lo,hi:=Vec2{1e30,1e30},Vec2{-1e30,-1e30}
                            for point in grandchild.points { lo={min(lo.x,point.x),min(lo.y,point.y)}; hi={max(hi.x,point.x),max(hi.y,point.y)} }
                            testing.expect(t,outline_width(grandchild.points)/max(hi.x-lo.x,hi.y-lo.y)>0.1,"Chunk must not create thin corner fans from small shared-edge bends")
                        }
                        if recipe.triangulate { testing.expect(t,len(grandchild.points)==3); refined_triangles+=1 }
                    }
                }
            }
            if !recipe.triangulate { testing.expect(t,concave_parents>0,"Shared-edge displacement must remain enabled in this regression") }
            else { testing.expect(t,refined_triangles>0) }
        }
    }

    package main
    
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:math"
    
    Sandbox_Settings :: struct {
        blast_radius: f32,
        blast_mode: Blast_Mode,
        pattern: int,
        fragment_strength, connection_strength, flexibility: f32,
        generate_children: bool,
        seed: u8,
    }
    DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS :: Sandbox_Settings{blast_radius=5.0,fragment_strength=35,connection_strength=20,flexibility=0,generate_children=true,seed=42}
    YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM :: f32(-3)
    YARD_BASE_DEPTH :: f32(0.25)
    sandbox_material :: proc(settings: Sandbox_Settings) -> Material {
        material:=material_preset(settings.pattern)
        material.subdivision_strength=settings.fragment_strength
        material.connection_strength=settings.connection_strength
        material.flexibility=settings.flexibility
        return material
    }
    Sandbox :: struct {
        scene: Scene,
        floor: b2.BodyId,
        player: Player,
        bomb_rain: Bomb_Rain,
        applied,draft: Sandbox_Settings,
        previous: map[u64]Pose,
        previous_player: Vec2,
        panel_open,inspection,tuning_open,surface,joints: bool,
        block_jump,block_blast,jump_queued: bool,
        selected: u64,
        accumulator: f32,
        status: string,
        status_time: f32,
    }
    sandbox_create :: proc(settings: Sandbox_Settings = DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS) -> Sandbox {
        game:=Sandbox{applied=settings,draft=settings,previous=make(map[u64]Pose),surface=true,joints=true}
        sandbox_reset(&game)
        return game
    }
    sandbox_destroy :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        scene_destroy(&game.scene)
        delete(game.bomb_rain.bombs); delete(game.bomb_rain.bursts)
        delete(game.previous)
        game^={}
    }
    sandbox_notice :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,text: string) { game.status=text; game.status_time=2.5 }
    sandbox_clear_input :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        game.accumulator=0
        game.jump_queued=false
        game.block_jump=true
        game.block_blast=true
        player_clear_input(&game.player)
        clear(&game.previous)
        game.previous_player=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body))
    }
    sandbox_reset :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        revision:=game.scene.revision+1
        scene_destroy(&game.scene)
        s:=&game.scene
        s^=new_scene(0.10)
        s.revision=revision
        material:=add_material(s,sandbox_material(game.applied))
        seed:=game.applied.seed
        if !game.applied.generate_children { seed=0 }
        owner:=add_piece(s,material,seed)
        // A stepped stack, with one common reference frame and real shared edges.
        for row in 0..<3 {
            for column in 0..<4-row {
                // Start on the floor: the former 5 mm drop overloaded stiff joints on landing.
                x,y:=f32(1.5)+f32(column)*0.85,f32(row)*0.85
                points:=[4]Vec2{{x,y},{x+0.85,y},{x+0.85,y+0.85},{x,y+0.85}}
                outline:=Polygon{points=points[:]}
                id:=add_subdivision(s,owner,outline,Pose{position=centroid(outline)})
                // Stable block coordinates give neighboring roots distinct birth contexts.

    vadd :: proc(a, b: Vec2) -> Vec2 { return {a.x+b.x, a.y+b.y} }
    vsub :: proc(a, b: Vec2) -> Vec2 { return {a.x-b.x, a.y-b.y} }
    vmul :: proc(a: Vec2, s: f32) -> Vec2 { return {a.x*s, a.y*s} }
    vdot :: proc(a, b: Vec2) -> f32 { return a.x*b.x+a.y*b.y }
    vcross :: proc(a, b: Vec2) -> f32 { return a.x*b.y-a.y*b.x }
    vlen :: proc(a: Vec2) -> f32 { return math.sqrt(vdot(a,a)) }
    vrotate :: proc(a: Vec2, angle: f32) -> Vec2 {
        c, s := f32(math.cos(angle)), f32(math.sin(angle))
        return {a.x*c-a.y*s,a.x*s+a.y*c}
    }
    centroid :: proc(p: Polygon) -> Vec2 {
        area, x, y: f32
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) {
            a, b := p.points[i], p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]
            cross := vcross(a,b)
            area += cross
            x += (a.x+b.x)*cross
            y += (a.y+b.y)*cross
        }
        if math.abs(area) < 0.00001 {
            for point in p.points { x += point.x; y += point.y }
            return {x/f32(len(p.points)),y/f32(len(p.points))}
        }
        return {x/(3*area),y/(3*area)}
    }
    posed_point :: proc(sub: Subdivision, rest: Vec2) -> Vec2 {
        return vadd(sub.pose.position,vrotate(vsub(rest,sub.rest_center),sub.pose.angle))
    }
    posed_polygon :: proc(sub: Subdivision) -> Polygon {
        result := Polygon{points=make([]Vec2,len(sub.outline.points))}
        for point,i in sub.outline.points { result.points[i]=posed_point(sub,point) }
        return result
    }
    make_polygon :: proc(points: []Vec2) -> Polygon {
        result:=Polygon{points=make([]Vec2,len(points))}
        copy(result.points,points)
        return result
    }

    import "core:net"
