    SNAPSHOT_PORT :: 9901
    MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES :: 4*1024*1024
    Snapshot_Server :: struct {
        listener,client: net.TCP_Socket,
        active,connected: bool,
        pending: []byte,
        sent: int,
        elapsed: f32,
        last_revision: u64,
    }
    Snapshot_Stream :: struct { socket: net.TCP_Socket, buffer: [dynamic]byte, connected: bool }
    snapshot_server_start :: proc(port: int = SNAPSHOT_PORT) -> Snapshot_Server {
        listener,err:=net.listen_tcp(net.Endpoint{address=net.IP4_Loopback,port=port})
        if err!=nil { return {} }
        if net.set_blocking(listener,false)!=.None { net.close(listener); return {} }
        return Snapshot_Server{listener=listener,active=true}
    }
    snapshot_server_destroy :: proc(server: ^Snapshot_Server) {
        if server.connected { net.close(server.client) }
        if server.active { net.close(server.listener) }
        delete(server.pending); server^={}
    }
    frame_snapshot :: proc(data: []byte) -> []byte {
        assert(len(data)<=MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES)
        frame:=make([]byte,len(data)+4)
        length:=u32(len(data))
        for i in 0..<4 { frame[i]=u8(length>>uint(8*i)) }
        copy(frame[4:],data)
        return frame
    }
    snapshot_server_update :: proc(server: ^Snapshot_Server,s: ^Scene,dt: f32) {
        if !server.active { return }
        server.elapsed+=dt
        accepted:=false
        if !server.connected {
            client,_,err:=net.accept_tcp(server.listener,{no_delay=true})
            if err!=.None { return }
            if net.set_blocking(client,false)!=.None { net.close(client); return }
            server.client=client; server.connected=true; accepted=true
        }
        // Send complete state on changes and at 10 Hz for motion interpolation.
        // Finish an in-flight frame before taking a newer state; queues cannot grow.
        if len(server.pending)==0 && (accepted || s.revision!=server.last_revision || server.elapsed>=0.1) {
            data,ok:=encode_snapshot(s)
            defer delete(data)
            if !ok || len(data)>MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES { return }
            server.pending=frame_snapshot(data)
            server.sent=0; server.elapsed=0; server.last_revision=s.revision
        }
        if len(server.pending)==0 { return }
        n,err:=net.send_tcp(server.client,server.pending[server.sent:])
        server.sent+=n
        if err!=.None && err!=.Would_Block {
            net.close(server.client); server.connected=false
            delete(server.pending); server.pending=nil; server.sent=0
            return
        }
        if server.sent==len(server.pending) { delete(server.pending); server.pending=nil; server.sent=0 }
    }
    snapshot_stream_connect :: proc(port: int = SNAPSHOT_PORT) -> Snapshot_Stream {
        socket,err:=net.dial_tcp_from_endpoint(net.Endpoint{address=net.IP4_Loopback,port=port},net.TCP_Options{no_delay=true})
        if err!=nil { return {} }
        if net.set_blocking(socket,false)!=.None { net.close(socket); return {} }
        return Snapshot_Stream{socket=socket,connected=true}
    }
    snapshot_stream_destroy :: proc(stream: ^Snapshot_Stream) {
        if stream.connected { net.close(stream.socket) }
        delete(stream.buffer); stream^={}
    }

    polygon_area :: proc(p: Polygon) -> f32 {
        a: f32

    clip_polygon :: proc(p: Polygon, axis: int, cut: f32, keep_low: bool) -> Polygon {
        points: [dynamic]Vec2
        defer delete(points)
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) {
            a,b := p.points[i],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]
            av,bv := a.x-cut,b.x-cut
            if axis == 1 { av = a.y-cut; bv = b.y-cut }
            if !keep_low { av = -av; bv = -bv }
            inside_a, inside_b := av <= 0,bv <= 0
            if inside_a { append(&points,a) }
            if inside_a != inside_b {
                t := av/(av-bv)
                append(&points,vadd(a,vmul(vsub(b,a),t)))
            }
        }
        return make_polygon(points[:])
    }

    convex_hull :: proc(points: []Vec2) -> [dynamic]Vec2 {
        sorted: [dynamic]Vec2
        defer delete(sorted)
        for point in points { append(&sorted,point) }
        for i in 1..<len(sorted) {
            j:=i
            for j>0 && (sorted[j].x<sorted[j-1].x || (sorted[j].x==sorted[j-1].x && sorted[j].y<sorted[j-1].y)) { sorted[j],sorted[j-1]=sorted[j-1],sorted[j]; j-=1 }

            for len(hull)>=2 && vcross(vsub(hull[len(hull)-1],hull[len(hull)-2]),vsub(p,hull[len(hull)-1]))<=0 { resize(&hull,len(hull)-1) }

        for i:=len(sorted)-2; i>=0; i-=1 {

        if math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(b.a,a.a))) > 0.0001*length || math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(b.b,a.a))) > 0.0001*length { return {},false }

    derive_seed :: proc(seed: u8, identity: u64) -> u8 {
        if seed == 0 { return 0 }
        x := identity ~ (u64(seed)*0x9e3779b97f4a7c15)
        x ~= x >> 30; x *= 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9
        x ~= x >> 27; x *= 0x94d049bb133111eb
        x ~= x >> 31
        return u8(x%255+1)
    }
    piece_width :: proc(s: ^Scene, ids: []u64) -> f32 {
        if len(ids) == 0 { return 0 }
        points: [dynamic]Vec2
        defer delete(points)
        for id in ids { for point in s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[id]].outline.points { append(&points,point) } }
        return outline_width(points[:])
    }

    package main
    
    import "core:encoding/json"
    import "core:fmt"
    import "core:os"
    
    Preview_Branch :: struct {
    	parent_index: int,
    	seed: u8,
    	width: f32,
    	status: string,
    	children: [dynamic]Polygon,
    }
    Preview_Case :: struct {
    	material: Material,
    	seed: u8,
    	root: Polygon,
    	first: [dynamic]Polygon,
    	second: [dynamic]Preview_Branch,
    }
    main :: proc() {
    	assert(len(os.args)==2,"Supply the JSON output path")
    	points:=[4]Vec2{{1.5,0},{2.35,0},{2.35,0.85},{1.5,0.85}}
    	root:=Polygon{points=points[:]}
    	seed:=u8(42)
    	cases: [dynamic]Preview_Case
    	defer {
    		for item in cases {
    			for child in item.first { delete(child.points) }; delete(item.first)
    			for branch in item.second {
    				for child in branch.children { delete(child.points) }; delete(branch.children)
    			}
    			delete(item.second)
    		}
    		delete(cases)
    	}
    	for pattern in 0..<3 {
    		settings:=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS; settings.pattern=pattern
    		recipe:=sandbox_material(settings)
    		item:=Preview_Case{material=recipe,seed=seed,root=root}
    		item.first=generate_children(root,recipe,seed)
    		max_width:=f32(0)
    		for child in item.first { max_width=max(max_width,outline_width(child.points)) }
    		for child,i in item.first {
    			child_seed:=derive_seed(seed,u64(i+1))
    			if max_width<0.10 { child_seed=0 }
    			branch:=Preview_Branch{parent_index=i,seed=child_seed,width=outline_width(child.points)}
    			if child_seed==0 || branch.width<=0.10 { branch.status="size guard (carried unchanged)" }
    			else {
    				branch.children=generate_children(child,recipe,child_seed)
    				if len(branch.children)==0 { branch.status="generation failed (direct removal if overloaded)" }
    				else { branch.status="generated" }
    			}
    			append(&item.second,branch)
    		}
    		append(&cases,item)
    	}
    	data,err:=json.marshal(cases,{pretty=true}); assert(err==nil); defer delete(data)
    	assert(os.write_entire_file(os.args[1],data)==nil)
    	for item in cases {
    		count,failed,guarded:=0,0,0
    		for branch in item.second {
    			count+=len(branch.children)
    			if branch.status=="generation failed (direct removal if overloaded)" { failed+=1 }
    			if branch.status=="size guard (carried unchanged)" { guarded+=1 }
    		}
    		fmt.printf("%s: first=%d, second_generated=%d, failed_parents=%d, size_guarded=%d\n",item.material.name,len(item.first),count,failed,guarded)
    	}
    }

    BG, TEXT, MUTED = '#111b28', '#e2edf5', '#9fb2c4'
    
    def area(poly):
        p = poly['points']; x0, y0 = p[0]['x'], p[0]['y']
        return abs(sum((a['x']-x0)*(b['y']-y0)-(a['y']-y0)*(b['x']-x0) for a,b in zip(p,p[1:]+p[:1]))) / 2
    
    def leaves(case, level):
        if level == 1:
            return [(p, i, False) for i,p in enumerate(case['first'])]
        result = []
        for branch in case['second']:
            i = branch['parent_index']
            if branch['status'] == 'generated':
                result.extend((p, i, False) for p in branch['children'])
            else:
                # A guard means no new subdivision detail; retain the live geometry.
                result.append((case['first'][i], i, branch['status'].startswith('generation failed')))
        return result
    
    def panel(draw, case, level, x, y, size, title_size=25):
        polygons = leaves(case, level)
        draw.text((x,y), f"Jitter {'ON' if case['_mode']=='on' else 'OFF'}  |  {len(polygons)} fragments", font=font(title_size, True), fill=TEXT)
        top = y + title_size + 19
        def point(p):
            return (round(x+(p['x']-1.5)/0.85*size), round(top+size-p['y']/0.85*size))
        for poly, i, failed in polygons:
            rgb = colorsys.hsv_to_rgb((i * .141 + .52) % 1, .36, .72)
            fill = tuple(round(c*255) for c in rgb)
            if failed: fill = (180,65,65)
            draw.polygon([point(p) for p in poly['points']], fill=fill)
        for poly, i, failed in polygons:
            pts = [point(p) for p in poly['points']]
            draw.line(pts+[pts[0]], fill='#e3edf4', width=max(1,round(size/430)), joint='curve')
        corners = [point(p) for p in case['root']['points']]
        draw.line(corners+[corners[0]], fill='#edf5fc', width=3)
    
    summary = []

    Temporary comparison of shared-boundary jitter
    ============================================
    
    ![Both generations, all materials](comparison.png)
    
    | Material | Generation 1, jitter on / off | Generation 2, jitter on / off |
    | --- | ---: | ---: |
    | Chunk | 3 / 3 | 9 / 9 |
    | Splinter | 5 / 5 | 25 / 25 |
    | Shatter | 32 / 10 | 538 / 90 |
    
    These are total visible logical subdivisions at each level. Generation 2 includes unchanged parents stopped by the existing size guard: Shatter retains 15 with jitter and 2 without it. Its newly generated second-generation triangles number 523 versus 88. Chunk and Splinter have no size-guarded parents in this fixture.
    
    Observed shapes
    ---------------
    
    - **Chunk:** Jitter makes the first cuts slightly bent. At the second generation, it also produces angled, wedge-shaped partitions, including long diagonals into a corner. Without jitter, this fixture stays rectangular and grid-like. Counts stay unchanged. [Larger image](chunk-comparison.png).
    - **Splinter:** Both variants retain elongated pieces. Jitter adds small bends, and the second generation includes several long diagonal wedges. Without jitter, the partitions are straighter strips and rectangular sections. Counts stay unchanged. [Larger image](splinter-comparison.png).
    - **Shatter:** Both variants deliberately generate triangles. With jitter, the extra seam vertices are subsequently triangulated, creating many additional small triangles and dense clusters of narrow tips. Without jitter, the triangles are fewer and generally larger, although narrow triangles and corner convergence remain. [Larger image](shatter-comparison.png).
    
    The large Shatter count increase and the remaining wedges are observations only; no generator correction or tuning was attempted. This is one controlled fixture, not a seed sweep or a gameplay performance comparison.
    
    Inputs and method
    -----------------
    
    - Identical root square for all six cases: `(1.5,0)` to `(2.35,0.85)`, using the current f32 geometry.
    - Generation context **42** for each root. This is an explicitly chosen common generator seed; it is not the first yard block's derived birth context (85).
    - Existing Chunk, Splinter and Shatter recipes, with current sandbox material settings: strengths 35/20, flexibility 0; generation counts 3/5/6 and aspect ratios 1/0.2/1 respectively. Shatter's triangulate flag remains enabled.
    - Each second-generation branch uses `derive_seed(42, child_ordinal + 1)`, matching current child context assignment. A shared ordinal therefore gets the same context in each variant. Shatter creates different numbers of first-generation children, so there is no one-to-one correspondence between all its second-generation branches.
    - Preview refines every eligible first-generation child once, using the existing 0.10 size cutoff and terminal-batch rule. Ineligible live geometry is shown unchanged. There is no explosion, failure selection, physics, body creation, or final piece-width filtering. These counts describe the refinement preview, not debris counts after a particular blast.
    - All displayed lines are logical polygon outlines. No rendering-only triangulation edges are added. Colors group second-generation descendants by their first-generation parent.
    - Only an isolated copy was compiled. The sole generator alteration in that copy gated `displace_shared_boundaries(result[:],seed)` with a compile-time boolean. The on/off executables differed only in that boolean; the preview driver supplied identical inputs. No UI or settings were added.
    
    Checks and problems
    -------------------
    
    Both variants built and ran successfully. All requested generation attempts returned genuine partitions; none failed in this fixture. Repeat executions produced byte-identical JSON. Independent double-precision shoelace sums over exported coordinates found a maximum parent-versus-children area discrepancy of approximately **3.62e-8 square units**. This checks total area, not a separate exhaustive proof against compensating gaps and overlaps. No full gameplay test suite was run for this observational comparison.
    
    The on/off geometry exports are [jitter-on.json](jitter-on.json) and [jitter-off.json](jitter-off.json). [summary.json](summary.json) records counts, triangle counts, guarded parents and area errors. The temporary code and executables were removed. SHA-256 checks of every original top-level file, including production Odin source and BOM.exe, matched the before-run manifest; see [verification.json](verification.json).

    # Odin destruction sandbox
    
    A standalone implementation of `destruction-model-implementation-plan.md` and `playable-sandbox-ux-plan.md`, using Odin's bundled Box2D, raylib and raygui libraries. The default application is a small playable destruction yard. The original diagnostic lab and localhost snapshot transport remain available.
    
    ## Run
    
    Requires an Odin installation with compiled `vendor:box2d` and `vendor:raylib` libraries. Tested on Windows with Odin `dev-2026-05-nightly:ea5175d`.
    
    ```powershell
    odin run .
    odin test . -out:BOM-tests.exe
    odin build . -o:speed -out:BOM.exe
    ```
    
    The application opens into a fixed side-view yard with a destructible floor, an invulnerable capsule player and a destructible stepped tower. Walk, jump onto or push debris, aim outside a solid shape and click to blast. Ordinary gravity runs at a fixed 60 Hz with four Box2D substeps. The camera keeps the yard framed when the window resizes. Falling outside the yard returns the player to spawn.
    
    The floor starts as one 17-by-3 rectangle with a deterministic generation context. Future detail is generated locally on demand, including for blasts near either end of that large outline. A connected ground section stays anchored while it retains an edge on the bottom support plane; sections cut free use ordinary dynamic physics. A thin indestructible base underneath spans beyond the playable edges and catches the player, bombs and rubble above the bottom of the screen. The fixed view includes the pit bottom. Aim just above the surface to excavate it; solid floor interiors follow the same invalid-origin rule as the tower. Reset restores the single floor root. Use this destructible-floor yard for subsequent destruction-feel comparisons.
    
    | Control | Action |
    | --- | --- |
    | A / D or left / right arrows | Move |
    | Space | Jump, with a 0.1 second jump buffer and coyote window |
    | Left click in the world | One blast at a valid cursor position |
    | Mouse wheel over the world | Adjust blast radius and power |
    | R / Reset button | Restore the same applied setup and seed |
    | Tab / Escape / Settings button | Open settings and pause; close to resume |
    | F3 | Toggle IDs, connections, counts and inspection tools |
    
    The aiming circle shows the active blast radius. A red cross and message mark origins inside or on live logical outlines; those blasts are suppressed. UI clicks do not blast the world. The settings panel pauses physics, fading and player actions without accumulating simulation time.
    
    In Settings, switch **Manual blasts / Falling bombs** to choose the explosion source immediately, without resetting the yard. Falling bombs spawn at random horizontal positions across the yard every 1â€“2.5 seconds. Each is an ordinary circle body that collides with the floor, debris and player. Its one-second fuse starts on first landing on a supporting surface, including the tower; airborne time and side contacts do not start the fuse. A red countdown ring marks a lit fuse. The body disappears when it explodes at its current position, using the current blast radius, with a brief expanding flash. Manual placement and its aiming circle are disabled in this mode. Returning to Manual clears pending bombs. Settings pauses drops, fuses and flashes along with physics. Reset clears bombs and repeats the applied seed's drop sequence, independently of destruction generation.
    
    Mode and radius changes are immediate, including inside settings. Breakup pattern, fragment strength, connection strength, flexibility and Generate children are staged until **Apply & Reset**. Resume keeps the previously applied setup. Strength and flexibility stay independent of Chunk / Splinter / Shatter. The initial setup uses manual blasts, seed 42, strengths 35 / 20, flexibility 0 (stiff welds) and radius 5.0. These strengths retain more material while releasing attachments over a wider area. Positive flexibility remains available in Settings. Turning Generate children off uses seed zero; geometry stays live until it fails.
    
    With F3 enabled: right click selects, Delete or Ctrl+click directly removes a region, Shift+click or X near an anchor breaks a connection, J toggles links, V toggles the cosmetic surface, and S saves `snapshot.json`. D and Space retain movement and jump in inspection mode.
    
    Run `odin run . -- --lab` for the original zero-gravity diagnostic fixture and its legacy shortcuts (projectile I, presets 1/2/3, terminal T, pause/step Space/N, radius Q/E, pan/zoom, and snapshot save/load S/L). The existing sender and receiver use that diagnostic fixture; player and indestructible-base replication are outside this local milestone. The logical destructible floor uses the ordinary geometry records.
    
    For automated execution:
    
    ```powershell
    odin run . -- --headless
    odin run . -- --smoke
    odin run . -- --smoke-settings
    odin run . -- --smoke-input
    ```
    
    `--headless` evaluates the original diagnostic blast, runs 60 physics ticks, validates the graph, writes `snapshot.json`, and reconstructs a receiver. `--smoke` renders the yard in a hidden window to `sandbox-preview.png`. `--smoke-settings` renders the expanded paused panel to `sandbox-settings-preview.png`. Both exit after two frames.
    
    `--smoke-input` uses raylib's native automation events in a hidden window to exercise the actual keyboard bindings and raygui widgets: movement, holding jump through landing, paused settings, closing a slider drag with Escape, immediate radius updates, staged pattern/generation changes, Apply & Reset, the first subsequent blast click, inspection, R reset, switching into Falling bombs, automatic spawning, landing, detonation and switching back to manual placement. It then restores generation through Settings and excavates both ends of the floor in all three patterns. It asserts the results and exports `sandbox-playthrough.png`, `sandbox-bombs-preview.png` and `sandbox-ground-0.png` through `sandbox-ground-2.png`. The normal behavior suite stays independent of a window or display.
    
    ## Live transmission
    
    Build once, then run these in separate terminals:
    
    ```powershell
    .\BOM.exe --serve
    .\BOM.exe --receive
    ```
    
    The sender listens on **127.0.0.1:9901** for one receiver. It sends explicit complete snapshots after structural changes and at 10 Hz for motion. The receiver renders polygons, connections, ownership and interpolated motion without simulating physics. Destroy or split the wall in the sender to see the receiver update.
    
    Frames contain a four byte little endian payload length followed by UTF-8 JSON, capped at 4 MiB. Partial reads, partial writes, coalesced frames and disconnects are handled. One in-flight send is retained; the sender does not accumulate a queue of old states. `read_state`, `encode_snapshot` and `decode_snapshot` can also be used with another transport.
    
    Snapshots carry current geometry, materials, stable IDs, piece memberships, future generation seeds, structural revision, and body motion. Version 2 retains each subdivision's birth seed context; version 1 snapshots still load using their original piece contexts. Widths and anchors are derived from the transmitted outlines. Infinite strengths have explicit flags so snapshots remain valid JSON. Seeds never reconstruct existing damaged geometry.
    
    ## Implementation
    
    | File | Responsibility |
    | --- | --- |
    | `model.odin` | Stable identity, shared reference vertex pool, birth contexts, cached outline widths, memberships and group filtering |
    | `geometry.odin` | Shared boundaries, displaced cuts, convex hull and collision decomposition |
    | `destruction.odin` | Seeded generation, blast evaluation and the shared structural update |
    | `physics.odin` | Box2D bodies, fixtures, weld joints, interaction aggregation and load policy |
    | `state.odin` | State reader, snapshot validation, serialization and pose interpolation |
    | `transmission.odin` | Framed localhost TCP snapshots and the receiver application |
    | `debug_view.odin` | Native controls, rendering and material presets |
    | `player.odin` | Capsule controller, contact support, buffered jumps and respawn |
    | `yard.odin` | Yard creation/reset, applied and staged settings, aim validation and input routing |
    | `bombs.odin` | Falling-bomb mode, independent drop randomness, physics bodies, landing fuses and explosions |
    | `sandbox_view.odin` | Fixed camera, compact HUD, raygui panel and inspection input |
    | `sandbox_smoke.odin` | Hidden-window native input and widget playthrough |
    | `behavior_test.odin` | Focused behavior and integration checks |
    | `recursive_blast_test.odin` | Same-blast termination, child contexts, conservative deletion and recursive agreement |
    | `generation_test.odin` | Concave parent merging, material patterns, partition coverage and distinct yard birth contexts |
    | `ground_test.odin` | Local floor refinement, anchored and detached ground, partition coverage and the sealed bottom |
    | `sandbox_test.odin` | Gravity stability, movement, debris contact, resets, settings and input consumption |
    | `bombs_test.odin` | Real landing contacts, one-second fuses, blast integration, pause, mode switches and bomb cleanup |
    
    IDs are monotonic and mapped to storage rows. Removed rows and outline ranges remain retained until `scene_destroy`; no world repacking is performed. Subdivision outlines use ranges into one append-only vertex pool in a common undeformed reference frame. Their `outline` slices are derived views refreshed when the pool grows. Borrowed polygon views must not be held across scene mutations. `add_subdivision` copies its input; the caller retains ownership of that input allocation. `make_polygon` creates an owned polygon.
    
    Current subdivisions and connections exist when a piece is created. Future geometry is generated only when a subdivision fails. `apply_failures` stages one generation for physics reactions and manual failures. `blast_pass` reuses that staging operation in a simple loop: evaluate the current geometry, replace failures, and evaluate new children and connections against the same blast until nothing else fails. Only then regroup affected pieces, filter connected groups and synchronize physics. A failed connection cannot be healed by proximity; only surviving old attachments are inherited. Failure IDs and groups use stable ordering, including when storage rows are shuffled. `discard_subdivisions` provides direct removal independently of a generative seed.
    
    Each child receives its future seed context at birth, derived from its parent's context and child ordinal. Allocation IDs and later ownership changes do not affect that context. When every sibling's cached outline width is at or below the subdivision cutoff, the whole batch receives seed zero. Mixed batches retain nonzero contexts, with an individual width guard before further generation. Seed-zero geometry remains live until it fails. Connected-group width filtering remains a separate final step.
    
    Before generating a failed outline, the blast can remove it directly when its farthest posed vertex proves every descendant will fail. This assumes partition-preserving generation, shared material strength, an unoccluded radial load and unchanged transforms during the event. The bound rounds distance outward with `nextafter`, uses a strict `1e-4` load margin and declines nonfinite inputs. Skipping a branch leaves other branches' seeds unchanged. `blast_pass(..., false)` disables the shortcut for correctness comparisons; normal play enables it.
    
    Generation clips convex regions. For a concave Chunk or Splinter parent, the existing convex decomposition merges adjacent triangulation ears before applying the requested cuts; a small shared-edge bend does not automatically become a fan of independent fragments. Shatter deliberately retains triangulation. Each internal displaced cut is generated once and installed in both adjacent outlines. Displacement is limited by clearance to other edges as well as area and length. Outside boundaries remain intact. Count is a target before final triangulation; complex concave outlines and the shatter preset can produce more children. If generation cannot produce a genuine partition of at least two smaller regions, the failed subdivision is removed directly. A valid partition is retained even when area limits prevent reaching the requested count. Aspect ratio biases cut direction. Self-intersecting outlines and polygons with holes are outside this implementation's input domain. Starting yard blocks derive distinct birth contexts from the applied seed and their stable grid coordinates; reset repeats the same contexts.
    
    The load policy uses the strongest individual interaction, preserving opposing interactions against different bodies. Contact points and convex fixtures against the same other body are combined. Joint reactions also load their endpoint subdivisions. Thresholds use `load > 0 && load >= strength`; strength records are never reduced by prior events. `physics_tick` accepts a replacement `Load_Calculator` function.
    
    Blast radius controls both reach and power: direct load is `10 * max(0, radius - distance)`, with zero load for nonpositive radii. The fixed global `BLAST_LOAD_MULTIPLIER` is 10; increasing radius increases load at a fixed distance, without a fixed maximum. For example, a sample 0.5 units away receives load 5 at radius 1 and load 25 at radius 3, enough to fail strength 20. At the default radius 5.0 and strengths 35 / 20, subdivision samples can fail within 1.5 units and connection samples within 3.0. Impulses are `direction * load * mass * 0.2`, applied through each final survivor's center once at its own sample. A surviving default-material fragment receives less than roughly 7 units/second of added speed. Generated motion includes the parent's linear and angular motion; removed ancestors receive no blast impulse. New contact and joint reactions wait for the next solver step. Both tuning constants and the falloff live in `destruction.odin`. The torque reference length is one world unit, and global joint damping is 0.7. Flexibility zero selects a stiff weld; positive flexibility selects spring softness.
    
    Before a yard blast, a floor outline whose edge reaches failure load while its centre survives is refined using the existing generator and inherited connections. A failing cell is also refined when its extent exceeds the damage radius, preventing the huge floor root from turning into coarse children whose centres all miss the impact. Smaller failed cells retain ordinary generation and the conservative deletion shortcut. This lets local hits reach the huge floor root without generating its future detail at reset. An unsuccessful spatial split retains its original outline for the actual damage decision; a genuinely failed subdivision still follows the existing direct-removal rule. The ordinary centre-sampled blast then resolves damage; all refinement shares one structural revision and only final survivors receive physics bodies and impulses. The optional physics support plane anchors connected pieces with a reference edge at the base, so subdivision alone does not introduce gravity loads into intact terrain. When a piece loses its last anchored connection, its existing bodies become dynamic with their logical mass and inertia. Logical links between anchored regions remain available to blast evaluation without creating unnecessary static-to-static solver constraints.
    
    Contact `totalNormalImpulse` is converted using the full tick interval. The installed binding's tangent and rolling impulses use the final substep interval. Joint reactions already supply force and torque. See the [Box2D simulation documentation](https://box2d.org/documentation/md_simulation.html) and [contact solver source](https://github.com/erincatto/box2d/blob/v3.1.1/src/contact_solver.c) for the underlying quantities.
    
    Collision decomposition merges adjacent convex regions. Box2D can collapse microscopic ears during hull welding; those ears are omitted from fixtures, and a subdivision with no resolvable fixture receives a small bounding box proxy. The destruction outline, logical identity, polygon mass and inertia remain retained. Collision fixtures never become additional destruction entities.
    
    Group width is the minimum projection width of its reference geometry's convex hull. Small subdivisions remain live when their connected group is wide enough. Narrow resulting groups become one second visual remnants before fading. New groups are filtered before any new bodies are created. Rendering interpolates poses and optionally blends shared presentation vertices across flexible joints; it does not modify collision or failure geometry.

    package main
    
    import "core:math"
    import "core:sync"
    import "core:testing"
    
    // Independent double-precision area and triangle intersection checks catch
    // compensating gaps/overlaps that a sum of the generator's f32 areas can miss.
    Partition_Point :: struct { x,y: f64 }
    partition_area :: proc(points: []Vec2) -> f64 {
        area: f64
        for p,i in points {
            q:=points[(i+1)%len(points)]
            area+=(f64(p.x)-f64(points[0].x))*(f64(q.y)-f64(points[0].y))-(f64(p.y)-f64(points[0].y))*(f64(q.x)-f64(points[0].x))
        }
        return math.abs(area)*0.5
    }
    partition_side :: proc(a,b,p: Partition_Point) -> f64 { return (b.x-a.x)*(p.y-a.y)-(b.y-a.y)*(p.x-a.x) }
    partition_triangle_overlap :: proc(a,b: Polygon) -> f64 {
        points: [12]Partition_Point
        for p,i in a.points { points[i]={f64(p.x),f64(p.y)} }
        count:=len(a.points)
        clip: [3]Partition_Point
        for p,i in b.points { clip[i]={f64(p.x),f64(p.y)} }
        orientation:=f64(1)
        if partition_side(clip[0],clip[1],clip[2])<0 { orientation=-1 }
        for edge in 0..<3 {
            next: [12]Partition_Point
            next_count:=0
            for i in 0..<count {
                p,q:=points[i],points[(i+1)%count]
                ps:=orientation*partition_side(clip[edge],clip[(edge+1)%3],p)
                qs:=orientation*partition_side(clip[edge],clip[(edge+1)%3],q)
                if ps>=0 { next[next_count]=p; next_count+=1 }
                if (ps>=0)!=(qs>=0) {
                    fraction:=ps/(ps-qs)
                    next[next_count]={p.x+(q.x-p.x)*fraction,p.y+(q.y-p.y)*fraction}; next_count+=1
                }
            }
            points=next; count=next_count
        }
        area: f64
        for i in 0..<count { area+=partition_side(points[0],points[i],points[(i+1)%count]) }
        return math.abs(area)*0.5
    }
    expect_generation_partition :: proc(t: ^testing.T,parent: Polygon,children: []Polygon) {
        testing.expect(t,len(children)>=2)
        parent_area:=partition_area(parent.points)
        tolerance:=max(f64(0.00000005),parent_area*0.00005)
        parent_triangles:=triangulate_polygon(parent)
        defer { for triangle in parent_triangles { delete(triangle.points) }; delete(parent_triangles) }
        triangles: [dynamic][dynamic]Polygon
        defer { for batch in triangles { for triangle in batch { delete(triangle.points) }; delete(batch) }; delete(triangles) }
        area: f64
        for child in children {
            child_area:=partition_area(child.points)
            area+=child_area
            testing.expect(t,child_area>0 && child_area<parent_area)
            parts:=triangulate_polygon(child)
            inside: f64
            for part in parts { for triangle in parent_triangles { inside+=partition_triangle_overlap(part,triangle) } }
            testing.expectf(t,math.abs(inside-child_area)<=tolerance,"Every child must stay within its parent, including displaced seams: area %.8f, clipped %.8f, points %v",child_area,inside,child.points)
            append(&triangles,parts)
        }
        testing.expect(t,math.abs(area-parent_area)<=tolerance,"The partition must preserve its parent's area")
        for i in 0..<len(triangles) {
            for j in i+1..<len(triangles) {
                overlap: f64
                for a in triangles[i] { for b in triangles[j] { overlap+=partition_triangle_overlap(a,b) } }
                testing.expect(t,overlap<=tolerance,"Sibling interiors must not overlap")
            }
        }
        // Each child edge must be covered by the parent boundary or an exact sibling
        // seam. T junctions may split one side into several collinear segments.
        for child,i in children {
            perimeter,covered:=f32(0),f32(0)
            boundaries: [dynamic]Polygon
            append(&boundaries,parent)
            for other,j in children { if i!=j { append(&boundaries,other) } }
            for p,k in child.points {
                q:=child.points[(k+1)%len(child.points)]
                length:=vlen(vsub(q,p)); perimeter+=length
                if length==0 { continue }
                unit:=vmul(vsub(q,p),1/length)
                intervals: [dynamic][2]f32
                for other in boundaries {
                    for a,j in other.points {
                        if seam,ok:=segment_overlap(Segment{p,q},Segment{a,other.points[(j+1)%len(other.points)]}); ok {
                            lo,hi:=vdot(vsub(seam.a,p),unit),vdot(vsub(seam.b,p),unit)
                            append(&intervals,[2]f32{max(f32(0),min(lo,hi)),min(length,max(lo,hi))})
                        }
                    }
                }
                for j in 1..<len(intervals) {
                    n:=j
                    for n>0 && intervals[n][0]<intervals[n-1][0] { intervals[n],intervals[n-1]=intervals[n-1],intervals[n]; n-=1 }
                }
                // Measure the union: tolerance-near seams can overlap, and a duplicate
                // match must neither fail coverage nor cancel a real gap elsewhere.
                end:=f32(0)
                for interval in intervals {
                    if interval[1]>end { covered+=interval[1]-max(end,interval[0]); end=interval[1] }
                }
                delete(intervals)
            }
            delete(boundaries)
            testing.expectf(t,math.abs(covered-perimeter)<0.0001,"Every generated edge must retain a matching shared boundary: perimeter %.8f, coverage %.8f, points %v",perimeter,covered,child.points)
        }
    }
    
    @(test)
    triangulation_keeps_small_valid_corners_from_refined_ground :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        a:=[8]Vec2{{4.5152297,-0.4394615},{4.5316315,-0.7697342},{4.5756717,-0.84055817},{4.6283793,-0.9051913},{4.6355357,-0.6723415},{4.6283793,-0.43949175},{4.6283793,-0.4394615},{4.5718045,-0.44398749}}
        b:=[7]Vec2{{4.7738128,-0.43949175},{4.757686,0},{4.6283793,0},{4.6197467,-0.21973075},{4.6283793,-0.4394615},{4.6283793,-0.43949175},{4.701096,-0.43367442}}
        fixtures:=[2]Polygon{{points=a[:]},{points=b[:]}}
        for parent in fixtures {
            parts:=triangulate_polygon(parent)
            defer { for part in parts { delete(part.points) }; delete(parts) }
            testing.expect(t,len(parts)==len(parent.points)-2,"Every ear of these simple outlines must be retained")
            expect_generation_partition(t,parent,parts[:])
        }
    }
    
    @(test)
    concave_generation_merges_ears_and_preserves_material_patterns :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        points:=[4]Vec2{{1.5,0.005},{2.35,0.005},{2.35,0.855},{1.5,0.855}}
        parent:=Polygon{points=points[:]}
        seeds:=[4]u8{42,85,177,98}
        for pattern in 0..<3 {
            recipe:=material_preset(pattern)
            concave_parents:=0
            refined_triangles:=0
            for seed in seeds {
                // Sweep the affected non-triangular recipes; one known Shatter fixture
                // checks that its deliberately triangular generations remain available.
                if recipe.triangulate && seed!=42 { continue }
                children:=generate_children(parent,recipe,seed)
                defer { for child in children { delete(child.points) }; delete(children) }
                if !testing.expectf(t,len(children)>=2,"Pattern %d, seed %d did not produce a partition",pattern,seed) { continue }
                expect_generation_partition(t,parent,children[:])
                if !recipe.triangulate { testing.expect(t,len(children)==recipe.generation_count) }
                largest:=0
                for child,i in children { if polygon_area(child)>polygon_area(children[largest]) { largest=i } }
                for child,i in children {
                    if recipe.triangulate {
                        testing.expect(t,len(child.points)==3,"Shatter deliberately retains triangular subdivisions")
                        if i!=largest { continue } // Refine a triangle large enough for the existing area guard.
                    }
                    if !is_convex(child) { concave_parents+=1 }
                    if pattern==1 {
                        lo,hi:=Vec2{1e30,1e30},Vec2{-1e30,-1e30}
                        for point in child.points { lo={min(lo.x,point.x),min(lo.y,point.y)}; hi={max(hi.x,point.x),max(hi.y,point.y)} }
                        testing.expect(t,hi.y-lo.y>2*(hi.x-lo.x),"Splinter must keep its elongated cuts")
                    }
                    grandchildren:=generate_children(child,recipe,derive_seed(seed,u64(i+1)))
                    defer { for grandchild in grandchildren { delete(grandchild.points) }; delete(grandchildren) }
                    expect_generation_partition(t,child,grandchildren[:])
                    if !recipe.triangulate {
                        testing.expect(t,len(grandchildren)==recipe.generation_count,"A bent boundary must not turn triangulation ears into extra fragments")
                    }
                    for grandchild in grandchildren {
                        if pattern==0 {
                            lo,hi:=Vec2{1e30,1e30},Vec2{-1e30,-1e30}
                            for point in grandchild.points { lo={min(lo.x,point.x),min(lo.y,point.y)}; hi={max(hi.x,point.x),max(hi.y,point.y)} }
                            testing.expect(t,outline_width(grandchild.points)/max(hi.x-lo.x,hi.y-lo.y)>0.1,"Chunk must not create thin corner fans from small shared-edge bends")
                        }
                        if recipe.triangulate { testing.expect(t,len(grandchild.points)==3); refined_triangles+=1 }
                    }
                }
            }
            if !recipe.triangulate { testing.expect(t,concave_parents>0,"Shared-edge displacement must remain enabled in this regression") }
            else { testing.expect(t,refined_triangles>0) }
        }
    }
    
    @(test)
    yard_roots_get_distinct_deterministic_generation_contexts :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
        game:=sandbox_create(); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
        seeds: [10]u8
        for sub,i in game.scene.subdivisions {
            seeds[i]=sub.seed
            testing.expect(t,sub.seed!=0)
            for j in 0..<i { testing.expect(t,seeds[j]!=sub.seed,"Adjacent starting blocks must not reuse the same generation context") }
        }
        children_a:=generate_children(game.scene.subdivisions[0].outline,game.scene.materials[0],seeds[0])
        children_b:=generate_children(game.scene.subdivisions[1].outline,game.scene.materials[0],seeds[1])
        defer { for child in children_a { delete(child.points) }; delete(children_a); for child in children_b { delete(child.points) }; delete(children_b) }
        a:=vsub(centroid(children_a[0]),game.scene.subdivisions[0].rest_center)
        b:=vsub(centroid(children_b[0]),game.scene.subdivisions[1].rest_center)
        testing.expect(t,!close_vec(a,b),"Translated copies of neighboring blocks should not generate identical partitions")
        sandbox_reset(&game)
        for sub,i in game.scene.subdivisions { testing.expect(t,sub.seed==seeds[i],"Reset must repeat the applied setup's birth contexts") }
        game.applied.generate_children=false
        sandbox_reset(&game)
        for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { testing.expect(t,sub.seed==0,"Seed zero must still disable future generations") }
    }

            progress:=burst.age/BOMB_BURST_TIME
            color:=rl.Color{255,200,112,u8(220*(1-progress))}
            rl.DrawCircleLinesV(screen_point(view,burst.position),burst.radius*view.scale*(0.2+0.8*progress),color)
        }
        for bomb in game.bomb_rain.bombs {
            position:=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(bomb.body))
            if !game.panel_open { position=vadd(bomb.previous,vmul(vsub(position,bomb.previous),game.accumulator*60)) }
            center:=screen_point(view,position)
            radius:=BOMB_RADIUS*view.scale
            color:=rl.Color{245,206,133,255}
            if bomb.landed { color={255,132,112,255} }
            rl.DrawCircleV(center,radius,{39,42,50,255})
            rl.DrawCircleLinesV(center,radius,color)
            tip:=rl.Vector2{center.x+radius*0.5,center.y-radius*1.4}
            rl.DrawLineEx({center.x,center.y-radius*0.7},tip,2,color)
            rl.DrawCircleV(tip,2,color)
            if bomb.landed { rl.DrawRing(center,radius+3,radius+5,-90,-90+360*bomb.fuse/BOMB_FUSE,24,color) }
        }
    }
    sandbox_draw_world :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,view: View,poses: map[u64]Pose) {
        s:=&game.scene
        left,top:=screen_point(view,{-9.5,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM}),screen_point(view,{10.5,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM-YARD_BASE_DEPTH})
        rl.DrawRectangleRec({left.x,left.y,top.x-left.x,top.y-left.y},{42,58,68,255})
        rl.DrawLineEx(left,screen_point(view,{10.5,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM}),3,{116,151,151,255})
        for i in -15..=16 {
            x:=f32(i)*0.5
            rl.DrawLineEx(screen_point(view,{x,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM-0.04}),screen_point(view,{x+0.12,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM-0.20}),2,{66,86,91,255})
        }
        draw_scene(s,view,poses,game.selected,game.surface,game.inspection && game.joints,game.inspection)
        spawn:=screen_point(view,{PLAYER_SPAWN.x,0})
        rl.DrawLineEx({spawn.x-16,spawn.y+12},{spawn.x+16,spawn.y+12},3,YARD_ACCENT)
        rl.DrawText("SPAWN",i32(spawn.x)-24,i32(spawn.y)+27,12,YARD_MUTED)
        sandbox_draw_bombs(game,view)
        position:=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body))
        if !game.panel_open { position=vadd(game.previous_player,vmul(vsub(position,game.previous_player),game.accumulator*60)) }
    package main
    
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:fmt"
    
    // raylib 5.x automation event IDs (rcore.c); the Odin binding exposes the raw event.
    smoke_key :: proc(key: rl.KeyboardKey,down: bool) -> rl.AutomationEvent {
        type:=u32(1); if down { type=2 }
        return {type=type,params={i32(key),0,0,0}}
    }
    smoke_mouse :: proc(x,y: i32) -> rl.AutomationEvent {
        dpi:=rl.GetWindowScaleDPI()
        return {type=7,params={i32(f32(x)*dpi.x),i32(f32(y)*dpi.y),0,0}}
    }
    smoke_button :: proc(down: bool) -> rl.AutomationEvent {
        type:=u32(5); if down { type=6 }
        return {type=type,params={0,0,0,0}}
    }
    sandbox_smoke_frame :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,target: rl.RenderTexture2D,events: ..rl.AutomationEvent) {
        for event in events { rl.PlayAutomationEvent(event) }
        width,height:=f32(rl.GetScreenWidth()),f32(rl.GetScreenHeight())
        view:=sandbox_view(width,height)
        mouse:=rl.GetMousePosition()
        over_ui:=sandbox_over_hud(mouse,width,height,game.inspection)
        raw:=sandbox_read_input()
        input:=sandbox_route_input(game,raw,over_ui)
        if !raw.menu_pressed && !raw.reset_pressed {
            if !sandbox_inspect_input(game,world_point(view,mouse),view,over_ui) && input.blast_pressed { sandbox_blast(game,world_point(view,mouse)) }
        }
        sandbox_advance(game,1.0/60.0,input)
        poses:=make(map[u64]Pose); defer delete(poses)
        rl.BeginDrawing()
        rl.BeginTextureMode(target)
        rl.ClearBackground({19,28,42,255})
        sandbox_draw_world(game,view,poses)
        if !game.panel_open && !over_ui { sandbox_draw_aim(game,view,mouse) }
        action:=sandbox_draw_hud(game,width,height)
        rl.EndTextureMode()
        rl.EndDrawing()
        sandbox_handle_ui(game,action)
    }
    sandbox_smoke_click :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,target: rl.RenderTexture2D,x,y: i32) {
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(x,y),smoke_button(true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(x,y),smoke_button(false))
    }
    sandbox_smoke_inputs :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        rl.SetTargetFPS(0)
        target:=rl.LoadRenderTexture(rl.GetScreenWidth(),rl.GetScreenHeight())
        defer rl.UnloadRenderTexture(target)
        for _ in 0..<60 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(30,40)) }
        assert(game.player.grounded,"Player did not land")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.D,true))
        for _ in 0..<45 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target) }
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.D,false))
        assert(b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body).x>PLAYER_SPAWN.x+2,"D did not move the player")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.SPACE,true))
        assert(b2.Body_GetLinearVelocity(game.player.body).y>5,"Space did not jump")
        // Keep holding jump through landing: there must be no repeated jump.
        for _ in 0..<120 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target) }
        assert(game.player.grounded,"Holding Space repeated a jump")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.SPACE,false))
        revision:=game.scene.revision
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,1180,43)
        assert(game.panel_open && game.scene.revision==revision,"Settings click leaked into the world")
        pose:=b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body)
        for _ in 0..<30 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.D,true),smoke_key(.SPACE,true)) }
        assert(b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body)==pose,"Menu did not pause the player")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.D,false),smoke_key(.SPACE,false))
        // Begin a slider drag, close with Escape, release outside, then reopen by button.
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(820,294),smoke_button(true))
        assert(game.applied.blast_radius>5.1,"Radius slider did not update the preview value")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,true))
        assert(!game.panel_open && !rl.WindowShouldClose(),"Escape should resume without exiting")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,false),smoke_mouse(550,450),smoke_button(false))
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,1180,43)
        assert(game.panel_open,"Closing a slider during drag left toolbar buttons captured")
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,785,368)
        assert(game.draft.pattern==2 && game.applied.pattern==0,"Breakup choice should be staged")
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,400,416)
        assert(!game.draft.generate_children && game.applied.generate_children)
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,780,622)
        assert(!game.panel_open && game.scene.materials[0].triangulate && game.scene.pieces[0].seed==0,"Apply & Reset did not apply the staged settings")
        assert(game.scene.materials[0].subdivision_strength==35 && game.scene.materials[0].connection_strength==20 && game.scene.materials[0].flexibility==0,"Pattern changed independent tuning")
        a,b,c:=counts_runtime(&game.scene)
        assert(a==10 && b==11 && c==2,"Apply click also blasted the yard")
        // Blast outside the tower, then inspect and reset the moving result.
        view:=sandbox_view(1280,800)
        aim:=screen_point(view,{1,1.3})
        revision=game.scene.revision
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,i32(aim.x),i32(aim.y))
        remaining,_,_:=counts_runtime(&game.scene)
        assert(game.scene.revision>revision && remaining<10,"The first fresh world click after Apply did not blast")
        for _ in 0..<30 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target) }
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,true))
        assert(game.inspection)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,false))
        image:=rl.LoadImageFromTexture(target.texture)
        rl.ImageFlipVertical(&image)
        _ = rl.ExportImage(image,"sandbox-playthrough.png")
        rl.UnloadImage(image)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.R,true))
        assert(b2.World_GetCounters(game.scene.physics.world).bodyCount==12 && len(game.scene.subdivisions)==10,"R did not restore a clean yard")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.R,false))
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,1180,43)
        revision=game.scene.revision
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,785,230)
        assert(game.applied.blast_mode==.Falling_Bombs && game.scene.revision==revision,"Falling bombs toggle should apply without resetting the yard")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,false))
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,i32(aim.x),i32(aim.y))
        assert(game.scene.revision==revision,"World click still caused a manual blast in bomb mode")
        for _ in 0..<160 {
            sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target)
            if len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)>0 { break }
        }
        assert(len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)>0,"Bomb mode did not spawn a falling physics object")
        first_bomb:=game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].body
        for _ in 0..<180 {
            if game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed { break }
            sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target)
        }
        assert(game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed,"The falling bomb did not land")
        for _ in 0..<20 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target) }
        bomb_image:=rl.LoadImageFromTexture(target.texture)
        rl.ImageFlipVertical(&bomb_image)
        _ = rl.ExportImage(bomb_image,"sandbox-bombs-preview.png")
        rl.UnloadImage(bomb_image)
        for _ in 0..<45 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target) }
        assert(!b2.Body_IsValid(first_bomb),"The landed bomb did not explode and disappear")
        for _ in 0..<160 {
            if len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)>0 { break }
            sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target)
        }
        bomb_body:=game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].body
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,1180,43)
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,480,230)
        assert(game.applied.blast_mode==.Manual && len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)==0 && !b2.Body_IsValid(bomb_body),"Manual mode toggle did not remove pending bombs")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,false))
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,i32(aim.x),i32(aim.y))
        assert(game.scene.revision>revision,"Switching back did not restore manual blasts")
        // Restore generation through the real panel, then excavate both ends of the
        // single floor root in each breakup pattern. Keep rendered results for review.
        sandbox_set_radius(game,DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS.blast_radius)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,false))
        for pattern in 0..<3 {
            sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,1180,43)
            sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,468+i32(pattern)*168,368)
            if !game.draft.generate_children { sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,400,416) }
            sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,780,622)
            assert(!game.panel_open && game.applied.generate_children && game.applied.pattern==pattern)
            root:=game.scene.subdivisions[9].id
            for _ in 0..<30 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(30,40)) }
            positions:=[2]f32{6,-6}
            for x in positions {
                point:=screen_point(view,{x,0.2})
                sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,i32(point.x),i32(point.y))
                assert(!game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[root]].live,"A distant floor hit did not generate local destruction")
                for _ in 0..<60 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(30,40)) }
            }
            assert(b2.Body_IsValid(game.floor) && b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body).y>=YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM+PLAYER_HALF_HEIGHT-0.03,"Excavation opened the bottom of the screen")
            ground_image:=rl.LoadImageFromTexture(target.texture)
            rl.ImageFlipVertical(&ground_image)
            _ = rl.ExportImage(ground_image,rl.TextFormat("sandbox-ground-%d.png",pattern))
            rl.UnloadImage(ground_image)
        }
        fmt.println("Sandbox input smoke passed: movement, held jump, paused settings, slider drag, staged apply, blast, inspection, reset, both bomb-mode toggles, bomb landing and detonation, and destructible ground in all three patterns.")
    }
    package main
    
    import "core:math"
    import "core:sync"
    import "core:testing"
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    
    @(test)
    stronger_blast_still_excavates_when_the_huge_floor_centre_fails :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
        radii:=[2]f32{5,6}
        removed: [2]f32
        for radius,i in radii {
            // These strengths put the huge root centre outside radius 5's failure
            // region and inside radius 6's, reproducing the coarse-generation miss.
            settings:=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS; settings.blast_radius=radius; settings.fragment_strength=30; settings.connection_strength=24
            game:=sandbox_create(settings); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
            root:=game.scene.subdivisions[9]
            point:=Vec2{1,1.3}
            testing.expect(t,fails(blast_load(vlen(vsub(root.pose.position,point)),radius),settings.fragment_strength)==(radius==6))
            testing.expect(t,sandbox_blast(&game,point))
            area: f32
            for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { if sub.live && sub.rest_center.y<0 { area+=polygon_area(sub.outline) } }
            removed[i]=17*-YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM-area
            testing.expect(t,sandbox_valid_aim(&game.scene,{1,-0.25}),"Both powers must excavate below the impact")
            if radius==6 { testing.expect(t,sandbox_valid_aim(&game.scene,{1,-1}),"A failed huge parent must not turn into intact children across the crater") }
            expect_valid(t,&game.scene)
        }
        testing.expect(t,removed[0]>0 && removed[1]>removed[0],"The larger failure region must remove more floor in this fixture")
    }
    
    @(test)
    ground_root_refines_at_distant_blasts_and_preserves_coverage :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
        positions:=[2]f32{-6,6}
        for pattern in 0..<3 {
            for x in positions {
                settings:=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS; settings.pattern=pattern
                game:=sandbox_create(settings); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
                root:=game.scene.subdivisions[9]
                outline:=make_polygon(root.outline.points); defer delete(outline.points)
                testing.expect(t,root.seed!=0 && close(polygon_area(outline),17*-YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM))
                testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetType(game.scene.physics.bodies[root.id])==.staticBody)
                blast:=Blast{position={x,0.2},radius=game.applied.blast_radius}
                testing.expect(t,!fails(blast_load(vlen(vsub(root.pose.position,blast.position)),blast.radius),settings.fragment_strength),"The distant shot must miss the huge root's centre")
                testing.expect(t,sandbox_refine_ground(&game.scene,blast),"A reachable edge must generate detail even when the root centre survives")
                children: [dynamic]Polygon
                defer delete(children)
                for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { if sub.live && sub.rest_center.y<0 { append(&children,sub.outline) } }
                expect_generation_partition(t,outline,children[:])
                testing.expect(t,len(game.scene.physics.bodies)==10,"Refinement must finish before creating any replacement physics bodies")
                revision:=game.scene.revision
                testing.expect(t,sandbox_blast(&game,blast.position))
                testing.expect(t,game.scene.revision==revision+1,"All blast refinement must commit as one structural event")
                testing.expect(t,!game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[root.id]].live)
                testing.expect(t,sandbox_valid_aim(&game.scene,{x,-0.25}),"The impact must excavate a real hole")
                testing.expect(t,!sandbox_valid_aim(&game.scene,{-x,-0.25}),"Ground far from the shot must retain solid coverage")
                testing.expect(t,len(game.scene.subdivisions)>10+game.scene.materials[0].generation_count,"The floor must support multiple refinement generations")
                for _ in 0..<120 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
                testing.expect(t,b2.Body_IsValid(game.floor))
                expect_valid(t,&game.scene)
            }
        }
    }
    
    @(test)
    excavated_ground_keeps_player_bombs_and_rubble_above_screen_bottom :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
        settings:=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS; settings.blast_mode=.Falling_Bombs
        game:=sandbox_create(settings); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
        game.bomb_rain.until_drop=1000
        // Expose the base completely and retain one ordinary debris body. Infinite
        // strength isolates support contacts from the separate impact-failure tests.
        game.scene.materials[0].subdivision_strength=math.inf_f32(1)
        game.scene.materials[0].connection_strength=math.inf_f32(1)
        retained:=game.scene.subdivisions[3].id
        failures:=Failures{}; defer free_failures(&failures)
        for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { if sub.id!=retained { append(&failures.discard_subdivisions,sub.id) } }
        apply_failures(&game.scene,failures)
        physics_sync_structure(&game.scene)
        body:=game.scene.physics.bodies[retained]
        b2.Body_SetTransform(body,{2,2.5},b2.MakeRot(0))
        b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(body,{})
        bomb_spawn(&game,{-2,2})
        game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].fuse=100
        bomb:=game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].body
        for _ in 0..<240 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
        testing.expect(t,game.player.grounded && close(b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body).y,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM+PLAYER_HALF_HEIGHT))
        testing.expect(t,game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].landed && math.abs(b2.Body_GetPosition(bomb).y-(YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM+BOMB_RADIUS))<0.025)
        testing.expect(t,b2.Body_IsValid(body) && math.abs(b2.Body_GetPosition(body).y-(YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM+0.425))<0.025)
        testing.expect(t,b2.Body_IsValid(game.floor) && b2.Body_GetType(game.floor)==.staticBody)
        sizes:=[3]Vec2{{1280,800},{900,700},{1600,900}}
        for size in sizes {
            bottom:=screen_point(sandbox_view(size.x,size.y),{0,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM})
            testing.expect(t,bottom.y<size.y-56,"The unbreakable base must catch objects above the bottom HUD")
        }
        expect_valid(t,&game.scene)
    }
    
    @(test)
    ground_descendants_release_when_their_connection_to_support_breaks :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
        s:=new_scene(0.1); defer scene_destroy(&s)
        recipe:=material_preset(0)
        recipe.subdivision_strength=math.inf_f32(1); recipe.connection_strength=math.inf_f32(1)
        material:=add_material(&s,recipe)
        owner:=add_piece(&s,material,42)
        points:=[4]Vec2{{-1,-1},{1,-1},{1,1},{-1,1}}
        outline:=Polygon{points=points[:]}
        root:=add_subdivision(&s,owner,outline,Pose{position=centroid(outline)})
        append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].subdivisions,root)
        physics_init(&s,{0,-9.8},-1)
        testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetType(s.physics.bodies[root])==.staticBody)
        failures:=Failures{}; append(&failures.subdivisions,root)
        apply_failures(&s,failures); free_failures(&failures)
        physics_sync_structure(&s)
        loose:=u64(0)
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetType(s.physics.bodies[sub.id])==.staticBody,"Refinement alone must preserve the anchored piece's support")
            bottom:=f32(1e30)
            for point in sub.outline.points { bottom=min(bottom,point.y) }
            if bottom>-1 { loose=sub.id }
        }
        testing.expect(t,loose!=0,"The partition must include a region above the support edge")
        retained_body:=s.physics.bodies[loose]
        for c in s.connections { if c.live && (c.a==loose || c.b==loose) { append(&failures.connections,c.id) } }
        apply_failures(&s,failures); free_failures(&failures)
        physics_sync_structure(&s)
        body:=s.physics.bodies[loose]
        testing.expect(t,body==retained_body,"Release must preserve the existing physics handle")
        testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetType(body)==.dynamicBody,"Losing the last anchored connection must release an existing body")
        testing.expect(t,close(b2.Body_GetMass(body),polygon_area(s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[loose]].outline)),"Released ground must recover its logical polygon mass")
        before:=b2.Body_GetPosition(body)
        b2.Body_ApplyLinearImpulseToCenter(body,{0,2},true)
        physics_tick(&s,1.0/60.0)
        testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetPosition(body).y>before.y,"Detached ground must respond to impulses through the ordinary solver")
        expect_valid(t,&s)
    }
    
    Collision decomposition merges adjacent convex regions. Box2D can collapse microscopic ears during hull welding; those ears are omitted from fixtures, and a subdivision with no resolvable fixture receives a small bounding box proxy. The destruction outline, logical identity, polygon mass and inertia remain retained. Collision fixtures never become additional destruction entities.
    
    Group width is the minimum projection width of its reference geometry's convex hull. Small subdivisions remain live when their connected group is wide enough. Narrow resulting groups become one second visual remnants before fading. New groups are filtered before any new bodies are created. Rendering interpolates poses and optionally blends shared presentation vertices across flexible joints; it does not modify collision or failure geometry.
    
    ## Verification
    
    `odin test .` covers bridge and subdivision removal; surviving and broken inherited attachments; simultaneous endpoint replacement; processing and storage order independence; seed zero; subthreshold and infinite strengths; same-blast child and connection failure; shared terminal batches and mixed-width guards; termination even with a zero width cutoff; removal of unsplittable attached regions under repeated failure; valid partial partitions; radius-dependent blast power above strength 20; rotational motion inheritance; a single impulse per final survivor; rotation independent width; group filtering; retained bodies; concave collision fixtures; physical impacts; overloaded joints; replaceable load policies; flexibility; repeated blasts for all presets; snapshots; interpolation; and real TCP transfer of a wall and its split. Shortcut comparisons check exact surviving outlines, seeds, links, memberships, fading and motion against ordinary recursive evaluation for partial and complete deletion in all three patterns, including a later blast. Odin's test allocator tracks allocations and reports leaks.
    
    Sandbox checks exercise the intact tower under gravity, player movement and a full jump, buffered and coyote jumps, standing on and pushing an actual detached region, repeated clean resets after blasts and respawn, independent staged tuning, menu/UI input consumption, frozen fading, valid/invalid posed aim, and fixed framing at multiple window sizes. The playable controls and settings remain independent of the destruction transaction.
    
    Bomb checks cover gravity, airborne and side-contact fuse suppression, landing on the floor and destructible surfaces, a full second before detonation, multiple simultaneous explosions, current-radius destruction, removal of exploded and out-of-bounds bodies, independent random intervals and positions, deterministic resets, paused spawning/fuses and switching back to manual control without resetting geometry. Use a separate test output as shown above so running tests preserves the playable `BOM.exe`.
    
    Generation checks refine displaced outlines again in all three patterns, checking target counts, chunky versus elongated cuts, intentional Shatter triangles and distinct repeatable yard seeds.     deletion_shortcut_agrees_with_recursive_blasts :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        for pattern in 0..<3 {
            for whole in 0..<2 {
                a:=make_wall(42,0.08); defer scene_destroy(&a)
                b:=make_wall(42,0.08); defer scene_destroy(&b)
                scenes:=[2]^Scene{&a,&b}
                for s in scenes {
                    s.materials[0]=material_preset(pattern)
                    s.materials[0].subdivision_strength=6
                    s.materials[0].connection_strength=4
                    for &sub in s.subdivisions {
                        sub.pose.position=vadd(Vec2{2,-1},vrotate(sub.rest_center,0.7))
                        sub.pose.angle=0.7
                        sub.pose.velocity=vadd(Vec2{1,2},Vec2{-2*sub.pose.position.y,2*sub.pose.position.x})
                        sub.pose.angular_velocity=2
                    }
                }
                blast:=Blast{position=vadd(Vec2{2,-1},vrotate(Vec2{-1,0.25},0.7)),radius=3.5}
                if whole==1 { blast.radius=10 }
                blast_pass(&a,blast,true); blast_pass(&b,blast,false)
                testing.expect(t,len(a.subdivisions)<len(b.subdivisions),"The proven deletion must avoid actual generation work")
                expect_same_blast_result(t,&a,&b)
                if whole==0 {
                    remaining,_,_:=counts(&a)
                    testing.expect(t,remaining>0)
                    // Future events must also agree: a skipped earlier branch cannot
                    // shift seeds through IDs, piece regrouping or an RNG stream.
                    next:=Blast{position=vadd(Vec2{2,-1},vrotate(Vec2{3.3,-0.2},0.7)),radius=1.7}
                    blast_pass(&a,next,true); blast_pass(&b,next,false)
                    expect_same_blast_result(t,&a,&b)
                }
            }
        }
    }

Older implementation and tuning plans are historical references; their original instructions do not override subsequent decisions documented here. The default application is a small playable destruction yard. The original diagnostic lab and localhost snapshot transport remain available.
    README.md:33:Mode and radius changes are immediate, including inside settings. **Breakup style**, fragment strength, connection strength, flexibility and Generate children are staged until **Apply & Reset**. Resume keeps the previously applied setup. The style options are **Chunks / Strips / Shards**: typical chunky, elongated and triangular output, respectively, rather than strict geometric categories or material toughness. Strength and flexibility stay independent of style. Internal preset indices and names (`chunk`, `splinter`, `shatter`) remain unchanged, including in snapshots. The initial setup uses manual blasts, Chunks, seed 42, strengths 35 / 20, flexibility 0 (stiff welds) and radius 5.0. These strengths retain more material while releasing attachments over a wider area. Positive flexibility remains available in Settings. Turning Generate children off uses seed zero; geometry stays live until it fails.
    README.md:98:Generation clips convex regions. For a concave parent in Chunks or Strips, the existing convex decomposition merges adjacent triangulation ears before applying the requested cuts; a small shared-edge bend does not automatically become a fan of independent fragments. Non-triangulated generation retains its existing boundary jitter and displacement amount: each internal displaced cut is generated once and installed in both adjacent outlines, limited by clearance to other edges as well as area and length. Shards deliberately retains triangulation but skips shared-boundary displacement whenever the material's `triangulate` flag is enabled. This prevents added seam vertices from multiplying into excessive tiny triangles; existing triangulation validity fixes remain in effect. Outside boundaries remain intact. Count is a target before final triangulation; complex concave outlines and the Shards style can produce more children. If generation cannot produce a genuine partition of at least two smaller regions, the failed subdivision is removed directly. A valid partition is retained even when area limits prevent reaching the requested count. Aspect ratio biases cut direction. Self-intersecting outlines and polygons with holes are outside this implementation's input domain. Starting yard blocks derive distinct birth contexts from the applied seed and their stable grid coordinates; reset repeats the same contexts.
    README.md:102:Blast radius controls both reach and power: direct load is `10 * max(0, radius - distance)`, with zero load for nonpositive radii. The fixed global `BLAST_LOAD_MULTIPLIER` is 10; increasing radius increases load at a fixed distance, without a fixed maximum. For example, a sample 0.5 units away receives load 5 at radius 1 and load 25 at radius 3, enough to fail strength 20. At the default radius 5.0 and strengths 35 / 20, subdivision samples can fail within 1.5 units and connection samples within 3.0. Impulses are `direction * load * mass * 0.2`, applied through each final survivor's center once at its own sample. A surviving default-material fragment receives less than roughly 7 units/second of added speed. Generated motion includes the parent's linear and angular motion; removed ancestors receive no blast impulse. New contact and joint reactions wait for the next solver step. Both tuning constants and the falloff live in `destruction.odin`. The torque reference length is one world unit, and global joint damping is 0.7. Flexibility zero selects a stiff weld; positive flexibility selects spring softness.

## User

Implement a basic in-game material test editor in the current Odin sandbox. Keep it small and reuse the existing destruction and physics model.

**Editing and testing**

- Provide a palette: **Wood, Glass, Rubber, Stone**.
- While editing, pause simulation and let the user drag axis-aligned rectangles to place objects with the selected material.
- Show a rectangle preview while dragging. Reject degenerate placements and avoid initial overlaps.
- Right-click removes a placed object.
- Provide an obvious Edit/Test toggle. Preserve Space for jumping during testing.
- Entering Test builds a fresh simulation from the authored rectangles. Returning to Edit restores the undamaged layout.
- R during Test restores that same layout and seed. Edits remain in memory until the application closes.
- Start with a clear building area above the existing destructible ground and sealed base.

Keep the authored layout separate from damaged simulation geometry. A small list of rectangle bounds and material choices is sufficient. No saving/loading, pinning, rotation tools, undo system, or general scene framework.

**Materials**

Use a small fixed preset table built from the existing Material properties:

- **Wood:** elongated breakup using the current Strips recipe.
- **Glass:** brittle breakup using Shards, with boundary jitter disabled.
- **Stone:** broader breakup using Chunks; use the current 35/20 strengths as its starting baseline.
- **Rubber:** a connected internal grid that visibly bends/stretchs through soft joints, while individual cells remain removable at finite failure thresholds.

For rubber, use one consistent cell-size setting during construction. Its cells can be terminal—seed zero—so they remain live until failure but do not recursively acquire a different deformation mesh. Connections should withstand ordinary deformation long enough to demonstrate the rubber behavior.

Choose provisional wood/glass/rubber values using the existing fields and briefly report them. These are gameplay presets, not a new material simulation system.

Each placed object has one material. Separate objects collide normally without automatically becoming glued together. Keep the ground’s material independent of the currently selected palette item.

**Scope and existing behavior**

Keep blast radius, falling bombs, movement, inspection tools, and existing destruction rules. Material presets should determine object properties; global material sliders must not silently override them. Keep abstract diagnostic tuning available in the existing lab rather than building another editor panel.

Preserve deterministic generation, same-blast recursion, inherited connections, and one impulse per final survivor. Rubber uses ordinary dynamic bodies; the terrain rule that freezes an entire anchored group must not freeze rubber objects.

**Verification**

Run the existing tests and update the native smoke playthrough for the editor flow. Check placement, deletion, material assignment, Test/Edit transitions, repeatable reset, and UI input consumption.

Specifically verify that rubber deforms before breaking and that removing a cell leaves the remaining connected material functional. Inspect one breakup example per other material. Use focused checks, without a new capture or parameter-sweep framework.

        game:=sandbox_create(); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
        for _ in 0..<360 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
        a,b,c:=counts(&game.scene)
        testing.expect(t,a==10 && b==11 && c==2,"The tower and single floor root must remain intact under ordinary gravity")
        testing.expect(t,game.player.grounded)
        testing.expect(t,close(b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body).y,PLAYER_HALF_HEIGHT))
        for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { testing.expect(t,vlen(vsub(sub.pose.position,sub.rest_center))<0.04) }
        for _ in 0..<50 { sandbox_tick(&game,1,false) }
        testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body).x > PLAYER_SPAWN.x+2)
        sandbox_tick(&game,0,true)
        testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetLinearVelocity(game.player.body).y>5 && !game.player.grounded)
        max_height:=f32(0)
        for _ in 0..<150 {
            sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
            max_height=max(max_height,b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body).y)
        }
        testing.expect(t,max_height>2 && game.player.grounded,"One jump must reach its apex and land without another airborne jump")
        testing.expect(t,close(b2.Body_GetRotation(game.player.body).s,0))
        expect_valid(t,&game.scene)
    }
    
    @(test)
    player_stands_on_and_pushes_a_real_fragment :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
        game:=sandbox_create(); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
        // Detach a ground-level block, leaving an actual destruction body to stand on.
        id:=game.scene.subdivisions[3].id
        failures:=Failures{}
        for connection in game.scene.connections {
            if connection.a==id || connection.b==id { append(&failures.connections,connection.id) }
        }
        apply_failures(&game.scene,failures); free_failures(&failures)
        physics_sync_structure(&game.scene)
        body:=game.scene.physics.bodies[id]
        position:=b2.Body_GetPosition(body)
        b2.Body_SetTransform(game.player.body,{position.x,1.6},b2.MakeRot(0))
        for _ in 0..<120 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
        testing.expect(t,game.player.grounded && b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body).y>1.35,"Support must come from fragment contacts")
        // Move alongside the detached block and push it using the same collision world.
        b2.Body_SetTransform(body,{-1,0.43},b2.MakeRot(0))
        b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(body,{})
        b2.Body_SetTransform(game.player.body,{-2,0.6},b2.MakeRot(0))
        b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(game.player.body,{})
        for _ in 0..<30 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
        start:=b2.Body_GetPosition(body).x
        for _ in 0..<30 { sandbox_tick(&game,1,false) }
        testing.expect(t,b2.Body_IsValid(body),"Routine player contact should leave the fragment intact")
        if b2.Body_IsValid(body) { testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetPosition(body).x>start+0.05,"The player should physically push debris") }
    }

    sandbox_menu_and_ui_consume_input_without_catchup :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {

        game:=sandbox_create(); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
        _ = sandbox_route_input(&game,{},false)
