    package main
    
    import "core:math"
    
    Palette :: enum { Wood, Glass, Rubber, Stone }
    RUBBER_CELL_SIZE :: f32(0.4)
    Authored_Rect :: struct { lo,hi: Vec2, material: Palette, identity: u64 }
    Material_Editor :: struct {
    	enabled,editing,dragging: bool,
    	palette: Palette,
    	start,cursor: Vec2,
    	next_identity: u64,
    	objects: [dynamic]Authored_Rect,
    }
    // Gameplay presets use the ordinary material fields, not the diagnostic sliders.
    editor_material :: proc(choice: Palette) -> Material {
    	m: Material
    	switch choice {
    	case .Wood:
    		m=material_preset(1); m.name="wood"; m.subdivision_strength=28; m.connection_strength=22; m.flexibility=0
    	case .Glass:
    		m=material_preset(2); m.name="glass"; m.subdivision_strength=16; m.connection_strength=12; m.flexibility=0
    	case .Rubber:
    		m=material_preset(0); m.name="rubber"; m.subdivision_strength=90; m.connection_strength=120; m.flexibility=0.5
    	case .Stone:
    		m=material_preset(0); m.name="stone"; m.subdivision_strength=35; m.connection_strength=20; m.flexibility=0
    	}
    	return m
    }
    sandbox_editor_create :: proc() -> Sandbox {
    	game:=Sandbox{applied=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS,draft=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS,previous=make(map[u64]Pose),surface=true,joints=true}
    	game.editor.enabled=true; game.editor.editing=true
    	sandbox_reset(&game)
    	return game
    }
    editor_rectangle :: proc(a,b: Vec2,material: Palette) -> Authored_Rect {
    	return Authored_Rect{lo={min(a.x,b.x),min(a.y,b.y)},hi={max(a.x,b.x),max(a.y,b.y)},material=material}
    }
    editor_overlaps :: proc(a,b: Authored_Rect) -> bool {
    	return a.lo.x<b.hi.x && a.hi.x>b.lo.x && a.lo.y<b.hi.y && a.hi.y>b.lo.y
    }
    editor_valid_rectangle :: proc(editor: ^Material_Editor,r: Authored_Rect) -> bool {
    	if !valid_vec(r.lo) || !valid_vec(r.hi) || r.hi.x-r.lo.x<0.2 || r.hi.y-r.lo.y<0.2 { return false }
    	if r.lo.x< -7.5 || r.hi.x>8.5 || r.lo.y<0 || r.hi.y>4.8 { return false }
    	// Reserve the initial player's footprint, too; no body starts inside a solid.
    	spawn:=Authored_Rect{lo={PLAYER_SPAWN.x-PLAYER_RADIUS,0},hi={PLAYER_SPAWN.x+PLAYER_RADIUS,PLAYER_SPAWN.y+PLAYER_HALF_HEIGHT}}
    	if editor_overlaps(r,spawn) { return false }
    	for object in editor.objects { if editor_overlaps(r,object) { return false } }
    	return true
    }
    editor_place :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,a,b: Vec2) -> bool {
    	if !game.editor.editing || game.panel_open { return false }
    	r:=editor_rectangle(a,b,game.editor.palette)
    	if !editor_valid_rectangle(&game.editor,r) { sandbox_notice(game,"Place a rectangle above ground, clear of objects and spawn"); return false }
    	game.editor.next_identity+=1; r.identity=game.editor.next_identity
    	append(&game.editor.objects,r)
    	return true
    }
    editor_remove :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,point: Vec2) -> bool {
    	if !game.editor.editing || game.panel_open { return false }
    	for object,i in game.editor.objects {
    		if point.x>=object.lo.x && point.x<=object.hi.x && point.y>=object.lo.y && point.y<=object.hi.y {
    			ordered_remove(&game.editor.objects,i); return true
    		}
    	}
    	return false
    }
    sandbox_toggle_editor :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
    	if !game.editor.enabled || game.panel_open { return }
    	game.editor.editing=!game.editor.editing
    	game.editor.dragging=false
    	sandbox_reset(game)
    	if game.editor.editing { sandbox_notice(game,"Edit: undamaged layout restored") }
    	else { sandbox_notice(game,"Test: R restores this layout and seed") }
    }
    editor_build_objects :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
    	s:=&game.scene
    	materials: [4]int
    	for choice in Palette { materials[int(choice)]=add_material(s,editor_material(choice)) }
    	if game.editor.editing { return }
    	for object in game.editor.objects {
    		seed:=derive_seed(game.applied.seed,object.identity)
    		if object.material==.Rubber { seed=0 }
    		owner:=add_piece(s,materials[int(object.material)],seed)
    		nx,ny:=1,1
    		if object.material==.Rubber {
    			nx=int(math.ceil((object.hi.x-object.lo.x)/RUBBER_CELL_SIZE))
    			ny=int(math.ceil((object.hi.y-object.lo.y)/RUBBER_CELL_SIZE))
    		}
    		// Uniform fitted cells: one target size, no tiny leftover edge strips.
    		dx,dy:=(object.hi.x-object.lo.x)/f32(nx),(object.hi.y-object.lo.y)/f32(ny)
    		ids:=make([]u64,nx*ny)
    		for row in 0..<ny {
    			for column in 0..<nx {
    				x0,x1:=object.lo.x+f32(column)*dx,object.lo.x+f32(column+1)*dx
    				y0,y1:=object.lo.y+f32(row)*dy,object.lo.y+f32(row+1)*dy
    				points:=[4]Vec2{{x0,y0},{x1,y0},{x1,y1},{x0,y1}}
    				outline:=Polygon{points=points[:]}
    				id:=add_subdivision(s,owner,outline,Pose{position=centroid(outline)})
    				append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].subdivisions,id)
    				index:=row*nx+column; ids[index]=id
    				if column>0 { connection:=add_connection(s,ids[index-1],id); assert(connection!=0); append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].connections,connection) }
    				if row>0 { connection:=add_connection(s,ids[index-nx],id); assert(connection!=0); append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].connections,connection) }
    			}
    		}
    		delete(ids)
    	}
    }

    package main
    
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    
    editor_color :: proc(name: string) -> rl.Color {
    	switch name {
    	case "wood": return {180,136,82,230}
    	case "glass": return {106,191,215,195}
    	case "rubber": return {178,121,199,230}
    	}
    	return {143,158,164,230}
    }
    editor_screen_rect :: proc(view: View,r: Authored_Rect) -> rl.Rectangle {
    	lo,hi:=screen_point(view,{r.lo.x,r.hi.y}),screen_point(view,{r.hi.x,r.lo.y})
    	return {lo.x,lo.y,hi.x-lo.x,hi.y-lo.y}
    }
    sandbox_draw_editor :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,view: View) {
    	if !game.editor.editing { return }
    	for object in game.editor.objects {
    		box:=editor_screen_rect(view,object)
    		material:=editor_material(object.material)
    		rl.DrawRectangleRec(box,editor_color(material.name))
    		rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx(box,2,YARD_INK)
    		rl.DrawText(rl.TextFormat("%s",material.name),i32(box.x)+5,i32(box.y)+5,16,YARD_INK)
    	}
    	if game.editor.dragging {
    		r:=editor_rectangle(game.editor.start,game.editor.cursor,game.editor.palette)
    		box:=editor_screen_rect(view,r)
    		color:=rl.Color{111,220,190,100}
    		if !editor_valid_rectangle(&game.editor,r) { color={244,132,131,100} }
    		rl.DrawRectangleRec(box,color); color.a=255
    		rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx(box,2,color)
    	}
    }
    sandbox_editor_input :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,point: Vec2,over_ui: bool) {
    	if game.panel_open { game.editor.dragging=false; return }
    	if rl.IsMouseButtonPressed(.RIGHT) && !over_ui {
    		game.editor.dragging=false
    		editor_remove(game,point)
    	}
    	if rl.IsMouseButtonPressed(.LEFT) && !game.block_blast && !over_ui {
    		game.editor.dragging=true; game.editor.start=point
    	}
    	if game.editor.dragging {
    		game.editor.cursor=point
    		if rl.IsMouseButtonReleased(.LEFT) {
    			if !over_ui { editor_place(game,game.editor.start,point) }
    			game.editor.dragging=false
    		}
    	}
    }

    rubber_deforms_before_failure_and_survives_a_removed_cell :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
    	sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
    	game:=sandbox_editor_create(); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
    	game.editor.palette=.Rubber
    	testing.expect(t,editor_place(&game,{0,0},{2.4,0.8}))
    	sandbox_toggle_editor(&game)
    	owner:=game.scene.pieces[0].id
    	ids:=game.scene.pieces[0].subdivisions
    	initial_links:=len(game.scene.connections)
    	testing.expect(t,len(ids)==12 && initial_links==16)
    	for id in ids {
    		sub:=game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[id]]
    		testing.expect(t,sub.seed==0 && sub.owner==owner && b2.Body_GetType(game.scene.physics.bodies[id])==.dynamicBody)
    	}
    	for _ in 0..<60 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
    	// A local nudge deforms the soft mesh under normal finite failure checks.
    	b2.Body_ApplyLinearImpulseToCenter(game.scene.physics.bodies[ids[len(ids)-1]],{0,0.3},true)
    	max_gap,max_angle:=f32(0),f32(0)
    	for _ in 0..<12 {
    		sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    		for c in game.scene.connections {
    			if !c.live { continue }
    			a,b:=game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[c.a]],game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[c.b]]
    			max_gap=max(max_gap,vlen(vsub(posed_point(a,c.rest_point),posed_point(b,c.rest_point))))
    			max_angle=max(max_angle,math.abs(a.pose.angle-b.pose.angle))
    		}
    	}
    	live,links,pieces:=counts(&game.scene)
    	testing.expectf(t,live==13 && links==initial_links && pieces==2,"Ordinary deformation must precede failure: %d regions, %d links, %d pieces",live,links,pieces)
    	testing.expectf(t,max_gap>0.015 && max_angle>0.02,"Rubber must stretch and bend: gap %.4f, angle %.4f",max_gap,max_angle)
    	removed:=ids[8]
    	f:=Failures{}; append(&f.discard_subdivisions,removed)
    	apply_failures(&game.scene,f); free_failures(&f)
    	physics_sync_structure(&game.scene)
    	testing.expect(t,!b2.Body_IsValid(game.scene.physics.bodies[removed]))
    	live,links,pieces=counts(&game.scene)
    	testing.expect(t,live==12 && links>0 && pieces==2,"Removing one internal cell must leave the remaining grid connected")
    	for _ in 0..<120 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
    	live,links,pieces=counts(&game.scene)
    	testing.expect(t,live==12 && links>0 && pieces==2)
    	expect_valid(t,&game.scene)
    	// A sufficiently close ordinary radius-5 blast can remove finite cells.
    	testing.expect(t,sandbox_blast(&game,{-0.2,0.5}))
    	testing.expect(t,counts_live_subdivisions(&game.scene)<live)
    	expect_valid(t,&game.scene)
    }

            rl.DrawText("INSPECTION  /  F3",40,120,18,YARD_ACCENT)
            a,b,c:=counts_runtime(&game.scene)
            rl.DrawText(rl.TextFormat("%d regions  /  %d links  /  %d pieces",a,b,c),40,150,17,YARD_INK)
            rl.DrawText("Right click: select   Delete / Ctrl+click: remove",40,180,16,YARD_MUTED)
            rl.DrawText("Shift+click / X: break link   J: links   V: surface",40,204,16,YARD_MUTED)
            rl.DrawText("S: save snapshot   D: move   Space: jump",40,228,16,YARD_MUTED)
        }
        if game.panel_open { return sandbox_draw_panel(game,width,height) }
        return .None
    }
    sandbox_inspect_input :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,point: Vec2,view: View,over_ui: bool) -> bool {
        if !game.inspection || game.panel_open { return false }
        if rl.IsKeyPressed(.J) { game.joints=!game.joints }
        if rl.IsKeyPressed(.V) { game.surface=!game.surface }
        if rl.IsKeyPressed(.S) {
            if save_snapshot(&game.scene,"snapshot.json") { sandbox_notice(game,"Saved snapshot.json") }
        }
        if over_ui { return false }
        hover:=pick_subdivision(&game.scene,point)
        if rl.IsMouseButtonPressed(.RIGHT) { game.selected=hover }
        remove:=rl.IsKeyPressed(.DELETE)
        link:=rl.IsKeyPressed(.X)
        consumed:=false
        if rl.IsMouseButtonPressed(.LEFT) && !game.block_blast {
            if rl.IsKeyDown(.LEFT_CONTROL) || rl.IsKeyDown(.RIGHT_CONTROL) { game.selected=hover; remove=true; consumed=true }
            if rl.IsKeyDown(.LEFT_SHIFT) || rl.IsKeyDown(.RIGHT_SHIFT) { link=true; consumed=true }
        }
        failures:=Failures{}
        if remove && game.selected!=0 { append(&failures.discard_subdivisions,game.selected); game.selected=0 }
        if link {
            id:=pick_connection(&game.scene,point,24/view.scale)
            if id!=0 { append(&failures.connections,id) }
        }
        if len(failures.discard_subdivisions)+len(failures.connections)>0 {
            apply_failures(&game.scene,failures)
            physics_sync_structure(&game.scene)
            clear(&game.previous)
        }
        delete(failures.discard_subdivisions); delete(failures.connections)
        return consumed
    }
    sandbox_read_input :: proc() -> Sandbox_Input {
    editor_build_objects :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        s:=&game.scene
        materials: [4]int
        for choice in Palette { materials[int(choice)]=add_material(s,editor_material(choice)) }
        if game.editor.editing { return }
        for object in game.editor.objects {
            seed:=derive_seed(game.applied.seed,object.identity)
            if object.material==.Rubber { seed=0 }
            owner:=add_piece(s,materials[int(object.material)],seed)
            nx,ny:=1,1
            if object.material==.Rubber {
                nx=int(math.ceil((object.hi.x-object.lo.x)/RUBBER_CELL_SIZE))
                ny=int(math.ceil((object.hi.y-object.lo.y)/RUBBER_CELL_SIZE))
            }
            // Uniform fitted cells: one target size, no tiny leftover edge strips.
            dx,dy:=(object.hi.x-object.lo.x)/f32(nx),(object.hi.y-object.lo.y)/f32(ny)
            ids:=make([]u64,nx*ny)
            for row in 0..<ny {
                for column in 0..<nx {
                    x0,x1:=object.lo.x+f32(column)*dx,object.lo.x+f32(column+1)*dx
                    y0,y1:=object.lo.y+f32(row)*dy,object.lo.y+f32(row+1)*dy
                    points:=[4]Vec2{{x0,y0},{x1,y0},{x1,y1},{x0,y1}}
                    outline:=Polygon{points=points[:]}
                    id:=add_subdivision(s,owner,outline,Pose{position=centroid(outline)})
                    append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].subdivisions,id)
                    index:=row*nx+column; ids[index]=id
                    if column>0 { connection:=add_connection(s,ids[index-1],id); assert(connection!=0); append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].connections,connection) }
                    if row>0 { connection:=add_connection(s,ids[index-nx],id); assert(connection!=0); append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].connections,connection) }
                }
            }
            delete(ids)
        }
    }

    package main
    
    import "core:math"
    
    Palette :: enum { Wood, Glass, Rubber, Stone }
    RUBBER_CELL_SIZE :: f32(0.4)
    Authored_Rect :: struct { lo,hi: Vec2, material: Palette, identity: u64 }
    Material_Editor :: struct {
        enabled,editing,dragging: bool,
        palette: Palette,
        start,cursor: Vec2,
        next_identity: u64,
        objects: [dynamic]Authored_Rect,
    }
    // Gameplay presets use the ordinary material fields, not the diagnostic sliders.
    editor_material :: proc(choice: Palette) -> Material {
        m: Material
        switch choice {
        case .Wood:
            m=material_preset(1); m.name="wood"; m.subdivision_strength=28; m.connection_strength=22; m.flexibility=0
        case .Glass:
            m=material_preset(2); m.name="glass"; m.subdivision_strength=16; m.connection_strength=12; m.flexibility=0
        case .Rubber:
            m=material_preset(0); m.name="rubber"; m.subdivision_strength=45; m.connection_strength=90; m.flexibility=0.5
        case .Stone:
            m=material_preset(0); m.name="stone"; m.subdivision_strength=35; m.connection_strength=20; m.flexibility=0
        }
        return m
    }
    sandbox_editor_create :: proc() -> Sandbox {
        game:=Sandbox{applied=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS,draft=DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS,previous=make(map[u64]Pose),surface=true,joints=true}
        game.editor.enabled=true; game.editor.editing=true
        sandbox_reset(&game)
        return game
    }
    editor_rectangle :: proc(a,b: Vec2,material: Palette) -> Authored_Rect {
        return Authored_Rect{lo={min(a.x,b.x),min(a.y,b.y)},hi={max(a.x,b.x),max(a.y,b.y)},material=material}
    }
    editor_overlaps :: proc(a,b: Authored_Rect) -> bool {
        return a.lo.x<b.hi.x && a.hi.x>b.lo.x && a.lo.y<b.hi.y && a.hi.y>b.lo.y
    }
    editor_valid_rectangle :: proc(editor: ^Material_Editor,r: Authored_Rect) -> bool {
        if !valid_vec(r.lo) || !valid_vec(r.hi) || r.hi.x-r.lo.x<0.2 || r.hi.y-r.lo.y<0.2 { return false }
        if r.lo.x< -7.5 || r.hi.x>8.5 || r.lo.y<0 || r.hi.y>4.8 { return false }
        // Reserve the initial player's footprint, too; no body starts inside a solid.
        spawn:=Authored_Rect{lo={PLAYER_SPAWN.x-PLAYER_RADIUS,0},hi={PLAYER_SPAWN.x+PLAYER_RADIUS,PLAYER_SPAWN.y+PLAYER_HALF_HEIGHT}}
        if editor_overlaps(r,spawn) { return false }
        for object in editor.objects { if editor_overlaps(r,object) { return false } }
        return true
    }
    editor_place :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,a,b: Vec2) -> bool {
        if !game.editor.editing || game.panel_open { return false }
        r:=editor_rectangle(a,b,game.editor.palette)
        if !editor_valid_rectangle(&game.editor,r) { sandbox_notice(game,"Place a rectangle above ground, clear of objects and spawn"); return false }
        game.editor.next_identity+=1; r.identity=game.editor.next_identity
        append(&game.editor.objects,r)
        return true
    }
    editor_remove :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,point: Vec2) -> bool {
        if !game.editor.editing || game.panel_open { return false }
        for object,i in game.editor.objects {
            if point.x>=object.lo.x && point.x<=object.hi.x && point.y>=object.lo.y && point.y<=object.hi.y {
                ordered_remove(&game.editor.objects,i); return true
            }
        }
        return false
    }
    sandbox_toggle_editor :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        if !game.editor.enabled || game.panel_open { return }
        game.editor.editing=!game.editor.editing
        game.editor.dragging=false
        sandbox_reset(game)
        if game.editor.editing { sandbox_notice(game,"Edit: undamaged layout restored") }
        else { sandbox_notice(game,"Test: R restores this layout and seed") }
    }
    editor_build_objects :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        s:=&game.scene
        materials: [4]int
        for choice in Palette { materials[int(choice)]=add_material(s,editor_material(choice)) }
        if game.editor.editing { return }
        for object in game.editor.objects {
            seed:=derive_seed(game.applied.seed,0x10000+object.identity)
            if object.material==.Rubber { seed=0 }
            owner:=add_piece(s,materials[int(object.material)],seed)
            nx,ny:=1,1
            if object.material==.Rubber {
                nx=int(math.ceil((object.hi.x-object.lo.x)/RUBBER_CELL_SIZE-0.00001))
                ny=int(math.ceil((object.hi.y-object.lo.y)/RUBBER_CELL_SIZE-0.00001))
            }
            // Uniform fitted cells: one target size, no tiny leftover edge strips.
            dx,dy:=(object.hi.x-object.lo.x)/f32(nx),(object.hi.y-object.lo.y)/f32(ny)
            ids:=make([]u64,nx*ny)
            for row in 0..<ny {
                for column in 0..<nx {
                    x0,x1:=object.lo.x+f32(column)*dx,object.lo.x+f32(column+1)*dx
                    y0,y1:=object.lo.y+f32(row)*dy,object.lo.y+f32(row+1)*dy
                    points:=[4]Vec2{{x0,y0},{x1,y0},{x1,y1},{x0,y1}}
                    outline:=Polygon{points=points[:]}
                    id:=add_subdivision(s,owner,outline,Pose{position=centroid(outline)})
                    append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].subdivisions,id)
                    index:=row*nx+column; ids[index]=id
                    if column>0 { connection:=add_connection(s,ids[index-1],id); assert(connection!=0); append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].connections,connection) }
                    if row>0 { connection:=add_connection(s,ids[index-nx],id); assert(connection!=0); append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].connections,connection) }
                }
            }
            delete(ids)
        }
    }
    package main
    
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:math"
    
    Sandbox_Settings :: struct {
        blast_radius: f32,
        blast_mode: Blast_Mode,
        pattern: int,
        fragment_strength, connection_strength, flexibility: f32,
        generate_children: bool,
        seed: u8,
    }
    DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS :: Sandbox_Settings{blast_radius=5.0,fragment_strength=35,connection_strength=20,flexibility=0,generate_children=true,seed=42}
    YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM :: f32(-3)
    YARD_BASE_DEPTH :: f32(0.25)
    sandbox_material :: proc(settings: Sandbox_Settings) -> Material {
        material:=material_preset(settings.pattern)
        material.subdivision_strength=settings.fragment_strength
        material.connection_strength=settings.connection_strength
        material.flexibility=settings.flexibility
        return material
    }
    Sandbox :: struct {
        scene: Scene,
        editor: Material_Editor,
        floor: b2.BodyId,
        player: Player,
        bomb_rain: Bomb_Rain,
        applied,draft: Sandbox_Settings,
        previous: map[u64]Pose,
        previous_player: Vec2,
        panel_open,inspection,tuning_open,surface,joints: bool,
        block_jump,block_blast,jump_queued: bool,
        selected: u64,
        accumulator: f32,
        status: string,
        status_time: f32,
    }
    // Retain the original tower fixture for diagnostic behavior/terrain checks.
    // The playable application starts with sandbox_editor_create.
    sandbox_create :: proc(settings: Sandbox_Settings = DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SETTINGS) -> Sandbox {
        game:=Sandbox{applied=settings,draft=settings,previous=make(map[u64]Pose),surface=true,joints=true}
        sandbox_reset(&game)
        return game
    }
    sandbox_destroy :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        scene_destroy(&game.scene)
        delete(game.bomb_rain.bombs); delete(game.bomb_rain.bursts)
        delete(game.previous); delete(game.editor.objects)
        game^={}
    }
    sandbox_notice :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,text: string) { game.status=text; game.status_time=2.5 }
    sandbox_clear_input :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        game.accumulator=0
        game.jump_queued=false
        game.block_jump=true
        game.block_blast=true
        player_clear_input(&game.player)
        clear(&game.previous)
        game.previous_player=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body))
    }
    sandbox_reset :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        revision:=game.scene.revision+1
        scene_destroy(&game.scene)
        s:=&game.scene
        s^=new_scene(0.10)
        s.revision=revision
        ground_material:=sandbox_material(game.applied)
        if game.editor.enabled { ground_material=editor_material(.Stone) }
        material:=add_material(s,ground_material)
        seed:=game.applied.seed
        if !game.editor.enabled && !game.applied.generate_children { seed=0 }
        if game.editor.enabled {
            editor_build_objects(game)
        } else {
            owner:=add_piece(s,material,seed)
            // A stepped stack, with one common reference frame and real shared edges.
            for row in 0..<3 {
                for column in 0..<4-row {
                    // Start on the floor: the former 5 mm drop overloaded stiff joints on landing.
                    x,y:=f32(1.5)+f32(column)*0.85,f32(row)*0.85
                    points:=[4]Vec2{{x,y},{x+0.85,y},{x+0.85,y+0.85},{x,y+0.85}}
                    outline:=Polygon{points=points[:]}
                    id:=add_subdivision(s,owner,outline,Pose{position=centroid(outline)})
                    // Stable block coordinates give neighboring roots distinct birth contexts.
                    s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[id]].seed=derive_seed(seed,u64(row*4+column+1))
                    append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].subdivisions,id)
                }
            }
            for a in 0..<len(s.subdivisions) {
                for b in a+1..<len(s.subdivisions) { add_connection(s,s.subdivisions[a].id,s.subdivisions[b].id) }
            }
            for connection in s.connections { append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].connections,connection.id) }
        }
        // One large root, with future floor detail generated only near a blast.
        ground:=add_piece(s,material,derive_seed(seed,13))
        ground_points:=[4]Vec2{{-8,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM},{9,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM},{9,0},{-8,0}}
        ground_outline:=Polygon{points=ground_points[:]}
        id:=add_subdivision(s,ground,ground_outline,Pose{position=centroid(ground_outline)})
        append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[ground]].subdivisions,id)
        physics_init(s,{0,-9.8},YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM)
        def:=b2.DefaultBodyDef()
        def.position={0.5,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM-YARD_BASE_DEPTH*0.5}
        game.floor=b2.CreateBody(s.physics.world,def)
        shape:=b2.DefaultShapeDef(); shape.material.friction=0.65
        // Extend beyond the playable edges so excavation never opens the screen bottom.
        _ = b2.CreatePolygonShape(game.floor,shape,b2.MakeBox(10,YARD_BASE_DEPTH*0.5))
        game.player=player_create(s.physics.world)
        bomb_rain_reset(&game.bomb_rain,game.applied.seed)
        game.selected=0
        game.editor.dragging=false
        sandbox_clear_input(game)
        sandbox_notice(game,"Yard reset")
    }
    sandbox_set_panel :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,open: bool) {
        game.panel_open=open
        game.editor.dragging=false
        if open { game.draft=game.applied }
        sandbox_clear_input(game)
    }
    sandbox_set_radius :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,radius: f32) {
        game.applied.blast_radius=clamp(radius,f32(0.5),f32(6))
        game.draft.blast_radius=game.applied.blast_radius
    }
    sandbox_apply_settings :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        game.applied=game.draft
        sandbox_reset(game)
        game.panel_open=false
        sandbox_notice(game,"Settings applied")
    }
    // Inclusive edges are solid too. Use the logical posed outline, not the cosmetic mesh.
    point_in_subdivision :: proc(sub: Subdivision,point: Vec2) -> bool {
        local:=vadd(sub.rest_center,vrotate(vsub(point,sub.pose.position),-sub.pose.angle))
        inside:=false
        for a,i in sub.outline.points {
            b:=sub.outline.points[(i+1)%len(sub.outline.points)]
            edge:=vsub(b,a); relative:=vsub(local,a)
            if math.abs(vcross(edge,relative))<0.00001 && vdot(relative,edge)>=0 && vdot(relative,edge)<=vdot(edge,edge) { return true }
            if (a.y>local.y)!=(b.y>local.y) && local.x<(b.x-a.x)*(local.y-a.y)/(b.y-a.y)+a.x { inside=!inside }
    # Odin destruction sandbox
    
    A standalone destruction sandbox using Odin's bundled Box2D, raylib and raygui libraries. This README is the authoritative description of current behavior and defaults. Older implementation and tuning plans are historical references; their original instructions do not override subsequent decisions documented here. The default application is a small playable destruction yard. The original diagnostic lab and localhost snapshot transport remain available.
    
    ## Run
    
    Requires an Odin installation with compiled `vendor:box2d` and `vendor:raylib` libraries. Tested on Windows with Odin `dev-2026-05-nightly:ea5175d`.
    
    ```powershell
    odin run .
    odin test . -out:BOM-tests.exe
    odin build . -o:speed -out:BOM.exe
    ```
    
    The application opens in **Edit**, paused, with a clear building area above the destructible floor and an invulnerable capsule player. Choose Wood, Glass, Rubber or Stone in the bottom palette and drag rectangles into the world. Click **Test** (or Enter) to build and run the layout; walk, jump onto or push debris, aim outside a solid shape and click to blast. Ordinary gravity runs at a fixed 60 Hz with four Box2D substeps. The camera keeps the yard framed when the window resizes. Falling outside the yard returns the player to spawn.
    
    The floor starts as one 17-by-3 rectangle with a deterministic generation context. Future detail is generated locally on demand, including for blasts near either end of that large outline. A connected ground section stays anchored while it retains an edge on the bottom support plane; sections cut free use ordinary dynamic physics. A thin indestructible base underneath spans beyond the playable edges and catches the player, bombs and rubble above the bottom of the screen. The fixed view includes the pit bottom. Aim just above the surface to excavate it; solid floor interiors follow the same invalid-origin rule as the tower. Reset restores the single floor root. Use this destructible-floor yard for subsequent destruction-feel comparisons.
    
    | Control | Action |
    | --- | --- |
    | Left drag in Edit | Preview and place a rectangle using the selected material |
    | Right click in Edit | Remove the authored object under the cursor |
    | Edit / Test button or Enter | Start a fresh test / restore the undamaged edit layout |
    | A / D or left / right arrows in Test | Move |
    | Space in Test | Jump, with a 0.1 second jump buffer and coyote window |
    | Left click in Test | One blast at a valid cursor position |
    | Mouse wheel over the world in Test | Adjust blast radius and power |
    | R / Reset button in Test | Rebuild the same authored layout and seed |
    | Tab / Escape / Settings button | Open settings and pause; close to resume |
    | F3 in Test | Toggle IDs, connections, counts and inspection tools |
    
    The aiming circle shows the active blast radius. A red cross and message mark origins inside or on live logical outlines; those blasts are suppressed. UI clicks do not blast the world. The settings panel pauses physics, fading and player actions without accumulating simulation time.
    
    In Settings, switch **Manual blasts / Falling bombs** to choose the explosion source immediately, without resetting the yard. Falling bombs spawn at random horizontal positions across the yard every 1â€“2.5 seconds. Each is an ordinary circle body that collides with the floor, debris and player. Its one-second fuse starts on first landing on a supporting surface, including the tower; airborne time and side contacts do not start the fuse. A red countdown ring marks a lit fuse. The body disappears when it explodes at its current position, using the current blast radius, with a brief expanding flash. Manual placement and its aiming circle are disabled in this mode. Returning to Manual clears pending bombs. Settings pauses drops, fuses and flashes along with physics. Reset clears bombs and repeats the applied seed's drop sequence, independently of destruction generation.
    
    Mode and radius changes are immediate, including inside Settings. Objects use fixed palette presets; global material sliders do not override them. Abstract recipe/strength/flexibility tuning remains in `--lab` (F4), separate from the editor. The initial setup uses manual blasts, seed 42, radius 5.0 and impulse scale 0.2. The independent ground uses Stone's Chunks recipe, strengths 35/20 and flexibility 0.
    
    The authored layout is a small in-memory list of rectangle bounds, material and stable identity, separate from damaged geometry. Entering Test, R during Test, and returning to Edit rebuild the scene without changing that list. Separate objects collide without acquiring shared logical connections. Editing pauses physics, bombs, fuses and fading. Dragging onto UI cancels placement. Rectangles must be at least 0.2 units wide/high, stay inside x [-7.5,8.5], y [0,4.8], and avoid existing rectangle interiors and the player's spawn footprint. Touching rectangle edges are allowed. There is no saving, loading, pinning, rotation or undo for authored layouts; application close discards them.
    
    | Palette material | Breakup | Fragment / connection strength | Flexibility |
    | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
    | Wood | Strips (`splinter` recipe) | 28 / 22 | 0 |
    | Glass | Shards (`shatter` recipe), no boundary jitter | 16 / 12 | 0 |
    | Rubber | Connected terminal grid | 45 / 90 | 0.5 |
    | Stone | Chunks (`chunk` recipe) | 35 / 20 | 0 |
    
    These provisional gameplay presets use the existing Material properties and shared solver. **Chunks / Strips / Shards** describe typical output, not strict geometric categories or toughness. Non-rubber objects begin as one live rectangle with future detail generated on demand. Each object receives a deterministic context derived from seed 42 and its stable authored identity (in a separate namespace from the ground); deleting another object does not reseed it.
    
    Rubber uses one construction setting, `RUBBER_CELL_SIZE = 0.4`: divide each rectangle into a uniform fitted grid whose cells are at most approximately that size. Each cell is an ordinary dynamic rigid body, joined to its grid neighbors by the existing soft welds. Cells have seed zero: they remain live until failure, without recursively replacing their deformation mesh. Links are only internal to that object. Rubber cannot be terrain-anchored because authored objects lie above the ground and never have reference edges on the bottom support plane.
    
    Material limitations: this is not a continuous elastic or volume-preserving material model. Rubber bends/stretches at soft joints while its cells remain rigid; sufficiently strong hits can remove cells and split the grid. Its higher connection strength lets normal deformation survive, while finite cell strength permits destruction. Wood/glass/stone toughness still depends on shape, size, impacts and the existing centroid samples; large or elevated brittle objects can fracture from landing loads, and strong blasts can erase most of them. The mass/density, friction, damping and center-applied blast impulse policies are unchanged.
    
    With F3 enabled: right click selects, Delete or Ctrl+click directly removes a region, Shift+click or X near an anchor breaks a connection, J toggles links, V toggles the cosmetic surface, and S saves `snapshot.json`. D and Space retain movement and jump in inspection mode.
    
    Run `odin run . -- --lab` for the original zero-gravity diagnostic fixture, F4 abstract material sliders (opening pauses; closing resumes), and its legacy shortcuts (projectile I, presets 1/2/3, terminal T, pause/step Space/N, radius Q/E, pan/zoom, and snapshot save/load S/L). The existing sender and receiver use that diagnostic fixture; player and indestructible-base replication are outside this local milestone. The logical destructible floor uses the ordinary geometry records.
    
    For automated execution:
    
    ```powershell
    odin run . -- --headless
    odin run . -- --smoke
    odin run . -- --smoke-settings
    odin run . -- --smoke-input
    ```
    
    `--headless` evaluates the original diagnostic blast, runs 60 physics ticks, validates the graph, writes `snapshot.json`, and reconstructs a receiver. `--smoke` renders the yard in a hidden window to `sandbox-preview.png`. `--smoke-settings` renders the expanded paused panel to `sandbox-settings-preview.png`. Both exit after two frames.
    
    `--smoke-input` uses raylib native automation events in a hidden window to exercise the actual palette widgets, drag preview and placement, overlap/degenerate rejection, right-click deletion, UI consumption, paused editing, Test/Edit restoration, R reset, movement and held jump, radius, inspection and falling bombs. It exports `sandbox-editor.png`, one breakup example each in `sandbox-material-wood.png`, `sandbox-material-glass.png`, `sandbox-material-stone.png`, and rubber views in `sandbox-material-rubber.png` and `sandbox-rubber-cell-removed.png`. The normal behavior suite stays independent of a window or display. The original tower setup remains an internal fixture for existing destruction, movement and terrain regressions; it is not the editor's initial layout.
    
    ## Live transmission
    
    Build once, then run these in separate terminals:
    
    ```powershell
    .\BOM.exe --serve
    .\BOM.exe --receive
    ```
    
    The sender listens on **127.0.0.1:9901** for one receiver. It sends explicit complete snapshots after structural changes and at 10 Hz for motion. The receiver renders polygons, connections, ownership and interpolated motion without simulating physics. Destroy or split the wall in the sender to see the receiver update.
    
    Frames contain a four byte little endian payload length followed by UTF-8 JSON, capped at 4 MiB. Partial reads, partial writes, coalesced frames and disconnects are handled. One in-flight send is retained; the sender does not accumulate a queue of old states. `read_state`, `encode_snapshot` and `decode_snapshot` can also be used with another transport.
    
    Snapshots carry current geometry, materials, stable IDs, piece memberships, future generation seeds, structural revision, and body motion. Version 2 retains each subdivision's birth seed context; version 1 snapshots still load using their original piece contexts. Widths and anchors are derived from the transmitted outlines. Infinite strengths have explicit flags so snapshots remain valid JSON. Seeds never reconstruct existing damaged geometry.
    
    ## Implementation
    
    | File | Responsibility |
    | --- | --- |
    | `model.odin` | Stable identity, shared reference vertex pool, birth contexts, cached outline widths, memberships and group filtering |
    | `geometry.odin` | Shared boundaries, displaced cuts, convex hull and collision decomposition |
    | `destruction.odin` | Seeded generation, blast evaluation and the shared structural update |
    | `physics.odin` | Box2D bodies, fixtures, weld joints, interaction aggregation and load policy |
    | `state.odin` | State reader, snapshot validation, serialization and pose interpolation |
    | `transmission.odin` | Framed localhost TCP snapshots and the receiver application |
    | `debug_view.odin` | Native controls, rendering and material presets |
    | `player.odin` | Capsule controller, contact support, buffered jumps and respawn |
    | `yard.odin` | Yard creation/reset, shared settings, aim validation, input routing and retained tower fixture |
    | `editor.odin` | Authored rectangle list, fixed material palette, validation, deterministic construction and Test/Edit transitions |
    | `editor_view.odin` | Rectangle previews, material colors and editor pointer input |
    | `editor_test.odin` | Placement, material assignment, layout/reset independence, input consumption and rubber deformation/removal |
    package main
    
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    
    YARD_INK :: rl.Color{229,239,241,255}
    YARD_MUTED :: rl.Color{144,165,178,255}
    YARD_ACCENT :: rl.Color{111,220,190,255}
    
    // Fit a fixed rectangle with letterboxing. Fragments never affect the camera.
    sandbox_view :: proc(width,height: f32) -> View {
        scale:=min((width-64)/16,(height-170)/8.4)
        return View{offset={width*0.5-0.5*scale,(height+30)*0.5+0.8*scale},scale=scale}
    }
    sandbox_settings_button :: proc(width: f32) -> rl.Rectangle { return {width-174,24,150,38} }
    sandbox_reset_button :: proc(width: f32) -> rl.Rectangle { return {width-284,24,98,38} }
    sandbox_over_hud :: proc(mouse: rl.Vector2,width,height: f32,inspection: bool) -> bool {
        if mouse.y<88 || mouse.y>height-56 { return true }
        return inspection && rl.CheckCollisionPointRec(mouse,{24,106,450,150})
    }
    sandbox_gui_style :: proc() {
        rl.GuiLoadStyleDefault()
        rl.GuiSetStyle(.DEFAULT,i32(rl.GuiDefaultProperty.TEXT_SIZE),18)
        rl.GuiSetStyle(.DEFAULT,i32(rl.GuiControlProperty.BORDER_COLOR_NORMAL),transmute(i32)u32(0x435969ff))
        rl.GuiSetStyle(.DEFAULT,i32(rl.GuiControlProperty.BASE_COLOR_NORMAL),transmute(i32)u32(0x233444ff))
        rl.GuiSetStyle(.DEFAULT,i32(rl.GuiControlProperty.TEXT_COLOR_NORMAL),transmute(i32)u32(0xe5eff1ff))
        rl.GuiSetStyle(.DEFAULT,i32(rl.GuiControlProperty.BORDER_COLOR_FOCUSED),transmute(i32)u32(0x6fdcbeff))
        rl.GuiSetStyle(.DEFAULT,i32(rl.GuiControlProperty.BASE_COLOR_FOCUSED),transmute(i32)u32(0x304e58ff))
        rl.GuiSetStyle(.DEFAULT,i32(rl.GuiControlProperty.TEXT_COLOR_FOCUSED),transmute(i32)u32(0xe5fff4ff))
        rl.GuiSetStyle(.DEFAULT,i32(rl.GuiControlProperty.BORDER_COLOR_PRESSED),transmute(i32)u32(0x6fdcbeff))
        rl.GuiSetStyle(.DEFAULT,i32(rl.GuiControlProperty.BASE_COLOR_PRESSED),transmute(i32)u32(0x416d68ff))
        rl.GuiSetStyle(.DEFAULT,i32(rl.GuiControlProperty.TEXT_COLOR_PRESSED),transmute(i32)u32(0xffffffff))
    }
    sandbox_slider :: proc(x,y,width: f32,label: cstring,value: ^f32,low,high: f32,decimals: bool = false) {
        rl.DrawText(label,i32(x),i32(y),17,YARD_INK)
        text:=rl.TextFormat("%.0f",value^)
        if decimals { text=rl.TextFormat("%.2f",value^) }
        rl.DrawText(text,i32(x+width)-rl.MeasureText(text,17),i32(y),17,YARD_ACCENT)
        _ = rl.GuiSliderBar({x,y+25,width,16},nil,nil,value,low,high)
    }
    Sandbox_UI_Action :: enum { None, Open, Resume, Apply, Reset, Toggle_Editor }
    sandbox_draw_panel :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,width,height: f32) -> Sandbox_UI_Action {
        rl.DrawRectangle(0,0,i32(width),i32(height),{8,14,23,205})
        x,y:=(width-560)*0.5,(height-360)*0.5
        rl.DrawRectangleRounded({x,y,560,360},0.025,8,{23,35,49,255})
        x+=28; y+=24
        rl.DrawText("SETTINGS / PAUSED",i32(x),i32(y),24,YARD_INK)
        y+=54
        mode:=i32(game.applied.blast_mode)
        _ = rl.GuiToggleGroup({x,y,248,32},"Manual blasts;Falling bombs",&mode)
        sandbox_set_blast_mode(game,Blast_Mode(mode))
        y+=48
        radius:=game.applied.blast_radius
        sandbox_slider(x,y,504,"Blast radius",&radius,0.5,6,true)
        sandbox_set_radius(game,radius)
        y+=70
        rl.DrawText("Objects use their palette material. Ground stays Stone.",i32(x),i32(y),16,YARD_MUTED)
        y+=26
        rl.DrawText("Abstract recipe tuning: launch with --lab (F4).",i32(x),i32(y),16,YARD_MUTED)
        y+=42
        if rl.GuiButton({x,y,504,36},"Resume") { return .Resume }
        return .None
    }
    sandbox_draw_bombs :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,view: View) {
        for burst in game.bomb_rain.bursts {
            progress:=burst.age/BOMB_BURST_TIME
            color:=rl.Color{255,200,112,u8(220*(1-progress))}
            rl.DrawCircleLinesV(screen_point(view,burst.position),burst.radius*view.scale*(0.2+0.8*progress),color)
        }
        for bomb in game.bomb_rain.bombs {
            position:=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(bomb.body))
            if !game.panel_open && !game.editor.editing { position=vadd(bomb.previous,vmul(vsub(position,bomb.previous),game.accumulator*60)) }
            center:=screen_point(view,position)
            radius:=BOMB_RADIUS*view.scale
            color:=rl.Color{245,206,133,255}
            if bomb.landed { color={255,132,112,255} }
            rl.DrawCircleV(center,radius,{39,42,50,255})
            rl.DrawCircleLinesV(center,radius,color)
            tip:=rl.Vector2{center.x+radius*0.5,center.y-radius*1.4}
            rl.DrawLineEx({center.x,center.y-radius*0.7},tip,2,color)
            rl.DrawCircleV(tip,2,color)
            if bomb.landed { rl.DrawRing(center,radius+3,radius+5,-90,-90+360*bomb.fuse/BOMB_FUSE,24,color) }
        }
    }
    sandbox_draw_world :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,view: View,poses: map[u64]Pose) {
        s:=&game.scene
        left,top:=screen_point(view,{-9.5,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM}),screen_point(view,{10.5,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM-YARD_BASE_DEPTH})
        rl.DrawRectangleRec({left.x,left.y,top.x-left.x,top.y-left.y},{42,58,68,255})
        rl.DrawLineEx(left,screen_point(view,{10.5,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM}),3,{116,151,151,255})
        for i in -15..=16 {
            x:=f32(i)*0.5
            rl.DrawLineEx(screen_point(view,{x,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM-0.04}),screen_point(view,{x+0.12,YARD_FLOOR_BOTTOM-0.20}),2,{66,86,91,255})
        }
        draw_scene(s,view,poses,game.selected,game.surface,game.inspection && game.joints,game.inspection,game.editor.enabled)
        sandbox_draw_editor(game,view)

| Glass — Shards, no jitter | 16 / 12 | 0 |
| Rubber — terminal grid | 45 / 90 | 0.5 |
| Stone — Chunks | 35 / 20 | 0 |

    package main
    
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:math"
    
    View :: struct { offset: Vec2, scale: f32 }
    screen_point :: proc(view: View,point: Vec2) -> rl.Vector2 { return {view.offset.x+point.x*view.scale,view.offset.y-point.y*view.scale} }
    world_point :: proc(view: View,point: rl.Vector2) -> Vec2 { return {(point.x-view.offset.x)/view.scale,(view.offset.y-point.y)/view.scale} }
    piece_color :: proc(id: u64,alpha: u8 = 255) -> rl.Color {
        colors := [6]rl.Color{{64,173,165,255},{97,142,206,255},{194,134,204,255},{212,161,88,255},{139,178,113,255},{211,116,125,255}}
        c:=colors[id%6]; c.a=alpha; return c
    }
    render_subdivision :: proc(s: ^Scene,sub: Subdivision,poses: map[u64]Pose) -> Subdivision {
        result:=sub
        if pose,ok:=poses[sub.id]; ok { result.pose=pose }
        return result
    }
    point_on_boundary :: proc(point: Vec2,a,b: Polygon) -> bool {
        for i in 0..<len(a.points) {
            for j in 0..<len(b.points) {
                if segment,ok:=segment_overlap(Segment{a.points[i],a.points[(i+1)%len(a.points)]},Segment{b.points[j],b.points[(j+1)%len(b.points)]}); ok {
                    d:=vsub(segment.b,segment.a); length:=vlen(d)
                    projection:=vdot(vsub(point,segment.a),d)/(length*length)
                    if projection >= -0.0001 && projection <= 1.0001 && math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(point,segment.a))) < 0.0001*length { return true }
                }
            }
        }
        return false
    }
    // Only presentation vertices are blended. Stored outlines and fixtures stay exact.
    cosmetic_point :: proc(s: ^Scene,sub: Subdivision,rest: Vec2,poses: map[u64]Pose) -> Vec2 {
        self:=render_subdivision(s,sub,poses)
        point:=posed_point(self,rest)
        flex:=clamp(s.materials[sub.material].flexibility,f32(0),f32(1))
        if flex==0 { return point }
        weighted:=point
        count:=f32(1)
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            other_id:=u64(0)
            if c.a==sub.id { other_id=c.b } else if c.b==sub.id { other_id=c.a }
            if other_id==0 { continue }
            other:=render_subdivision(s,s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[other_id]],poses)
            if point_on_boundary(rest,sub.outline,other.outline) { weighted=vadd(weighted,posed_point(other,rest)); count+=1 }
        }
        return vadd(point,vmul(vsub(vmul(weighted,1/count),point),flex))
    }
    draw_polygon :: proc(view: View,outline: Polygon,color: rl.Color,stroke: rl.Color) {
        triangles:=triangulate_polygon(outline)
        for triangle in triangles {
            a,b,c:=screen_point(view,triangle.points[0]),screen_point(view,triangle.points[1]),screen_point(view,triangle.points[2])
            // Raylib's triangle winding uses the screen's downward Y axis.
            cross:=vcross(vsub(triangle.points[1],triangle.points[0]),vsub(triangle.points[2],triangle.points[0]))
            if cross > 0 { rl.DrawTriangle(a,b,c,color) } else { rl.DrawTriangle(c,b,a,color) }
            delete(triangle.points)
        }
        delete(triangles)
        for i in 0..<len(outline.points) { rl.DrawLineEx(screen_point(view,outline.points[i]),screen_point(view,outline.points[(i+1)%len(outline.points)]),2,stroke) }
    }
    pick_subdivision :: proc(s: ^Scene,point: Vec2) -> u64 {
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            points: [dynamic]rl.Vector2
            for rest in sub.outline.points { p:=posed_point(sub,rest); append(&points,rl.Vector2{p.x,p.y}) }
    package main
    
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    
    editor_color :: proc(name: string) -> rl.Color {
        switch name {
        case "wood": return {180,136,82,230}
        case "glass": return {106,191,215,195}
        case "rubber": return {178,121,199,230}
        }
        return {143,158,164,230}
    }
    editor_screen_rect :: proc(view: View,r: Authored_Rect) -> rl.Rectangle {
        lo,hi:=screen_point(view,{r.lo.x,r.hi.y}),screen_point(view,{r.hi.x,r.lo.y})
        return {lo.x,lo.y,hi.x-lo.x,hi.y-lo.y}
    }
    sandbox_draw_editor :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,view: View) {
        if !game.editor.editing { return }
        for object in game.editor.objects {
            box:=editor_screen_rect(view,object)
            material:=editor_material(object.material)
            rl.DrawRectangleRec(box,editor_color(material.name))
            rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx(box,2,YARD_INK)
            rl.DrawText(rl.TextFormat("%s",material.name),i32(box.x)+5,i32(box.y)+5,16,YARD_INK)
        }
        if game.editor.dragging {
            r:=editor_rectangle(game.editor.start,game.editor.cursor,game.editor.palette)
            box:=editor_screen_rect(view,r)
            color:=rl.Color{111,220,190,100}
            if !editor_valid_rectangle(&game.editor,r) { color={244,132,131,100} }
            rl.DrawRectangleRec(box,color); color.a=255
            rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx(box,2,color)
        }
    }
    sandbox_editor_input :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,point: Vec2,over_ui: bool) {
        if game.panel_open { game.editor.dragging=false; return }
        if rl.IsMouseButtonPressed(.RIGHT) && !over_ui {
            game.editor.dragging=false
            editor_remove(game,point)
        }
        if rl.IsMouseButtonPressed(.LEFT) && !game.block_blast && !over_ui {
            game.editor.dragging=true; game.editor.start=point
        }

    sandbox_smoke_inputs :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        rl.SetTargetFPS(0)
        target:=rl.LoadRenderTexture(rl.GetScreenWidth(),rl.GetScreenHeight())
        defer rl.UnloadRenderTexture(target)
        assert(game.editor.editing && len(game.editor.objects)==0)
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,1180,43)
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,357,770)
        assert(game.editor.palette==.Wood && game.panel_open,"Settings must consume clicks on the underlying palette")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,false))
        pose:=b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body)
        for _ in 0..<60 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(30,40)) }
        assert(b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body)==pose,"Editing must pause simulation")
        // Use each actual palette widget and drag into the clear building area.
        for choice in 0..<4 {
            sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,69+i32(choice)*96,770)
            assert(int(game.editor.palette)==choice)
            x:=f32(choice)*2.0-2.0
            editor_smoke_drag(game,target,{x,0},{x+1.2,1.2})
            assert(len(game.editor.objects)==choice+1 && int(game.editor.objects[choice].material)==choice)
        }
        editor_smoke_drag(game,target,{-2,0},{-0.8,1.2})
        assert(len(game.editor.objects)==4,"Overlap was not rejected")
        editor_smoke_drag(game,target,{0,2},{0,3})
        assert(len(game.editor.objects)==4,"Degenerate rectangle was not rejected")
        // Right mouse deletes an authored object, not its damaged graph.
        p:=screen_point(sandbox_view(1280,800),{4.5,0.5})

    README.md:3:A standalone destruction sandbox using Odin's bundled Box2D, raylib and raygui libraries. This README is the authoritative description of current behavior and defaults. Older implementation and tuning plans are historical references; their original instructions do not override subsequent decisions documented here. The default application is a small playable destruction yard. The original diagnostic lab and localhost snapshot transport remain available.
    README.md:17:The floor starts as one 17-by-3 rectangle with a deterministic generation context. Future detail is generated locally on demand, including for blasts near either end of that large outline. A connected ground section stays anchored while it retains an edge on the bottom support plane; sections cut free use ordinary dynamic physics. A thin indestructible base underneath spans beyond the playable edges and catches the player, bombs and rubble above the bottom of the screen. The fixed view includes the pit bottom. Aim just above the surface to excavate it; solid floor interiors follow the same invalid-origin rule as authored objects. Reset restores the single floor root. Use this destructible-floor yard for subsequent destruction-feel comparisons.
    README.md:34:In Settings, switch **Manual blasts / Falling bombs** to choose the explosion source immediately, without resetting the yard. Falling bombs spawn at random horizontal positions across the yard every 1–2.5 seconds. Each is an ordinary circle body that collides with the floor, debris and player. Its one-second fuse starts on first landing on a supporting surface, including authored objects; airborne time and side contacts do not start the fuse. A red countdown ring marks a lit fuse. The body disappears when it explodes at its current position, using the current blast radius, with a brief expanding flash. Manual placement and its aiming circle are disabled in this mode. Returning to Manual clears pending bombs. Settings pauses drops, fuses and flashes along with physics. Reset clears bombs and repeats the applied seed's drop sequence, independently of destruction generation.
    README.md:53:With F3 enabled: right click selects, Delete or Ctrl+click directly removes a region, Shift+click or X near an anchor breaks a connection, J toggles links, V toggles the cosmetic surface, and S saves `snapshot.json`. D and Space retain movement and jump in inspection mode. Diagnostic snapshots contain simulation geometry, not the authored editor layout.
    README.md:55:Run `odin run . -- --lab` for the original zero-gravity diagnostic fixture, F4 abstract material sliders (opening pauses; closing resumes), and its legacy shortcuts (projectile I, presets 1/2/3, terminal T, pause/step Space/N, radius Q/E, pan/zoom, and snapshot save/load S/L). The existing sender and receiver use that diagnostic fixture; player and indestructible-base replication are outside this local milestone. The logical destructible floor uses the ordinary geometry records.
    README.md:61:odin run . -- --smoke
    README.md:62:odin run . -- --smoke-settings
    README.md:63:odin run . -- --smoke-input
    README.md:66:`--headless` evaluates the original diagnostic blast, runs 60 physics ticks, validates the graph, writes `snapshot.json`, and reconstructs a receiver. `--smoke` renders the yard in a hidden window to `sandbox-preview.png`. `--smoke-settings` renders the paused settings panel to `sandbox-settings-preview.png`. Both exit after two frames.
    README.md:68:`--smoke-input` uses raylib native automation events in a hidden window to exercise the actual palette widgets, drag preview and placement, overlap/degenerate rejection, right-click deletion, UI consumption, paused editing, Test/Edit restoration, R reset, movement and held jump, radius, inspection and falling bombs. It exports `sandbox-editor.png`, one breakup example each in `sandbox-material-wood.png`, `sandbox-material-glass.png`, `sandbox-material-stone.png`, and rubber views in `sandbox-material-rubber.png` and `sandbox-rubber-cell-removed.png`. The normal behavior suite stays independent of a window or display. The original tower setup remains an internal fixture for existing destruction, movement and terrain regressions; it is not the editor's initial layout.
    README.md:79:The sender listens on **127.0.0.1:9901** for one receiver. It sends explicit complete snapshots after structural changes and at 10 Hz for motion. The receiver renders polygons, connections, ownership and interpolated motion without simulating physics. Destroy or split the wall in the sender to see the receiver update.
    README.md:81:Frames contain a four byte little endian payload length followed by UTF-8 JSON, capped at 4 MiB. Partial reads, partial writes, coalesced frames and disconnects are handled. One in-flight send is retained; the sender does not accumulate a queue of old states. `read_state`, `encode_snapshot` and `decode_snapshot` can also be used with another transport.
    README.md:83:Snapshots carry current geometry, materials, stable IDs, piece memberships, future generation seeds, structural revision, and body motion. Version 2 retains each subdivision's birth seed context; version 1 snapshots still load using their original piece contexts. Widths and anchors are derived from the transmitted outlines. Infinite strengths have explicit flags so snapshots remain valid JSON. Seeds never reconstruct existing damaged geometry.
    README.md:93:| `state.odin` | State reader, snapshot validation, serialization and pose interpolation |
    README.md:94:| `transmission.odin` | Framed localhost TCP snapshots and the receiver application |
    README.md:103:| `sandbox_smoke.odin` | Hidden-window native input and widget playthrough |
    README.md:135:`odin test . -out:BOM-tests.exe` covers bridge and subdivision removal; surviving and broken inherited attachments; simultaneous endpoint replacement; processing and storage order independence; seed zero; subthreshold and infinite strengths; same-blast child and connection failure; shared terminal batches and mixed-width guards; termination even with a zero width cutoff; removal of unsplittable attached regions under repeated failure; valid partial partitions; radius-dependent blast power above strength 20; rotational motion inheritance; a single impulse per final survivor; rotation independent width; group filtering; retained bodies; concave collision fixtures; physical impacts; overloaded joints; replaceable load policies; flexibility; repeated blasts for all presets; snapshots; interpolation; and real TCP transfer of a wall and its split. Shortcut comparisons check exact surviving outlines, seeds, links, memberships, fading and motion against ordinary recursive evaluation for partial and complete deletion in all three patterns, including a later blast. Odin's test allocator tracks allocations and reports leaks.
    README.md:139:Bomb checks cover gravity, airborne and side-contact fuse suppression, landing on the floor and destructible surfaces, a full second before detonation, multiple simultaneous explosions, current-radius destruction, removal of exploded and out-of-bounds bodies, independent random intervals and positions, deterministic resets, paused spawning/fuses and switching back to manual control without resetting geometry. Use a separate test output as shown above so running tests preserves the playable `BOM.exe`.
    README.md:147:The implementation intentionally uses ordinary arrays, complete affected-piece membership rebuilds, local candidate scans, and explicit snapshots. Large-world spatial selection, compression, rollback and parallel simulation can be added when a measured workload calls for them.

    package main
    
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:fmt"
    
    // raylib 5.x automation event IDs (rcore.c); the Odin binding exposes the raw event.
    smoke_key :: proc(key: rl.KeyboardKey,down: bool) -> rl.AutomationEvent {
        type:=u32(1); if down { type=2 }
        return {type=type,params={i32(key),0,0,0}}
    }
    smoke_mouse :: proc(x,y: i32) -> rl.AutomationEvent {
        dpi:=rl.GetWindowScaleDPI()
        return {type=7,params={i32(f32(x)*dpi.x),i32(f32(y)*dpi.y),0,0}}
    }
    smoke_button :: proc(down: bool) -> rl.AutomationEvent {
        type:=u32(5); if down { type=6 }
        return {type=type,params={0,0,0,0}}
    }
    sandbox_smoke_frame :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,target: rl.RenderTexture2D,events: ..rl.AutomationEvent) {
        for event in events { rl.PlayAutomationEvent(event) }
        width,height:=f32(rl.GetScreenWidth()),f32(rl.GetScreenHeight())
        view:=sandbox_view(width,height)
        mouse:=rl.GetMousePosition()
        over_ui:=sandbox_over_hud(mouse,width,height,game.inspection && !game.editor.editing)
        raw:=sandbox_read_input()
        input:=sandbox_route_input(game,raw,over_ui)
        if !raw.menu_pressed && !raw.reset_pressed {
            if game.editor.editing { sandbox_editor_input(game,world_point(view,mouse),over_ui) }
            else if !sandbox_inspect_input(game,world_point(view,mouse),view,over_ui) && input.blast_pressed { sandbox_blast(game,world_point(view,mouse)) }
        }
        sandbox_advance(game,1.0/60.0,input)
        poses:=make(map[u64]Pose); defer delete(poses)
        rl.BeginDrawing()
        rl.BeginTextureMode(target)
        rl.ClearBackground({19,28,42,255})
        sandbox_draw_world(game,view,poses)
        if !game.panel_open && !over_ui { sandbox_draw_aim(game,view,mouse) }
        action:=sandbox_draw_hud(game,width,height)
        rl.EndTextureMode()
        rl.EndDrawing()
        sandbox_handle_ui(game,action)
    }
    sandbox_smoke_click :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,target: rl.RenderTexture2D,x,y: i32) {
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(x,y),smoke_button(true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(x,y),smoke_button(false))
    }
    sandbox_smoke_export :: proc(target: rl.RenderTexture2D,name: cstring) {
        image:=rl.LoadImageFromTexture(target.texture); rl.ImageFlipVertical(&image)
        assert(rl.ExportImage(image,name)); rl.UnloadImage(image)
    }
    editor_smoke_drag :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,target: rl.RenderTexture2D,a,b: Vec2) {
        view:=sandbox_view(1280,800)
        p,q:=screen_point(view,a),screen_point(view,b)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(i32(p.x),i32(p.y)),smoke_button(true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(i32(q.x),i32(q.y)))
        assert(game.editor.dragging,"Rectangle preview did not start")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(i32(q.x),i32(q.y)),smoke_button(false))
    }
    sandbox_smoke_inputs :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) {
        rl.SetTargetFPS(0)
        target:=rl.LoadRenderTexture(rl.GetScreenWidth(),rl.GetScreenHeight())
        defer rl.UnloadRenderTexture(target)
        assert(game.editor.editing && len(game.editor.objects)==0)
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,1180,43)
        assert(game.outlines)
        revision_before_toggle:=game.scene.revision
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,698,352)
        assert(!game.outlines && game.scene.revision==revision_before_toggle,"Outline toggle must only change presentation")
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,357,770)
        assert(game.editor.palette==.Wood && game.panel_open,"Settings must consume clicks on the underlying palette")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,false))
        pose:=b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body)
        for _ in 0..<60 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(30,40)) }
        assert(b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body)==pose,"Editing must pause simulation")
        // Use each actual palette widget and drag into the clear building area.
        for choice in 0..<4 {
            sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,69+i32(choice)*96,770)
            assert(int(game.editor.palette)==choice)
            x:=f32(choice)*2.0-2.0
            editor_smoke_drag(game,target,{x,0},{x+1.2,1.2})
            assert(len(game.editor.objects)==choice+1 && int(game.editor.objects[choice].material)==choice)
        }
        editor_smoke_drag(game,target,{-2,0},{-0.8,1.2})
        assert(len(game.editor.objects)==4,"Overlap was not rejected")
        editor_smoke_drag(game,target,{0,2},{0,3})
        assert(len(game.editor.objects)==4,"Degenerate rectangle was not rejected")
        // Right mouse deletes an authored object, not its damaged graph.
        p:=screen_point(sandbox_view(1280,800),{4.5,0.5})
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(i32(p.x),i32(p.y)),rl.AutomationEvent{type=6,params={1,0,0,0}})
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,rl.AutomationEvent{type=5,params={1,0,0,0}})
        assert(len(game.editor.objects)==3)
        editor_smoke_drag(game,target,{4,0},{5.2,1.2})
        assert(len(game.editor.objects)==4)
        // A drag ending over palette controls is cancelled.
        p=screen_point(sandbox_view(1280,800),{6,2})
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(i32(p.x),i32(p.y)),smoke_button(true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(60,770),smoke_button(false))
        assert(len(game.editor.objects)==4 && !game.editor.dragging)
        sandbox_smoke_export(target,"sandbox-editor.png")
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,930,43)
        assert(!game.editor.editing && len(game.scene.pieces)==5)
        revision:=game.scene.revision
        for _ in 0..<90 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(30,40)) }
        assert(game.player.grounded)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.D,true))
        for _ in 0..<15 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target) }
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.D,false),smoke_key(.SPACE,true))
        assert(b2.Body_GetLinearVelocity(game.player.body).y>5,"Space must jump in Test")
        for _ in 0..<120 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target) }
        assert(game.player.grounded,"Held jump must not repeat")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.SPACE,false))
        // Settings consume input and keep radius/mode live without material overrides.
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,1180,43)
        assert(game.panel_open && len(game.editor.objects)==4)
        pose=b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body)
        for _ in 0..<15 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.D,true)) }
        assert(b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body)==pose)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.D,false))
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,820,381)
        assert(game.applied.blast_radius>5.1)
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,640,500)
        assert(!game.panel_open)
        sandbox_set_radius(game,5)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,true))
        assert(game.inspection)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,false))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,false))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.R,true))
        assert(game.scene.revision>revision && len(game.editor.objects)==4 && !game.outlines,"Reset must preserve the outline preference")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.R,false))
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,930,43)
        assert(game.editor.editing && len(game.editor.objects)==4 && counts_live_subdivisions(&game.scene)==1)
        // One controlled breakup for each brittle/rigid material, through native clicks.
        choices:=[3]Palette{.Wood,.Glass,.Stone}
        for choice in choices {
            clear(&game.editor.objects)
            sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,69+i32(choice)*96,770)
            editor_smoke_drag(game,target,{1.5,0},{3.1,1.6})
            sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,930,43)
            original:=game.scene.subdivisions[0].id
            sandbox_set_radius(game,editor_material(choice).subdivision_strength/BLAST_LOAD_MULTIPLIER+1.2)
            aim:=screen_point(sandbox_view(1280,800),{1.2,0.8})
            sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,i32(aim.x),i32(aim.y))
            assert(!game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[original]].live,"Material example did not fracture")
            for _ in 0..<20 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(30,40)) }
            valid,message:=validate_scene(&game.scene); assert(valid,message)
            survivors:=0
            for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { if sub.live && sub.material==game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[original]].material { survivors+=1 } }
            assert(survivors>0,"The breakup example must retain visible material fragments")
            fmt.printf("%s breakup: %d surviving fragments\n",editor_material(choice).name,survivors)
            sandbox_smoke_export(target,rl.TextFormat("sandbox-material-%s.png",editor_material(choice).name))
            sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,930,43)
            assert(game.editor.editing && len(game.editor.objects)==1)
        }
        sandbox_set_radius(game,5)
        // Rubber: record a localized nudge, then a missing cell, using the same mesh.
        clear(&game.editor.objects)
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,261,770)
        editor_smoke_drag(game,target,{1,0},{3.4,0.8})
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,930,43)
        for _ in 0..<60 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(30,40)) }
        ids:=game.scene.pieces[0].subdivisions
        b2.Body_ApplyLinearImpulseToCenter(game.scene.physics.bodies[ids[len(ids)-1]],{0,0.3},true)
        for _ in 0..<6 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target) }
        sandbox_smoke_export(target,"sandbox-material-rubber.png")
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,false))
        cell:=game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[ids[len(ids)/2+2]]]
        p=screen_point(sandbox_view(1280,800),cell.pose.position)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_mouse(i32(p.x),i32(p.y)),rl.AutomationEvent{type=6,params={1,0,0,0}})
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,rl.AutomationEvent{type=5,params={1,0,0,0}})
        assert(game.selected==cell.id)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.DELETE,true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.DELETE,false))
        assert(!game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[cell.id]].live)
        for _ in 0..<60 { sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target) }
        valid,message:=validate_scene(&game.scene); assert(valid,message)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.F3,false))
        sandbox_smoke_export(target,"sandbox-rubber-cell-removed.png")
        // Bomb controls still use their native settings widgets and real contacts.
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,1180,43)
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,785,313)
        assert(game.applied.blast_mode==.Falling_Bombs)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,false))
        for _ in 0..<160 {
            sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target)
            if len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)>0 { break }
        }
        assert(len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)>0)
        first:=game.bomb_rain.bombs[0].body
        for _ in 0..<300 {
            sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target)
            if !b2.Body_IsValid(first) { break }
        }
        assert(!b2.Body_IsValid(first),"Falling bomb did not land and explode")
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,1180,43)
        sandbox_smoke_click(game,target,480,313)
        assert(game.applied.blast_mode==.Manual && len(game.bomb_rain.bombs)==0)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,true))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ESCAPE,false))
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ENTER,true))
        assert(game.editor.editing && len(game.editor.objects)==1)
        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,smoke_key(.ENTER,false))
        fmt.println("Editor native smoke passed: palette, drag preview, overlap/degenerate rejection, deletion, UI consumption, paused edit, Test/Edit restoration, reset, movement/jump, inspection, radius, material breakups, rubber, and falling bombs.")
    }

    $ Get-Content main.odin
    package main
    
    import "core:fmt"
    import "core:os"
    
    main :: proc() {
        for arg in os.args[1:] {
            if arg=="--smoke" { run_sandbox(true); return }
            if arg=="--smoke-settings" { run_sandbox(true,true); return }
            if arg=="--smoke-input" { run_sandbox(true,false,true); return }
            if arg=="--lab" { run_debug_view(false); return }
            if arg=="--headless" { run_headless(); return }
            if arg=="--serve" { run_debug_view(false,true); return }
            if arg=="--receive" { run_receiver(); return }
            if arg=="--help" { fmt.println("odin run . -- [--headless | --smoke | --smoke-settings | --smoke-input | --lab | --serve | --receive | --help]"); return }
        }
        run_sandbox()
    }
    
    run_headless :: proc() {
        s:=make_wall(42,0.08)
        defer scene_destroy(&s)
        physics_init(&s)
        fmt.println("Initial:",counts_runtime(&s))
        blast_pass(&s,Blast{position={1.5,0.5},radius=0.8})
        fmt.println("After blast:",counts_runtime(&s))
        for _ in 0..<60 { physics_tick(&s,1.0/60.0) }
        valid,message:=validate_scene(&s)
        assert(valid,message)
        assert(save_snapshot(&s,"snapshot.json"))
        fmt.println("After 60 ticks:",counts_runtime(&s),"| snapshot.json saved")
        receiver,ok:=load_snapshot("snapshot.json")
        assert(ok,"Snapshot receiver failed")
        defer scene_destroy(&receiver)
        fmt.println("Receiver:",counts_runtime(&receiver))
    }

    sandbox_draw_bombs :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,view: View) {
        for burst in game.bomb_rain.bursts {
            progress:=burst.age/BOMB_BURST_TIME
            color:=rl.Color{255,200,112,u8(220*(1-progress))}
            rl.DrawCircleLinesV(screen_point(view,burst.position),burst.radius*view.scale*(0.2+0.8*progress),color)
        }
        for bomb in game.bomb_rain.bombs {
            position:=from_b2(b2.Body_GetPosition(bomb.body))
            if !game.panel_open && !game.editor.editing { position=vadd(bomb.previous,vmul(vsub(position,bomb.previous),game.accumulator*60)) }
            center:=screen_point(view,position)
            radius:=BOMB_RADIUS*view.scale
            color:=rl.Color{245,206,133,255}
            if bomb.landed { color={255,132,112,255} }
            rl.DrawCircleV(center,radius,{39,42,50,255})
            rl.DrawCircleLinesV(center,radius,color)
            tip:=rl.Vector2{center.x+radius*0.5,center.y-radius*1.4}
            rl.DrawLineEx({center.x,center.y-radius*0.7},tip,2,color)
            rl.DrawCircleV(tip,2,color)
            if bomb.landed { rl.DrawRing(center,radius+3,radius+5,-90,-90+360*bomb.fuse/BOMB_FUSE,24,color) }
        }
    }

    sandbox_draw_aim :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,view: View,mouse: rl.Vector2) {

            rl.DrawLineEx({mouse.x+7,mouse.y-7},{mouse.x-7,mouse.y+7},2,color)
            label:=cstring("Aim outside the solid shape")

            y:=clamp(mouse.y+18,f32(94),f32(rl.GetScreenHeight()-80))
            rl.DrawRectangle(i32(x)-7,i32(y)-5,rl.MeasureText(label,16)+14,26,{19,28,42,240})
            rl.DrawText(label,i32(x),i32(y),16,color)

        }

            rl.DrawText("INSPECTION  /  F3",40,120,18,YARD_ACCENT)

            rl.DrawText(rl.TextFormat("%d regions  /  %d links  /  %d pieces",a,b,c),40,150,17,YARD_INK)
            rl.DrawText("Right click: select   Delete / Ctrl+click: remove",40,180,16,YARD_MUTED)
            rl.DrawText("Shift+click / X: break link   J: links   V: surface",40,204,16,YARD_MUTED)
            rl.DrawText("S: save snapshot   D: move   Space: jump",40,228,16,YARD_MUTED)
        }
        if game.panel_open { return sandbox_draw_panel(game,width,height) }
        return .None
