    package main
    
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    import "core:fmt"
    import "core:os"
    import "core:encoding/json"
    import "core:math"
    
    Wood_Origin :: struct { parent: u64, generation, born: int }
    Wood_Pair :: struct { self, other: u64 }
    Wood_Load :: struct {
    	contact,joint: f32,
    	contact_force,contact_torque: f32,
    	other, joint_id: u64,
    	joint_age: int,
    	contact_was_present,ancestor_contact: bool,
    }
    Wood_Size :: struct { id: u64, x,y,width,area: f32, seed: u8 }
    Wood_Event :: struct {
    	tick: int, phase: string, parent: u64, material,generation: int,
    	parent_size: Wood_Size, load: Wood_Load, children: [dynamic]Wood_Size,
    }
    Wood_Joint_Event :: struct { tick: int, phase: string, id,a,b: u64, age: int,load: f32 }
    Wood_Step :: struct {
    	tick: int, phase: string,
    	wood_subs,wood_links,wood_pieces,ground_subs,ground_links,ground_pieces: int,
    	max_speed,max_spin,max_joint_gap,wood_area: f32,
    	failed: bool,
    }
    Wood_Trace :: struct {
    	origin: map[u64]Wood_Origin, joint_birth: map[u64]int,
    	previous_contacts,contacts: map[Wood_Pair]bool,
    	loads: map[u64]Wood_Load,
    	events: [dynamic]Wood_Event, joint_events: [dynamic]Wood_Joint_Event, steps: [dynamic]Wood_Step,
    	tick: int, phase: string,
    }
    wood_trace: Wood_Trace
    
    wood_size :: proc(sub: Subdivision) -> Wood_Size {
    	lo,hi:=Vec2{1e30,1e30},Vec2{-1e30,-1e30}
    	for p in sub.outline.points { lo={min(lo.x,p.x),min(lo.y,p.y)}; hi={max(hi.x,p.x),max(hi.y,p.y)} }
    	return {id=sub.id,x=hi.x-lo.x,y=hi.y-lo.y,width=sub.width,area=polygon_area(sub.outline),seed=sub.seed}
    }
    wood_body_id :: proc(s: ^Scene,body: b2.BodyId) -> u64 {
    	for id,b in s.physics.bodies { if b==body { return id } }
    	return 0
    }
    wood_observe_contact :: proc(s: ^Scene,id: u64,other: b2.BodyId,i: Interaction) {
    	load:=interaction_load(i)
    	if load<=0 { return }
    	other_id:=wood_body_id(s,other)
    	pair:=Wood_Pair{id,other_id}
    	wood_trace.contacts[pair]=true
    	observed:=wood_trace.loads[id]
    	if load>observed.contact {
    		observed.contact=load; observed.other=other_id
    		observed.contact_force=vlen(i.force); observed.contact_torque=math.abs(i.torque)
    		observed.contact_was_present=wood_trace.previous_contacts[pair]
    		ancestor:=wood_trace.origin[id].parent
    		for ancestor!=0 {
    			if wood_trace.previous_contacts[Wood_Pair{ancestor,other_id}] { observed.ancestor_contact=true }
    			ancestor=wood_trace.origin[ancestor].parent
    		}
    		wood_trace.loads[id]=observed
    	}
    }
    wood_observe_joint :: proc(s: ^Scene,c: Connection,load_a,load_b,load: f32) {
    	age:=wood_trace.tick-wood_trace.joint_birth[c.id]
    	for id,index in [2]u64{c.a,c.b} {
    		endpoint_load:=load_a; if index==1 { endpoint_load=load_b }
    		observed:=wood_trace.loads[id]
    		if endpoint_load>observed.joint { observed.joint=endpoint_load; observed.joint_id=c.id; observed.joint_age=age; wood_trace.loads[id]=observed }
    	}
    	if fails(load,s.materials[s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]].material].connection_strength) {
    		append(&wood_trace.joint_events,Wood_Joint_Event{wood_trace.tick,wood_trace.phase,c.id,c.a,c.b,age,load})
    	}
    }
    wood_observe_parent :: proc(s: ^Scene,parent: Subdivision,seed: u8) {
    	event:=Wood_Event{tick=wood_trace.tick,phase=wood_trace.phase,parent=parent.id,material=parent.material,generation=wood_trace.origin[parent.id].generation,parent_size=wood_size(parent),load=wood_trace.loads[parent.id]}
    	append(&wood_trace.events,event)
    }
    wood_observe_children :: proc(s: ^Scene,parent: u64,children: []u64) {
    	event:=&wood_trace.events[len(wood_trace.events)-1]
    	assert(event.parent==parent)
    	for id in children {
    		child:=s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[id]]
    		wood_trace.origin[id]=Wood_Origin{parent,event.generation+1,wood_trace.tick}
    		append(&event.children,wood_size(child))
    	}
    }
    wood_record :: proc(s: ^Scene,failed: bool) -> Wood_Step {
    	step:=Wood_Step{tick=wood_trace.tick,phase=wood_trace.phase,failed=failed}
    	for sub in s.subdivisions {
    		if !sub.live { continue }
    		if sub.material==1 {
    			step.wood_subs+=1; step.wood_area+=polygon_area(sub.outline)
    			step.max_speed=max(step.max_speed,vlen(sub.pose.velocity)); step.max_spin=max(step.max_spin,math.abs(sub.pose.angular_velocity))
    		} else { step.ground_subs+=1 }
    	}
    	for c in s.connections {
    		if !c.live { continue }
    		a,b:=s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]],s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
    		if a.material==1 {
    			step.wood_links+=1
    			step.max_joint_gap=max(step.max_joint_gap,vlen(vsub(posed_point(a,c.rest_point),posed_point(b,c.rest_point))))
    		} else { step.ground_links+=1 }
    	}
    	for p in s.pieces { if p.live { if p.material==1 { step.wood_pieces+=1 } else { step.ground_pieces+=1 } } }
    	append(&wood_trace.steps,step)
    	return step
    }
    wood_tick :: proc(game: ^Sandbox) -> Wood_Step {
    	clear(&wood_trace.loads); clear(&wood_trace.contacts)
    	start_events,start_joints:=len(wood_trace.events),len(wood_trace.joint_events)
    	sandbox_tick(game,0,false)
    	for c in game.scene.connections {
    		if _,known:=wood_trace.joint_birth[c.id]; !known { wood_trace.joint_birth[c.id]=wood_trace.tick }
    	}
    	clear(&wood_trace.previous_contacts)
    	for pair in wood_trace.contacts { wood_trace.previous_contacts[pair]=true }
    	valid,message:=validate_scene(&game.scene); assert(valid,message)
    	return wood_record(&game.scene,len(wood_trace.events)>start_events || len(wood_trace.joint_events)>start_joints)
    }
    wood_render :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,target: rl.RenderTexture2D,path: cstring) {
    	poses:=make(map[u64]Pose); defer delete(poses)
    	view:=View{offset={-45,610},scale=300}
    	rl.BeginDrawing(); rl.BeginTextureMode(target)
    	rl.ClearBackground({19,28,42,255})
    	sandbox_draw_world(game,view,poses)
    	rl.EndTextureMode(); rl.EndDrawing()
    	sandbox_smoke_export(target,path)
    }
    wood_capture_pair :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,target: rl.RenderTexture2D,name: cstring) {
    	game.outlines=true; wood_render(game,target,rl.TextFormat("../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-impact/%s-on.png",name))
    	game.outlines=false; wood_render(game,target,rl.TextFormat("../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-impact/%s-off.png",name))
    	assert(save_snapshot(&game.scene,fmt.tprintf("../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-impact/%s.json",name)))
    }
    run_wood_diagnosis :: proc() {
    	wood_trace=Wood_Trace{origin=make(map[u64]Wood_Origin),joint_birth=make(map[u64]int),previous_contacts=make(map[Wood_Pair]bool),contacts=make(map[Wood_Pair]bool),loads=make(map[u64]Wood_Load)}
    	rl.SetTraceLogLevel(.WARNING); rl.SetConfigFlags({.WINDOW_HIDDEN,.MSAA_4X_HINT,.WINDOW_HIGHDPI})
    	rl.InitWindow(1280,800,"Wood diagnosis"); defer rl.CloseWindow(); rl.SetTargetFPS(0)
    	game:=sandbox_editor_create(); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
    	game.editor.palette=.Wood
    	assert(editor_place(&game,{1.5,0},{3.1,1.6}))
    	sandbox_toggle_editor(&game)
    	for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { wood_trace.origin[sub.id]={generation=0,born=-120} }
    	target:=rl.LoadRenderTexture(1280,800); defer rl.UnloadRenderTexture(target)
    	wood_trace.phase="initial settling"
    	for tick in -119..=0 { wood_trace.tick=tick; _=wood_tick(&game) }
    	wood_capture_pair(&game,target,"settled-before")
    	fmt.println("Initial settled:",wood_trace.steps[len(wood_trace.steps)-1])
    	// One controlled 0.30 m lift and release, no impulse and no further input.
    	for sub in game.scene.subdivisions {
    		if sub.live && sub.material==1 {
    			body:=game.scene.physics.bodies[sub.id]
    			position:=b2.Body_GetPosition(body); position.y+=0.3
    			b2.Body_SetTransform(body,position,b2.Body_GetRotation(body))
    		}
    	}
    	physics_read_motion(&game.scene)
    	wood_trace.phase="drop"
    	wood_capture_pair(&game,target,"drop-before")
    	game.outlines=false
    	for frame in 0..<15 { wood_render(&game,target,rl.TextFormat("frames/frame-%04d.png",frame)) }
    	last_change,quiet:=0,0
    	first_failure:=false
    	for tick in 1..=1200 {
    		wood_trace.tick=tick
    		step:=wood_tick(&game)
    		if step.failed {
    			last_change=tick
    			fmt.println("Change:",step)
    			if !first_failure { wood_capture_pair(&game,target,"first-failure"); first_failure=true }
    			assert(save_snapshot(&game.scene,fmt.tprintf("wave-%04d.json",tick)))
    		}
    		if tick%2==0 && tick<=360 { wood_render(&game,target,rl.TextFormat("frames/frame-%04d.png",14+tick/2)) }
    		if tick==30 { wood_capture_pair(&game,target,"early-after") }
    		if tick-last_change>120 && step.max_speed<0.005 && step.max_spin<0.005 { quiet+=1 } else { quiet=0 }
    		if quiet>=120 { fmt.println("Settled:",step); break }
    	}
    	wood_capture_pair(&game,target,"settled-after")
    	data,err:=json.marshal(wood_trace,{pretty=true}); assert(err==nil); defer delete(data)
    	assert(os.write_entire_file("trace.json",data))
    }

## Assistant

The rectangle survived the two-second initial settle as one body, so this case cleanly separates startup behavior from damage after release. I also caught a setup issue in the temporary driver: lifting a sleeping Box2D body does not wake it. I’ve corrected the driver so the body actually drops under gravity.

        def comps(snapshot,drop=()):
         ids={s['id'] for s in snapshot['subdivisions'] if s['material']==1}; adj={i:set() for i in ids}
         for c in snapshot['connections']:
          if c['id'] not in drop and c['a'] in ids and c['b'] in ids: adj[c['a']].add(c['b']);adj[c['b']].add(c['a'])
         out=[]
         while ids:
          todo=[min(ids)];found=set()
          while todo:
           x=todo.pop()
           if x in found: continue
           found.add(x);todo+=list(adj[x]-found)
          out.append(found);ids-=found
         return out
        parent={c['id']:e['parent'] for e in p['events'] for c in e['children']}
        for tick,before in [(27,26),(33,32)]:

         def ancestor(i):
          while i not in oldids: i=parent[i]
          return i
         projected={frozenset(ancestor(i) for i in g) for g in comps(b)}
         limited={frozenset(g) for g in comps(a,broken)}

    # Wood: internal refinement after one damaging drop
    
    **Verified result:** one damaging drop takes an initially intact Wood rectangle to **29 live regions, 42 links, 6 separate connected pieces**, with almost the same rectangular silhouette. Much of the additional detail remains inside stiff connected groups. This is logical geometry with a body per region, not rendering-only triangulation.
    
    ## Case and method
    
    One authored Wood rectangle, bounds (1.5, 0)–(3.9, 2.4), dimensions **2.4 × 2.4** world units. Yard seed **42**, authored identity **1**, derived object birth context **178**. Current Wood preset: fragment/connection strengths **28/22**, flexibility **0**, Strips recipe with generation count **5**, aspect ratio **0.2**, triangulation off and normal boundary displacement on. Gravity, density, friction, solver, ground and all other settings were unchanged (60 Hz, four substeps; minimum width 0.1). No blasts were used.
    
    The object first settled for 120 ticks on the existing destructible ground. **No Wood or ground subdivision occurred during this initial settling.** The sleeping rectangle was then lifted by 0.50 units, tilted 0.15 radians (8.59°), awakened, and released with no added velocity. Its lowest corner started about 0.334 above the ground. No further input or deliberate impacts were applied.
    
    Input-selection limitation: the existing 1.6 × 1.6 smoke-check example did not fail in preliminary 0.30-unit flat and slightly tilted drops. Those nondamaging checks are not the evidence for the conclusion below. The documented case uses the larger rectangle above; no material or physics parameters were swept. An initial capture-driver attempt also left the lifted body asleep; awakening it corrected that setup error.
    
    Temporary hooks observed the existing contact and joint load calculations and parent/child creation. The reported loads are the current calculator's equivalent force/torque loads, not impact energy. A second run with captures reproduced the same failure events, child geometry and structural timeline. The table uses that captured run.
    
    ## Generations
    
    Sizes below are undeformed axis-aligned bounding boxes, in world units. Ranges describe the generated shapes, not rectangular approximations used for physics. **S / L / P** means live Wood subdivisions / surviving Wood connections / separate connected Wood pieces, immediately after the stated update. Ground is excluded from these counts.
    
    | Generation/update | Time from release | Parents → children; sizes | Why failure continues | S / L / P |
    |---|---:|---|---|---:|
    | Initial settling | Before release | One 2.4 × 2.4 root; no children | No failure | 1 / 0 / 1 |
    | G1 | Tick 26, 0.433 s | Root → **5** strips, x extents **0.355–0.602**, each 2.4 high | Landing/continued floor contact: **92.21** load exceeds 28; no Wood joints existed yet | **5 / 4 / 1** |
    | G2 | Tick 27, 0.450 s | **4** G1 parents, 0.355–0.602 × 2.4 → **5 each, 20 total**; child x extents **0.159–0.338**, y extents **0.505–1.378**; true minimum widths **0.153–0.316** | All four exceed 28 from **one-tick-old weld reactions, 32.49–66.01**. One also has **43.30** floor-contact load; the other three have zero direct contact load. Three old links fail | **21 / 30 / 4** |
    | Link break only | Tick 32, 0.533 s | No new children | A five-tick-old joint reaches **27.18**, above connection strength 22 but below fragment strength 28 | **21 / 29 / 4** |
    | G3 | Tick 33, 0.550 s | **2** G2 parents, **0.266 × 1.209** and **0.287 × 1.201** → **5 each, 10 total**; child x extents **0.057–0.160**, y extents **0.519–0.684**; true minimum widths **0.057–0.155** | Both endpoints see **48.37** from the same six-tick-old weld, which also breaks. Direct contact is only **13.35** on one parent and zero on the other | **29 / 44 / 5** |
    | Later link breaks; settled | Ticks 36 and 46; held to tick 286 | No further generation | Existing joints reach **22.30** and **25.19**; neither reaches fragment threshold. Last structural change at **0.767 s** | **29 / 42 / 6** |
    
    These are responses to the one drop: continued contact with the ground and reactions in the newly built constraint network. There is no second imposed strike. The ground itself refines from 1 to 3 to 5 regions at ticks 26–27, remains one anchored piece, and introduces replacement floor colliders. Thus the new contact at tick 27 is part of the same landing against refined terrain, not evidence of a new external hit.
    
    ## What the detail accomplishes
    
    - **G1:** adds five bodies and four stiff welds, but leaves one connected piece with exactly the parent's geometry at creation. It supplies the strip boundaries that can subsequently break.
    - **G2:** creates three additional separate pieces. However, a graph check on the recorded G1 state shows that removing its three failed links alone gives **the same four component groupings** as the actual refinement, after mapping children back to their G1 parents. The twenty children mainly add internal resolution inside those groups.
    - **G3:** adds another separate piece. Removing just its failed existing link from the recorded pre-update graph likewise gives **the same five groupings** as the actual update. The ten new children mainly refine those groups internally.
    - **Later:** a link-only failure makes the sixth piece. At rest, the six pieces contain **5, 5, 5, 5, 1 and 8** regions. There is little visible spacing between them. Maximum surviving-joint anchor separation during the response was **0.00445** units; at the final capture it was **0.000453**. This is not appreciable rubber-like deformation.
    
    Wood area stays **5.76**, within floating-point rounding: no Wood region or thin connected component was removed. Final world bounds are approximately **2.4003 × 2.4012**, versus the original 2.4 × 2.4, after allowing for translation/rotation. Motion remains below 0.005 units/s and radians/s after tick 110; final velocities are zero. The graph check above is a static topology comparison, **not** a modified-physics replay, so it does not establish identical future dynamics without refinement.
    
    ## Answers and proposed direction
    
    1. **What fixes the final scale? — Verified:** the five-child Strips recipe and deterministic cuts set each refinement's geometry; repeated load evaluations decide whether another generation appears. All children retain strength 28. Changing body mass, contact distribution and constraint loads as regions shrink, together with dissipating motion, eventually leaves the measured loads below threshold. At rest the largest live Wood contact/joint loads are about **5.37 / 3.66**. The general width/terminal/unsplittable rules remain available, but **they did not terminate this example**: all 29 survivors have nonzero seeds, and the 0.057-wide region remains live while attached to a wider piece.
    2. **Which generations change breakup? — Verified:** G1 provides the first possible strip seams. G2 and G3 coincide with real link breaks, but their extra internal subdivision does not add component separation beyond those breaks in the recorded graphs. Later link failures also change connectivity without generating detail. **Design judgment:** the 29-region mesh is excessive for the immediate visible breakup shown here; it may influence future damage, which this one-drop test does not evaluate.
    3. **Is this deliberate Wood detail? — Verified distinction:** elongated strips and a five-child recipe are explicit preset choices. The third generation is an emergent consequence of applying fresh endpoint failure tests to reactions from newly created joints, then reconnecting generated children. There is no explicit desired final wood grain size or fracture-energy budget. Calling this amount of detail unnecessary is a design judgment, rather than proof of an invalid partition or solver bug.
    4. **Smallest candidate change — Proposed, not implemented:** when a joint is already scheduled to break, exclude **that same joint's reaction** from the endpoint subdivision-failure calculation for that update. Break the joint and reassess on the next solver step. Keep direct contact loads, loads from other surviving joints, and later independent damage eligible to subdivide. This addresses the repeated refinement source observed here without changing strengths or imposing a generation cap. It would not suppress the tick-27 child's independently excessive floor contact. A follow-up replay is needed to establish the resulting fracture count and feel; a few coarser independent strips can still rest together with a similar silhouette.
    
    ## Captures
    
    Each on/off pair is the **same paused state**, with no simulation or interpolation between renders. All use the same close framing. Surface blending remains at its default; Wood has zero flexibility. The fade effect was not changed.

[Compact measurements](observations.json) contain the failing-parent and joint loads without per-frame logs. **Verified: Wood gained substantial internal detail after a legitimate damaging impact, while retaining nearly the same silhouette.**

The documented case was a **2.4 × 2.4 Wood rectangle**, seed **42**, lifted **0.50 units** and released slightly tilted. It survived initial settling intact. No further deliberate impacts were applied.

| Step | Generated geometry | Failure source | Wood regions / links / pieces |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Initial settle | One intact rectangle | No failure | 1 / 0 / 1 |
| G1 | 5 strips, approximately 0.36–0.60 × 2.4 | Floor-contact load **92.21**, above strength 28 | 5 / 4 / 1 |
| G2 | Four strips generate 20 children, approximately 0.16–0.34 × 0.50–1.38 | One-tick-old weld reactions **32–66**; one parent also receives excessive floor contact | 21 / 30 / 4 |
| G3 | Two regions generate 10 children, approximately 0.06–0.16 × 0.52–0.68 | A six-tick-old weld reaction of **48.37** | 29 / 44 / 5 |
| Settled | No further subdivision; later links break | Loads fall below threshold | **29 / 42 / 6** |

1. **Final scale:** repeated load evaluation, shrinking bodies, changing constraint loads and settling determine where refinement stops. The size cutoff did **not** terminate this example.
2. **Meaningful breakup:** G1 supplies the first seams. At G2 and G3, removing only the failed existing links produces the same component groupings as the actual refinement. The additional cells mostly supply internal resolution, with little deformation.
3. **Design judgment:** elongated strips are deliberate; this depth of refinement follows from repeatedly testing joint-loaded endpoints. For this immediate breakup, the resulting detail appears excessive.
4. **Smallest candidate change:** when a joint breaks, exclude that same reaction from endpoint subdivision failure for that update, then reassess next solver step. Preserve direct contact damage and later refinement. This proposal was **not implemented or replay-tested**.

The [full report](C:/Users/jblic/Documents/BOM/playtests/2026-11-01-wood-impact/report.md) includes exact dimensions, loads, snapshots and paired captures.     package main
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    import "core:fmt"
    import "core:math"
    import "core:encoding/json"
    import "core:os"
    
    ab_variant: bool
    ab_tick: int
    ab_generations: map[u64]int
    AB_Event :: struct { tick,generation,material: int, parent: u64, parent_width,area: f32, children: int, child_min_width,child_max_width: f32 }
    AB_State :: struct { tick,regions,links,pieces,ground_regions: int, area,speed,spin,gap: f32 }
    AB_Result :: struct { label: string,events: [dynamic]AB_Event,changes: [dynamic]AB_State,initial,final: AB_State, last_moving_tick: int }
    ab_result: AB_Result
    ab_parent :: proc(parent: Subdivision) {
    	append(&ab_result.events,AB_Event{tick=ab_tick,generation=ab_generations[parent.id]+1,material=parent.material,parent=parent.id,parent_width=parent.width,area=polygon_area(parent.outline)})
    }
    ab_children :: proc(s: ^Scene,parent: u64,children: []u64) {
    	e:=&ab_result.events[len(ab_result.events)-1]; assert(e.parent==parent)
    	e.children=len(children); e.child_min_width=1e30
    	for id in children { sub:=s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[id]]; ab_generations[id]=e.generation; e.child_min_width=min(e.child_min_width,sub.width); e.child_max_width=max(e.child_max_width,sub.width) }
    }
    ab_state :: proc(s: ^Scene) -> AB_State {
    	r:=AB_State{tick=ab_tick}
    	for sub in s.subdivisions {
    		if !sub.live { continue }
    		if sub.material==1 { r.regions+=1; r.area+=polygon_area(sub.outline); r.speed=max(r.speed,vlen(sub.pose.velocity)); r.spin=max(r.spin,math.abs(sub.pose.angular_velocity)) } else { r.ground_regions+=1 }
    	}
    	for c in s.connections {
    		if !c.live { continue }
    		a,b:=s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]],s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
    		if a.material==1 { r.links+=1; r.gap=max(r.gap,vlen(vsub(posed_point(a,c.rest_point),posed_point(b,c.rest_point)))) }
    	}
    	for p in s.pieces { if p.live && p.material==1 { r.pieces+=1 } }
    	return r
    }
    ab_render :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,target: rl.RenderTexture2D,path: cstring) {
    	poses:=make(map[u64]Pose); defer delete(poses)
    	rl.BeginDrawing(); rl.BeginTextureMode(target); rl.ClearBackground({19,28,42,255})
    	sandbox_draw_world(game,View{offset={100,650},scale=200},poses)
    	rl.EndTextureMode(); rl.EndDrawing(); sandbox_smoke_export(target,path)
    }
    ab_pair :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,target: rl.RenderTexture2D,name: cstring) {
    	game.outlines=true; ab_render(game,target,rl.TextFormat("../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-ab/%s-%s-on.png",ab_result.label,name))
    	game.outlines=false; ab_render(game,target,rl.TextFormat("../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-ab/%s-%s-off.png",ab_result.label,name))
    	assert(save_snapshot(&game.scene,fmt.tprintf("../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-ab/%s-%s.json",ab_result.label,name)))
    }
    run_wood_ab :: proc() {
    	rl.SetTraceLogLevel(.WARNING); rl.SetConfigFlags({.WINDOW_HIDDEN,.MSAA_4X_HINT,.WINDOW_HIGHDPI}); rl.InitWindow(1280,800,"Wood A/B"); defer rl.CloseWindow(); rl.SetTargetFPS(0)
    	target:=rl.LoadRenderTexture(1280,800); defer rl.UnloadRenderTexture(target)
    	labels:=[2]string{"A","B"}
    	for label in labels {
    		ab_variant=label=="B"; ab_result=AB_Result{label=label}; ab_generations=make(map[u64]int)
    		game:=sandbox_editor_create(); game.editor.palette=.Wood; assert(editor_place(&game,{1.5,0},{3.9,2.4})); sandbox_toggle_editor(&game)
    		for tick in -119..=0 { ab_tick=tick; sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
    		ab_result.initial=ab_state(&game.scene); assert(ab_result.initial.regions==1 && len(ab_result.events)==0)
    		for sub in game.scene.subdivisions {
    			if sub.live && sub.material==1 {
    				body:=game.scene.physics.bodies[sub.id]; position:=b2.Body_GetPosition(body); position.y+=0.5
    				b2.Body_SetTransform(body,position,b2.MakeRot(0.15)); b2.Body_SetAwake(body,true)
    			}
    		}
    		physics_read_motion(&game.scene); ab_pair(&game,target,"before")
    		for frame in 0..<15 { ab_render(&game,target,rl.TextFormat("frames-%s/frame-%04d.png",label,frame)) }
    		last:=ab_result.initial
    		for tick in 1..=600 {
    			ab_tick=tick; sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    			valid,message:=validate_scene(&game.scene); assert(valid,message)
    			r:=ab_state(&game.scene)
    			if r.regions!=last.regions || r.links!=last.links || r.pieces!=last.pieces || r.ground_regions!=last.ground_regions { append(&ab_result.changes,r); fmt.println(label,r) }
    			if r.speed>=0.005 || r.spin>=0.005 { ab_result.last_moving_tick=tick }
    			last=r
    			if tick%2==0 && tick<=300 { ab_render(&game,target,rl.TextFormat("frames-%s/frame-%04d.png",label,14+tick/2)) }
    			if tick==26 { ab_pair(&game,target,"first-failure") }
    		}
    		ab_result.final=ab_state(&game.scene); ab_pair(&game,target,"after")
    		bytes,err:=json.marshal(ab_result,{pretty=true}); assert(err==nil)
    		assert(os.write_entire_file(fmt.tprintf("../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-ab/%s-measurements.json",label),bytes)==nil); delete(bytes)
    		fmt.println(label,"FINAL",ab_result.final)
    		sandbox_destroy(&game); delete(ab_generations); delete(ab_result.events); delete(ab_result.changes)
    	}
    }

    Exactly two fresh runs were made: **A = current rule; B = proposed rule**. Both used the previous investigation's 2.4 × 2.4 Wood rectangle at (1.5, 0)–(3.9, 2.4), seed 42, identity 1/birth context 178, 120 initial settling ticks, then a 0.50-unit lift and 0.15-radian tilt, awakened and released without added velocity. No further input or deliberate impacts. Current material strengths, flexibility, generation, physics, destructible terrain, surface rendering and fade behavior were preserved.
    
    In B only, when the existing load check schedules a joint to break, calculation continues to the next joint before adding that reaction to endpoint subdivision loads. Contacts and other surviving joint reactions still contribute normally. There is no delay timer, subdivision cap, strength adjustment or other behavioral change.
    
    ## Verified comparison
    
    The before-release snapshots and first-failure snapshots are **identical between A and B**. Both survive initial settling without damage and first fail at tick 26. A reproduces the previous investigation's structural sequence.
    
    | Stage | A: regions / links / pieces | B: regions / links / pieces |
    |---|---:|---:|
    | Initial settled | 1 / 0 / 1 | 1 / 0 / 1 |
    | Tick 26: root generates five strips | 5 / 4 / 1 | 5 / 4 / 1 |

    | Last Wood structural change | Tick 46: 29 / 42 / 6 | Tick 48: 13 / 14 / 5 |

The later failure must come from a still-eligible load; this replay did not separately record its contact versus surviving-joint contributions.

    package main
    
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:math"
    
    View :: struct { offset: Vec2, scale: f32 }
    screen_point :: proc(view: View,point: Vec2) -> rl.Vector2 { return {view.offset.x+point.x*view.scale,view.offset.y-point.y*view.scale} }
    world_point :: proc(view: View,point: rl.Vector2) -> Vec2 { return {(point.x-view.offset.x)/view.scale,(view.offset.y-point.y)/view.scale} }
    piece_color :: proc(id: u64,alpha: u8 = 255) -> rl.Color {
        colors := [6]rl.Color{{64,173,165,255},{97,142,206,255},{194,134,204,255},{212,161,88,255},{139,178,113,255},{211,116,125,255}}
        c:=colors[id%6]; c.a=alpha; return c
    }
    render_subdivision :: proc(s: ^Scene,sub: Subdivision,poses: map[u64]Pose) -> Subdivision {
        result:=sub
        if pose,ok:=poses[sub.id]; ok { result.pose=pose }
        return result
    }
    point_on_boundary :: proc(point: Vec2,a,b: Polygon) -> bool {
        for i in 0..<len(a.points) {
            for j in 0..<len(b.points) {
                if segment,ok:=segment_overlap(Segment{a.points[i],a.points[(i+1)%len(a.points)]},Segment{b.points[j],b.points[(j+1)%len(b.points)]}); ok {
                    d:=vsub(segment.b,segment.a); length:=vlen(d)
                    projection:=vdot(vsub(point,segment.a),d)/(length*length)
                    if projection >= -0.0001 && projection <= 1.0001 && math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(point,segment.a))) < 0.0001*length { return true }
                }
            }
        }
        return false
    }
    // Only presentation vertices are blended. Stored outlines and fixtures stay exact.
    cosmetic_point :: proc(s: ^Scene,sub: Subdivision,rest: Vec2,poses: map[u64]Pose) -> Vec2 {
        self:=render_subdivision(s,sub,poses)
        point:=posed_point(self,rest)
        flex:=clamp(s.materials[sub.material].flexibility,f32(0),f32(1))
        if flex==0 { return point }
        weighted:=point
        count:=f32(1)
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            other_id:=u64(0)
            if c.a==sub.id { other_id=c.b } else if c.b==sub.id { other_id=c.a }
            if other_id==0 { continue }
            other:=render_subdivision(s,s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[other_id]],poses)
            if point_on_boundary(rest,sub.outline,other.outline) { weighted=vadd(weighted,posed_point(other,rest)); count+=1 }
        }
        return vadd(point,vmul(vsub(vmul(weighted,1/count),point),flex))
    }
    draw_polygon :: proc(view: View,outline: Polygon,color: rl.Color,stroke: rl.Color,outlines: bool = true) {
        triangles:=triangulate_polygon(outline)
        for triangle in triangles {
            a,b,c:=screen_point(view,triangle.points[0]),screen_point(view,triangle.points[1]),screen_point(view,triangle.points[2])
            // Raylib's triangle winding uses the screen's downward Y axis.
            cross:=vcross(vsub(triangle.points[1],triangle.points[0]),vsub(triangle.points[2],triangle.points[0]))
            if cross > 0 { rl.DrawTriangle(a,b,c,color) } else { rl.DrawTriangle(c,b,a,color) }
            delete(triangle.points)
        }
        delete(triangles)
        if outlines {
            for i in 0..<len(outline.points) { rl.DrawLineEx(screen_point(view,outline.points[i]),screen_point(view,outline.points[(i+1)%len(outline.points)]),2,stroke) }
        }
    }
    pick_subdivision :: proc(s: ^Scene,point: Vec2) -> u64 {
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            points: [dynamic]rl.Vector2
            for rest in sub.outline.points { p:=posed_point(sub,rest); append(&points,rl.Vector2{p.x,p.y}) }
            hit:=rl.CheckCollisionPointPoly({point.x,point.y},raw_data(points),i32(len(points)))
            delete(points)
            if hit { return sub.id }
        }
        return 0
    }
    pick_connection :: proc(s: ^Scene,point: Vec2,max_distance: f32) -> u64 {
        best:=u64(0); distance:=max_distance
        for c in s.connections { if c.live { d:=vlen(vsub(point,connection_sample(s,c))); if d<distance { distance=d; best=c.id } } }
        return best
    }
    material_preset :: proc(index: int) -> Material {
        switch index {
        case 1: return Material{name="splinter",subdivision_strength=7,connection_strength=6,flexibility=0.6,generation_count=5,aspect_ratio=0.2}
        case 2: return Material{name="shatter",subdivision_strength=5,connection_strength=4,flexibility=0.05,generation_count=6,aspect_ratio=1,triangulate=true}
        }
        return Material{name="chunk",subdivision_strength=6,connection_strength=4,flexibility=0.25,generation_count=3,aspect_ratio=1}
    }
    reset_demo :: proc(s: ^Scene,preset: int,terminal: bool) {
        scene_destroy(s)
        seed:=u8(42); if terminal { seed=0 }
        s^=make_wall(seed,0.08)
        s.materials[0]=material_preset(preset)
        physics_init(s)
    }
    add_projectile :: proc(s: ^Scene) {
        material:=add_material(s,Material{name="projectile",subdivision_strength=math.inf_f32(1),connection_strength=math.inf_f32(1),generation_count=2,aspect_ratio=1})
        owner:=add_piece(s,material,0)
        points:=[4]Vec2{{-1.2,0.3},{-0.8,0.3},{-0.8,0.7},{-1.2,0.7}}
        outline:=make_polygon(points[:]); defer delete(outline.points)
        id:=add_subdivision(s,owner,outline,Pose{position=centroid(outline),velocity={8,0}})
        append(&s.pieces[s.piece_rows[owner]].subdivisions,id)
        physics_sync_structure(s)
        b2.Body_SetBullet(s.physics.bodies[id],true)
        s.revision+=1
    }
    draw_scene :: proc(s: ^Scene,view: View,poses: map[u64]Pose,selected: u64,surface,joints: bool,ids: bool = true,material_colors: bool = false,outlines: bool = true) {
        for i in -20..=20 {
            tint:=rl.Color{31,44,62,255}
            if i==0 { tint={45,65,85,255} }
            rl.DrawLineEx(screen_point(view,Vec2{f32(i),-20}),screen_point(view,Vec2{f32(i),20}),1,tint)
            rl.DrawLineEx(screen_point(view,Vec2{-20,f32(i)}),screen_point(view,Vec2{20,f32(i)}),1,tint)
        }
        for remnant in s.remnants {
            sub:=s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[remnant.subdivision]]; sub.pose=remnant.pose
            outline:=posed_polygon(sub)
            draw_polygon(view,outline,rl.Color{140,152,170,u8(160*(1-remnant.age))},rl.Color{140,152,170,u8(160*(1-remnant.age))},outlines)
            delete(outline.points)
        }
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            outline:=Polygon{points=make([]Vec2,len(sub.outline.points))}
            posed:=render_subdivision(s,sub,poses)
            for rest,i in sub.outline.points {
                point:=posed_point(posed,rest)
                if surface { point=cosmetic_point(s,sub,rest,poses) }
                outline.points[i]=point
            }
            stroke:=rl.Color{202,220,231,255}
            if sub.id==selected { stroke={255,255,255,255} }
            fill:=piece_color(sub.owner,210)
            if material_colors { fill=editor_color(s.materials[sub.material].name) }
            draw_polygon(view,outline,fill,stroke,outlines)
            delete(outline.points)
            center:=screen_point(view,posed.pose.position)
            if ids { rl.DrawText(rl.TextFormat("%d",sub.id),i32(center.x)-5,i32(center.y)-23,16,rl.Color{16,29,40,255}) }
        }
        if joints {
            for c in s.connections {
                if !c.live { continue }
                a,b:=render_subdivision(s,s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]],poses),render_subdivision(s,s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]],poses)
                anchor:=vmul(vadd(posed_point(a,c.rest_point),posed_point(b,c.rest_point)),0.5)
                color:=rl.Color{248,205,109,255}
                rl.DrawLineEx(screen_point(view,a.pose.position),screen_point(view,b.pose.position),2,color)
                rl.DrawCircleV(screen_point(view,anchor),5,color)
                p:=screen_point(view,anchor)
                rl.DrawText(rl.TextFormat("c%d",c.id),i32(p.x)+7,i32(p.y)+7,14,color)
            }
    package main

    editor_color :: proc(name: string) -> rl.Color {
        switch name {
        case "wood": return {180,136,82,230}

        return {lo.x,lo.y,hi.x-lo.x,hi.y-lo.y}
    }
    sandbox_draw_editor :: proc(game: ^Sandbox,view: View) {
        if !game.editor.editing { return }
        for object in game.editor.objects {
            box:=editor_screen_rect(view,object)
            material:=editor_material(object.material)
            rl.DrawRectangleRec(box,editor_color(material.name))

            rl.DrawText(rl.TextFormat("%s",material.name),i32(box.x)+5,i32(box.y)+5,16,YARD_INK)
        }

    // Contact points and fixtures against the same other body form one interaction.
    // Joint reactions are already forces; totalNormalImpulse covers the full tick.
    // Box2D's tangent/rolling impulses cover the final substep in this binding version.
    calculate_physics_loads :: proc(s: ^Scene, dt: f32) -> Failures {
        assert(dt > 0)
        failures := Failures{}
        loads := make(map[u64]f32)
        defer delete(loads)
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            body := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]
            capacity := int(b2.Body_GetContactCapacity(body))
            buffer := make([]b2.ContactData,capacity)
            contacts := b2.Body_GetContactData(body,buffer)
            interactions := make(map[b2.BodyId]Interaction)
            for contact in contacts {
                body_a,body_b := b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdA),b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdB)
                other := body_b
                sign := f32(-1)
                if body_b == body { other=body_a; sign=1 }
                normal := from_b2(contact.manifold.normal)
                tangent := Vec2{normal.y,-normal.x}
                interaction := interactions[other]
                for k in 0..<int(contact.manifold.pointCount) {
                    point := contact.manifold.points[k]
                    force := vadd(equivalent_force(vmul(normal,point.totalNormalImpulse*sign),dt),equivalent_force(vmul(tangent,point.tangentImpulse*sign),dt/f32(PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS)))
                    interaction.force = vadd(interaction.force,force)
                    interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(from_b2(point.point),sub.pose.position),force)
                }
                interaction.torque += contact.manifold.rollingImpulse*sign/(dt/f32(PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS))
                interactions[other] = interaction
            }
            for _,interaction in interactions { loads[sub.id] = max(loads[sub.id],interaction_load(interaction)) }
            delete(interactions); delete(buffer)
        }
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            joint,exists := s.physics.joints[c.id]
            if !exists { continue }
            interaction := Interaction{force=from_b2(b2.Joint_GetConstraintForce(joint)),torque=b2.Joint_GetConstraintTorque(joint)}
            load := interaction_load(interaction)
            a,b := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]],s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
            a_interaction,b_interaction := interaction,interaction
            a_interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(posed_point(a,c.rest_point),a.pose.position),interaction.force)
            b_interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(posed_point(b,c.rest_point),b.pose.position),interaction.force)
            loads[c.a] = max(loads[c.a],interaction_load(a_interaction))
            loads[c.b] = max(loads[c.b],interaction_load(b_interaction))
            material := s.materials[s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]].material]
            if fails(load,material.connection_strength) { append(&failures.connections,c.id) }
        }
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if sub.live && fails(loads[sub.id],s.materials[sub.material].subdivision_strength) { append(&failures.subdivisions,sub.id) }
        }
        return failures
    }
    Load_Calculator :: #type proc(s: ^Scene,dt: f32) -> Failures
    physics_tick :: proc(s: ^Scene, dt: f32,calculate_loads: Load_Calculator = calculate_physics_loads) {
        assert(s.physics.active && dt > 0)
        physics_sync_structure(s)
        b2.World_Step(s.physics.world,dt,PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS)
        physics_read_motion(s)
        failures := calculate_loads(s,dt)
        apply_failures(s,failures)
        delete(failures.subdivisions); delete(failures.connections)
        delete(failures.discard_subdivisions)
        physics_sync_structure(s)
        fade_step(s,dt)
    }

    rubber_deforms_before_failure_and_survives_a_removed_cell :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)

        ids:=game.scene.pieces[0].subdivisions
        initial_links:=len(game.scene.connections)
        testing.expect(t,len(ids)==12 && initial_links==16)
        for id in ids {
            sub:=game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[id]]
            testing.expect(t,sub.seed==0 && sub.owner==owner && b2.Body_GetType(game.scene.physics.bodies[id])==.dynamicBody)
        }
        grid: [dynamic]Polygon
        defer delete(grid)
        for id in ids { append(&grid,game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[id]].outline) }
        points:=[4]Vec2{{0,0},{2.4,0},{2.4,0.8},{0,0.8}}
        expect_generation_partition(t,Polygon{points=points[:]},grid[:])
        for _ in 0..<60 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
        // A local nudge deforms the soft mesh under normal finite failure checks.
        b2.Body_ApplyLinearImpulseToCenter(game.scene.physics.bodies[ids[len(ids)-1]],{0,0.3},true)
        max_gap,max_angle:=f32(0),f32(0)
        for _ in 0..<12 {
            sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
            for c in game.scene.connections {
                if !c.live { continue }
                a,b:=game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[c.a]],game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[c.b]]
                max_gap=max(max_gap,vlen(vsub(posed_point(a,c.rest_point),posed_point(b,c.rest_point))))
                max_angle=max(max_angle,math.abs(a.pose.angle-b.pose.angle))
            }
        }
        live,links,pieces:=counts(&game.scene)
        testing.expectf(t,live==13 && links==initial_links && pieces==2,"Ordinary deformation must precede failure: %d regions, %d links, %d pieces",live,links,pieces)
        testing.expectf(t,max_gap>0.015 && max_angle>0.02,"Rubber must stretch and bend: gap %.4f, angle %.4f",max_gap,max_angle)
        removed:=ids[8]
        f:=Failures{}; append(&f.discard_subdivisions,removed)
        apply_failures(&game.scene,f); free_failures(&f)
        physics_sync_structure(&game.scene)
        testing.expect(t,!b2.Body_IsValid(game.scene.physics.bodies[removed]))
        live,links,pieces=counts(&game.scene)
        testing.expect(t,live==12 && links>0 && pieces==2,"Removing one internal cell must leave the remaining grid connected")
        for _ in 0..<120 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
        live,links,pieces=counts(&game.scene)
        testing.expect(t,live==12 && links>0 && pieces==2)
        expect_valid(t,&game.scene)
        // A sufficiently close ordinary radius-5 blast can remove finite cells.
        testing.expect(t,sandbox_blast(&game,{-0.2,0.5}))
        rubber_remaining:=0
        for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { if sub.live && game.scene.materials[sub.material].name=="rubber" { rubber_remaining+=1 } }
        testing.expect(t,rubber_remaining<11,"Finite terminal rubber cells must be removable by the blast")
        expect_valid(t,&game.scene)
    }

    // Merge adjacent triangles whenever their union is convex. In particular this
    // avoids feeding thin ears from a displaced boundary to Box2D as tiny fixtures.
    convex_decomposition :: proc(outline: Polygon) -> [dynamic]Polygon {
        parts:=triangulate_polygon(outline)
        for {
            merged:=false
            for i in 0..<len(parts) {
                for j in i+1..<len(parts) {
                    if length,_:=shared_boundary(parts[i],parts[j]); length<=0 { continue }
                    points: [dynamic]Vec2
                    for point in parts[i].points { append(&points,point) }
                    for point in parts[j].points { append(&points,point) }
                    hull:=convex_hull(points[:]); delete(points)
                    combined:=make_polygon(hull[:]); delete(hull)
                    error:=math.abs(polygon_area(combined)-polygon_area(parts[i])-polygon_area(parts[j]))
                    if len(combined.points)<=8 && error<0.000001 {
                        delete(parts[i].points); delete(parts[j].points)
                        parts[i]=combined; ordered_remove(&parts,j); merged=true; break
                    }
                    delete(combined.points)
                }
                if merged { break }
            }
            if !merged { break }
        }
        return parts
    }

    package main
    
    import "core:math"
    
    Segment :: struct { a,b: Vec2 }
    Cut_Boundary :: struct { a,b: int, segment: Segment }
    convex_hull :: proc(points: []Vec2) -> [dynamic]Vec2 {
        sorted: [dynamic]Vec2
        defer delete(sorted)
        for point in points { append(&sorted,point) }
        for i in 1..<len(sorted) {
            j:=i
            for j>0 && (sorted[j].x<sorted[j-1].x || (sorted[j].x==sorted[j-1].x && sorted[j].y<sorted[j-1].y)) { sorted[j],sorted[j-1]=sorted[j-1],sorted[j]; j-=1 }
        }
        hull: [dynamic]Vec2
        if len(sorted)<2 { for p in sorted { append(&hull,p) }; return hull }
        for p in sorted {
            for len(hull)>=2 && vcross(vsub(hull[len(hull)-1],hull[len(hull)-2]),vsub(p,hull[len(hull)-1]))<=0 { resize(&hull,len(hull)-1) }
            append(&hull,p)
        }
        upper_start:=len(hull)+1
        for i:=len(sorted)-2; i>=0; i-=1 {
            p:=sorted[i]
            for len(hull)>=upper_start && vcross(vsub(hull[len(hull)-1],hull[len(hull)-2]),vsub(p,hull[len(hull)-1]))<=0 { resize(&hull,len(hull)-1) }
            append(&hull,p)
        }
        resize(&hull,len(hull)-1)
        return hull
    }
    segment_overlap :: proc(a,b: Segment) -> (Segment,bool) {
        d := vsub(a.b,a.a)
        length := vlen(d)
        if length < 0.00001 { return {},false }
        if math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(b.a,a.a))) > 0.0001*length || math.abs(vcross(d,vsub(b.b,a.a))) > 0.0001*length { return {},false }
        unit := vmul(d,1/length)
        t0,t1 := vdot(vsub(b.a,a.a),unit),vdot(vsub(b.b,a.a),unit)
        lo,hi := max(f32(0),min(t0,t1)),min(length,max(t0,t1))
        if hi-lo <= 0.0001 { return {},false }
        return Segment{vadd(a.a,vmul(unit,lo)),vadd(a.a,vmul(unit,hi))},true
    }
    shared_segments :: proc(a,b: Polygon) -> [dynamic]Segment {
        result: [dynamic]Segment
        for i in 0..<len(a.points) {
            for j in 0..<len(b.points) {
                if segment,ok := segment_overlap(Segment{a.points[i],a.points[(i+1)%len(a.points)]},Segment{b.points[j],b.points[(j+1)%len(b.points)]}); ok { append(&result,segment) }
            }
        }
        return result
    }
    inherits_old_boundary :: proc(a,b,old_a,old_b: Polygon) -> bool {
        current := shared_segments(a,b)
        original := shared_segments(old_a,old_b)
        defer delete(current); defer delete(original)
        for x in current { for y in original { if _,ok := segment_overlap(x,y); ok { return true } } }
        return false
    }
    insert_polygon_vertex :: proc(p: ^Polygon,index: int,point: Vec2) {
        points:=make([]Vec2,len(p.points)+1)
        copy(points[:index],p.points[:index]); points[index]=point
        copy(points[index+1:],p.points[index:])
        delete(p.points); p.points=points
    }
    insert_boundary_endpoint :: proc(p: ^Polygon,point: Vec2) {
        for existing in p.points { if vlen(vsub(existing,point)) < 0.00001 { return } }
        for i in 0..<len(p.points) {
            a,b := p.points[i],p.points[(i+1)%len(p.points)]
            edge := vsub(b,a)
            length := vlen(edge)
            if length < 0.00001 { continue }
            t := vdot(vsub(point,a),edge)/(length*length)
            if t > 0 && t < 1 && math.abs(vcross(edge,vsub(point,a))) < 0.00001*length { insert_polygon_vertex(p,i+1,point); return }
        }
    }

    package main
    import rl "vendor:raylib"
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:fmt"
    
    seam_impact :: proc() {
    	rl.SetTraceLogLevel(.WARNING); rl.SetConfigFlags({.WINDOW_HIDDEN,.MSAA_4X_HINT,.WINDOW_HIGHDPI}); rl.InitWindow(1280,800,"Impact"); defer rl.CloseWindow(); rl.SetTargetFPS(0)
    	target:=rl.LoadRenderTexture(1280,800); defer rl.UnloadRenderTexture(target)
    	game:=sandbox_editor_create(); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
    	game.editor.palette=.Wood; assert(editor_place(&game,{1.5,0},{3.9,2.4})); sandbox_toggle_editor(&game)
    	for _ in 0..<120 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
    	for sub in game.scene.subdivisions {
    		if sub.live && sub.material==1 { body:=game.scene.physics.bodies[sub.id]; p:=b2.Body_GetPosition(body); p.y+=0.5; b2.Body_SetTransform(body,p,b2.MakeRot(0.15)); b2.Body_SetAwake(body,true) }
    	}
    	physics_read_motion(&game.scene)
    	// Same close camera as the seam diagnostics and previous A/B.
    	for tick in 1..=360 {
    		sandbox_tick(&game,0,false)
    		if tick%2==0 { seam_render(&game.scene,target,rl.TextFormat("frames/frame-%04d.png",tick/2-1),false) }
    		if tick==180 {
    			assert(save_snapshot(&game.scene,"../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-seams/before-side-impact.json"))
    			seam_render(&game.scene,target,"../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-seams/before-side-impact-on.png",true)
    			seam_render(&game.scene,target,"../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-seams/before-side-impact-off.png",false)
    			// One outward horizontal impulse to the top region of the rightmost group.
    			chosen:=u64(0); right:=f32(-1e30)
    			for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { if sub.live && sub.material==1 { score:=sub.pose.position.x+sub.pose.position.y*0.2; if score>right { right=score; chosen=sub.id } } }
    			sub:=game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[chosen]]
    			fmt.printf("Impulse target %d owner %d, position %.5f %.5f, mass %.5f, impulse +2 x\n",chosen,sub.owner,sub.pose.position.x,sub.pose.position.y,b2.Body_GetMass(game.scene.physics.bodies[chosen]))
    			for p in game.scene.pieces { if p.live && p.material==1 { fmt.printf("Before owner %d: %v\n",p.id,p.subdivisions[:]) } }
    			for id in game.scene.physics.joints { c:=game.scene.connections[game.scene.conn_rows[id]]; assert(c.live && game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[c.a]].owner==game.scene.subdivisions[game.scene.sub_rows[c.b]].owner) }
    			b2.Body_ApplyLinearImpulseToCenter(game.scene.physics.bodies[chosen],{2,0},true)
    		}
    		if tick==210 || tick==360 {
    			physics_read_motion(&game.scene)
    			for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { if sub.live && sub.material==1 { fmt.printf("Tick %d sub %d owner %d pos %.5f %.5f v %.5f %.5f\n",tick,sub.id,sub.owner,sub.pose.position.x,sub.pose.position.y,sub.pose.velocity.x,sub.pose.velocity.y) } }
    			assert(save_snapshot(&game.scene,fmt.tprintf("../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-seams/after-side-impact-%d.json",tick)))
    			seam_render(&game.scene,target,rl.TextFormat("../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-seams/after-side-impact-%d-on.png",tick),true)
    			seam_render(&game.scene,target,rl.TextFormat("../playtests/2026-11-01-wood-seams/after-side-impact-%d-off.png",tick),false)
    		}
    		valid,message:=validate_scene(&game.scene); assert(valid,message)
    	}
    }

    92:| `physics.odin` | Box2D bodies, fixtures, weld joints, interaction aggregation and load policy |
    121:The load policy uses the strongest individual interaction, preserving opposing interactions against different bodies. Contact points and convex fixtures against the same other body are combined. Joint reactions also load their endpoint subdivisions. Thresholds use `load > 0 && load >= strength`; strength records are never reduced by prior events. `physics_tick` accepts a replacement `Load_Calculator` function.
    123:Blast radius controls both reach and power: direct load is `10 * max(0, radius - distance)`, with zero load for nonpositive radii. The fixed global `BLAST_LOAD_MULTIPLIER` is 10; increasing radius increases load at a fixed distance, without a fixed maximum. For example, a sample 0.5 units away receives load 5 at radius 1 and load 25 at radius 3, enough to fail strength 20. At the default radius 5.0 and strengths 35 / 20, subdivision samples can fail within 1.5 units and connection samples within 3.0. Impulses are `direction * load * mass * 0.2`, applied through each final survivor's center once at its own sample. A surviving default-material fragment receives less than roughly 7 units/second of added speed. Generated motion includes the parent's linear and angular motion; removed ancestors receive no blast impulse. New contact and joint reactions wait for the next solver step. Both tuning constants and the falloff live in `destruction.odin`. The torque reference length is one world unit, and global joint damping is 0.7. Flexibility zero selects a stiff weld; positive flexibility selects spring softness.
    127:Contact `totalNormalImpulse` is converted using the full tick interval. The installed binding's tangent and rolling impulses use the final substep interval.     131:Group width is the minimum projection width of its reference geometry's convex hull. Small subdivisions remain live when their connected group is wide enough.     The tested B policy is now integrated: a reaction that breaks its connection is excluded from endpoint subdivision loads for that update. Contacts and surviving joint reactions still contribute normally. No strength, subdivision recipe, collision geometry, flexibility or fade changes were made.
    
    ## Rendering diagnosis and fix
    
    The following captures use the **same paused B post-drop snapshot**, the same poses and the same close camera (scale 200). No simulation occurs between renders:

    Opacity removes faint shading/grid-through, but does not remove the dark pinholes. Those have two distinct causes in this state:
    
    - Tiny differences between the independently posed edges of intact connections: maximum endpoint discrepancy measured here **0.000310 world units**. Previous cosmetic blending returned early at zero flexibility. This leaves occasional raster-visible pinholes despite the live attachment.
    - Actual narrow openings between disconnected pieces. These should remain visible.

    ## Drop and sideways impact
    
    The repeat uses the same 2.4 × 2.4 Wood rectangle at (1.5,0)–(3.9,2.4), seed 42/birth context 178. After 120 settling ticks, it is lifted 0.50 units, tilted 0.15 radians and released under ordinary gravity. It settles to the B result: **13 regions / 14 links / 5 pieces**.
    
    At release tick 180 (3 seconds), one controlled **+2 horizontal impulse** is applied to the center of region 25, the upper region of the rightmost group. This is a direct impulse representing a sideways strike, without a pusher body. Its mass is 0.16745, so the immediate local velocity increment is about 11.94 units/s: this is a substantial localized strike, not a gentle nudge.

The moving group breaks into two connected groups; the other groups remain standing. Physics joint inspection before the strike found no joint across disconnected owners. No unexpected sticking was observed: the packed block can separate under an outward force. Subsequent collisions of the departing material with the ground generate additional detail.

## User

the basic placement behavior still needs fixing. I was too quick to treat the remaining issue as a playtest judgment.

There’s a concrete suspect in the supplied code: contact forces are tested against damage thresholds without distinguishing ordinary support from a damaging impact. Mass increases with polygon area, while the material’s failure threshold stays fixed. A larger rectangle can therefore overload the check during settling. The floor receives the corresponding contact load, which could explain why it subdivides too.

B reduced the extra subdivision caused by breaking joints. It left that initial contact-damage calculation unchanged. The exact first failure still needs tracing to distinguish support load, landing impact and a startup correction.

I’d make the next Codex task a focused fix:
- Reproduce drawing a block and entering Test, using approximately this size, for Wood and Stone.
- Record the first failure’s load source and incoming contact velocity.
- Make ordinary placement and negligible settling leave both the object and floor intact.
- Verify that a substantial impact and a blast still cause destruction.
My preferred simple direction is to make contact damage respond to meaningful impacts, while ordinary resting contact remains harmless. A check based on incoming closing speed may be enough if the trace supports it; joint stress can remain a separate damage source.

Raising material strengths deserves care because those same strengths also govern blast destruction. I’d first fix what qualifies as damaging contact, then reassess how much subdivision a qualifying impact produces.

    // Contact points and fixtures against the same other body form one interaction.
    // Joint reactions are already forces; totalNormalImpulse covers the full tick.
    // Box2D's tangent/rolling impulses cover the final substep in this binding version.
    calculate_physics_loads :: proc(s: ^Scene, dt: f32) -> Failures {
        assert(dt > 0)
        failures := Failures{}
        loads := make(map[u64]f32)
        defer delete(loads)
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if !sub.live { continue }
            body := s.physics.bodies[sub.id]
            capacity := int(b2.Body_GetContactCapacity(body))
            buffer := make([]b2.ContactData,capacity)
            contacts := b2.Body_GetContactData(body,buffer)
            interactions := make(map[b2.BodyId]Interaction)
            for contact in contacts {
                body_a,body_b := b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdA),b2.Shape_GetBody(contact.shapeIdB)
                other := body_b
                sign := f32(-1)
                if body_b == body { other=body_a; sign=1 }
                normal := from_b2(contact.manifold.normal)
                tangent := Vec2{normal.y,-normal.x}
                interaction := interactions[other]
                for k in 0..<int(contact.manifold.pointCount) {
                    point := contact.manifold.points[k]
                    force := vadd(equivalent_force(vmul(normal,point.totalNormalImpulse*sign),dt),equivalent_force(vmul(tangent,point.tangentImpulse*sign),dt/f32(PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS)))
                    interaction.force = vadd(interaction.force,force)
                    interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(from_b2(point.point),sub.pose.position),force)
                }
                interaction.torque += contact.manifold.rollingImpulse*sign/(dt/f32(PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS))
                interactions[other] = interaction
            }
            for _,interaction in interactions { loads[sub.id] = max(loads[sub.id],interaction_load(interaction)) }
            delete(interactions); delete(buffer)
        }
        for c in s.connections {
            if !c.live { continue }
            joint,exists := s.physics.joints[c.id]
            if !exists { continue }
            interaction := Interaction{force=from_b2(b2.Joint_GetConstraintForce(joint)),torque=b2.Joint_GetConstraintTorque(joint)}
            load := interaction_load(interaction)
            material := s.materials[s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]].material]
            if fails(load,material.connection_strength) {
                append(&failures.connections,c.id)
                // This reaction breaks the attachment; reassess its endpoints next tick.
                // Independent contacts and surviving joints still contribute below.
                continue
            }
            a,b := s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.a]],s.subdivisions[s.sub_rows[c.b]]
            a_interaction,b_interaction := interaction,interaction
            a_interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(posed_point(a,c.rest_point),a.pose.position),interaction.force)
            b_interaction.torque += vcross(vsub(posed_point(b,c.rest_point),b.pose.position),interaction.force)
            loads[c.a] = max(loads[c.a],interaction_load(a_interaction))
            loads[c.b] = max(loads[c.b],interaction_load(b_interaction))
        }
        for sub in s.subdivisions {
            if sub.live && fails(loads[sub.id],s.materials[sub.material].subdivision_strength) { append(&failures.subdivisions,sub.id) }
        }
        return failures
    }
    Load_Calculator :: #type proc(s: ^Scene,dt: f32) -> Failures
    physics_tick :: proc(s: ^Scene, dt: f32,calculate_loads: Load_Calculator = calculate_physics_loads) {
        assert(s.physics.active && dt > 0)
        physics_sync_structure(s)
        b2.World_Step(s.physics.world,dt,PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS)
        physics_read_motion(s)
        failures := calculate_loads(s,dt)
        apply_failures(s,failures)
        delete(failures.subdivisions); delete(failures.connections)
        delete(failures.discard_subdivisions)
        physics_sync_structure(s)
        fade_step(s,dt)
    }

    // A manifold point is a contact point belonging to a contact manifold.
    // It holds details related to the geometry and dynamics of the contact points.
    // Box2D uses speculative collision so some contact points may be separated.

    ManifoldPoint :: struct {
        // Location of the contact point in world space. Subject to precision loss at large coordinates.
        //    @note Should only be used for debugging.
        point:            Vec2,
    
        // Location of the contact point relative to shapeA's origin in world space
        //    @note When used internally to the Box2D solver, this is relative to the body center of mass.
        anchorA:          Vec2,
    
        // Location of the contact point relative to shapeB's origin in world space
        // @note When used internally to the Box2D solver, this is relative to the body center of mass.
        anchorB:          Vec2,
    
        // The separation of the contact point, negative if penetrating
        separation:       f32,
    
        // The total normal impulse applied across sub-stepping and restitution. This is important
        // to identify speculative contact points that had an interaction in the time step.
        totalNormalImpulse: f32,
    
        // The friction impulse
        tangentImpulse:   f32,
    
        // The maximum normal impulse applied during sub-stepping

        maxNormalImpulse: f32,
    
        // Relative normal velocity pre-solve. Used for hit events. If the normal impulse is

        normalVelocity:   f32,
    
        // Uniquely identifies a contact point between two shapes

        sandbox_smoke_frame(game,target,rl.AutomationEvent{type=5,params={1,0,0,0}})

        assert(len(game.editor.objects)==4 && !game.editor.dragging)

    package main
    import b2 "vendor:box2d"
    import "core:fmt"
    
    Placement_Load :: struct { contact,joint,closing,impulse: f32, separation: f32 }
    placement_loads: map[u64]Placement_Load
    placement_first: map[int]bool
    placement_tick: int
    placement_case: string
    placement_point :: proc(id: u64,p: b2.ManifoldPoint) { d:=placement_loads[id]; d.closing=max(d.closing,-p.normalVelocity); d.impulse+=p.totalNormalImpulse; d.separation=min(d.separation,p.separation); placement_loads[id]=d }
    placement_contact :: proc(id: u64,load: f32) { d:=placement_loads[id]; d.contact=max(d.contact,load); placement_loads[id]=d }
    placement_joint :: proc(id: u64,load: f32) { d:=placement_loads[id]; d.joint=max(d.joint,load); placement_loads[id]=d }
    placement_failure :: proc(s: ^Scene,sub: Subdivision) {
    	if placement_first[sub.material] { return }; placement_first[sub.material]=true
    	fmt.printf("%s FIRST material %d id %d tick %d strength %.3f: %v\n",placement_case,sub.material,sub.id,placement_tick,s.materials[sub.material].subdivision_strength,placement_loads[sub.id])
    }
    placement_trace :: proc() {
    	placement_loads=make(map[u64]Placement_Load); placement_first=make(map[int]bool)
    	choices:=[2]Palette{.Wood,.Stone}; sizes:=[3]f32{2.4,3.8,2.4}
    	for choice in choices {
    		for size,i in sizes {
    			clear(&placement_first)
    			g:=sandbox_editor_create(); g.editor.palette=choice
    			x:=f32(1.5); if i==2 { x=2 }
    			assert(editor_place(&g,{x,0},{x+size,size})); sandbox_toggle_editor(&g)
    			placement_case=fmt.tprintf("%v %.1f x=%.1f placed",choice,size,x)
    			for tick in 1..=180 {
    				placement_tick=tick; clear(&placement_loads); sandbox_tick(&g,0,false)
    				if tick==1 { fmt.printf("%s first tick root: %v\n",placement_case,placement_loads[2]) }
    			}
    			fmt.printf("%s final %d/%d/%d\n",placement_case,counts_runtime(&g.scene))
    			sandbox_destroy(&g)
    		}
    		clear(&placement_first)
    		g:=sandbox_editor_create(); g.editor.palette=choice; assert(editor_place(&g,{1.5,0},{3.9,2.4})); sandbox_toggle_editor(&g)
    		placement_case=fmt.tprintf("%v tilted .5 drop",choice)
    		for _ in 0..<120 { clear(&placement_loads); sandbox_tick(&g,0,false) }
    		for sub in g.scene.subdivisions { if sub.live && sub.material==int(choice)+1 { body:=g.scene.physics.bodies[sub.id]; p:=b2.Body_GetPosition(body); p.y+=0.5; b2.Body_SetTransform(body,p,b2.MakeRot(0.15)); b2.Body_SetAwake(body,true) } }
    		for tick in 1..=180 { placement_tick=tick; clear(&placement_loads); sandbox_tick(&g,0,false) }
    		sandbox_destroy(&g)
    	}
    }

## Assistant

The trace confirms the suspect. A 3.8 × 3.8 block fails on Test’s first tick at **zero incoming closing speed**: the object’s contact load is 35.34, and the floor’s torque-based load is 105.12. Both Wood and Stone fail. Even a 2.4 × 2.4 block farther right can refine the floor while leaving the object intact.

The same block’s deliberate tilted drop first fails with a closing speed of **2.61 units/s**. I’ll use Box2D’s recorded pre-solve contact speed to qualify impacts, keeping support out of the damage check and leaving joint stress separate.

## Assistant

The placement checks now pass with the speed gate. The existing checks caught two details I’m addressing:

- The “opposing contacts” test used stationary overlapping walls, so it needs actual inward motion under the new policy.
- In the fast-impact test, Box2D records an 11-unit/s closing speed and a positive peak impulse, but zero total impulse at that step. I’ll use the recorded peak as a fallback for a qualified impact so the gate doesn’t discard a genuine hit.

The material strengths remain unchanged.

        for sub in game.scene.subdivisions { testing.expect(t,vlen(vsub(sub.pose.position,sub.rest_center))<0.04) }

        testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetLinearVelocity(game.player.body).y>5 && !game.player.grounded)
        max_height:=f32(0)

            max_height=max(max_height,b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body).y)
        }
        testing.expect(t,max_height>2 && game.player.grounded,"One jump must reach its apex and land without another airborne jump")

    player_stands_on_and_pushes_a_real_fragment :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
        sync.mutex_lock(&physics_test_mutex); defer sync.mutex_unlock(&physics_test_mutex)
        game:=sandbox_create(); defer sandbox_destroy(&game)
        // Detach a ground-level block, leaving an actual destruction body to stand on.
        id:=game.scene.subdivisions[3].id
        failures:=Failures{}
        for connection in game.scene.connections {
            if connection.a==id || connection.b==id { append(&failures.connections,connection.id) }
        }
        apply_failures(&game.scene,failures); free_failures(&failures)
        physics_sync_structure(&game.scene)
        body:=game.scene.physics.bodies[id]
        position:=b2.Body_GetPosition(body)
        b2.Body_SetTransform(game.player.body,{position.x,1.6},b2.MakeRot(0))
        for _ in 0..<120 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
        testing.expect(t,game.player.grounded && b2.Body_GetPosition(game.player.body).y>1.35,"Support must come from fragment contacts")
        // Move alongside the detached block and push it using the same collision world.
        b2.Body_SetTransform(body,{-1,0.43},b2.MakeRot(0))
        b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(body,{})
        b2.Body_SetTransform(game.player.body,{-2,0.6},b2.MakeRot(0))
        b2.Body_SetLinearVelocity(game.player.body,{})
        for _ in 0..<30 { sandbox_tick(&game,0,false) }
        start:=b2.Body_GetPosition(body).x
        for _ in 0..<30 { sandbox_tick(&game,1,false) }
        testing.expect(t,b2.Body_IsValid(body),"Routine player contact should leave the fragment intact")
        if b2.Body_IsValid(body) { testing.expect(t,b2.Body_GetPosition(body).x>start+0.05,"The player should physically push debris") }
    }

    # Placement support versus contact damage
    
    ## Confirmed first failure
    
    The original contact-damage check counted ordinary support as damage. Reproductions used the current editor/presets, seed 42, objects placed directly on the floor, and entered Test without any deliberate motion. Loads below are the existing calculator's equivalent force/torque loads; speed is Box2D's contact-point pre-solve relative closing speed.
    
    | Original case | First failing geometry | Tick | Contact load | Closing speed | Joint load |
    |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
    | Wood 3.8 × 3.8, x=1.5 | Object | 1 | 35.3414 vs strength 28 | **0** | 0 |
    | Stone 3.8 × 3.8, x=1.5 | Object | 1 | 35.3414 vs strength 35 | **0** | 0 |
    | Either large object | Floor | 1 | 105.1166 vs strength 35 | **0** | 0 |
    | Either material, 2.4 × 2.4, x=2 | Floor only | 1 | 38.9760 vs strength 35 | **0** | 0 |
    
    Recorded initial contact separation was zero: this first failure was ordinary gravity/support loading, not a landing impact or pre-existing overlap correction. The 2.4 × 2.4 rectangle at x=1.5 stayed intact in the original code; its translation to x=2 overloaded the floor's force/torque check. This explains why the previous drop case could settle initially while other ordinary placements failed.
    
    ## Focused change
    
    - A contact interaction qualifies for damage only if it contains an incoming point closing at **at least 1 world unit/s** with a positive recorded normal impulse. The existing load threshold still has to be exceeded.
    - Qualification is per other body. Points/fixtures against that body remain aggregated; an impact against one body cannot activate unrelated support against another.
    - Ordinary support and negligible settling still produce their normal physical response. They simply do not contribute contact damage. Joint stress and the integrated B policy remain separate and unchanged.
    - A genuine fast impact can expose a positive `maxNormalImpulse` while `totalNormalImpulse` is zero in the installed solver. The existing high-speed impact check reproduced this at an 11-unit/s closing speed. For an incoming qualifying point only, a zero total now falls back to its recorded peak; otherwise the impact could be missed and only later support loads observed.
    
    Material strengths, mass, physics stepping, collision geometry, blast load/impulse, flexibility, subdivision generation, rendering and fade were not tuned.
    
    ## Verification
    
    After the change, all listed placements retain exactly **one object root and one floor root**, with no connections or refinement. Automated coverage includes Wood and Stone, both 2.4-square positions, a 3.8-square object, and a 0.005-unit settling gap, each for 300 ticks. The native smoke also draws both large materials using the actual palette/drag/Test widgets and checks intact geometry after 120 frames.
    
    The previous deliberate 0.50-unit tilted drop still destroys both Wood and Stone and damages the floor. With the positive-peak fallback, first failure is detected at the initial landing on **tick 17**, closing speed **2.6133**; joint load is zero. Previously first failure appeared on tick 26 during continued landing contact, closing speed 2.6139. The newly detected contact loads are approximately 1674.72 on the object and 1949.06 on the floor. After 180 ticks, this landing leaves **21 Wood regions** or **7 Stone regions** in the respective runs. These impact magnitudes and resulting detail were recorded, not tuned in this pass.
    
    A default-radius-5 blast still destroys both materials and the floor. The existing fast-impact, surviving-joint stress, B-policy, graph, geometry, recursion, snapshot, Rubber and bomb checks pass. **All 63 tests passed**, and the expanded native input smoke passed. The playable executable was rebuilt.
    
    Two existing test fixtures were aligned with the intended distinction: opposing-contact aggregation now uses moving inward walls rather than stationary overlap; the player-support test starts on the surface and uses a slow push rather than a drop and running collision. Their destruction/physical-support assertions remain. A real running collision or hard landing on finite debris remains eligible for damage.
    
    Limit: steady crushing or sliding below the closing-speed threshold does not generate contact damage; joint stress still can. This is an impact qualification policy, not an energy or pressure model. How much fragmentation a qualified hit should produce remains a separate decision, especially now that the first real hit is reliably detected.
    
    Temporary trace/probe code was removed. The source change is local to contact-load calculation, focused checks/native smoke coverage, and documentation.

    set -eu
    
    VERSION="3.1.1"
    RELEASE="https://github.com/erincatto/box2d/archive/refs/tags/v$VERSION.tar.gz"
    
    cd "$(dirname "$0")"
    
    curl -O -L "$RELEASE"
    tar -xzvf "v$VERSION.tar.gz"
    
    cd "box2d-$VERSION"
    
    FLAGS="-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBOX2D_SAMPLES=OFF -DBOX2D_VALIDATE=OFF -DBOX2D_UNIT_TESTS=OFF"
    
    case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin)
        export MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET="11"
    
        case "$(uname -m)" in
        "x86_64" | "amd64")
            rm -rf build
            mkdir build
            cmake $FLAGS -DBOX2D_AVX2=ON -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=x86_64 -S . -B build
            cmake --build build
            cp build/src/libbox2d.a ../lib/box2d_darwin_amd64_avx2.a
    
            rm -rf build
            mkdir build
            cmake $FLAGS -DBOX2D_AVX2=OFF -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=x86_64 -S . -B build
            cmake --build build
            cp build/src/libbox2d.a ../lib/box2d_darwin_amd64_sse2.a
            ;;
        *)
            rm -rf build
            mkdir build
            cmake $FLAGS -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -S . -B build
            cmake --build build
            cp build/src/libbox2d.a ../lib/box2d_darwin_arm64.a
            ;;
        esac
        ;;
    *)
        case "$(uname -m)" in
        "x86_64" | "amd64")
            rm -rf build
            mkdir build
            cmake $FLAGS -DBOX2D_AVX2=ON -S . -B build
            cmake --build build
            cp build/src/libbox2d.a ../lib/box2d_other_amd64_avx2.a
    
            rm -rf build
            mkdir build
            cmake $FLAGS -DBOX2D_AVX2=OFF -S . -B build
            cmake --build build
            cp build/src/libbox2d.a ../lib/box2d_other_amd64_sse2.a
            ;;
        *)
            rm -rf build
            mkdir build
            cmake $FLAGS -S . -B build
            cmake --build build
            cp build/src/libbox2d.a ../lib/box2d_other.a
            ;;
        esac
        ;;
    esac
    
    cd ..
    
    set +e
    make -f wasm.Makefile
    if [[ $? -ne 0 ]]; then
        printf "\e[30;43mwarning:\e[0m Native Box2D libraries were built successfully, the WASM build failed, likely because your default C compiler and/or linker doesn't support WASM, you can set the CC and LD environment variables to point to a compiler and linker that support it\n"
    fi
    make -f wasm.Makefile clean
    set -e
    
    rm -rf "v$VERSION.tar.gz"
    rm -rf box2d-"$VERSION"

## Assistant

I found a binding mismatch. The linked library reports **Box2D 3.1.1**. In its header, the slots the installed Odin binding calls `totalNormalImpulse` and `maxNormalImpulse` are actually `normalImpulse` and `totalNormalImpulse`.

So the apparent “positive peak with zero total” was a field-reading error: it was zero final-substep impulse with a positive total. I’m checking that total against momentum change before deciding whether the existing conversion is sound.
